title: #2035 Catheter cleaning brush manipulations in peritoneal dialysis
authors: Matthias Zeiler; Anastasia Mancini; Simona Silvestri; Antonio Granata; Stefano Santarelli
abstract:
Background and Aims
Catheter malfunction is the Achilles heel of peritoneal dialysis. The approach to catheter malfunction is multi-faceted ranging from laxative prescription to laparoscopic catheter revision. We re-evaluated retrospectively the catheter brushing method utilizing a channel cleaning brush in peritoneal dialysis patients presenting dialysate inflow or outflow problems.
Method
In a bedside setting, the peritoneal catheter was forceful flushed with a 50 ml syringe, successively, if possible, the abdominal cavity was filled with dialysate fluid of about 1000 ml in order to distend the abdomen. Furthermore, the intraperitoneal part of the PD catheter was examined by ultrasound. Successively the dialysate drainage was observed. In the case of difficult filling or draining the PD catheter was closed with a plastic clamp and the transfer set removed after having disinfected the connection with sodium hypochlorite solution 0.5%. Aseptically the channel-cleaning brush (Olympus BW-15B, autoclavable cleaning brush for endoscopes with minimum working channel size of 2.0–3.2 mm, length 95 cm, coil sheath guidewire with nylon bristles close to the flexible ball tip) was inserted in the catheter and advanced. In most cases the patient referred localized pain at the contact of the bristles or brush-tip with the peritoneum, consecutively the brush was forcefully retracted. The brushing manipulation was repeated at least two to three times and the material/tissue attached to the nylon bristles removed. After the guidewire manipulation, a dialysate exchange procedure was performed and catheter function observed. We analyzed the outcome of 86 brushing manipulations in 76 patients.
Results
No case of peritonitis, bowel or bladder damage was reported. In 31% of manipulations, slight intraperitoneal self-limiting bleeding was observed. 89% of these cases were associated to omental entrapment into the catheter lumen or side holes, and regained catheter function only after laparoscopic revision. Displaced catheters without signs of omental wrapping at ultrasound examination could be relocated and regained function in 62% of cases. Curled catheters in the absence of omental wrapping regained function in 54% as the spiral position changed during the manipulation. 86% of cases in which a fibrin thrombus had been removed during the brushing manipulation regained catheter function.
Conclusion
Brushing of the catheter even without fluoroscopy control seems to be safe. The flexible guidewire with metal blunt tip and nylon bristles was able to remove effectively intraluminal obstruction by fibrin thrombus, indicated the catheter position by localized pain, helped to relocate catheters in absence of omental wrapping and was useful in at least half of the cases to change the spiral position of curled catheters. The success rate of catheter brushing depends on the catheter malfunction cause with highest rates in fibrin thrombus obstruction and lowest in omental entrapment. Slight bleeding is an indicator of omental wrapping.

title: #1635 Pre-operative vascular mapping and the prognostic value of vascular calcification in advanced CKD
authors: Tiago Assis Pereira; Patrícia Alves; Ana Sofia Domingos; João Figueiredo Martins; Luís Santos; Paula Milhazes Guimarães; Cristina Jorge
abstract:
Background and Aims
Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is associated with major complications, including the initiation of renal replacement therapy, cardiovascular (CV) events, and accelerated mortality. One of the major factors underlying this clinical scenario is vascular calcification (VC). Currently, with the widespread use of ultrasound (US) for pre-surgical mapping in advanced CKD patients proposed for vascular access, VC can be easily diagnosed and stratified. This presents an opportunity to develop a newer and more accessible score with clinical relevance for CKD patients.
Method
This observational cohort study included all CKD patients referred for US mapping to create vascular access. All eligible patients underwent demographic, clinical and vascular data collection, during the mapping procedure.
Arterial calcification was assessed in each major arm artery (brachial, radial, and ulnar). Calcification severity was determined based on wall involvement and luminal narrowing. Each artery was categorized as having either none/non-significant calcification or significant calcification. A calcification score (CS) was developed, reflecting the number of arm arteries with significant calcification (range: 0–6).
Following the identification of the main predictors for calcification and higher CS, we aimed to validate the CS as predictor of hard outcomes, including CV events, all-cause mortality, and a combined endpoint.
Results
A total of 303 patients were evaluated, with a mean follow-up period of 401 ± 170 days. The mean age was 67 years, and 57% of the cohort were male and 77% were white. Sixty-seven percent of the cohort were pre-dialysis (mean eGFR 15 mL/min/1.73 m2), while 25% were already on hemodialysis (HD).
The calcification evaluation showed that 42% presented at least one artery with severe calcification, and that higher scores (5 to 6 arteries) were restricted to 12%.
Only diabetes (p = 0.000), male gender (p = 0.018), and heart failure (p = 0.025) revealed as predictors for CS > 0 in a multivariate model.
Severe diffuse vascular calcification, defined as a CS ≥ 5, was associated with advanced age, diabetes, peripheral arterial disease (PAD), and obesity. Subsequent multivariate analysis identified diabetes (p = 0.005) and PAD (p = 0.002) as the most significant predictors of severe calcification.
During follow-up, all-cause death, CV events, and the combined endpoint (all-cause death or CV event) occurred in 8%, 13%, and 19% of patients, respectively.
Regarding these clinical outcomes, multivariate analysis demonstrated that CV events and the combined endpoint were significantly associated with advanced age (p = 0.004), heart failure (p = 0.001), and CS scale (p = 0.005), particularly when CS > 3 (p = 0.006). Advanced age (p = 0.000) was the sole predictor for all-cause mortality.
Kaplan-Meier survival analysis revealed that only a CS ≥ 5 was significantly associated with a higher risk of CV events (log-rank p = 0.011) and the combined endpoint (p = 0.038) (Figs 1 and 2).
Conclusion
VC is a hallmark finding in CKD, reflecting prior exposure to risk factors and serving as a strong predictor of adverse cardiovascular outcomes. While VC is prevalent in CKD, only a subset of patients experiences accelerated and severe calcification. Identifying these high-risk individuals is crucial for developing and implementing targeted therapeutic strategies to improve clinical outcomes.
This study showed stronger association of VC with advanced age and PAD. Focusing in the highest calcification index, diabetes and PAD were the most significant.
Finally, this study confirmed the validity of an US-based calcification score in predicting CV events. Further, a longer and more tailored evaluation could confirm its prognostic value for CV and all-cause death. Importantly, a similar extended study should be implemented in earlier stages of CKD to elucidate the natural progression of VC and assess the potential role of therapeutic interventions in mitigating its development and associated CV risks.

title: #1894 Kidney transplantation with a functional AV fistula is associated to long-term risk of de novo heart failure and atrial fibrillation
authors: Ulrika Hahn Lundström; Marie Evans
abstract:
Background and Aims
Cardiovascular disease is the main cause of mortality in kidney transplanted (KTx) patients. Although the arterio venous fistula (AVF) is the preferred access option for patients undergoing hemodialysis, its role in KTx patients is debated mainly due to its possible link to higher post-transplantation cardiovascular disease, (CVD) rates. This study aimed to investigate the association between a functional AVF at the time of KTx and incidence of de novo heart failure (HF) and atrial fibrillation (AF) post transplantation, and whether there is a difference in risk between forearm AVFs and upper arm AVFs.
Method
In this observational cohort study, we included patients from the Swedish Renal Registry (SRR) who underwent kidney transplantation between Jan 1st, 2009 and Dec 31st, 2020. KTx patients with a functional forearm and upper arm AVF were compared to KTx patients without any AVF (peritoneal dialysis and pre-emptive KTx). Patient and vascular access characteristics, including clinical data and laboratory measurements were collected from the SRR. Use of medications were ascertained by the National Registry for Dispensed drugs, whereas comorbidities (ICD-10 codes) were obtained through a linkage with the Patient Registry. The outcomes (time to first hospitalization for heart failure [HF] and atrial fibrillation [AF] were obtained from the Patient Registry. The patients were followed until they experienced an event, death, ligation of the AVF or end of follow-up (Dec 31, 2021). Cumulative incidence curves and adjusted cause-specific cox proportional hazards regression models were used to assess time to each outcome of interest. Models were adjusted for age, sex, vintage (time on dialysis), comorbidities (diabetes, ischemic heart disease, stroke, peripheral arterial disease, cancer, history of AF/HF), medication (ACE/ARB, betablockers, diuretics, statins, oral anticoagulants, insulin), blood pressure, BMI, and lab (albumin, hemoglobin, crp, s-creatinine, and phosphate).
Results
In total 3,361 KTx patients were included (without an AVF [n = 2236], with forearm AVF [n = 829] and upper arm AVF [n = 296]. Patients in the no AVF group were slightly younger (51 years compared to 55 and 56 years) and had somewhat lower prevalence of comorbidities, and vintage. The perioperative access flow at access creation was higher in upper arm AVF (350 ml/min) than forearm AVFs (200 ml/min). During a median follow-up time of 6.1 years there were 174 deaths (5.2%), 197 incident AF and 163 incident HF events. The HF incidences in no AVF, lower and upper arm AVF were 0.6%, 1.7% and 1,9%, while the AF incidences were 0.9%, 1.8% and 1.5%, respectively. The adjusted hazard ratio of de novo HF was significantly higher for both lower and upper arm AVFs compared to no AVF (2.22 [CI 1.52;3.24] (P < 0.001) vs 2.55 [CI 1.56;4.15] (P < 0.001)), but there was no statistically significant difference between lower and upper arm AVF (P = 0.08). For de novo AF, a forearm AVF was associated with an increased risk (adj HR 1.57 [CI1.13;2.19] while upper arm AVF was associated with a non-significantly increased risk (adj HR 1.34 [CI0.83;2.18].
Conclusion
This large observational cohort study in patients who were KTx found an association between having a functional AVF at the time of transplantation and long-term risk of de novo HF and AF incidence. These findings underscore the importance of future trials where the effects of ligation of AVFs post transplantation are assessed.

title: #1295 The effect of low dialysate sodium concentration on ambulatory aortic blood pressure and arterial stiffness in patients with intradialytic hypertension: a randomized crossover study
authors: Fotini Iatridi; Marieta P Theodorakopoulou; Robert Ekart; Artemios Karagiannidis; Konstantinos Malandris; Areti Georgiou; Efstathios Xagas; Ioanna Revela; Ioannis Tsouchnikas; Panagiotis Giamalis; Pantelis Sarafidis
abstract:
Background and Aims
Intradialytic hypertension (IDH) is associated with increased cardiovascular risk. Arterial stiffness is a strong predictor of adverse outcomes in dialysis patients and may contribute to the development of the phenomenon, as patients with IDH exhibit higher ambulatory aortic blood pressure (BP) and arterial stiffness parameters than patients without IDH.
Method
This analysis examined the effect of low (137 mEq/L) compared to standard (140 mEq/L) dialysate sodium concentration on 48-hour aortic BP and arterial stiffness parameters in IDH patients. In this prespecified secondary analysis of a randomized, single-blind, crossover study, 29 IDH patients underwent four hemodialysis sessions with low followed by four sessions with standard dialysate sodium or vice-versa. Mean 48-hour, pre-/post-dialysis and intradialytic aortic systolic/diastolic BP (SBP/DBP), and arterial stiffness indices were assessed.
Results
Mean 48-hour aortic SBP/DBP were significantly lower with low versus standard dialysate sodium (124.1 ± 16.4/83.0± 14.1 mmHg vs 128.5 ± 12.9/85.8 ± 14.1 mmHg, P = 0.013/P = 0.006 respectively). Low dialysate sodium also significantly reduced pre-dialysis aortic SBP (126.4 ± 17.4 vs 135.6 ± 18.6 mmHg, P = 0.044) and post-dialysis aortic SBP (137.0 ± 20.0 vs 147.9 ± 18.1 mmHg, P = 0.01). All wave reflection indices were numerically lower with low dialysate sodium; among them, heart rate-adjusted augmentation index (AIx (75)) was significantly lower during the 48-hour (26.3 ± 6.7 vs 27.7 ± 5.8%, P = 0.03), 44-hour, day-time and intradialytic periods. Low dialysate sodium resulted in decreased 48-hour pulse wave velocity (PWV) (9.9 ± 2.5 vs 10.1 ± 2.6m/s, P = 0.008); similar differences for PWV were observed during all examined time intervals.
Conclusion
In conclusion, ambulatory 48-hour aortic BP and arterial stiffness parameters were significantly lower using low compared to standard dialysate sodium in IDH patients. These findings further support the use of low dialysate sodium for BP management in this population.

title: #1319 Effect of dapagliflozin in patients with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis
authors: Álvaro Álvarez López; Jaime Hernán Merino; Sergio Barroso-Hernandez; María Victoria Martín Hidalgo Barquero; Jorge Alberto Rodriguez Sabillon; Teresa de Jesús Giraldo Rua; Beatriz Gómez Gallego; Lucia Martin Jiménez; Baldomero Romero Cancho; Nicolas Roberto Robles Perez-Monteoliva
abstract:
Background and Aims
Sodium-glucose cotransporter type 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) have been shown to provide renal and cardiovascular benefits in patients with heart failure, diabetes mellitus, and/or chronic kidney disease. However, patients with end-stage renal disease were excluded from clinical trials, so these drugs have limited use in patients with a glomerular filtration rate (GFR) below 20 ml/min. Currently, there is little evidence regarding the pharmacokinetics of these medications in patients with reduced GFR, although it is known that the renal elimination of dapagliflozin is less than 1%.
Our objective was to evaluate the safety of dapagliflozin in a small series of patients on hemodialysis, as well as its effect on anemia, residual urine output, and body composition.
Method
A case series of 8 patients on chronic hemodialysis who began treatment with dapagliflozin between November 2021 and March 2023. All of them had residual urine output > 500 ml/day, residual urea clearance (Kru) > 3 ml/min, and normal C-peptide levels. The follow-up period ranged from 6 to 12 months after starting the medication. Prior to initiation, informed consent was obtained from the patients, which was documented in their medical records. Analytical parameters, bioimpedance data, and residual urine volume were collected.
The baseline characteristics of the sample were a mean age of 77.1 years (87% male). 50% of the patients were on online post-hemodiafiltration. 62.5% of the patients were dialyzed through an arteriovenous fistula. All of them, regardless of vascular access, achieved optimal Kt/v values.
Results
The medication was well tolerated by all patients, and none of them required discontinuation due to adverse effects. We observed an improvement in erythropoietin resistance indices from the start of treatment, which persisted throughout the follow-up period. Hemoglobin levels and body mass index remained stable. Regarding bioimpedance, a decrease in total body volume was noted without variation between intracellular and extracellular volumes. Additionally, there was a trend toward a decrease in lean body mass, with a reduction in muscle mass and an increase in fat-free mass.
Conclusion
In our experience, we can conclude that dapagliflozin is a safe and well-tolerated medication in patients with advanced kidney disease on hemodialysis. The results found are similar to those observed in patients with a GFR > 20 ml/min. The main limitations of our study are the small number of patients and the lack of a control group. Nevertheless, we believe this study can serve as a starting point for conducting clinical trials in this population, which has a high cardiovascular morbidity and mortality rate.

title: #2612 Synbiotic supplementation for chronic constipation in patients under peritoneal dialysis: an italian multicenter prospective study
authors: Gennaro Argentino; Giuseppe Paribello; Carlo Garofalo; Andrea Foderini; Federica Marzano; Simona Andriella; Tino Paolo Ambrosino; Francesco Cascone; Luigi Di Martino; Francesco Romano; Lucio Selvaggi; Silvio Borrelli
abstract:
Background and Aims
Chronic constipation is a common issue in patients undergoing peritoneal dialysis (PD), which can interfere with the proper functioning of the dialysis catheter and increase the risk of serious complications. Patients under PD show a profound alteration of their intestinal microbiome, which plays a crucial role in maintaining gastrointestinal function.

Method

title: #3628 Rationale and study design of EXCITE, a pilot study to evaluate safety and efficacy of PolyCore, a ternary combination of xylitol, L-carnitine and polydextrIn, to treat end-stage kidney disease patients starting peritoneal dialysis
authors: Silvio Borrelli; Tommaso Prosdocimi; Mario Bonomini; Francesco Trepiccione; Luca Nardelli; Valerio Vizzardi; Richard Corbett; Sarah Lawman; Giuseppe Paribello; Lorenzo Di Liberato; Carlo Garofalo; Arduino Arduini
abstract:
Background
Incremental Peritoneal Dialysis (PD) is a strategy for initiating PD that aims to reduce dialysis burden and, consequently, improve patients’ therapy acceptance and quality of life. Incremental PD may help to preserve diuresis, reduce costs and minimize plastic waste, with no observed difference in mortality compared to standard PD.
Almost all PD fluids exploit glucose as an osmotic agent that rapidly diffuses across the peritoneal membrane, potentially resulting in metabolic abnormalities such as hyperglycemia, hyperinsulinemia, obesity, and hyperlipidemia. Moreover, glucose itself induces significant morphological and functional changes in the peritoneum leading to ultrafiltration failure. Xylitol and L-carnitine have been proposed as potential alternatives to glucose and, after successful preclinical testing, are now in phase III of clinical development (ELIXIR study, EU CT n° 2024-513562-19-00).
Here we report the design of EXCITE, the first pilot study to assess the safety and efficacy of PolyCore, a bimodal PD solution formulated as a ternary combination of xylitol, L-carnitine and Polydextrin, in ESKD patients treated with incremental PD.
Study design
EXCITE is a single-arm, pilot, multicenter study to evaluate the safety and efficacy of PolyCore, a ternary combination of xylitol, l-carnitine and polydextrin, to treat end-stage kidney disease patients starting peritoneal dialysis.
The study shall enroll ESKD patients, in stable clinical conditions, incident to IPD or who have been receiving IPD for no more than 6 months, with GFR ≥ 5 ml/min/1.73 m2, Kt/V urea ≥ 1.7, and being treated with two PD exchanges per day encompassing one Icodextrin (7.5%)-based solution and a Glucose (up to 1.5%)-based. Main exclusion criteria are having experienced a peritonitis in the three months preceding screening, severe pulmonary/cardiac/hepatic insufficiency and clinically significant abnormal liver function.
Enrolled patients shall enter a 28-day run-in period starting or continuing their pre-study incremental PD. The run-in period shall allow to verify the PD treatment adequacy and to genetically test patients for primary hyperoxaluria type 1 and 2. After the run-in period, patients will be switched to PolyCore for 28 days according to the following schedule: - PolyCore, two extended duration exchanges [8–12 hours] or- PolyCore, one extended duration exchange [8–12 hours] and one short dwell exchange [4–6 hours]
Patients who need to transition to a full dose of PD treatment during the study will drop out of the study.
The primary endpoints, related to safety, include the evaluation of Adverse Events, blood chemistry and hematology, 24 h diuresis and dialysate analyses, weekly Kt/V and residual kidney function. Secondary endpoints, related to efficacy, include peritoneal ultrafiltration, sodium removal, glycemic and lipidic parameters, peritoneal clearances and quality of life by KDQOL-SF.
Given the nature of the study, single-arm and pilot without formal formulation of the hypotheses to be tested, 28 patients, including drop-outs, will be enrolled. This number is sufficient to obtain sufficiently valid summary measures of efficacy estimates to allow a formal calculation for the design of a proof of efficacy study.
Conclusions
Osmo-metabolic agents, currently in Phase III trials, offer a promising alternative to the many adverse effects of glucose. The EXCITE study, a pilot trial, aims to provide the first scientific insights into the use of osmo-metabolic agents in combination with polydextrin, a key component of existing glucose-free alternatives, with the aim of yielding a single product for incremental peritoneal dialysis, combining the local and systemic biocompatibility of xylitol and L-carnitine with ultrafiltration performance of Polydextrin.

title: #2472 Evaluation of peritoneal dialysis dropouts: a single centre observational study over 3-year follow-up
authors: Varun Mamidi; Henry Wu; Joanne Collier; Joanne Martin; David Lewis; Rajkumar Chinnadurai
abstract:
Background and Aims
Peritoneal dialysis (PD) offers greater flexibility, a better quality of life, a lower risk of infections, better preservation of residual kidney function, and lower healthcare costs in comparison to in-centre hemodialysis (HD). Despite the known advantages associated with PD, over 35% of patients transition from PD to HD annually in the UK. The most common reasons for PD dropouts include mechanical failure, infection, inadequate clearance and death whilst receiving PD. We conducted a retrospective observational study at our centre investigating the characteristics of patients who dropped out of their PD regimens and the reasons for PD dropout over a 3-year follow-up period.
Method
There were 114 adult patients under the care of the renal medicine department at Northern Care Alliance NHS Foundation Trust who dropped out of PD between January 2022 and September 2024. Specific patient characteristics and the reasons for PD dropout were evaluated over this time period. Data collated include patient demographic characteristics, Charlson comorbidity index (CCI) scores prior to PD catheter insertion, issues identified during home visit assessments prior to PD initiation, and attendance to dialysis education visits. PD catheter-related information including the catheter insertion method (i.e. medical vs surgical insertion), whether an elective outpatient vs inpatient procedure was received, and the occurrence of acute complications post PD catheter insertion (e.g. catheter malposition) were recorded. In this study, continuous variables are expressed as median (interquartile range) with p values calculated via the Kruskal–Wallis H test or Mann–Whitney U test. Categorical variables are expressed as numbers (percentage) with p values calculated by the Chi-squared test. Comparisons were made between PD dropouts after catheter removal due to ’undesirable cause’ (UC) (i.e. infection and/or PD catheter dysfunction) versus ’natural causes’ (NC) (i.e. death, receipt of kidney transplantation or patient choice). Logistic regression statistics were applied to represent the findings of this comparative analysis.
Results
There were 43 patients in 2022, 42 patients in 2023, and 29 patients in 2024 who dropped out of PD. The cohort’s median age was 55.3 years, in which patients were predominantly male (69%) and of White ethnicity (81.3%). Patient characteristics relating to the pre-PD assessments—including CCI scores, issues identified during home visit assessments prior to PD initiation, and attendance to dialysis education visits—were similar between 2022 and 2024. The rates of medical PD catheter insertion (81.4% in 2022 vs 81% in 2023 vs 75.9% in 2024, P = 0.826) and elective outpatient catheter insertion (70% in 2022 vs 76.2% in 2023 vs 79.3% in 2024, P = 0.630) were similar across the 3 years. No differences were observed in terms of peri-operative characteristics relating to PD catheter insertion between 2022 and 2024, including constipation issues post-procedure, pre-procedure CCI scores or the number of medications received. There were an increased proportion of patients who dropped out of PD due to availability for kidney transplantation between 2022 and 2024 (21% in 2022 vs 28.6% in 2023 vs 48% in 2024, P = 0.005). Nevertheless, PD dropouts because of UC appeared similar over the years (35% in 2022 vs 43% in 2023 vs 31% in 2024, P = 0.564).
Of the 114 patients, 42 had PD drop off due to UC and 72 had a NC. A comparison between the two groups showed a higher proportion of patients who had an emergency PD catheter insertion as inpatients eventually dropped off PD due to an UC (40.5% UC vs 16.7% NC, P = 0.005) (Table 1). Binary logistic regression analysis noted emergency inpatient catheter insertion as a significant predictor of UC for PD removal/drop out (OR 3.40, 95% CI 1.41–8.14, P = 0.006).
Conclusion
Our study highlights emergency inpatient PD catheter insertion as a risk factor that predicts for future ’undesirable‘ PD dropout. This study’s findings strengthen the stance that meticulous pre-procedure assessments in advanced kidney care services and dialysis preparation clinics are warranted to prevent ’undesirable‘ PD dropouts.

title: #2720 Real-world effectiveness of patiromer among hemodialysis (HD) patients prescribed various treatment schedules over a one-year follow-up
authors: Linda Ficociello; Meijiao Zhou; Joanna Willetts; Maria Gil-Mir; Hans-Juergen Arens; Maria Navarro; Michael Anger
abstract:
Background and Aims
Patiromer (PAT) is a non-absorbed, calcium-based potassium (K) binding polymer that is sodium-free and indicated for treating hyperkalemia. We conducted a retrospective analysis to assess the changes in dialysate and serum potassium (sK) along with other electrolytes before and after PAT prescription in hemodialysis (HD) patients over a one-year follow-up.
Method
To be included in the analysis, patients were adult, thrice-weekly HD, prevalent HD patients first prescribed PAT monotherapy between 1/2016 and 12/2022 at Fresenius Kidney Care. Patients had sK measured during a 91-day (pre-PAT) baseline (bl) and during PAT treatment (follow up; Q1 to Q4). Furthermore, they had a starting PAT treatment schedule of (1) less than once a day, (2) once a day, (3) greater than once a day, or (4) as directed.
Results
Table 1 shows serum electrolyte levels including sK from BL to Q4 by PAT treatment schedule. The largest group of patients were prescribed PAT once a day (n = 6,069). Overall, 91.2% of patients were prescribed 8.4 g and for patients with once a day 89.9% were on 8.4 g. We observed that although only 33.9% of these patients had a sK < 5.5 mEq/L at BL, during PAT treatment 68.4% of patients had sK < 5.5 mEq/L. Similar patterns were seen with other treatment schedules. Patients with a schedule of “as directed” had the highest baseline (40.7%) and Q4 (74.2%) percent sK < 5.5 mEq/L. All groups showed a decrease in the percent of patients receiving at least one 1K dialysate bath from BL to Follow-up (Fig. 1). For example, patients prescribed PAT once a day had a decrease in patients receiving at least one 1K dialysate from 18.9% at BL to 12% by Q4.
Conclusion
In a real-world analysis of adult, prevalent HD patients, various treatment schedules were prescribed for PAT, although the most common was once a day with 8.4 g per packet. All treatment schedule groups had a decrease in mean sK, an increase in the percent of patients achieving < 5.5 mEq/L and a decrease in patients receiving at least one treatment with 1K dialysate bath.

title: #3013 Association of physical function and fear of falling with the number of falls over a 12-month period in patients on hemodialysis
authors: Maycon Moura Reboredo; Luciana Angélica Da Silva de Jesus; Emanuele Poliana Lawall Gravina; Rodrigo Garcia; Ana Carolina Braga; Barbara Sthefanie de Oliveira; Lígia Brito Matoso; Clara Santos; Maria Luiza Reis; Heitor Ribeiro; Leda Marília Fonseca Lucinda
abstract:
Background and Aims
Patients on hemodialysis have cardiovascular complications and impairments in physical and postural balance, which contribute to a higher risk of falls.
Therefore, this study evaluated the association of physical function and fear of falling with the number of falls over a 12-month period in patients undergoing hemodialysis.
Method
This 12-month prospective study included patients on regular hemodialysis. Physical function was assessed using gait speed over 15 feet, the Timed Up and Go (TUG) test, the 5-repetition sit-to-stand (5-STS) test, and handgrip strength. Fear of falling was measured using the Falls Efficacy Scale-International (FES-I). Following the initial assessment, the number of falls was monitored monthly for 12 months using a standardized evaluation. A fall was defined as an unexpected event in which the individual came to rest on the ground, floor, or lower level. A univariate negative binomial regression model was used to evaluate the association of the number of falls with physical function, fear of falling, and sociodemographic, clinical, and laboratory data. Variables significantly associated with the number of falls were included as independent variables in a multivariate negative binomial regression model, with the number of falls as the dependent variable. A p-value of <0.05 was considered statistically significant.
Results
This study included 112 patients (58.7 ± 12.9 years, 56.3% male). The incidence of falls was 31.3%. Falls occurred predominantly on nondialysis day and at the patient’s home. In the multivariate negative binomial regression model, the number of falls was significantly associated with performance in the TUG (OR: 1.37; 95% CI: 1.16–1.62), gait speed (OR: 0.22; 95% CI: 0.06–0.77), handgrip strength (OR: 0.95; 95% CI: 0.91–0.99) and FES-I score (OR: 1.11; 95% CI: 1.06–1.17), after adjustment for potential confounders (age, gender, educational level, body mass index, history of fall, cardiovascular disease and calcium levels).
Conclusion
The number of falls was associated with physical function and fear of falling in patients undergoing hemodialysis.

title: #465 Relationship between tissue hydration and peritoneal membrane transport
authors: Fansan Zhu; Nadja Grobe; Xiaoling Wang; Hasib Absar; Xin Wang; Lela Tisdale; Laura Rosales Merlo; Maricar Villamar; Jun Yi; Manuela Stauss-Grabo; Len Usvyat; Peter Kotanko
abstract:
Background and Aims
The peritoneal equilibration test (PET) is essential for understanding peritoneal membrane transport in peritoneal dialysis (PD) treatment. However, peritoneal membrane function can be influenced by numerous factors, including fluid status. The aim of this study was to investigate whether tissue hydration influences PET results, including D/P creatinine and D/D0 glucose.
Method
Standard PET was performed with 2.5% glucose and 2 L of dialysate for a 4-hour dwell. Whole body and calf bioimpedance (Hydra 4200, Xitron Technologies, San Diego, CA) were measured in a sitting position, both pre- and post-PD treatment. Whole body extracellular volume (wECV) was estimated using the Xitron program. title: #536 Impact of adipose tissue on estimating extracellular resistance in hemodialysis patients using a two-compartment model
authors: Fansan Zhu; Peter Kotanko
abstract:
Background and Aims
Determination of fluid status in dialysis patients is a key in clinical practice. Although multi-frequency bioimpedance spectroscopy (BIS) is a valuable technique in clinical research for assessing body composition and fluid status, it presents challenges when estimating body hydration in routine clinical settings for individual patients. Standard BIS method is based on a two-compartment (2C) model, which processes raw resistance and reactance data to account for extracellular and intracellular volumes yet excluding adipose tissue (fat). We proposed an electrical equivalent circuit for a three-compartment (3C) model. The aim of this study was to evaluate whether adipose tissue influence the accuracy of extracellular resistance by the 2C model.
Method
Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and bioimpedance measurements (Hydra 4200, Xitron Technologies) were performed within 10 cm of the calf in a group of hemodialysis patients prior to dialysis. Calf circumference at maximal (Cmax) and minimal (Cmin) cross-sectional areas within a 10 cm distance were measured, respectively. The standard 2C model (Cole model, Fig. 1A) was used to calculate extracellular resistance (RE-2C), intracellular resistance (RI-2C), and capacitance (CM) using the Xitron program. We propose a 3C model that incorporates fat resistance (RF) and capacitance (CF) through curve-fitting methods (Zhu et al., Physiol Meas, 26:S133–S143, 2005) to calculate RF, RE-3C and RI-3C in the calf (Fig. 1B). The calf geometric volume (VCalf = L*C2/4π) can be calculated by the average circumference (C = (Cmax + Cmin)/2) and the length (L = 10 cm) of the calf. Calf fat-free mass (cFFM) was calculated as the difference between VCalf and adipose tissue (ATCalf). The thickness of ATCalf was calculated as the difference in cross-sectional area between VCalf and cFFM. Linear regression analysis was used to determine the relationship between the variables.
Results
Eighteen HD patients (5 females; age 56.1 ± 10.7 years; weight 79.6 ± 17.9 kg) were studied. Absolute RF values were strongly negatively correlated with ATCalf as determined by MRI (R2 = 0.69, P < 0.0001; Fig. 2). RE-2C was significantly higher than RE-3C (45.5 ± 8.3 vs. 42.8 ± 7.1 Ω; P < 0.01). On the other hand, there was no statistical difference in intracellular resistance between RI-2C and RI-3C (60.8 ± 18.4 vs. 57.9 ± 20.9 Ω; P = 0.23). RE-2C correlated strongly with RE-3C (R2 = 0.77, P < 0.0001); however, RE-2C systematically overestimated values compared to RE-3C (Fig. 3). Additionally, RE-2C was positively correlated with the thickness of ATCalf (Fig. 4). Moreover, the difference between RE-2C and RE-3C was found to be inversely associated with cFFM (Fig. 5).
Conclusion
This study demonstrated that higher extracellular resistance as estimated by the 2C model is associated with greater adipose tissue thickness. Since overestimating resistance can lead to an underestimation of body fluid, the effect of adipose tissue on calculations of body fluid in individuals cannot be ignored. Our study found that the accuracy of extracellular resistance estimated by the two-compartment (2C) model (Cole model) may be affected in obese subjects, as the fat component is ignored in the 2C model. Adding a third component, the 3C model may improve the accuracy of fluid estimation using bioimpedance. It is important to note that the 3C model presented in this study assumes that skin impedance does not affect body bioimpedance measurements. However, this assumption may not hold true for patients with very dry or very wet skin. Incorporating skin impedance into the model could further enhance the accuracy of bioimpedance measurements.

title: #3427 Perdialytic infusion of sodium octanoate improves the dialytic clearance of protein-bound uremic toxins in anephric pigs
authors: Laure-Anne Raillon; Florine Payelle; Lionel Augeul; Nans Florens; Elodie Diaf; Aziz Aberkane; Marie Martin; Jean-Claude Alvarez; Ziad Massy; Mikael Croyal; Fitsum Guebre-Egziabher; Christophe Soulage
abstract:
Background and Aims
Protein-bound uremic toxins (PBUTs) remain a concerning burden in patients with end-stage renal disease since their removal in hemodialysis (HD) is limited by their strong binding to plasma proteins. By increasing their circulating free fraction during HD, binding competitors of serum albumin could be used to increase their dialytic clearance. Medium chain fatty acids (MCFAs) are physiological ligands of serum albumin and potent candidates for that purpose. The aim of this work was to evaluate whether the perfusion of sodium octanoate (a 8-carbon MCFA) could improve the removal of PBUTs during an experimental session of hemodialysis in anephric pigs.
Method
Under sevoflurane anesthesia, kidney failure was induced by ligation of both renal pedicles on 17 pigs (35–40 kg). Two protein bound uremic toxins (indoxyl-sulfate – IS and p-cresyl-sulfate – pCS) were injected at 5 mg/kg. Pigs were dialyzed for 2 hours through a 2 lumen jugular catheter using a dialysis generator Physidia S3 with a blood flow of 200 mL/min and a dialysate flow of 200 mL/min. During the HD session, sodium octanoate (333 mmol/L) was perfused intravenously at a dose of 6 (n = 5) or 47 mmol/hour (n = 6) while perfusion of saline was used as control (n = 6). Protein bound uremic toxins were iteratively assayed in plasma and effluent dialysate using LC-MS/MS. Octanoate concentrations were iteratively assayed in plasma and effluent dialysate by GC-MS. Data were expressed as median (interquartile range) and compared using Kruskall & wallis tests
Results
Perfusion of sodium octanoate increased the median plasma concentration of octanoate from nearly undetectable 0.002 (0.001–0.005) to 1.95 (0.89–2.71) and 640 (406–10941) µmol/L in pigs perfused with 6 or 47 mmol/h of octanoate, respectively (P < 0.001, compared to controls). Perfusion of octanoate significantly improved the dialytic clearance of both toxins as evidenced by their increased fractional removal, dialysate concentration and clearance (all P < 0.05). The clearance of IS was increased from 13 (12–14) mL/min to 29 (20–32) and 60 (49–76) mL/min in pigs perfused with 6 or 47 mmol/h of octanoate, respectively (P < 0.04 and P < 0.0001, compared to controls) (Fig. 1A). Similarly, the clearance of pCS was increased from 12 (11–14) mL/min to 23 (18–26) and 60 (47–70) mL/min in pigs perfused with 6 or 47 mmol/h of octanoate, respectively (P = 0.08 and P < 0.001, compared to controls) (Fig. 1B). Tolerance for all animals was good and no side effect was reported (no hypertriglyceridemia and no hemolysis).
Conclusion
Sodium octanoate is a very promising candidate to displace the binding of PBUTs such as p-CS and IS. The per-dialytic administration of octanoate significantly enhanced the removal of PBUTs and could constitute a new strategy to get rid of these compounds and prevent their accumulation in end-stage kidney disease patients. Due to their relative inocuity (limited toxicity and good metabolic profile), MCFAs could be better tolerated than other chemical compounds that has already been tested clinically such as ibuprofen. Further clinical studies are however needed to carefully evaluate this potentially new therapeutic option and its’ impact on clinical outcomes.

title: #3849 Behavior of left ventricular diastolic dysfunction during the dialysis session
authors: Ana Alicia Astroña Rojas; María de Los Ángeles Fernández Rojo; María Antonia García Rubiales; Carlos Jesús Cabezas Reina; Desirée Bustos Jiménez; Narda Lorena Avila Molina; Iván Carmena Rodríguez; Kevin Palmero Klein; David Carro Herrero; Francisco Javier Ahijado Hormigos
abstract:
Background and Aims
Left ventricular diastolic dysfunction is common in hemodialysis patients and is associated with a worse prognosis. Its prevalence ranges from 48%–73% in dialysis patients. The challenge in detecting it lies in its definition. Although it would include not only echocardiographic parameters (E/A ratio < 1, and E/e’ ratio >10) but also clinical ones, current interest focuses on detecting early and asymptomatic abnormalities to prevent intradialytic hemodynamic events.
Method
A prospective observational study was conducted on 46 stable hemodialysis patients with a median age of 63.4 years (IQR 56.2–78.5), 47% of whom were diabetic and 97.5% hypertensive. Echocardiography and tissue Doppler were performed before and after dialysis. The study population was divided into those who experienced hypotension during the session, defined as Fall20 [(preHD SBP – minimum intraHD SBP) ≥ 20 mmHg], and differences in echocardiographic parameters between the two groups were analyzed.
Results
Among the baseline structural and functional disorders, the following stood out: diastolic dysfunction (DD) (60%), left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) (91%), and left atrial dilation (LAD) (66.6%). Table 1 shows the values of the echocardiographic parameters for the population before and after dialysis. Notably, diastolic dysfunction worsened in the post-dialysis echocardiogram (E/A wave ratio (1.02 ± 0.4 vs 0.85 ± 0.3; P < 0.001)).
Intradialytic hypotension (IDH) occurred in 24 patients (51.19%). There were no differences when comparing echocardiographic parameters before and after dialysis between the two groups (hypotension vs no hypotension). There were no differences in the prevalence of LAD or LVH between the two groups; however, patients in the intradialytic hypotension group showed a significantly higher prevalence of diastolic dysfunction (81% vs 43.5%; P < 0.015).
Conclusion
There is a reduction in cardiac chamber volumes during the dialysis session. Left ventricular diastolic function worsens during a hemodialysis session, and its prevalence is much higher in the group of patients who experience hemodynamic instability during the session.

title: #3650 Importance of characterizing intradialytic hemodynamic changes using bioreactance and echocardiography methods
authors: María de Los Ángeles Fernández Rojo; Ana Alicia Astroña Rojas; Carlos Jesús Cabezas Reina; María Antonia García Rubiales; Desirée Bustos Jiménez; María Mercedes Baltasar López; Nicolás Morell Alba; Alberto Cubas Sánchez-Beato; David Carro Herrero; Iván Carmena Rodríguez; Francisco Javier Ahijado Hormigos
abstract:
Background and Aims
The measurement of intradialytic blood pressure (BP) and heart rate (HR) are currently the main parameters used for hemodynamic monitoring during hemodialysis. Since BP depends on cardiac output and total peripheral resistance, understanding these parameters could help improve the hemodynamic condition of patients, who also have a high percentage of cardiac functional and anatomical abnormalities.
Method
We conducted a prospective observational study on 46 stable hemodialysis patients. During one dialysis session, continuous non-invasive monitoring was performed using bioreactance (Starling SV. Baxter) to evaluate the indexed cardiac output (ICO), indexed stroke volume (ISV), and total peripheral resistance index (TPRI). Cardiac preload data were obtained by measuring the increase in stroke volume (achieved with a bolus infusion maneuver). These data were correlated with the results of echocardiography and tissue Doppler performed before and after dialysis.
Results
The recruited patients (32 men and 14 women) had a median age of 63.4 years (IQR 56.2–78.5), and 47% were diabetic. Among the baseline structural and functional disorders, diastolic dysfunction was noted in 60%; left ventricular hypertrophy in 91%; and left atrial dilation in 66.6%, with worsening diastolic dysfunction and right ventricular function during the session as measured by the E/A wave (1.02 ± 0.4 vs 0.85 ± 0.3; P < 0.001) and TAPSE (21.6 ± 4.9 vs 20.15 ± 4.6; P < 0.001), respectively.
Hemodynamic measurements showed a decrease in ISV (38.9 ± 2 vs 38.7 ± 16; P < 0.001), but ICO remained stable (2.66 ± 0.14 vs 2.68 ± 0.10; ns), with a significant increase in HR (68.3 ± 1.9 vs 71 ± 1.4; P < 0.001). The ΔISV during predialysis was 2.15% ± 7.2%, and post-dialysis was 13.11% ± 8.7%. Regarding the predialysis condition, the LVEF was higher in patients with less volume overload (58 ± 10 vs 66 ± 7; P = 0.008). In the post-dialysis echocardiogram, a close relationship was observed between right ventricular volume and cardiac preload at the end of the session (ΔISV < or >10%) (40.5 ± 7 vs 35.4 ± 5.1; P = 0.01).
Conclusion
Non-invasive evaluation of patient responses to HD provides relevant hemodynamic information that exceeds what is provided by BP measurements. Understanding cardiac functional and structural abnormalities, combined with hemodynamic data and real-time assessment of volume status, can guide the prescription of dialysis protocols and help prevent hemodynamic events, particularly asymptomatic ones, which lead to significant morbidity in these patients.

title: #845 Effectiveness of microwave ablation in the treatment of non-primary hyperparathyroidism in dialysis patients
authors: Mahmud Islam; Onur Taydaş; Zafer Ercan; Musa Pınar; Peruze Yüksel; Esen Ülker; Taner Demirci; Ahmed Cihad Genç; Feyza Bayrakdar Caglayan; Hamad Dheir
abstract:
Background and Aims
Secondary and tertiary hyperparathyroidism are not infrequent in dialysis patients. Optimal medical management depends on both patients’ tolerance and side effects. This is usually limited by aberrant calcium and phosphorous levels or drug intolerance. Patients with adenomas are expected to need higher doses. Recently, microwave ablation (MWA) have shown promise as a minimally invasive treatment option for primary and secondary parathyroid nodules. This study, aimed to evaluate the effect of MWA of non-primary parathyroid nodules on patients’ PTH levels and the need for PTH suppressive therapy.
Method
This retrospective study included 46 patients on renal replacement therapy (RRT) (42; 91.3% on HD) who received thermal ablation therapy for the presence of parathyroid nodule(s) and followed in our center. We included patients reluctant to or not feasible for surgery and or intolerant to medical therapy. Those with malignancy, <18 years old, and who are not receiving RRT were excluded. Analysis of PTH was evaluated using the Roche Cobas e 801 analytical unit (Made in Germany). The intervention was performed by one experienced interventional radiologist using a 2.45-GHz microwave generator (MaxBlate, Canyon, China), and an 18-gauge water-cooled antenna was employed for the ablation under ultrasound guidance. Basal blood levels, as well as one hour post-procedure samples, were collected with the patients’ consent. Data analysis was performed by using SPSS-22 for Windows (Statistical Package for Social Science, SPSS Inc. Chicago IL, USA®Z).

title: #2046 Effect of proton pump inhibitors and histamine-2 receptor antagonists on peritoneal dialysis-associated peritonitis: a territory-wide, propensity-weighted cohort in Hong Kong
authors: Kit-Chung Ng; Chun Kau Gordon Chan; Terry Yip; Grace Wong; Cheuk Chun Szeto
abstract:
Background and Aims
Proton pump inhibitors (PPI) and histamine-2 receptor antagonists (H2A) are commonly prescribed to patients undergoing peritoneal dialysis (PD), who are prone to gastrointestinal complications, especially with concurrent use of antiplatelet agents. However, whether PPI and/or H2A increases the risk of PD-associated peritonitis remains uncertain.
Method
This retrospective, territory-wide cohort study used an electronic public healthcare database in Hong Kong to identify patients who received PD from 1st January 2009 to 31st December 2023. The primary outcome was the occurrence of first episode of peritonitis (by any organisms). Secondary outcomes included occurrence of organism-specific peritonitis and all-cause mortality. Inverse probability of treatment weighting based on propensity score (PS) was adopted after missing value imputation to balance baseline confounding factors between PPI users, H2A users, and those who received neither medication (control group). Weighted Cox proportional hazards regression was used to estimate the weighted hazard ratios (wHRs) of PPI and H2A on clinical outcomes.
Results
A total of 18,880 PD patients (mean age 60.5 ± 12.7 years, 61.4% male, 82.5% on continuous ambulatory PD) were studied. At baseline, 5,477 (29.0%) patients were prescribed PPI and 4,737 (25.1%) were prescribed H2A, while the remaining 8,666 (45.9%) received neither medication. Over a median follow-up of 29.9 months (IQR 14.2 to 54.3), 6,674 patients (35.5%) experienced their first episode of peritonitis. Compared with control group, PPI users (wHR 1.27, 95% CI: 1.14–1.41, P < 0.001) showed an increased risk of developing all-cause peritonitis, while the risk of H2A users just marginally reached significance (wHR 1.15, 95% CI: 1.00–1.32, P = 0.0495). Specifically, the risk of Gram positive (wHR 1.35, 95% CI: 1.13–1.61), enteric peritonitis (wHR 1.33, 95% CI 1.02–1.74), and culture negative peritonitis (wHR 1.30, 95% CI 1.11–1.52) significantly increased among PPI users but not H2A users. Furthermore, the use of PPI was associated with all-cause mortality (wHR 1.19, 95% CI 1.14–1.26, P < 0.001). Sensitivity analysis by considering transfer to hemodialysis, transplantation and death as competing events showed that PPI remained an independent predictor of all-cause peritonitis (weighted subdistribution HR 1.13, 95% CI 1.02–1.26, P = 0.02).
Conclusion
In this territory-wide, PS-weighted cohort which analyzed 6,674 peritonitis episodes, we observed a significant association between PPI use and all-cause peritonitis. The risk was especially pronounced in Gram positive, enteric and culture negative peritonitis, which was not observed in H2A users. Regular medication reviews to deprescribe unnecessary PPI may improve polypharmacy in PD patients and potentially reduce peritonitis rate.

title: #648 Effects of super high-flux vitamin E-coated and medium cut-off dialyzers on uremic toxins removal and biocompatibility: the E-FLUX randomized controlled study
authors: Mohamed Belmouaz; Etienne Cogne; Florent Joly; Estelle Desport; Romain Wong-Cheng; Thierry Hauet; Antoine Thierry; Frank Bridoux
abstract:
Background and Aims
Medium cut-off hemodialysis (MCO-HD) improves removal of middle molecules (MM) uremic toxins. The effects of the novel vitamin E-coated super high-flux (SHFVE) dialyzer on MM removal and biocompatibility parameters including inflammation and oxidative stress remain to be investigated.
Method
This non-inferiority cross-over prospective randomized study (NCT05610683) included 36 patients randomly assigned to receive either 3 months of MCO-HD followed by 3 months of SHFVE-HD, or vice-versa. At 3 months from randomization, each patient underwent a two-week High-flux hemodialysis washout period. The primary endpoint was beta2-microglobulin reduction ratio (RR) after 3 months. Secondary endpoints were other MM RR and biocompatibility parameters.
Results
Compared to MCO-HD, SHFVE-HD provided a non-inferior beta2-microglobulin RR: 74% [CI 95%: 71;77] versus 73% [CI 95%: 71;76] with a difference of 0.9% [CI 95%: −1.9%; 3.6] and similar mean RR of prolactin, alpha1-microglobulin, vascular endothelial growth factor, kappa and lambda free light chains. Although MCO-HD resulted in a higher mean myoglobin RR compared to SHFVE-HD (60 ± 6.6 vs 55 ± 7.3%, P = 0.022), SHFVE-HD was associated with a non-significant trend towards lower myoglobin pre-dialysis levels (P = 0.08).
Median pre-dialysis levels of interleukin 6 (0.8 [0–4.4] vs (1.7 [0.2–7.2] pg/ml, P = 0.032), asymmetric dimethylarginine (ADMA) (163 [122–260] vs 167 [133–270] ng/ml, P = 0.01], mean pre-dialysis soluble tumor necrosis factor receptor 1 (sTNFR1) levels (12.7 ± 3.5 vs 13.6 ± 3.6 ng/ml, P = 0.039) and mean post-dialysis oxidized low density lipoprotein (LDL) levels (54 ± 18 vs 63 ± 22 ng/ml, P = 0.01) decreased significantly with SHFVE-HD.
SHFVE-HD induced a significantly lower mean RR in blood leucocyte count 15 min after dialysis initiation (2.3 ± 7 vs 8.4 ± 11%, P = 0.009). This leucocyte fluctuation encompassed both polymorphonuclear neutrophils and monocytes.
Conclusion
Compared to MCO-HD, SHFVE-HD appears to provide similar MM RR and may be associated with improved biocompatibility parameters.

title: #3578 Value of the nutritional prognostic index as an indicator of cardiovascular risk in peritoneal dialysis
authors: Paula Jara Caro Espada; Paula Castillejo; Claudia Yuste Lozano; Gemma Valera; Maria del Mar Rodriguez San Pedro; Soledad Pizarro Sanchez; Julia María Carracedo Añón; Enrique Morales Ruiz
abstract:
Background and Aims
People undergoing peritoneal dialysis (PD) face a higher risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and so, have reduced survival rates compared to the general population. Recently, the importance of non-traditional cardiovascular risk factors, such as changes in inflammatory, immune, and endothelial functions, along with changes in nutritional status, have been highlighted.
Method
A single-centre descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted at a tertiary hospital involving patients undergoing peritoneal dialysis (PD) to analyze the relationship between nutritional and inflammatory status and cardiovascular events. Nutritional status was evaluated using the Prognostic Nutritional Index (PNI) and the Fresenius Body Composition Monitor (BCM). The assessment of pro-inflammatory status included cytokine measurements via Luminex techniques. Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) were defined as stroke, acute myocardial infarction (AMI), and severe peripheral arterial disease.
Results
Thirty-six prevalent PD patients (mean age 56.2 ± 13.4 years, 52.8% male, 91.7% with hypertension, and 30.6% with diabetes) were included, with 22% on manual PD and 78% on automatized PD. The median time on dialysis was 9.1 [6, 41] months. Most patients (83%) were overhydrated, with a mean excess fluid volume of 2.1 ± 1.8 L. The average PNI score was 46.4 ± 4.4 points. PNI showed an inverse correlation with pro-inflammatory cytokine receptors, including the IL-1 receptor (P = 0.044) and TNF-alpha receptor (P = 0.02), as well as with FGF21 (P = 0.046). Patients with PNI < 40 points (PNI < 40) were classified as severely malnourished (n = 9, 25%). There were no significant baseline differences between patients with PNI < 40 and PNI > 40 patients. Severely malnourished patients presented faster baseline peritoneal transport than those with better nutrition (Cr D/P 0.76 ± 0.09 PNI < 40 vs 0.67 ± 0.1 PNI > 40, p 0.022). PNI < 40 patients were more overhydrated compared with PNI < 40 patients (4.6 ± 2.9L PNI < 40 vs 2.0 ± 1.7L PNI > 40, p 0.045), with higher extracellular/intracellular water (ECW/ICW) ratio (1.1 ± 0.1 PNI 40, P = 0.004). Moreover, patients with PNI<40 had more MACE comorbidity than better nourished patients (88.9% vs 51.9% respectively, P = 0.048) and presented more MACE events during subsequent follow-up (33.7 ± 14.4 months) (77.8% PNI <40 vs 22.2% PNI > 40, P = 0.022). Finally, severely malnourished patients showed a significantly impaired inflammatory status, with higher levels of IL6 (0.75 [0.01–23.02] PNI < 40 vs 4.37 [1.1–45.99] PNI > 40, p 0.019) and IL1b (2.1 [0.55–20.7] PNI < 40 vs 4.4 [0.01–18.03] PNI > 40, p 0.05).
Conclusion
Twenty-five percent of our cohort of prevalent PD patients were classified as severely malnourished. These patients exhibited greater overhydration and a more pronounced pro-inflammatory status, which may explain the higher incidence of MACE events within this group.

title: #2682 Real costs of daily home hemodialysis compared to in-center hemodialysis in France
authors: Guy Rostoker; Jean-Jacques Dumas; Benoit Thomé; Victor Aragno; Michel Thomas; Bernard Canaud
abstract:
Background and Aims
Home hemodialysis (HD) offers several advantages over conventional in-center 3-times-weekly HD, with better preservation of health-related quality of life and treatment flexibility, but its true costs are poorly understood. We therefore aimed to compare the real costs of daily home hemodialysis versus in-center hemodialysis in France.
Method
Design: National, population-based, cohort study with propensity score matching (PSM) to mitigate selection bias on patient profiles.
Setting
Individual healthcare data from the French National Health Data System for patients with end-stage kidney disease undergoing dialysis cross-referenced with the French National Cost Scale of the health ministry.
Participants
A total of 72 358 patients receiving HD were identified and their data collected for the 24-month inclusion period, from January 2016 to December 2017. After exclusion of patients treated < 90 days, and those without a treatment schedule or incomplete data for a social disadvantage score, 42 605 patients were selected (28 317 prevalent and 14 288 incident HD patients). After PSM, 265 incident patients (in-center HD, n = 212; daily home HD, n = 53) and 765 prevalent patients (in-center HD, n = 612; daily home HD, n = 153) were analyzed.
Main outcome and measure
Global costs of in-center versus daily home HD for incident and prevalent patients after PSM.
Results
The global cost of daily home HD for incident patients was lower than in-center HD (€1403/week vs. €1652/week, respectively), resulting in annual costs of €72 956 vs. €85 904, respectively. We found similarly lower costs for prevalent patients (€1360/week vs. €1456/week, respectively). For daily home HD, 55% of the costs were directly related to patient renal care compared with 30% for in-center HD. Conversely, in-center HD allocated a larger proportion to transportation (18% (in-center HD) vs. 2% (daily home HD)), and hospitalization (16% (in-center HD) vs. 6% (daily home HD)).
Conclusion
Daily home HD is a more cost-effective and patient-centered treatment option than in-center HD.

title: #2750 Daily home hemodialysis is associated with a lower mortality rate compared with in-center hemodialysis in French patients
authors: Guy Rostoker; Jean-Jacques Dumas; Benoit Thomé; Victor Aragno; Michel Thomas; Bernard Canaud
abstract:
Background and Aims
Home hemodialysis (HD) offers several advantages over conventional 3-times-weekly in-center HD, with better preservation of health-related quality of life and treatment flexibility, but its effect on mortality is poorly understood. We therefore aimed to compare daily home hemodialysis with in-center hemodialysis in France for the risk of death in incident patients (to minimize the risk of bias).
Method
Design: National, population-based, cohort study with propensity score matching (PSM) to mitigate selection bias on patient profiles.
Setting
Individual healthcare data from the French National Health Data System for patients with end-stage kidney disease undergoing dialysis cross-referenced with the French National Cost Scale of the health ministry.
Participants
A total of 72 358 patients receiving HD were identified and their data collected for the 24-month inclusion period, from January 2016 to December 2017. After exclusion of patients treated < 90 days, and those without a treatment schedule or incomplete data for a social disadvantage score, 42 605 patients were selected (28 317 prevalent and 14 288 incident HD patients). After PSM, 265 incident patients (in-center HD, n = 212; daily home HD, n = 53) were analyzed for mortality after two years of a follow-up.
Main outcome and measure
Crude mortality in incident patients after PSM and the potential factors influencing death in daily home HD and in-center HD.
Results
The gross death rate after 2 years of follow-up in incident patients treated with in-center HD was 10.4% vs. 1.9% in patients treated with daily home HD (P = 0.049, Chi2 test; relative risk (RR)=5.5 [95% CI, 1.003 to 31.97].
Survival analysis using the Kaplan–Meier curve showed no censoring case and a significant difference in the cumulative risk of death between incident patients receiving in-center HD and patients receiving daily home HD (W = 5140, P = 0.03, Wilcoxon–Mann–Whitney test). Multivariate analysis using the Cox proportional hazards model showed that the hazard ratio (HR) for death was increased 7-fold by in-center HD compared with daily home HD. Similarly, diabetes mellitus and disability strongly increased the HR for death (approximately 3-fold) in incident patients in the multivariate analysis.
Conclusion
Daily home hemodialysis improves outcomes for French incident dialysis patients and significantly prolongs life expectancy compared to in-center hemodialysis.

title: #355 “Bringing the world in”—experiences of an art programme in renal dialysis units
authors: Alice Radley; Iain Drummond; Andrea Sergeant; Kate Gallacher; Alison Hyslop; Mun Woo
abstract:
Background and Aims
The transition from end-stage-kidney disease to haemodialysis (HD) forces patients to re-evaluate their personal relationships, role within their community and self-identity. Symptom burden, particularly fatigue, can erode autonomy and isolate patients from their support networks. Many patients feel trapped by their dependency on the HD machine, which becomes omnipresent. Low mood and anxiety are common, exacerbated by the uncertainty of their own mortality, unpredictability of HD complications and the intrusion of HD restrictions on “normal life”.
The Art in Renal Care project delivered art programmes in three renal dialysis units (RDUs) within NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde between April 2023 and May 2024. Each unit received weekly art sessions facilitated by trained artists over a four-month period. Sessions were held during HD and were open to all patients, with art materials provided. Exhibitions were held in January and November 2024.
This qualitative study aimed to explore patient and staff perspectives, evaluating whether participation in a structured art programme impacts patients’ experience of HD and their mental wellbeing.
Method
Focus groups, facilitated by the research team, were held in RDUs with all patients invited to participate. Focus groups were recorded and transcribed. Questionnaires were distributed to patients and staff unable to participate in the focus groups. Thematic analysis was performed using NVIVO.
Results

title: #1477 Improvement of serum calcification propensity in dialysis patients: comparison between low-flux and medium cut-off dialyzers
authors: Berfu Korucu; Joyce Xu; Henrike Hamer; Robert de Jonge; Serpil Muge Deger; Marc Vervloet
abstract:
Background and Aims
Vascular calcification contributes to mortality in hemodialysis patients. The elevated levels of uremic toxins are involved in this pathology. Medium cut-off (MCO) dialyzers have improved clearance of middle molecular weight uremic toxins compared to low flux (LF) dialyzers. The T50 test quantifies the calcification propensity and is independently associated with cardiovascular and all-cause mortality. Previous studies have demonstrated improvement of T50 with conventional dialyzers. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of MCO dialyzers on the T50 compared to LF dialyzers.
Method
A single-center cross-over study was designed, including hemodialysis patients initially treated with LF dialyzers before switching to MCO dialyzers. Pre- and post-dialysis blood was collected for laboratory measurements in mid-week hemodialysis sessions: first with LF dialyzers (baseline) and then six months after switching to MCO dialyzers. The change in T50 was statistically analyzed with a paired t-test and linear mixed-effect modeling using R.
Results
In total, 15 patients were included. At baseline, the mean T50 (pre-dialysis) was 199.9 min (±97.9) (Fig. 1). The change of T50 after dialysis was significant with both LF and MCO dialyzers (P < 0.001, both) with a median increase of 85.3% (IQR = 46.9%, 265.4%) and 56.3% (IQR = 21.8%, 217.7%), respectively. After adjustments for confounders (age, sex, dialysis vintage, pre-dialysis T50 levels, dialyzer type), a multivariate regression showed that the use of MCO dialyzers was independently associated with a less pronounced increase of T50 after dialysis compared to LF dialyzers (95% CI = −64.62 to −40.95, P = 0.033). Additionally, a lower T50 at the start of dialysis was independently associated with a higher increment of T50 (95% CI = −1.26 to −1.10, P < 0.001). After six months of dialyzing with MCO dialyzers, the mean T50 (pre-dialysis) was 191.7 min (±75.0) and not significantly different compared to pre-dialysis value at baseline T50 (adjusted for age, sex, smoking, dialysis vintage, diabetes mellitus).
Conclusion
A hemodialysis session with either LF or MCO dialyzer strongly improves the T50 value. After six months of treatment, MCO dialyzers did not demonstrate any significant advantage over LF dialyzers in terms of T50 values.

title: #2280 Cell-free plasma dna (cfDNA) in peritonitis is originated from apoptotic events and Caspase-3 activation
authors: Grazia Maria Virzi; Sabrina Milan Manani; Ilaria Tantillo; Claudio Ronco; Monica Zanella
abstract:
Background and Aims
Plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) is a circulating extracellular DNA fragments and originates from inflammation and tissue damage. High levels of cfDNA have been reported in many clinical conditions, including CKD, hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis (PD). In a recent work, we demonstrated that PD-related peritonitis induces cfDNA production. Unfortunately, we are unable to directly address the mechanism involved in cfDNA origin. The first aim of this study was confirmed the variation in plasma cfDNA after an episode of peritonitis in PD patients. The second purpose of this study was to elucidate the putative causative mechanism involved in cfDNA formation during peritonitis. In particular, we hypothesized that cfDNA production could be associated with apoptotic event and we investigated which pathway is involved in this process.
Method
We enrolled 54 PD patients and we divided them into 3 different groups: 25 PD patients without any history of peritonitis, 21 PD patients whose last episode of peritonitis was more than 3 months prior to enrollment, and 8 patients who had an episode of peritonitis within the 3 months prior to enrollment. CfDNA was extracted from plasma and was quantified by Real time PCR. Subsequent, analysis of apoptosis was qualitatively performed by DNA Ladder kit and quantitatively measured by ELISA tests for Caspase-3 (effector caspase), Caspase-8 (extrinsic pathway) and Caspase-9 (intrinsic pathway).
Results
Quantitative analysis of cfDNA showed significantly higher levels in patients who had an episode of peritonitis compared with PD patients without any history of peritonitis. This data confirmed our previously results. Firstly, qualitative analysis of cfDNA showed higher DNA ladder formations, suggesting presence of apoptotic events (Fig. 1). The increase of apoptotic events was confirmed by Caspase-3 activation (P < 0.01) (Fig. 2). In particular, the levels of Caspase-3 was significantly higher in patients with acute peritonitis within the last 3 months. Notably, a significant correlation was observed between cfDNA and Caspase-3 levels (Spearman’s rank correlation coefficient = 0.511, P < 0.01) (Fig. 3). On the contrary, we observed lower levels of cfDNA and Caspase-3 in patients with a longer peritonitis-free period. In addition, we observed a strong significant correlation between Caspase-3 and Caspase-9 levels (Spearman’s rank correlation coefficient = 0.66, P < 0.01) and a significant correlation between Caspase-3 and Caspase-8 (Spearman’s rank correlation coefficient = 0.43, P = 0.037).
Conclusion
Based on our results, we confirmed that cfDNA is increased in the plasma of PD patients with recent peritonitis and we elucidated that cell apoptosis is one of the potential sources of cfDNA. Furthermore, we noticed dual apoptotic pathway activation: the intrinsic and extrinsic pathways converged on Caspase-3 increasing apoptotic events and production of cfDNA in PD patients. In particular, cfDNA, apototic events and dual pathway activation were enhanced in PD patients with acute peritonitis within the last 3 months.

title: #2377 Comparison and validation of two laboratory platforms for peritoneal NGAL in PD patients with and without peritonitis
authors: Grazia Maria Virzi; Niccolò Morisi; Sabrina Milan Manani; Ilaria Tantillo; Claudio Ronco; Monica Zanella
abstract:
Background and Aims
Neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL) is a versatile protein known for its multifunctional roles, extending beyond its conventional use as a biomarker. It actively participates in many crucial biological processes. Elevated NGAL levels were identified in peritoneal fluids during peritonitis in 2009, establishing it as a biomarker for early Peritoneal Dialysis (PD)-associated peritonitis diagnosis (validated diagnostic value > 100 μg/L). While our PD medical Centre currently relies on the lab-based NGAL assay (NGALlab), advancements introduce the NGAL dipstick test (NGALds), offering a rapid and semi-quantitative colorimetric assessment. This study compares NGALds with NGALlab in clinical practice, assessing NGALds’s potential for early peritonitis detection in PD patients’ peritoneal fluid.
Method
This study involves a validation of diagnostic accuracy conducted through a retrospective analysis of parallel samples obtained from peritoneal effluents. Samples were obtained from both PD stable PD patients with suspected or confirmed peritonitis. The assessment of NGALds involved a direct comparison with the established NGALlab (BioPorto turbidimetric immunoassay). The NGALds, a rapid semi-quantitative assay, utilized colorimetric test strips. For NGALds, NGAL values were categorized into colour-coded levels: 25 μg/L, 50 μg/L, 100 μg/L, 150 μg/L, 300 μg/L, and 600 μg/L. For the reproducibility of the data, NGALds was determined by two different trained lab operators on all the patients in a blinded manner. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS Statistics 26.0 software (IBM Corp., Armonk, New York).
Results
Among the 301 peritoneal effluent samples analyzed, 156 were diagnosed with suspected peritonitis using NGALlab and ISPD criteria. Two different lab operators measured NGALds in a blinded mode. The reproducibility for the inter operator variability for peritoneal NGALds was 0.847 (P < 0.001) and the agreement was elevated (k = 0.786, P < 0.001).
In addition, NGALds demonstrated a robust correlation with NGALlab categories (Rs = 0.876, P < 0.001), accurately identifying 96% (150 out of 156) of peritonitis cases (Fig. 1). Discrepancies between NGALlab and NGALds, visualized in the Bland-Altman plot (Fig. 1), were most notable when NGAL values exceeded the 600 μg/L threshold. Nevertheless, these variations did not impact clinical significance, as both methods consistently diagnosed elevated NGAL values indicative of peritonitis.
After ROC analysis, which yielded an AUC of 0.82 (P < 0.001) (Fig. 2), the Youden Index was employed to identify a threshold value of 100 μg/L for the diagnosis of suspected peritonitis. Importantly, the application of this threshold to NGALds demonstrated a positive predictive value of 0.64 and a negative predictive value of 0.87
Conclusion
In conclusion, our study solidifies the significant correlation between NGAL values obtained through the laboratory standard (NGALlab) and the novel NGAL dipstick test (NGALds). Impressively, the NGALds showcased high inter-operator reproducibility and high efficacy, accurately identifying 96% of peritonitis cases as diagnosed by NGALlab. Furthermore, the high negative predictive value provides confidence in considering NGALds as a frontline diagnostic tool for suspected peritonitis. This robust performance positions the NGAL dipstick as a valuable and accessible alternative for rapid assessment in patients presenting symptoms indicative of peritonitis. The user-friendly attributes of NGALds, characterized by their simplicity, rapidity, and semi-quantitative colorimetric analysis, make it not only a practical diagnostic tool but also a patient-centric one. The ease of use and quick results introduce a promising avenue for improving clinical workflows, providing an opportunity for expedited and efficient peritonitis diagnosis. For instance, NGALds could find utility in centres where NGAL is unavailable in the laboratory or at the patient’s home.

title: #744 Calciphylaxis: a qualitative study of patient experiences
authors: Sharon Huish; Smeeta Sinha
abstract:
Background and Aims
Calciphylaxis, or calcific uremic arteriolopathy (CUA), is a rare but devastating condition predominantly seen in people (with kidney failure) undergoing dialysis. It occurs when small arterioles within the skin become calcified causing painful skin lesions. Prevalence of calciphylaxis is reported to be 1–4% in end stage kidney disease with a reported mortality rate of 50–60% within a year of diagnosis.
At present there are no diagnostic tests or licensed treatments and clinical management is largely informed by case series reports and small uncontrolled studies. This study aims to evaluate patient experiences of calciphylaxis diagnosis and treatment, to determine what occurs and what would help, for the benefit of i) informing and improving future patient care and ii) increasing awareness (earlier diagnosis).
Method
Ethical approval was received. The study was promoted to clinical care teams through the UK Kidney Association and UK Kidney Research Consortium, and directly to patients through Kidney Research UK and Kidney Wales. Inclusion criteria: ≥18 years of age and current or previous (<3 years) diagnosis of calciphylaxis, or carer/relative of someone with calciphylaxis. Study information was sent remotely by the research team and informed consent was undertaken by telephone or in person. Research interviews were conducted in-person, via video call or telephone. The recruitment target was 10-20 people to ensure data saturation was achieved (new participant repeats previous information and no new information is obtained). Interviews were transcribed (anonymised) and inductive thematic analysis is currently underway.
Results
Recruitment was open from October 2023 to December 2024 inclusive. 19 people living in England and Wales were approached and sent participant information sheets. 12 of 19 (63%) were identified by their clinical care team and 7 of 19 (37%) self-initiated participation in response to a study advert. 17 of 19 (89%) consented to participate (14 of whom were patients with current or previous calciphylaxis and 3 were relatives of calciphylaxis patients). The median patient age was 68 years (range 52-82) and 43% (6 of 14) were male. 1 patient withdrew from the study prior to interview (due to ill health). 16 interviews were successfully undertaken; 10 in person, 5 via video call, and 1 over the telephone. The average interview duration was 49 minutes (range 15–81 minutes). Theme saturation was achieved. Participants described the importance (and helpfulness) of continuity in wound care management/dressings, feeling informed, being given ‘good news’ stories (not just bad), good pain control and clear communication. The reported challenges related to: the diagnosis itself (delays, how the diagnosis was delivered, and a lack of information for both patients themselves and their relatives), limited understanding about the condition, a lack of overall support, and feelings of fear.
Conclusion
Qualitative research in calciphylaxis, a rare and devastating condition, has been lacking. This study was well received, participants were welcoming of the research and keen to share their journey. Findings identified areas that can be developed to improve the experiences of people diagnosed with calciphylaxis (and their families). This includes developing: i) educational resources for both patients and their relatives, ii) a best practice quick reference guide for clinicians, and iii) a care card for primary care, targeted at district nurses, explaining what calciphylaxis is and best practice advice for wound care management.
In a condition where there are no proven treatments and outcomes are poor, this study demonstrates the value of the patients’ voice in identifying areas of care that can be improved.

title: #3300 Achievement of hemodiafiltration (HDF) convective volumes (CV) &gt; 23 L/session in a dialysis center without selection of “healthy” patients: is it really possible?
authors: Bedel Lukoki Beudin; Tchilabalo Kakomkate; Wahiba Ibeghouchene; Moctar Coulibaly; Céline Carreira; Imen Ouertani; Falone Kougnizounde; Beya Fendri; David Attaf; Janette Mansour
abstract:
Background and Aims
HDF reduces mortality for a CV > 23 L/1.73 m2/session. This CV varies (clinical practices, patients…). CONVINCE study shows an achievement of CV target in 97% of patients with a dedicated protocol. Selection of healthy patients remains a debate. We aim to assess CV achievement in an unselected population.
Method
Prospective interventional monocentric study evaluating the rate of patients achieving a CV > 23 L/session with the CONVINCE protocol in our hemodialysis center (comorbid patients) and without selection of healthy patients. Inclusion of all incident/prevalent HD and HDF patients. All patients followed the CONVINCE protocol (↑ Qb, filtration fraction and session duration optimization). Patients are followed in 2 phases (see Fig. 1): (1) optimization of CV [1st Month]; (2) maintenance of CV [Month 1, 2 et 3]. At the end of the optimization phase, the proportion of patients reaching CV = 23 L is calculated.
Results
