title: #1560 Unveiling donor-originated BKPyV viremia in kidney transplant recipients
authors: Wouter Moest; Lianne Messchendorp; Helma Dolmans; Maarten Christiaans; Arjan van Zuilen; M Kho; Jan-Stephan F Sanders; M C W Feltkamp; Aiko De Vries; Joris Rotmans
abstract:
Background and Aims
BK Polyomavirus (BKPyV) is of notable concern in kidney transplant recipients, as it can lead to BKPyV DNAemia and progress to BKPyV-associated nephropathy (BKPyVAN). BKPyVAN can cause significant damage to the transplanted kidney, potentially resulting in graft loss. Currently, there is no effective treatment for BKPyV infection, underscoring the critical need for preventive strategies. There is emerging evidence that donor-derived BKPyV may play a role in the development of BKPyV DNAemia. To further explore this hypothesis, we have conducted a retrospective, multi-center cohort study to evaluate the risk of developing BKPyV DNAemia in kidney recipient pairs from the same deceased donor.
Method
At the Leiden University Medical Center (LUMC), we identified all recipients of deceased kidney donors between 2011 and 2021 who developed BKPyV DNAemia within the first year post-transplantation. An equal number of recipients from deceased donors who did not develop BKPyV DNAemia within the first year were randomly selected as a control group. The contralateral kidney recipients were identified through the Dutch Transplantation Foundation (Nederlandse Transplantatie Stichting), and relevant data were obtained with assistance from the respective transplant centers. Cox regression analysis was used to assess whether recipients from the same donor had an increased risk of developing BKPyV DNAemia within the first year when the LUMC recipient experienced BKPyV DNAemia, compared to pairs where the LUMC recipient did not develop BKPyV DNAemia.
Results
A total of 265 postmortem kidney transplant recipients at the LUMC were included in the study, of whom 128 developed BKPyV DNAemia within the first year. Data from 81 contralateral kidney recipients, transplanted across 4 centers (UMC Groningen, ErasmusMC, UMC Utrecht, and LUMC), were analyzed. The incidence of BKPyV DNAemia was significantly higher among recipients whose contralateral kidney recipient also developed BKPyV DNAemia compared to those whose contralateral recipient did not (28.6% [10/35] vs. 10.9% [5/46], P = 0.042). With an adjusted hazard ratio of 4.4 (95% CI: 1.3–15.1, P = 0.019).
Conclusion
This study highlights a significantly increased risk of BKPyV DNAemia in recipients of deceased kidney donors when the contralateral recipient develops BKPyV DNAemia. These findings underscore the critical influence of donor-related factors in BKPyV transmission in kidney transplantation. Future research should focus on further exploring and preventing the transmission of BKPyV from donor to recipient.

title: #1401 GlycA and all-cause mortality in kidney transplant recipients: results of the TransplantLines Biobank and Cohort Study
authors: Fernando Martín del Campo Sánchez; Jip Jonker; Manuela Yepes-Calderón; Robin P F Dullaart; Margery A Connelly; Martin H de Borst; Stephan J L Bakker
abstract:
Background and Aims
Despite the benefits of kidney transplantation compared to dialysis, life expectancy in kidney transplant recipients (KTR) remains 25%–30% lower than that of age-matched peers in the general population. Chronic inflammation is a key contributor to poor outcomes in KTR. GlycA is a composite biomarker of systemic inflammation associated with all-cause mortality in general population studies, but there are no data on GlycA concentrations and outcome in KTR.
Method
This prospective study was performed using data of stable outpatient KTR participating in the TransplantLines Biobank and Cohort Study. GlycA concentration was measured by nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy. We performed multivariable linear regression to analyze the association between concentrations of GlycA and conventional biomarkers of inflammation. To test for the association between GlycA concentration and all-cause mortality, Cox regression was used.
Results
We had data of 909 KTR, mean age 56 (±13) years, 557 (60.9%) males, and GlycA concentration 435 (±92) μmol/L. During a median follow-up of 5.5 [Interquartile range = 4.0–6.7] years, 196 (21.4%) KTR died. After adjusting for sex, age, and body mass index, GlycA was positively associated with log-transformed high sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) (standardized B coefficient (std B) = 0.68, P < 0.001) and negatively with albumin (Std B= −0.25, P < 0.001). With strengths of associations expressed per standard deviation change, GlycA was more associated with all-cause mortality than hsCRP (Hazard ratio (HR) = 1.56, 95% CI 1.41–1.73, P < 0.001 vs. HR = 1.25, 95% CI 1.16–1.39, P < 0.001, respectively). After adjusting for age, sex, and estimated glomerular filtration rate the respective HR were 1.46, 95% CI 1.30–1.64, P < 0.001 and 1.19, 95% CI 1.09–1.29, P < 0.001. After adjusting for hsCRP, GlycA was associated with all-cause mortality (HR= 1.55, 95% CI 1.30–1.84, P < 0.001). hsCRP was not associated with all-cause mortality after adjusting for GlycA (HR = 0.92, 95% CI 0.76–1.12, P = 0.40).
Conclusion
In KTR, GlycA showed an independent association with an elevated mortality risk. GlycA was more strongly associated with all-cause mortality than hsCRP. Further research is warranted to evaluate whether GlycA values could be relevant to improving clinical outcomes in KTR.

title: #1209 Delisting strategy in highly sensitised patients with preformed DSA
authors: José Manuel Amaro; Marta Alonso Mozo; Florentino Villanego; Luis Alberto Vigara; Blanca Serrano Muñoz; Arshdeep Singh; Marina Arnaiz Pérez; Cristhian David Orellana Chávez; Teresa García Álvarez; Antonio Nieto; Auxiliadora Mazuecos
abstract:
Background and Aims
The number of highly sensitised patients on the kidney transplant (KT) waiting list is increasing. HLA-banned antigen delisting strategies may allow transplantation of patients with pre-KT positive donor-specific antibodies (DSA) and negative crossmatch, although the reported data are scarce.
Method
Retrospective cohort study of KT patients with DSA pre-KT who underwent delisting strategies in our centre, from November 2019 to May 2024. We considered as unacceptable antigens those positive by CDC, complement-fixing (C1q), anti-HLA class I and class II antibodies with MFI > 5000 that do not decrease after dilution or antibodies against antigens of the partner/pre-KT with MFI x3 of the highest self-antigen of the same locus. We selected two controls for each case, the closest by date of KT and sensitised donor and recipient characteristics (PRA ≥ 75%) without DSA. We collected demographic and KT evolution variables.
Results
After delisting, 14 patients were transplanted, and 28 controls were selected. Median follow-up was 39 months. Median age was 56 years and 87.5% were women. There were no differences between groups in donor and recipient characteristics. The number of mismatches was similar and there was no difference in time on pre-KT dialysis. All received induction with thymoglobulin. In the case group there was greater use of rituximab in induction (P = 0.052) and i.v. immunoglobulin plasmapheresis (P = 0.005).
Renal function was similar in both groups at one year post-KT. The evolution of DSA in the delisting group was: 50% negative, 14.3% decreased, 28.6% stable and 7.1% increased. The development of de novo DSA post-KT was similar in both groups (P = 0.608). The rate of antibody-mediated acute rejection (AR) was higher in the delisting group (35% vs. 10.7%, P = 0.052) and the incidence of CMV infection (P = 0.004).
Two grafts were lost in each group, all due to immunological causes: graft survival at one year 85.7% in the delisting group, 96.4% in the control (P = 0.513). At one year one patient died in the control group (COVID-19) and none in the delisting group.
Conclusion
Delisting strategies are an option for highly sensitised patients with the presence of DSA, even without the use of imlifidase. The rate of AR and CMV infection was higher, but with acceptable survival data, so they can be considered in situations where the patient's immune status limits access to KT.

title: #2309 Use of radiofrequency echographic multi spectrometry (REMS) and cardio-ankle vascular index (CAVI) to evaluate the effects of immunosuppressive (IS) drugs on bone and vessel disease in renal transplant (RTX) patients
authors: Marzia Pasquali; Marta Catalfamo; Antonella Zaccaria; Chiara Mariani; Lida Tartaglione; Sandro Mazzaferro
abstract:
Background and Aims
Bedside evaluation of bone and vascular disease in RTX still claims for non-invasive routine diagnostic devices. We tested if REMS and CAVI were respectively able to discover associations between IS drugs and bone and vascular disease in RTX patients.
Method
We enrolled RTX patients (>18 years, who signed consent), who had been on IS drugs for >12 months and were in a stable clinical condition. We evaluated eGFR, mineral metabolism and IS drug exposure (steroid cumulative dose and average CNI blood levels in the last 12 months). We also obtained the 10y fracture risk (FRAX score) and the following REMS derived bone parameters: BMD, femoral and vertebral T-score and femoral and lumbar bone Fragility Score (bFrS, range 0–100). Pulse wave velocity was measured with the operator-independent CAVI equipment. Data are M ± SD or median (IQR 25–75) based on normality. Statistics: t-test and ANOVA with post hoc test or Mann-Whitney and Kruskal Wallis with post hoc analysis based on normality; Spearman's or Pearson's correlation was used to assess the monotonic covariation of measurements; Jonckheere–Terpstra test was used to analyze the p for trend.
Results
66 pts (33M/33F), aged 55.9 ± 13 y, transplanted since 81.5 (53.5–207.0) months, with eGFR 47.0 (31.5–72) ml/min/1.73 m2 and iPTH 99.4 ± 60 pg/ml (n.v. 15–65) were enrolled. IS drugs were steroids (80%), tacrolimus (64%) and/or cyclosporin (33%). According to REMS T score, 30% were osteoporotic (OP, TS-L −2.6 ± 0.4), 56% osteopenic (OPe, TS-L −1.5 ± 0.3) and 14% normal (N, TSL −0.6 ± 0,3). The REMS femoral bFrS averaged 27 ± 15%, with values higher in OP (34.2 ± 21.3%) than in OPe (20.3 ± 11.4%) or N (15.9 ± 6.8%); (Anova P = .0001; post hoc: OP vs OPe P = .003; OP vs N P = .008, Fig. 1). Similarly, lumbar bFrS was higher in OP (37.4 ± 19.8%) than in OPe (28.3 ± 11.3) or N cases (23.1 ± 3.8), (Anova P = .023; post hoc: OP vs n = .045). FRAX score averaged 6.4 (4.0–10) % and was higher in OP 8.4 (5.3–18.5)% as compared to OPe 5.2 (4–8.6)% and N 4.8 (3.4–8.4)% (Kruskal-Wallis P = .008, post hoc: OP vs OPe P = .034). Vascular stiffness CAVI index averaged 8.4 ± 1.9 in the whole population (normal = <8.0), with values higher in OP (9.2 ± 2.1) as compared to OPe (8.0 ± 1.7) or N (7.5 ± 1.0) (p trend 0.002, Fig. 2). OP pts had the highest cumulative dose of steroid, but no difference in CNI blood levels (Table 1). Average yearly levels of CsA progressively decreased from N to OP pts (p trend, P = .035, Fig. 3), while positive correlation between BMD F and CsA (r = .461; P = .030) and negative correlation between BMD L and Tac (r = −.357; P = .021) were present. Other negative correlations included CAVI vs BMD-F (r = −.323, P = .01), and CAVI vs bFrS-N and bFrS -L (Table 2). No correlation existed between CAVI and CsA or Tac.
Conclusion
Our data advocate possible effects of IS drugs on bone by confirming the depriving action of cumulative steroids. As for CNI, the experimental data indicating that CsA might have bone anabolic effects, while Tac might increase bone resorption are confirmed. As for vascular evaluation, the inverse association between bone and vascular disease is shown. REMS and CAVI are practical devices for non-invasive evaluation of bone and vascular involvement in renal TX patients.

title: #3509 Plasma uromodulin dynamics in deceased kidney donors and the association with transplant outcomes
authors: Ioannis Michelakis; Sarah Fawaz; Rebecca Vaughan; Edward Sharples; Smaragdi Marinaki; Ioannis Boletis; Maria Kaisar
abstract:
Background and Aims
Current tools to assess donor kidney quality have limitations in accurately predicting transplant outcomes, often leading to unnecessary organ discard or suboptimal graft function.
Uromodulin, a kidney-specific glycoprotein, has emerged as a promising biomarker of tubular integrity and renal function. Low plasma uromodulin has been associated with worse kidney outcomes, including kidney disease progression, function decline, and allograft failure, yet its role in deceased organ donation remains largely unexplored. This study aims to evaluate plasma uromodulin in deceased donors and assess its association with transplant outcomes.
Method
Plasma samples from 260 deceased donors (after brain, DBD and circulatory death, DCD) were obtained from the QUality in Organ Donation (QUOD) biobank. To assess the relationship between uromodulin and transplant outcomes, we analyzed paired kidney transplants, where both kidneys were transplanted and had comparable 12-month posttransplant outcomes.
Uromodulin (Umod), Cystatin-C (Cys) and Creatinine (Creat) were measured at two time points during donor management: following donor family consent (Umod1) and at the end of donor management, (Umod2) using Luminex assay. Umod decline (ΔUmod = Umod1 - Umod2), Umod/Creat and Umod/Cys ratios were calculated to assess the relationship between tubular function and overall kidney filtration capacity.
Descriptive statistics and multivariable regression models were used to explore the associations between Umod and donor characteristics. Additionally, Umod levels, ΔUmod and the derived ratios were examined for their impact on donor function at retrieval and recipient 3 & 12-month eGFR. Subgroup analyses were performed for DBD and DCD separately to account for differing donor pathophysiology.
Results
In total, 520 plasma samples from 134 DBD and 126 DCD donors were analyzed. The median donor age was 50 (IQR: 19) years, 44.4% were females, 27% had hypertension and 9% had diabetes. Among the donors, 40 (14.1%) developed acute kidney injury (AKI) prior to retrieval.

title: #3168 Reprogramming innate immune memory using tacrolimus-loaded nanobiologics promotes organ transplant acceptance
authors: Rianne Maas; Maaike Jacobs; Lisanne de Jong; William Wang; Anna Ranzenigo; Martin Umali; Yutaka Negishi; Musa Mhlanga; Nils Rother; Willem Mulder; Abraham Teunissen; Raphaël Duivenvoorden
abstract:
Background and Aims
Tacrolimus is a highly effective drug for preventing allograft rejection, but its long term use is associated with substantial side effects. While tacrolimus is primarily recognized for its immunosuppressive effects on T cells, we recently uncovered its influence on innate immune memory. This type of memory entails epigenetic and metabolic reprogramming of innate immune cells in both the bone marrow and peripheral tissues, resulting in long lasting alterations to the inflammatory responsiveness of the innate immune system. Our findings highlight the critical role of innate immune memory in organ transplant survival in both experimental models and human patients [1–3]. Here, we investigated the effects of myeloid-directed tacrolimus-loaded nanobiologics (Tac-NB) on innate immune memory in vitro, and their potential as an induction therapy to induce long term graft acceptance in a heart transplant mouse model.
Method
The biodistribution of Tac-NB was evaluated by injecting non-human primates and C57BL/6J mice heterotopically transplanted with BALB/c hearts with 89Zr-labelled Tac-NB followed by a PET-CT scan. To assess myeloid-specific targeting of Tac-NB, fluorescently labeled Tac-NBs were incubated with human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) or injected in mouse allogeneic heart transplant recipients and cellular uptake was measured using flow cytometry. PBMCs were stimulated for 24 h with innate immune memory inducer heat-killed Candida albicans (HKCA), in presence or absence of Tac-NBs, following a trained immunity model. The influence of Tac-NB on the cytokine production, transcription and metabolism of innate immune cells was studied using ELISA, RNA-sequencing and Seahorse technology, respectively. To assess the effects of Tac-NBs on graft survival, C57BL/6J mice heterotopically transplanted with BALB/c hearts received PBS, empty NB, bare tacrolimus, Tac-NBs and/or CTLA4-Ig induction therapy without subsequent immunosuppressive maintenance therapy.
Results
Tac-NB predominantly accumulated in hematopoietic organs, lymph nodes, the liver and kidneys in non-human primates and mice, with lower levels detected in the mice's grafts. Uptake of Tac-NB was primarily observed in myeloid cells, while T cells excluded the drug both in vitro and in vivo. Tac-NBs suppressed HKCA-induced IL-6 and TNF production upon restimulation in PBMCs. Transcriptomic analysis and metabolic profiling revealed that Tac-NBs reversed HKCA-induced regulation of genes involved in oxidative phosphorylation and interferon responses, and inhibited HKCA-induced metabolic activity. In the heart transplant mouse model, Tac-NBs induction treatment resulted into drastically improved graft survival compared to untreated controls (median 75 vs 8 days, P < 0.0001). Long term graft acceptance (>100 days) was achieved in 62.5% of the mice when Tac-NB was combined with a single dose of CTLA4-Ig, an inhibitor of the co-stimulatory B7-CTLA4 signal between myeloid cells and T cells.
Conclusion
Tac-NBs reach the hematopoietic organs and selectively deliver tacrolimus to myeloid cells. They suppress cellular metabolism, cytokine memory responses and inflammatory gene transcription in human monocytes in vitro. In a heart transplant mouse model, Tac-NBs markedly extend allograft survival, and can achieve long-term graft acceptance without maintenance immunosuppressive therapy when combined with a myeloid and T cell co-stimulation blocker (CTLA4-Ig). These findings demonstrate that short-term tacrolimus-induced reprogramming of innate immune cells offers a promising approach to promote durable graft acceptance.

title: #1265 Trends in creatinine and blood pressure after stent implantation in patients with significant stenosis of the renal arteries after kidney transplantation
authors: Natalya Belavina; Eugene Zeltyn-Abramov; Denis Fettser; Lyudmila Artyukhina; Nadiya Frolova; Alexandr Kondrashkin; Ilya Dmitriev; Pavel Drozdov; Igor Nesterenko; Nataliya Klochkova; Oleg Kotenko; Mariana Lysenko
abstract:
Background and Aims
Transplant renal artery stenosis (TRAS) is the most common vascular complication after kidney transplantation (KTx). The main clinical manifestations of TRAS are treatment-resistant hypertension and graft dysfunction. Endovascular intervention results in significant regression of graft dysfunction and stabilization of blood pressure (BP). The objective of the presented study is to analyze the features of the TRAS clinical picture along with the trends of plasma creatinine (Pcr) and mean BP (mBP) after successful percutaneous transluminal stenting (PTS).
Method
The single center retrospective study was conducted from June 2018 to June 2024. The diagnosis of TRAS was detected by duplex ultrasonography. In 32 recipients (51.6%) computed tomography angiography was done after duplex ultrasonography. The comparative analysis of Pcr (level before TRAS, at the time of TRAS diagnosis, 7–10 days and a month after PTS) and indicators of mBP (at the time of TRAS diagnosis and 7–10 days after PTS) was conducted. Statistical analysis was performed using the STATISTICA 13 (Mediana (Me) [IQR 25%; 75%], Wilcoxon-test).
Results
A total of 62 recipients were included, all allografts from deceased donors. Age of patients was 20–70 y, Mediana (Me) age—45 y [(IQR) 40; 54], female 43.5%. Body mass index 16.2–46.3 kg/m2, Me 24.3 kg/m2 [20.4; 27.2]. The most common cause of end stage renal disease was chronic glomerulonephritis (29%), 13 patients (21%) suffered from Diabetes Mellitus (in 8 recipients it was the cause of ESRD, in 5—posttransplant diabetes). 12 patients (19.3%) had coronary heart disease. 3 patients underwent pre-emptive KTx, the vintage of renal replacement therapy was 2 mo and16 y, Me 24 mo [12; 48], 12 patients (19.3%) had more, than one KTx. The donor's age was 30–63 y, Me 48.8 y [12.0; 16.75]. 22 recipients (35.5%) had delayed allograft function, the time of cold ischemia was 8.5–23.5 h, Me 14.0 h [12.0; 16.75]. The period between KTx and TRAS diagnosis was 2 mo and21 y, Me 6 mo [4.5; 16.1]. During a year after KTx TRAS was diagnosed in 46 recipients (74.2%). The clinical picture of TRAS was presented by a combination of progressive allograft dysfunction and treatment-resistant hypertension in 28 patients (45.2%), isolated allograft dysfunction in 23 (37%) and isolated treatment-resistant hypertension in 11 (17.7%). The successful PTS resulted in a decrease in Pcr by 20 µmol/L or more 7–10 days after the intervention in 42 recipients (67.7%), and a month after intervention in 48 (77.4%). mBP decreased by 10 mmHg or more 7–10 days after the intervention in 44 recipients (71%). Pcr level before TRAS was Me 160 µmol/L [130; 180], Pcr at the time of TRAS diagnosis—Me 201 µmol/L [172; 277], Pcr 7–10 days after PTS—Me 167 µmol/L [135; 212], Pcr a month after PTS—Me 155 µmol/L [126; 199]. mBP at the time of TRAS diagnosis was Me 120 mmHg [103; 131], mBP 7–10 days after PTS—Me 97 mmHg [93; 100]. The dynamics of Pcr and mBP are presented in Figs 1 and 2.
Conclusion
TRAS may manifest as isolated allograft dysfunction in the setting of stable BP in many recipients. Duplex ultrasonography should be conducted on all patients with progressive allograft dysfunction despite BP parameters. Successful PTS results in remarkable improvement in allograft function and reduced BP parameters.

title: #0791 Graft survival in kidney transplantation: a comparative analysis of IgA nephropathy vs non-IgAN kidney disease and the impact of recurrent IgAN
authors: Rashed Kamal; Mohamed Elewa; Durga Kanigicherla
abstract:
Background and Aims
IgA nephropathy (IgAN) is the most common primary glomerulonephritis and a leading cause of end-stage kidney disease. Underlying disease etiology can significantly influence kidney transplantation outcomes. While graft survival outcomes differ between IgAN and non-IgAN nephropathies, the precise magnitude and nature of these disparities remain ambiguous. As an immune-mediated disease, IgAN has the potential to recur post-transplant. Recurrence rates of IgAN have been extensively studied in the literature. However, a consensus regarding the specific impact of recurrence on graft survival has yet to be reached. This meta-analysis aims to synthesize published studies to clarify whether recurrence significantly influences graft survival, addressing a critical gap to guide post-transplant management strategies for patients with IgAN.
Method
We conducted a systematic literature search adhering to PRISMA guidelines using PubMed and Embase databases. Only comparative studies contrasting—(a) IgA nephropathy (IgAN) vs. non-IgAN, and (b) recurrent (IgAN R+) vs. non-recurrent IgAN (IgAN R−)—were included. The primary outcome was graft survival at 1, 5, and 10 years. A systematic meta-analysis using a random effects model to evaluate graft survival outcomes was conducted; heterogeneity was assessed through the I² statistic and forest plots were used to visualize the pooled results. Statistical analysis was performed using R software (version 2024.09.0+375).
Results
18 studies spanning from 1980 to 2015 were tabulated for the IgAN vs non-IgAN comparison, involving 9,614 participants in the IgAN group and 130,372 in the non-IgAN group. Mean age in the IgAN group was 36.7 years (±6.3), compared to 42.7 years (±10.6) in the non-IgAN group while the proportion of male participants was 69.7% and 61.0% respectively. Mean follow-up time was 5.84 years (±1.91). Pooled graft survival at 1, 5, and 10 years was 93.9%, 89.7%, and 73.7% for IgAN vs. 90.9%, 86.9%, and 72.6% for non-IgAN.
For the IgAN R- vs IgAN R+ comparison, 18 studies spanning from 1981 to 2024 were tabulated, with 11,051 IgAN R− and 1,142 IgAN R+ participants. Mean age for IgAN R− was 40.1 years (±5.7) vs. 36.6 years (±3.9) in IgAN R+, with proportion of males being 60.94% and 65.14% respectively. Mean follow-up was 6.8 years (±2.0) and Mean rate of recurrence was 20.2% (±11.1) across the studies. A random effects model was used to evaluate the pooled proportion of surviving grafts at specified time intervals. Pooled 5-year graft survival rates for IgAN R− and IgAN R+ were 0.91 (95% CI; 0.84–0.95) and 0.84 (95% CI; 0.77–0.89), respectively. Whereas, pooled 10-year graft survival rates for IgAN R− and IgAN R+ were 0.79 (95% CI; 0.69–0.86) and 0.61 (95% CI; 0.50–0.70). Subsequently, a random effects model was used to pool the survival differences within each study. The pooled survival difference between IgAN R− and IgAN R+ was 7% (95% CI; 1% – 13%, P = 0.022) at 5 years and 19% (95% CI; 6% – 32%, P = 0.004) at 10 years.
Conclusion
Whilst graft survival in IgAN and non-IgAN kidney diseases are comparable, stratifying IgAN by recurrence shows a significantly worse graft survival in IgAN R+ patients compared to IgAN R−. Marked heterogeneity was observed in the studies. Vigilant monitoring of IgAN recurrence post-transplant coupled with early intervention may improve graft survival. Further research into recurrence mechanisms and targeted therapies is essential to enhance long-term outcomes in this high-risk group.

title: #1269 Quantifying donor-derived cell-free DNA for monitoring kidney transplant recipients: a head-to-head comparison of NGS and ddPCR assays
authors: Lisa Loi; Marvin Reineke; Martin Zeier; Julia Beck; Ekkehard Schütz; Aylin Akifova; Klemens Budde; Hien Tran; Christian Morath; Louise Benning
abstract:
Background and Aims
Donor-derived cell-free DNA (dd-cfDNA) is recognized as a valuable biomarker for monitoring and risk-stratifying graft injury, evaluating anti-rejection therapy, and guiding re-biopsy decisions. Despite strong clinical evidence, its adoption in Europe remains limited by uncertainties about optimal testing strategies and costs. Additionally, while various dd-cfDNA assays exist, direct comparative data across the different platforms are scarce. In this study, we compared two commercially available dd-cfDNA assays in kidney transplant recipients undergoing indication biopsies.
Method
In this study, dd-cfDNA levels were quantified in 96 kidney transplant recipients using two commercially available assays. The first assay (AlloSeq, CareDx) employs next-generation sequencing with a multiplex PCR approach targeting 202 bi-allelic SNPs across 22 autosomes. The second assay (GraftAssure, Oncocyte) uses droplet digital PCR on a shared SNP subset, providing both absolute and relative quantification based on patient-specific variants. The manufacturers' reported lower limits of quantification are 0.23% for AlloSeq and 0.04% for GraftAssure.
Results
Overall, the two assays showed no significant difference (P = 0.35) and yielded consistent results across all BANFF-defined biopsy categories. Linear regression indicated no deviation from the line of identity [Assay2 = 1.0 × Assay1 (CI: 0.95–1.13) − 0.01 (−0.04–0.012)], with Pearson's r = 0.96 (Fig. 1). Using pre-defined cut-offs of 0.57% and 0.5%, agreement rates were 95% and 93%, respectively. Notably, dd-cfDNA levels were highest in patients with antibody-mediated rejection, with both assays producing comparable results (Assay1: mean 1.85 ± 1.33 vs Assay2: mean 1.90 ± 1.33; P = 0.98).
Conclusion
This study provides the first direct comparison of two commercially available dd-cfDNA test kits—one based on NGS and the other on ddPCR. The findings indicate equivalent dd-cfDNA measurements between the two platforms, highlighting their reliability and supporting their routine use in transplant care. By establishing assay equivalency, this work represents an important advance toward broader clinical implementation of dd-cfDNA monitoring.

title: #949 Vitamin K dependent proteins and bone quality in the first year after kidney transplantation
authors: Maria Fusaro; Andrea Aghi; Maurizio Gallieni; Althea Cossettini; Mario Plebani; Martina Zaninotto; Chiara Cosma; Pascale Khairallah; Giovanni Luigi Tripepi; Thomas Nickolas
abstract:
Background and Aims
Chronic kidney disease (CKD) often leads to mineral and bone disorders (CKD-MBD), which compromise bone quality and increase fracture risk. These bone complications frequently persist after kidney transplantation (K-Tx), primarily due to the lingering effects of pre-existing CKD-MBD. Our aim was to evaluate CKD-MBD biomarkers, bone turnover markers, vitamin K-dependent protein (VKDP) levels, and bone microarchitecture using HR-pQCT at the time of K-Tx (T0) and 12 months post-transplant (T2). The main objective was to establish the association between VKDPs and HR-pQCT-derived bone quality parameters.
Method
We analyzed data from a cohort of 61 K-Tx patients: mean age 50.9 ± 13.3 years, 67% male, 25 patients (41%) underwent pre-emptive K-Tx, median dialysis duration 12 months (36 patients, 59%), diabetes prevalence 25%, fracture history 32%. The median cumulative total steroid dose was 1194 mg of prednisone equivalent. The following CKD-MBD serum biomarkers and bone turnover markers were measured: 25(OH)D, 1,25(OH)2D, PTH, Bone ALP, P1NP, CTX, cFGF23, Klotho, IGF1, phosphate, calcium. Vitamin K-related proteins included Bone Gla Protein (BGP), undercarboxylated BGP (ucBGP), Matrix Gla Protein, and dephosphorylated-uc MGP (dp-ucMGP). In addition to HR-pQCT of the tibia and radius, DEXA scans of the lumbar spine, hip, and radius were performed at baseline and 12 months post-K-Tx. Spearman correlation (ρ, rho) was assessed between the percentage change in VKDPs, bone biomarkers (PTH, cFGF23), bone turnover markers (P1NP, CTX, Bone ALP), and the percentage change in HR-pQCT parameters of the tibia and radius.
Results
Significant improvements were observed in all CKD-MBD biomarkers and bone turnover markers 12 months post-transplant, except for Bone ALP and Klotho levels. PTH decreased from 100 to 27 ng/L, and CTX from 1524 to 246 pg/ml (Fig. 1). VKDP levels also showed significant improvement. The prevalence of vitamin K deficiency, based on a cut-off level of uc-BGP ≥4.5 ng/ml, decreased from 77% to 32% (P < 0.01, Delta % [median and IQR]: −55.22 [−69.50, −24.33]). Using a cut-off level of dp-uc MGP >500 pmol/L, the prevalence of vitamin K deficiency decreased non-significantly from 97% to 79% (P = 0.06). Our findings indicate significant inverse correlations between % Δ uc-BGP and Radius Total Volumetric BMD (r = −0.37, P < 0.05), Failure Load (r = −0.51, P < 0.05), and Stiffness (r = −0.49, P < 0.05). However, correlations between % Δ uc-BGP and Tibial parameters, including Tibial Total Volumetric BMD (r = −0.08), Failure Load (r = −0.11), and Stiffness (r = −0.11), did not reach statistical significance (P > 0.05) (Fig. 2).
Conclusion
Our data confirm an improvement in vitamin K status one year after K-Tx. Additionally, the inverse correlation between ucBGP and bone quality parameters assessed by HR-pQCT underscores the crucial role of BGP in bone health. To our knowledge, these are the first reported data in the literature.

title: #1711 Haemophagocytic histiolymphocytis after solid organ transplantation: preliminary data from a cohort study
authors: Rayane Benyahia; Jean-Baptiste Rieu; Nassim Kamar; Stanislas Faguer; Arnaud Del Bello
abstract:
Background and Aims
Haemophagocytic histiolymphocytis (HLH) is a rare but potentially fatal immune disorder characterized by overwhelming inflammation and cytokine storm, with an overall mortality rate of nearly 50%. Most HLH are secondary to infections, malignancies, or autoimmune diseases. However, HLH after solid organ transplantation (SOT-HLH) are scarcely reported and understudied, with the largest published case series to date quoting only 17 cases [1, 2]. Our study aims to thoroughly describe clinical and biological parameters at presentation and during follow-up from a large cohort of well-phenotyped adult SOT-HLH, administrated treatments, management of immunosuppression, patient and graft outcomes, as well as factors associated with poor prognosis.
Method
In this French monocentric, retrospective study, we identified 63 adult SOT patients between 1st July 2007 and 31st December 2024 with a bone marrow aspirate (BMA) compatible with haemophagocytosis and fulfilling HLH-2004 criteria (60% male, mean age 61 y.o).
Results
Fever was observed only in half of our patients. More than 75% of cases showed bi- or pancytopenia, lymphopenia, and hyperferritinemia (>1000 µg/L). Median H-score was 215. 29 cases were kidney recipients, 20 liver recipients, 2 (non-combined) liver-kidney recipients, and 12 heart recipients. One third and one half of all HLH cases occurred during the first 3 months and the first 12 months after last SOT, respectively. Concomitant SOT rejection happened in less than 10% of cases (mostly acute T-cell mediated rejections). Mean SOFA score at the date of BMA was 11 (vasopressor support 75%, mechanical ventilation 75%, renal replacement therapy 75%). Transfusion of labile blood products was required in more than 85% of cases. Mean length of hospitalisation was 44 days, and mortality rate was 55%. More than 80% of SOT-HLH were associated with suspected or proven infection (33% co-infected with bacteria and virus; 21% with virus only, the most frequent being CMV and EBV; 14% with bacteria only; 11% triply co-infected with bacteria, virus, and fungi; 21% of other scenarios). Polyvalent IV immunoglobulins and steroid therapy were provided in nearly 60% of cases. Other immunomodulators included tocilizumab (25%), etoposide (10%), the apolipoprotein A1 biomimetic CER-001 (<10%) anakinra (< 5%), rituximab (<5%), and plasma exchange (<5%). Apart from escalating steroid doses, the most frequent adjustments in anti-rejection regimen were the discontinuation of the antiproliferative agent without substitution (33%) and the reduction of the calcineurin inhibitor trough level target (12%). Blood and BMA findings, patient and graft outcomes, as well as risk factors for poor prognosis will be presented at the meeting.
Conclusion
Our study highlights the heterogeneity of clinico-biological profiles and therapeutic approaches for adult SOT-HLH. A high incidence of HLH was observed during the early months post-SOT, primarily driven by severe viral or bacterial infections, and associated with a high mortality rate. Future studies investigating optimal strategies for managing HLH in SOT patients remain an urgent medical need.

title: #3653 Health-related quality of life in the first year post kidney transplantation – a cohort study
authors: Habiba Ahmed; Frederik Haupenthal; Konstantin Doberer; Sebastian Kapps; Katharina Ebenberger; Bettina Gober; Gregor Bond
abstract:
Background and Aims
For patients suffering from end-stage renal disease, a kidney transplantation is the treatment of choice to improve health-related quality of life (HRQOL). An in-depth understanding of individual factors affecting HRQOL might help to develop strategies to support the process of HRQOL improvement. The AdTorque study was designed to prospectively assess HRQOL in the context of patient-related characteristics and follow-up data associated with HRQOL.
Method
This cohort study screened all 283 consecutive adult kidney graft recipients transplanted at the Medical University of Vienna between January 2018 and December 2019. HRQOL was monitored within the first-year post-transplant applying the WHOQOL-BREF questionnaire at 3 study-visits: at the first out-patient visit (P1), 3 months post-transplant (P2) and 12 months post-transplant (P3). The WHOQOL-BREF assesses the HRQOL perceived by patients in the previous month in 4 domains: physical health, psychological health, social relationships and environmental health. Each domain is scored between 0 and 100 and a total score for overall HRQOL is calculated by the sum of all domains (0–400). For subgroup analysis all patients were stratified according to sociodemographic, psycho-social and transplant-related variables.
Results
In the total cohort of 183 patients (33% females; median age 56 [IQR 46–53]) the median overall HRQOL was 315 (IQR 278–340) at P1, 322 (IQR 277–351) at P2 and 328 (IQR 289–359) at P3. A significant improvement was only detected in the physical health domain (71 [IQR 54–79] at P1 to 79 [IQR 56–89] at P3; P = 0.006). While male sex, younger age, higher education and donation from a living donor indicated a positive influence, smoking and living-alone affected the improvements in HRQOL negatively. Patients with psychological disorders (n = 67; 37%) reported a significantly reduced overall HRQOL compared to patients without such disorders (279 [IQR 251–323] vs. 329 [IQR 307–347, P < 0.001] at P1, 284 [IQR 244–335] vs. 333 [IQR 297–354, P < 0.001] at P2 and 302 [IQR 267–335] vs. 354 [IQR 307–371, P < 0.001] at P3).
Conclusion
Patients with a psychological disorder and fewer social relations perceived less improvement in their HRQOL over the first year post kidney transplantation. Our study emphasizes the need for psycho-social support in post-transplant routine care.

title: #2327 Monitoring of adherence to immunosuppressive drugs by electronic healthcare data in kidney transplant recipients
authors: Sebastian Kapps; Frederik Haupenthal; Konstantin Doberer; Gregor Bond
abstract:
Background and Aims
Medication non-adherence to immunosuppressive drugs is a major challenge in the management of kidney transplant recipients and a major risk factor for rejection and early graft loss. Utilizing electronic healthcare data in the form of pharmacy refill records (PRR) offers a practical method for estimating adherence in this setting. Analysis of the value of PRR in the context of a multimodal assessment of non-adherence in a real world setting is crucial for its application in routine post-transplant care.
Method
The prospective single-center AdTorque trial was initiated to conduct a multimodal and longitudinal evaluation of adherence to immunosuppressive medications among kidney transplant recipients including PRR. All 287 adult kidney graft recipients transplanted at the Medical University of Vienna between 2018 and 2019 were monitored for 2 years with a clinical follow-up of 4 years. PRR were analyzed using the standardized continuous measures of medication availability (CMA) calculations (CMA1-CMA9; primary analysis CMA7). These scores estimate adherence as a value from 0 to 100%, denoting complete non-adherence and perfect adherence to a given regimen, respectively.
Results
For this interim analysis only the 101 subjects with a complete record of dispensations and prescriptions for the first post-transplant year were included. Interestingly, PRR showed different adherence estimates between tacrolimus (TAC) and mycophenolic acid (MPA; mean CMA7: TAC: 72.4%; MPA: 87.3%, P < 0.001). Such differences were also found in the more basic CMAs scores. No differences in CMA scores were found regarding biopsy proven graft rejection and de novo donor specific antibodies. Notably, no association was found between CMA scores and adherence assessed using the self-report questionnaire BAASIS®, which in contrast to PRR picks up on irregularities concerning the time of drug intake during the day.
Conclusion
This study suggests that when using PRR to estimate adherence in a post-transplant setting TAC and MPA need to be considered separately and that the customary 80% cutoff to identify adherence might not be applicable. In case granular data is not available the more simple CMA scores seem to provide similar insight to more sophisticated CMAs, which take less assumptions but need more granular data to be computed. Furthermore, PRR alone might not be conclusive in this setting due to their blindness to timing issues.

title: #2342 Long term monitoring of torque teno virus load for the detection of infections in kidney transplantation
authors: Sebastian Kapps; Frederik Haupenthal; Konstantin Doberer; Gregor Bond
abstract:
Background and Aims
Personalized balance of immunosuppression is crucial to prevent organ rejection and infections in kidney transplant recipients. Plasma load of the non-pathogenic and highly prevalent torque teno virus (TTV) has been suggested to assess the state of immunosuppression. A cut-off value for risk prediction of infections in the first year post-transplant has been defined and is currently tested in an interventional randomized clinical trial (TTVguideIT). Defining cut-off values beyond year one post-transplant are crucial for the design of follow-up trials (e.g. TAOIST) and long term routine clinical care.
Method
For this secondary analysis of the prospective single-center AdTorque study, all 268 consecutive adult patients who underwent a kidney transplantation between January 1st, 2018 and December 31st, 2019 at the Medical University of Vienna were included and followed up for a maximum of 4 years. Over this time, all infectious events with respective treatments, hospitalizations and changes of immunosuppression were recorded. Infectious disease work up included syndromic PCR panel testing, among others including SARS-CoV-2 PCR. Additionally, immunologic monitoring via TTV PCR from plasma was performed.
Results
In a preliminary analysis including 150 patients (37.2% female; median age 52.7 years) 621 infectious events were recorded, with 24 patients not experiencing an infection. Of all events the majority were urinary tract infections (n = 204; 32.9%), 178 of all events led to hospitalization. The most commonly identified pathogens were cytomegalovirus (n = 97), Escherichia coli (n = 71) and SARS-CoV-2 (n = 53). The overall event rate declined over the first three years post-transplant, with a rise in the fourth year (year 1: 94.9%; year 2: 48.0%; year 3: 44.7%; year 4: 78.4%).
Conclusion
This interim analysis gives valuable insight on the epidemiology of infectious disease in the current post-transplant era. The strength of the study is the long term follow-up, the overlap with the height of the COVID-19 pandemic and the inclusion of multiplex PCR panels in routine work-up. The full data set including associations with TTV load and respective cutoffs are currently being assessed, and will be presented at ERA 2025 in case of acceptance.

title: #823 Role of high plasma levels of VWF and Ristocetin Cofactor in kidney transplant recipients
authors: Carmela Caputo
abstract:
Background and Aims
Von Willebrand Factor (VWF) is a glycoprotein of approximately 250 kDa, consisting of low, intermediate, and high molecular weight multimers. It is primarily synthesized by endothelial cells and serves to carry Factor VIII, which is essential for blood clot formation. VWF interacts with platelets, promoting their adhesion to collagen fibers exposed following damage to the vessel wall. The Von Willebrand Cofactor (Ristocetin Cofactor, R:CoF) measures VWF-mediated platelet agglutination in the presence of the antibiotic ristocetin. This assay represents a method for assessing the functional activity of VWF. Endothelial dysfunction in the transplanted kidney results in increased VWF secretion and is considered a key factor in the progression of atherosclerosis, which remains the leading cause of death post-transplantation. Previous research has observed elevated VWF levels in kidney transplant recipients after episodes of rejection. The objective of this cross-sectional study is to correlate plasma levels of VWF and its Cofactor with factors such as age, glomerular filtration rate (GFR), sex, graft survival time, and immunosuppressive therapy in a cohort of 105 kidney transplant recipients.
Method
A total of 105 kidney transplant patients, who underwent transplantation between January 2021 and December 2021, were included in the study. The participants' ages ranged from 21 to 79 years, with 47 females and 58 males. Serum creatinine levels in the population ranged from 0.8 to 5 mg/dL, but remained stable within the same patient over time. The patients were divided into the following groups based on demographic and clinical characteristics:
Age:
Group A1: 25 patients aged < 45 years
Group A2: 80 patients aged ≥ 45 years
GFR:
Group B1: 46 patients with GFR > 60 mL/min
Group B2: 59 patients with GFR ≤ 60 mL/min
Graft time:
Group C1: 70 patients with a graft survival time > 5 years
Group C2: 35 patients with a graft survival time < 5 years
Immunosuppressive therapy was evaluated in relation to VWF, although no specific groupings were made due to the heterogeneity and variability of treatments.
Laboratory Methods
The VWF antigen concentration was determined using a latex immunoturbidimetric assay. Reference ranges for VWF:Ag are 66%–176% for patients with blood groups A, B, or AB, and 42%–140% for patients with blood group O. The R:CoF test utilizes platelets to reproduce the ability of VWF to interact with its platelet receptor, the GPIb glycoprotein complex, in the presence of ristocetin. Reference ranges for R:CoF are 61–240 for blood groups A, B, AB, and 48–202 for blood group O.
Results
1) Statistically significant differences were found between Group A1 (Age < 45 years, n = 25) and Group A2 (Age ≥ 45 years, n = 80) for both VWF and ristocetin cofactor levels. The mean VWF level in Group A1 was significantly lower than in Group A2 (P = 0.002, one-tailed t-test). The normality of the data was verified using the Shapiro-Wilk test. These findings suggest that with increasing age, the pro-inflammatory processes lead to “inflammaging,” which triggers endothelial dysfunction and increased VWF secretion. Inflammation, thrombosis, and chronic rejection may thus be interlinked in this population.
2) No statistically significant difference was observed between Group B1 (GFR > 60 mL/min, n = 46) and Group B2 (GFR ≤ 60 mL/min, n = 59), despite higher levels of VWF in patients with GFR < 60 mL/min.
3) Patients treated with everolimus exhibited significantly higher VWF levels compared to those treated with other immunosuppressants (P = 0.03, one-tailed Student's t-test). Everolimus is associated with a procoagulant state in transplant recipients, potentially increasing the risk of thrombotic events.
Conclusion
VWF may serve as a valuable biomarker for assessing endothelial injury and could potentially be used to predict the risk of chronic rejection in kidney transplant recipients. Our results represent the starting point, but prospective studies are needed to clarify the direct role of VWF levels in the context of renal transplant rejection.

This assay represents a method for assessing the functional activity of VWF. Endothelial dysfunction in the transplanted kidney results in increased VWF secretion and is considered a key factor in the progression of atherosclerosis, which remains the leading cause of death post-transplantation. Previous research has observed elevated VWF levels in kidney transplant recipients after episodes of rejection. The objective of this cross-sectional study is to correlate plasma levels of VWF and its Cofactor with factors such as age, glomerular filtration rate (GFR), sex, graft survival time, and immunosuppressive therapy in a cohort of 105 kidney transplant recipients.
Method
A total of 105 kidney transplant patients, who underwent transplantation between January 2021 and December 2021, were included in the study. The participants' ages ranged from 21 to 79 years, with 47 females and 58 males. Serum creatinine levels in the population ranged from 0.8 to 5 mg/dL, but remained stable within the same patient over time. The patients were divided into the following groups based on demographic and clinical characteristics:
Age:
Group A1: 25 patients aged < 45 years
Group A2: 80 patients aged ≥ 45 years
GFR:
Group B1: 46 patients with GFR > 60 mL/min
Group B2: 59 patients with GFR ≤ 60 mL/min
Graft time:
Group C1: 70 patients with a graft survival time > 5 years
Group C2: 35 patients with a graft survival time < 5 years
Immunosuppressive therapy was evaluated in relation to VWF, although no specific groupings were made due to the heterogeneity and variability of treatments.
Laboratory Methods
The VWF antigen concentration was determined using a latex immunoturbidimetric assay. Reference ranges for VWF:Ag are 66%–176% for patients with blood groups A, B, or AB, and 42%–140% for patients with blood group O. The R:CoF test utilizes platelets to reproduce the ability of VWF to interact with its platelet receptor, the GPIb glycoprotein complex, in the presence of ristocetin. Reference ranges for R:CoF are 61–240 for blood groups A, B, AB, and 48–202 for blood group O.
Results
1) Statistically significant differences were found between Group A1 (Age < 45 years, n = 25) and Group A2 (Age ≥ 45 years, n = 80) for both VWF and ristocetin cofactor levels. The mean VWF level in Group A1 was significantly lower than in Group A2 (P = 0.002, one-tailed t-test). The normality of the data was verified using the Shapiro-Wilk test. These findings suggest that with increasing age, the pro-inflammatory processes lead to “inflammaging,” which triggers endothelial dysfunction and increased VWF secretion. Inflammation, thrombosis, and chronic rejection may thus be interlinked in this population.
2) No statistically significant difference was observed between Group B1 (GFR > 60 mL/min, n = 46) and Group B2 (GFR ≤ 60 mL/min, n = 59), despite higher levels of VWF in patients with GFR < 60 mL/min.
3) Patients treated with everolimus exhibited significantly higher VWF levels compared to those treated with other immunosuppressants (P = 0.03, one-tailed Student's t-test). Everolimus is associated with a procoagulant state in transplant recipients, potentially increasing the risk of thrombotic events.
Conclusion
VWF may serve as a valuable biomarker for assessing endothelial injury and could potentially be used to predict the risk of chronic rejection in kidney transplant recipients. Our results represent the starting point, but prospective studies are needed to clarify the direct role of VWF levels in the context of renal transplant rejection.

title: #2074 Immunosuppression reduction in kidney transplantation: can we rest assured?
authors: José Enrique Ruiz-Cabello Subiela; Andrea Cifuentes-Talavera; Natalia Polanco Fernández; Esther González Monte; Ana Maria Hernandez Vicente; Mario Fernandez; Hernando Trujillo Cuellar; Amado Andrés
abstract:
Background and Aims
Since the Symphony trial in 2007, no other immunosuppression strategy beyond triple therapy with tacrolimus (FK), mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) and glucocorticoids (GC) has shown better results. However, in the long term, over-immunosuppression increases the risk of infections, cardiovascular issues, and tumors. In these situations, antimetabolites withdrawal to reduce immunosuppression load is a frequent strategy. Some studies have suggested that FK monotherapy may be safe for a particular group of patients.
The aim of our study was to analyze the clinical outcomes of kidney transplant (KT) patients in whom MMF was withdrawn, maintaining FK monotherapy or FK + low-dose GC, without other changes.
Method
We retrospectively analyzed data from a prospective cohort of 689 patients who received KT from November 2014 to December 2022, in which MMF discontinuation was performed as an immunosuppression reduction strategy. The main outcomes were biopsy-proven allograft rejection (BPAR) and graft survival. Secondary outcomes included the development of donor-specific antibodies (DSA) and infectious episodes.
Results
A total of 48 patients were identified with a median age of 68 years, 69% male. Almost all patients (95.8%) were of low-moderate immunological risk. Median follow-up time was 17.9 months (8.5–29.3) and median time to discontinuation of MMF since transplantation was 3.9 months. The main indications for immunosuppression reduction were infections (37.5%), cytopenia (29.2%), and history or development of neoplasia (20.8%). Most cases (95.8%) were maintained under dual therapy with low-dose GC and FK with a mean FK trough level of 7.9 (1.3) μg/ml. Only one patient (2%) developed BPAR (T-cell-mediated rejection) and another patient developed de novo DSA, but with no signs of rejection in a graft biopsy. No differences were noted in kidney function during follow-up (eGFR 31 vs 33.5 ml/min/m2 at start and end of follow-up, respectively). Death-censored graft survival rate was 95.8% (Fig. 1). Infectious episodes that required admission for management were observed in 37.5% of the patients after MMF was stopped, highlighting that this was a group of relatively elderly vulnerable recipients (Table 1).
Conclusion
In a selected group of KT patients with low-moderate immunological risk and susceptibility to infectious complications, discontinuing MMF while maintaining FK-based regimens might be a safe and effective strategy, underlining the need for individualized management. Prospective controlled data regarding personalized maintenance immunosuppression in KT is urgently needed.

title: #605 Telitacicept therapy in recurrent IgA nephropathy post-kidney transplantation: a case series and literature review
authors: Ziyan Yan; Renfei Xia; Wenli Zeng; Jialiang Hui; Jian Xu; Yun Miao
abstract:
Background and Aims
Recurrent IgA nephropathy (IgAN) following kidney transplantation (KT) affects 9%–61% of patients, significantly increasing the risk of graft loss. Current management strategies are predominantly symptomatic, with no established therapies targeting the underlying pathogenesis. Telitacicept, a TACI-Fc fusion protein that dual-targets BLyS and APRIL, inhibits B cell maturation and differentiation, making it a potential therapeutic option for IgAN. Despite its promise, there is limited evidence supporting its use in post-transplant IgAN recurrence. This study reports three distinct cases of recurrent IgAN post-KT, exploring the efficacy and safety of telitacicept combined with cyclophosphamide-methylprednisolone pulse therapy. By analyzing these cases and reviewing the literature, we aim to address critical gaps in understanding and highlight telitacicept's potential as a novel therapeutic strategy for this challenging condition.
Method
We presented three cases of recurrent IgAN post-KT. Clinical history, laboratory results, pathological findings, and treatment courses were reviewed. Treatment efficacy and adverse events were monitored, and the findings were contextualized within existing literature.
Results
We observed that early recurrence of IgAN following KT often presents with minimal symptoms, and allograft damage is usually established by the time proteinuria is detected. Addressing allograft injury promptly is therefore a primary goal. Cyclophosphamide-methylprednisolone pulse therapy is commonly utilized to reduce inflammation and proteinuria, mitigating graft injury due to recurrent IgAN. Subsequent clinical courses varied, prompting the exploration of different therapeutic approaches:
No severe adverse events, including allergic reactions, severe infections, bone marrow suppression, or liver dysfunction, were observed during treatment. Literature suggests that the intensity of glomerular CD206+ and CD68+ macrophage infiltration may predict patient responsiveness to telitacicept therapy.
Conclusion
Telitacicept demonstrates efficacy in inhibiting B cell maturation and suppressing the release of Gd-IgA1 and anti-Gd-IgA1 antibodies, thereby preventing immune complex deposition in the renal mesangium. When combined with pulse therapy, telitacicept shows promising results in treating recurrent IgAN post-KT, significantly reducing proteinuria and hematuria, improving graft function, and exhibiting an excellent safety profile. This study underscores the importance of early diagnosis and proactive management of recurrent IgAN post-KT. By reporting these cases, we aim to highlight the potential of telitacicept as a cornerstone therapy in this context, providing a basis for further research. Multicenter studies are warranted to further validate the long-term efficacy and safety of this combination therapy for recurrent IgAN following KT.

title: #1353 Categorical state sequence analysis to identify pre-transplantation care trajectories among chronic kidney disease patients in France
authors: Latame Komla Adoli; Cécile Couchoud; Juliette Piveteau; Hoang Giang Pham; Cécile Vigneau; Sahar Bayat
abstract:
Background and Aims
Kidney transplantation is the best renal replacement therapy for eligible patients. There are several trajectories leading to kidney transplantation including various transitions between different states. Few studies have attempted to describe these trajectories. The aim of this study is to describe the care trajectories of chronic kidney disease patients prior to kidney transplantation as well as patients’ characteristics associated to them.
Method
Data were extracted from the REIN registry. All patients aged 18 years and over who underwent a kidney transplantation between 2015 and 2019 in France were included. Information on their comorbidities and dialysis modalities five years prior to transplantation was extracted. The care trajectory was defined as a sequence of states including a state without replacement therapy, dialysis modalities (self-dialysis, home dialysis, peritoneal dialysis, facility-based hemodialysis), waitlisting, follow-up of previous kidney transplantation and kidney transplantation. A state sequence analysis using an Optimal Matching approach followed by an ascending hierarchical classification was used to classify patients in “groups” regarding their care trajectories. A binary logistic regression was performed to study patients’ characteristics associated with the “trajectory group” with early access to kidney transplantation.
Results
A total of 14 426 patients were included in the study, 37% of whom were women. The median age was 55 years, interquartile range [44–66]. Sequence analysis identified 6322 distinct sequences. Hierarchical ascending classification using the Wald method identified four “groups” of care trajectories (Fig. 1). “Trajectory group 1” includes 8114 individuals (56.2% of all, 37% of women, median age 53.0-year-old) and is characterised by early transplantation and short time on dialysis before transplantation. ”Trajectory group 2” includes 1 905 individuals (13.2% of all, 35% of women, median age 56.6-year-old) and is characterised by patients who have mainly been on self-dialysis in the five years prior to transplantation. “Trajectory group 3” included 1210 individuals (8.4% of all, 37% of women, median age 59.7-year-old) and consisted mainly of patients who were on facility-based hemodialysis during the five years prior to kidney transplantation. ”Trajectory group 4” included 3197 individuals (22.2% of all, 38% of women, median age 58.9-year-old) and consisted of patients who had been on facility-based haemodialysis or self-dialysis for approximately three years prior to kidney transplantation (Fig. 2).
Multivariate logistic regression found that, the existence of a comorbidity, in particular cancer aOR: 0.4 CI 95% [0.3–0.5], diabetes aOR: 0.8 [0.7–0.9], a psychiatric disorder aOR: 0.4 [0.3 - 0.6] but also older age group compared with less than 40 years, aOR40-59 years: 0.6 [0.5–0.7], aOR60-69 years: 0.4 [0.3–0.45], aOR70-79 years: 0.4 [0.38–0.5], were associated with a lower probability of being in “trajectory group 1”, the trajectory group with early access to kidney transplantation. However, patients with cirrhosis aOR: 1.4 [1.1–1.8] or those who were autonomous aOR: 1.8 [1.2–3.3] were more likely to be in “trajectory group 1”. There is no sex effect aOR: 1.02 [0.95–1.10]. The patient's region of residence is significantly associated with the trajectory group 1.
Conclusion
This study identified 4 care trajectory groups prior to kidney transplantation. Half of the patients had a care trajectory marked by an early access to kidney transplantation, probably patients who were well followed up and for whom the recommendations on access to transplant have been successfully observed (Trajectory group 1). There was no sex effect on being in this first group. Patients with cirrhosis were more likely to have the “trajectory group 1” maybe because of the existence of dual kidney and liver transplantation in France from which they can benefit with priority. Further studies are needed to evaluate how pre-transplant trajectory might affect post-transplant outcomes.

title: #1364 Association between sex and hospitalisation during the period prior to kidney transplantation in France
authors: Latame Komla Adoli; Cécile Couchoud; Juliette Piveteau; Hoang Giang Pham; Cécile Vigneau; Sahar Bayat
abstract:
Background and Aims
The process to kidney transplantation involves several interactions between the patient and the healthcare system. Several events occur along the way, including consultations with general practitioners and specialists, and hospitalisations. Previous studies in France have shown that the use of healthcare is not the same for men and women before and after dialysis starting. However, no study has yet investigated the use of care in terms of hospitalisation prior to kidney transplantation among men and women. The aim of this study was to assess the association between sex and hospitalisation during the period before kidney transplantation, considering patient's characteristics.
Method
Data were extracted from the REIN registry, which gathered information on patients undergoing kidney replacement therapy in France. This database was linked to the national healthcare consumption database (SNDS) containing information on 98% of the French population. All patients transplanted between 2015 and 2019 and aged over 18 years were included. Our outcomes of interest were the total number of hospitalisations lasting more than 24 hours in the five years before kidney transplantation, excluding stays for dialysis and transplantation. A Poisson regression model adjusted for comorbidities and socio-demographic characteristics was used. A significance level of 5% was considered. The results of the model were presented as adjusted incident rate ratios (aIRR) with their confidence intervals (CI).
Results
We included a total of 12 872 kidney transplanted recipients. The mean age was 54 years (±14), and 37% were women. The total number of stays was in median four for men and five for women over the five years prior to transplantation. The stays lasted in median two days for men and three days for women. The results of the multivariate analysis showed that, men (compared to women) aIRR: 0.93, 95% CI [0.92–0.95], patients aged over 80 years (compared to under 30) aIRR: 0.93 [0.88–0.99], as well as patients with walking autonomy (compared to non-autonomous) aIRR: 0.76 [0.60–0.97] and patients with a body mass index (BMI) over 30 kg/m² (compared to BMI <18.5) aIRR: 0.84 [0.79–0.90] had a lower risk of being hospitalized during the five year before kidney transplantation. Patients with some co-morbidities, in particular cirrhosis aIRR: 1.82 [1.75–1.90], cancer aIRR: 1.23 [1.16–1.31] and patients with diabetes aIRR: 1.34 [1.32–1.36] were more likely to be hospitalized.
Conclusion
This study showed that hospitalisation in the five years prior to kidney transplantation is not homogeneous and that men were less likely to have a more than 24 h hospitalisation compared to women, despite adjusting for comorbidities. Comorbidities increase the risk of hospitalisation. There is a need to characterize these hospitalisations to prevent them.

title: #3540 The impact of living donor's pretransplant clinical features on 1st and 3rd year allograft functions
authors: Mehmet Emin Demir; Siren Sezer; Feyza Bayrakdar Caglayan; Simge Bardak Demir; Ulaş Sözener; Gülçin Türkmen Sarıyıldız; Merter Gülen; Mehmet Polat; Fatma Necla Özşeker; Öykü Kilci; Aylin Yeşim Burç
abstract:
Background and Aims
Allograft quality is associated with long-term allograft survival. Pretransplant donor assessment may indirectly reflect the allograft quality. By analyzing key donor parameters, including demographic characteristics, comorbidities, and renal function prior to donation, we aim to identify potential predictors of long-term allograft outcomes.
Method
This study includes data from kidney transplants performed at Medicana International Ankara Hospital between January 2017, and December2021. Recipient and donor data were obtained from the hospital's automation system and the manual records of the organ transplantation coordination unit. The primary parameters evaluated for recipients included recipient and allograft survival, graft loss, allograft function at 1, 3, 6, 12, 24, and 36 months (eGFR calculated by MDRD), and hospitalizations due to all causes. For donors, CKD-EPI 2021-based eGFR at the time of donation, BMI, smoking status, education level, comorbidities, age, sex, and total number of pregnancies in female donors were recorded. The relationship between these donor factors and the aforementioned recipient-related outcomes was analyzed. Statistical significance was set at as P < 0.05.
Results
A total of 271 kidney transplant recipients were analyzed over a mean follow-up of 5.9 years. The overall mortality rate was 18.5% (50 patients), with significantly higher mortality observed in recipients of deceased donor kidneys (41.4%) compared to living donor recipients (15.7%). Among the 221 surviving recipients (81.5%), 211 (77.9%) maintained a functioning allograft, while 10 (4.5%) experienced graft failure and returned to dialysis. The majority of transplants (89.3%) were from living donors, demonstrating superior long-term outcomes compared to deceased donor recipients (P = 0.012). The mean BMI of living donors was 28.2 ± 5.3 kg/m², with obesity prevalence of 16.9% for Class I, 7.4% for Class II, and 4.9% for Class III. Additionally, 19.4% of donors were smokers, 13.6% had hypertension, and 0.8% had diabetes. The mean eGFR of kidney transplant recipients remained stable during the first year post-transplant but demonstrated a gradual decline after 12 months, though not statistically significant. This decline was potentially influenced by donor characteristics, recipient BMI, and comorbidities. Univariate and multivariate analyses indicated that recipient age, immunological risk, and dialysis history significantly influenced allograft function. Preemptive dialysis was associated with better long-term outcomes (P < 0.05), while prolonged hemodialysis duration negatively impacted eGFR beyond two years (P < 0.05). These effects were particularly notable at 3, 6, 12, 24, and 36 months. Donor-related factors such as older age and higher BMI (≥35 kg/m²) were associated with a decline in eGFR, particularly after 12 months (P = 0.049, P = 0.043, and P = 0.056, respectively). Donor eGFR at the time of transplantation significantly influenced early post-transplant kidney function, with effects observed at 1 and 3 months (P = 0.015 and P = 0.030, respectively). While donor obesity up to Class II (BMI 30.0–39.9) did not significantly impact short- or long-term eGFR, Class II and III obesity (BMI ≥ 35) were associated with a significant decline in renal function after the first year (P = 0.058, P = 0.040, and P = 0.034 at 12, 24, and 36 months, respectively).
Conclusion
This study demonstrated that while allograft function remains stable during the first year post-transplant, a gradual decline is seen over time, influenced by factors such as donor age, BMI, and pretransplant kidney function. Higher donor BMI (≥35 kg/m²) and older donor age were linked to a progressive decrease in eGFR, highlighting the importance of careful donor selection. Additionally, recipient-related factors like immunological risk and dialysis history significantly impacted graft function.

This study demonstrated that while allograft function remains stable during the first year post-transplant, a gradual decline is seen over time, influenced by factors such as donor age, BMI, and pretransplant kidney function. Higher donor BMI (≥35 kg/m²) and older donor age were linked to a progressive decrease in eGFR, highlighting the importance of careful donor selection. Additionally, recipient-related factors like immunological risk and dialysis history significantly impacted graft function.

title: #1492 Carboxyhemoglobin, smoking exposure, and mortality in kidney transplant recipients
authors: Sovia Salamah; António W Gomes-Neto; Firas Farisi Alkaff; Jip Jonker; Jenny E Kootstra-Ros; Daan J Touw; Eva Corpeleijn; Transplantlines Investigators; Casper F M Franssen; Stephan J L Bakker
abstract:
Background and Aims
Smoking is a significant risk factor for increased mortality in kidney transplant recipients (KTR). While KDIGO guidelines recommend annual tobacco use screening for KTR, self-reported smoking status is often unreliable, and urinary cotinine testing, considered the gold standard, is costly. Carboxyhemoglobin (COHb) has emerged as a reliable and cost-effective biomarker for identifying active smokers in KTR, with a cutoff value of 1.5% to classify active smoking. This study aims to explore the association between COHb levels, smoking exposure, and mortality in this patient population.
Method
Plasma COHb was obtained from venous blood samples and measured using hemoxymetry as part of blood gas analysis. Smoking status was assessed through a questionnaire. Cox regression analyses were conducted to evaluate the association between COHb levels and mortality.
Results
Among 1328 KTR (mean age 57 ± 14 years, 49% female, median time post-transplant 12 [IQR 12–85] months), the median COHb level was 0.93% [IQR 0.83–1.23%]. The prevalence of active smokers and history of delayed graft function occurring directly after transplantation were higher according to increasing COHb level (P < 0.001 and P = 0.025, respectively). Triglycerides, C-reactive protein, and urinary albumin excretion were significantly higher according to increasing COHb level (P < 0.001, P < 0.001, and P = 0.026, respectively). Estimated glomerular filtration rate was not associated with COHb levels. During a median follow-up of 4 years, 189 (14.2%) patients died. Higher COHb levels were independently associated with higher mortality risk (hazard ratio (HR) [95% Confidence Interval (CI)] per standard deviation increase = 1.23 [1.11–1.37], P < 0.001). This association remained independent of adjustment for potential confounders, even including smoking status assessed by questionnaire (HR = 1.34 [95% CI 1.19–1.51], P < 0.001, model 4, Table 1). Kaplan-Meier curve analysis showed that patients survival probability was significantly lower among individuals with higher COHb levels (Fig. 1).
Conclusion
COHb, which was previously recognized as a reliable biomarker for detecting active smokers and more accessible than urinary cotinine, was found to be independently associated with an increased risk of mortality in KTR. Regular evaluation of COHb levels in clinical practice can improve physicians' awareness of patients' smoking status, enabling timely interventions to reduce mortality risk.

title: #3258 Immunosuppression management after kidney transplant failure and its impact on sensitization: where do we stand in 2025? A systematic review with meta-analysis
authors: Pedro Fragoso; Rita Leal; Clara Pardinhas; Luís Rodrigues; Maria Guedes Marques; Lídia Santos; Catarina Romãozinho; Andreia Borges; Francisco Caramelo; Arnaldo Figueiredo; Rui Alves
abstract:
Background and Aims
Kidney transplant (KT) recipients who return to dialysis face significant challenges in accessing a second transplant due to HLA sensitization. Although it is recognized that immunosuppression (IS) management after graft failure (KTF) can influence the sensitization status, there are no strong evidence-based guidelines, leading to widely variable clinical practices.
This systematic review with meta-analysis aims to evaluate the impact of different IS withdrawal strategies after kidney transplant failure on HLA sensitization.
Method
We systematically reviewed prospective and retrospective cohort studies assessing the impact of prolonged or earlier IS withdrawal strategies on the following outcomes after graft failure: HLA sensitization (including the development of de novo DSA and average cPRA values or cPRA variation rate) and graft nephrectomy or embolization rates.
We conducted a comprehensive search across Medline, Embase, and Cochrane Library and used the ROBINS-I scale to assess the risk of bias.
The results were synthesized in a meta-analysis, and combined odds ratios and weighted mean differences were calculated using a random-effects model.
The protocol for this meta-analysis was registered within PROSPERO (CRD42024496706).
Results
From 8008 citations, we identified 12 studies involving 1346 patients that fulfilled the eligibility criteria. Most of these studies were retrospective (n = 11), single-center (n = 10) cohorts and exhibited moderate to serious risk of bias. In all studies, the IS regimens in the prolonged withdrawal group involved maintaining more than one immunosuppressant for at least three months after graft failure.
Five studies comprising 600 patients reported post-KTF cPRA absolute values; three studies comprising 316 patients reported cPRA variation rates; four studies comprising 498 patients reported de novo DSA occurrence, and nine studies comprising 1112 patients reported graft nephrectomy or embolization rates.
Earlier IS withdrawal was significantly associated with decreased odds of cPRA maintenance (OR 0.22, 95% CI 0.05–0.96) and increased odds of graft nephrectomy or embolization (OR 2.13, 95% CI 1.39–3.26). While earlier IS withdrawal also favored a higher occurrence of de novo DSA (OR 2.41, 95% CI 0.43–13.46) and a higher absolute cPRA value (md +0.87, 95% CI −0.45–2.2), neither of these findings reached statistical significance.
Conclusion
While prolonged IS withdrawal did not prevent the development of de novo DSA or lower cPRA values, it appeared to have a role in preserving the sensitization status of KT recipients returning to dialysis.
Efforts were made to minimize heterogeneity among the included studies, particularly regarding the IS regimens compared and the methods and timing of HLA evaluation. Nonetheless, some heterogeneity remained, which may limit the generalizability of our findings.
Importantly, the protective effect of prolonged IS withdrawal against graft intolerance syndrome was consistently observed across studies.
This study also underscores the lack of multicenter and prospective research on this increasingly relevant topic, as the number of hypersensitized patients with previous graft failures on transplant waiting lists continues to grow.

title: #2839 Relationship between intra-abdominal pressure early after surgery and long-term kidney graft function
authors: Aya Moultamis; Teresa Ronda Serrat; Paula Ardura; Kenia Cobo Campuzano; María Fernández Martín; María Martínez Manrique; Ana Luisa Martins Da Silva; Ana Lucía Valencia Peláez; Pilar Pascual Núñez; Maria Isabel Acosta-Ochoa; Armando Coca Rojo
abstract:
Background and Aims
Kidney transplantation (KT) is the renal replacement therapy of choice for any eligible patients with end-stage renal disease. Due to the ever-growing increase in the allograft demand/supply ratio, it is mandatory to maximize the durability of each organ. Intra-abdominal pressure (IAP) is defined as the steady state pressure concealed within the abdominal cavity. IAP values above 12 mmHg define intra-abdominal hypertension, a condition that has been associated with increased rates of AKI, complications and mortality among the critically ill.
Previously, we described how increased IAP was associated with higher rates of delayed graft function among KT recipients. We now aim to describe the effect of IAP on repeated measures of eGFR over the first 24 months after transplantation.
Method
Single-center prospective cohort study of deceased-donor KTs. Anesthesia, surgical technique and immunosuppression were carried out according to the local protocol in a standardized manner. IAP monitoring was performed according to international guidelines using the urinary bladder technique (UnoMeter Abdo-Pressure kit). IAP values were registered every 8h during the first 72 h after surgery or until reoperation. Mean IAP values during the first 72 h (72 h-IAP) were used in this analysis. The study cohort included 205 kidney transplant recipients, which were subsequently followed for 24 months after transplantation or until death or graft failure. Statistical analysis was performed using IBM SPSS Statistics 26 and R Statistical Software (https://www.r-project.org/foundation, Vienna, Austria).
Results
Demographic and clinical characteristics of the study sample are summarized in Table 1. Multivariable linear mixed model regression analysis fit by restricted maximum likelihood (Table 2) was used to estimate the effects of clinical risk factors, including 72 h-IAP on the evolution of eGFR over time. T-tests were performed using Satterwaite's method. Only 72 h-IAP, delayed graft function and kidney donor profile index were independent predictors of eGFR, while other classic predictors such as recipient age, cold ischemia time or HLA mismatching were not associated with graft function in our sample.
Conclusion
In our sample, patients with higher 72 h-IAP presented significantly lower eGFR during the first 24 months after transplantation. The influence of IAP over graft function was independent of other potential predictors, such as recipient age, delayed graft function or kidney donor profile index. These results highlight the potential of IAP as a predictor for long-term kidney transplant outcomes.
