title: #2119 Chemical reprogramming of macrophages to facilitate renal repair after AKI
authors: Jin Wang; Shuangshuang Liu; Mengyun Wang; Lingting Kong; Yilin Zhang; Linli Lv; Bicheng Liu; Tao-Tao Tang
abstract:
Background and Aims
Macrophages are heterogeneous and play pivotal roles in renal injury and repair, making them prime therapeutic targets for kidney disease. However, their diversity and function in the transition from acute kidney injury (AKI) to chronic kidney disease (CKD) remain poorly understood. Here, we employed single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) to identify key macrophage subpopulations involved in renal repair after AKI. We also explored a chemical approach to reprogram macrophages for AKI recovery.
Method
A mouse model of renal ischemia-reperfusion AKI (IR-AKI) was established. Renal tissue was collected at different time points post-AKI for scRNA-seq analysis. Macrophages were identified and clustered based on gene expression profiles. Gene enrichment analysis and Cellchat were performed for the identification of pro-repair macrophage. Key transcription factors (TFs) were predicted to understand the gene regulatory network of pro-repair macrophages. To induce a pro-repair macrophage phenotype, small molecule compounds targeting key TFs and repair-associated factors were applied to RAW cells in various combinations. The efficacy of these chemical cocktails was evaluated by repair factors levels and transcriptome sequencing analysis. The repair function of chemically reprogrammed macrophages was validated in vitro using co-culture systems with tubular epithelial cells or vascular endothelial cells. Finally, chemical cocktails were administered to AKI mice to reprogram macrophages into a pro-repair functional phenotype to facilitate renal repair.
Results
We identified 2241 macrophages through renal scRNA-seq, which clustered into seven distinct subgroups. title: #1439 Heat acclimation protects against acute kidney injury in mice with heat stroke by inhibiting ferroptosis through activation of mitophagy
authors: Yongwei Song; Wang Ling; Junhui Deng; Huanzi Dai
abstract:
Background and Aims
Exposure to a intense heat stress environment can lead to impaired renal function and even induce acute kidney injury (AKI). Although heat acclimation (HA) is considered the best strategy to prevent heat-related illnesses, the mechanisms underlying its protective effects against heat stroke-induced acute kidney injury (HS-AKI) remain largely unknown. Ferroptosis is a programmed cell death form characterized by excessive accumulation of lipid peroxide and iron, which is involved in the development of multiple AKI and contributes to lung and brain damage induced by heat stroke. However, the role of ferroptosis in the HS-AKI mechanism remains elusive, and whether HA can exert a renal protective effect by reducing ferroptosis still needs further research. Furthermore, In addition, it has been shown that mitophagy can ameliorate cisplatin-induced AKI by inhibiting ferroptosis, but whether this mechanism plays a role in HS-AKI has not been reported as such. To investigate whether heat acclimation alleviates ferroptosis to prevent heat stress-induced acute kidney injury by enhancing mitophagy.
Method
We first established a mouse model of heat stroke and applied proteomics to detect the role of ferroptosis in HS-AKI. Subsequently, we established a mouse model of heat acclimation-pretreatment to clarify the protective effect of heat acclimation on HS-AKI by evaluating the heat tolerance, renal function, renal pathological changes, inflammation and apoptosis levels of mice. Next, we evaluated the levels of ferroptosis and mitophagy in heat acclimation-pretreated mice, and reversely confirmed the mechanism of heat acclimation in HS-AKI with ferroptosis inducers and mitophagy inhibitors.
Results
Performed protein spectrum detection and bioinformatics analysis of renal tissues showed that ferroptosis participated in triggering acute kidney injury in HS. In vivo experiments confirmed that HA significantly improved renal function, enhanced thermal endurance, and improved the survival rate of mice under HS conditions. Moreover, HA significantly enhanced mitophagy and alleviated HS-induced ferroptosis, inflammation, apoptosis. The administration of the ferroptosis inducer RSL3 to HA-pretreated mice confirmed that inducing ferroptosis exacerbates renal inflammation and apoptosis levels, and diminishes the capacity to enhance heat tolerance. Furthermore, the use of the mitochondrial autophagy inhibitor 3-MA in HA-pretreated mice demonstrated that inhibiting mitophagy can counteract the suppressive effect of heat acclimation on ferroptosis, while simultaneously reversing the protective effects of heat acclimation on heat stroke-induced renal inflammation and apoptosis
Conclusion
Heat acclimation can prevent heat stress-induced acute kidney injury by alleviating ferroptosis through enhanced mitophagy.

title: #3555 Pulmonary hypertension and chronic kidney disease: an intergroup variability of kidney function determinants
authors: Maxime Darjinoff; Alexandre Rodière; Christophe Mariat; Laurent Bertoletti; Nicolas Maillard
abstract:
Background and Aims
Chronic kidney disease is recognized as a distinct cause of pulmonary hypertension (group 5), but also as a risk factor for the progression of this disease. The determinants tied to renal function have recently been explored for patients with primary pulmonary hypertension (group 1), but the conditions associated to eGFR remain unknown for other groups (group 2: left heart failure; group 3: chronic pulmonary disease; and group 4: post-embolic pulmonary hypertension). In this study, we aimed at deciphering the variables associated to baseline eGFR in our registry of pulmonary hypertension for each group of this medical condition.
Method
We conducted a retrospective, monocentric, longitudinal cohort including adults patients with pulmonary hypertension assessed by right heart catheterization followed-up in the pulmonary hypertension reference center at the Saint-Étienne University Hospital, who had a serum creatinine value available during their first catheterism. We studied the relationship between renal function at the first visit, as well as various relevant parameters in patients being followed for pulmonary hypertension (e.g. symptoms, clinical signs, biological data, echocardiographic data, right heart catheterization data), stratifying the data according to pulmonary hypertension groups.
Results
We included 320 patients with a median age of 70 years, with an equal proportion of men and women. Our cohort was composed of 43% patients of group 1 pulmonary hypertension, 11% of group 2, 23% of group 3 and 22% of group 4. Average PAPm was 41 mmHg during first right heart catheterism. Median eGFR at baseline was 65.7 [51.9; 85.8] ml/min/1.73 m2 using CKD-EPI 2021 equation. eGFR decline over years was −0.93 [−6.4; 2.7] ml/min/1.73 m2/years during followed up who lasted 2.3 [1.0; 4.9] years.
The baseline eGFR in groups 1 and 2 was strongly associated with NT-proBNP and furosemide dose. Interestingly, eGFR was tightly linked to cardiac output in group 4 (post-embolic) as it was not in other groups. Only group 3 showed a relationship with right atrial pressure. A summary of those correlations is displayed in Table 1.
Considering the eGFR slope, the main determinant in group 1 was the right atrial pressure. In the group 4, the slope was strongly influenced by SvO2, oxygen therapy and 6-minutes walking test.
Conclusion
This study is the largest one aimed at evaluating the determinants of renal function through baseline eGFR and eGFR slope of pulmonary hypertension among different subtypes of the disease. Right congestive variables such as right heart pressure, NT-proBNP and edema showed relationship to kidney function.

title: #509 Neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL) for the assessment of persistent renal dysfunction after acute kidney injury
authors: Yacov Shacham; Shmuel Banai; Shir Frydman
abstract:
Background and Aims
Renal injury is a significant complication in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and is associated with poor outcomes. The recently introduced term acute kidney disease (AKD) describes persistent renal dysfunction lasting 7–90 days post-acute kidney injury (AKI). Neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL), a biomarker for tubular injury, has shown promise in predicting AKI. This study aimed to evaluate NGAL's diagnostic utility for predicting AKD in STEMI patients.
Method
This prospective observational study included 312 patients admitted with STEMI. NGAL levels were measured within 2 hours of admission. AKI and AKD were defined using KDIGO criteria, and patients with chronic inflammation or end-stage renal disease were excluded. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to evaluate NGAL's predictive value for AKD and its optimal value for prediction.
Results
Overall, 64 patients developed AKI (21%), with 30 (47%) progressing to AKD. Patients with AKD had higher admission NGAL levels (median 165 ng/ml) compared to those with resolved AKI (112 ng/ml) or no AKI (88 ng/ml, P < 0.001, Fig. 1). NGAL had a good predictive ability for AKD (area under the ROC of 0.784), with a threshold of >150 ng/ml having 65% sensitivity and 77% specificity for correct prediction (Fig. 2). Multivariate analysis confirmed NGAL >150 ng/ml as an independent predictor of AKD (OR 6.42, 95% CI 3.15–13.09, P < 0.001).
Conclusion
Elevated NGAL levels are independently associated with AKD development in STEMI patients. These findings suggest NGAL could be a valuable biomarker for early risk stratification, supporting timely interventions to mitigate persistent renal injury. Further research is warranted to confirm its clinical utility.

title: #737 Activated HIF-1a accelerates tubular repair in acute kidney injury via cell proliferation
authors: Yoshifumi Kurosaki; Mio Narita; Akemi Imoto; Fumitaka Kawakami; Yoshiko Iizuka; Motoshi Ouchi; Takafumi Ichikawa; Tsuneo Takenaka; Rikke Nielsen; Naohito Ishii
abstract:
Background and Aims
Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a common syndrome in hospitalized patients worldwide and is associated with progression to chronic kidney disease (CKD). Proximal tubule epithelial cells (PTECs) are highly susceptible to injury in AKI resulting in proliferation, which is suggested to be important for tubule recovery and prevention of CKD progression. Roxadustat, a hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF) stabilizer, is a novel drug for the treatment of CKD-related anemia. Some studies have reported the protective effect of Roxadustat on animal AKI models. However, it remains unclear whether Roxadustat induces proliferation and is associated with recovery of renal tubules. Here, we evaluated the effect of Roxadustat on proliferation of PTECs in vitro and in glycerol-induced AKI mice.
Method
Male C57BL/6J mice were randomly divided into four groups (n = 5–11): a control (i) and a glycerol (Gly) (ii) group received intramuscular injections of PBS or 50% glycerol (5 ml/kg) and a PBS+Rox (iii) and a Gly+Rox (iv) group received intraperitoneal injection of Roxadustat 10 mg/kg/day 2 days prior to glycerol or PBS injection. Urine, kidneys, and blood samples were collected 2 days after glycerol injection and renal dysfunction was evaluated (serum urea nitrogen and creatinine) as well as tubular damage (PAS staining, renal NGAL and Kim-1 expression, and urine NGAL excretion). Renal expression of PCNA, a proliferation marker, was determined by western blotting and immunohistochemistry. PTECs proliferation was analyzed in immortalized proximal tubular cells (RPTEC/TERT1, ATCC) treated with roxadustat by a CCK-8 assay, a wound-healing assay, and western blotting (Ki-67, cyclin A, and phosphorylated Rb).
Results
Roxadustat treatment significantly suppressed AKI markers (renal NGAL and Kim-1 expression and urine NGAL excretion) and tubular injury score (PAS staining) in glycerol-injected AKI mice. Additionally, Roxadustat treatment reduced serum urea nitrogen and creatinine levels in glycerol injected mice suggesting that it protects proximal tubules against injury, which leads to rescue of renal function. To investigate if the renoprotective effect of Roxadustat was mediated by stimulation of proliferation PCNA-positive PTECs were analyzed. Glycerol injected mice had an increase in PCNA positive cells compared to PBS treated mice as expected. The Gly+Rox group had the same level of PCNA positive PTEC cells as the Gly group despite less renal damage. These results indicate that there may be either a direct proliferative effect of Roxadustat or that the treatment by other mechanisms protect the kidney resulting in less proliferation. To investigate if there is a direct effect of Roxadustat on proliferation we analyzed Roxadustat treatment in RPTEC/TERT1 cells. Roxadustat treatment significantly induced the increase in HIF-1α protein in RPTEC/TERT1 cells. CCK-8 and wound-healing assays revealed that Roxadustat-treated cells showed significant increase in cell proliferation, which was supported by western blotting of Ki-67, cyclin A, and phosphorylated Rb. Furthermore, HIF-1α-knockdown by small interfering RNA tended to suppress the expression of proliferation markers.
Conclusion
The present study indicates that HIF-1α activation by Roxadustat treatment accelerates cell proliferation in PTECs as a part of the protective mechanism of Roxadustat on tubule damage and AKI.

title: #2485 Circular RNA circAASS inhibits renal fibrosis post AKI by modulating mitophagy and mitochondrial biogenesis in tubular epithelial cell
authors: Tongtong MA; Junfeng Hao; Huafeng Liu; Peng Wang
abstract:
Background and Aims
Acute kidney injury (AKI) results from the dysfunction of renal tubular epithelial cells (TECs) and often leads to renal fibrosis. Mitochondrial impairment in TECs is a common feature of different types of AKI, including sepsis-associated kidney injury (SAKI), ischemia/reperfusion-induced AKI (I/R-AKI), and cisplatin-induced AKI (CP-AKI). Both mitochondrial biogenesis and mitophagy are impaired in injured TECs, leading to insufficient removal of damaged mitochondria. Circular RNAs (termed circRNAs) are a unique class of non-coding RNA molecules. Compared to linear non-coding RNAs, circRNAs are covalently closed loop structures, making them resistant to exonucleases and more stable within cells. However, the role of circular RNAs (circRNAs) in regulating mitochondrial homeostasis during AKI and the resulting renal fibrosis is still not well understood. This study investigates the expression and functional role of circAASS in three distinct models of AKI: SAKI, I/R-AKI, and CP-AKI.
Method
We performed circRNA profiling with high throughput RNA sequencing using renal cortex from mice suffered with SAKI or I/R-AKI or CP-AKI. By taking the intersection of the results of these three datasets. circAASS, a circular RNA annotated as hsa_circ_0006919 in circBASE database, was found as a charming candidate. The sequence conservation between human and mouse circAASS was evaluated and the properties of circAASS was further examined in both normal and injured TECs.
To assess the impact of circAASS knockdown, we conducted RNA sequencing on an immortalized TECs cell line, HK2. Next, overexpression or depletion of circAASS was performed in HK2 cells to evaluate the role of circAASS regarding mitochondrial quality control, such as, mitochondrial biogenesis and mitophagy in TECs challenged with LPS treatment or hypoxia reoxygenation (H/R) or cisplatin treatment. To study the mechanisms that circAASS exerted, bioanalysis was conducted to reveal the role of cytoplasmic circAASS, while RNA pull-down followed by mass spectrometry was used to identify the protein interacted with nuclear circAASS. Adeno-associated virus serotype 9 carrying circAASS overexpression plasmid was used to deliver circAASS to the mouse kidney. Renal pathological analysis and blood creatinine measurement were used to evaluate the function of ectopic expression of circAASS in AKI mouse.
Results
circAASS, known as hsa_circ_0006919 in the circBASE database, was found to be decreased in all three datasets. circAASS was abundantly expressed in normal TECs, distributing both in the cytoplasm and the nucleus. Functionally, circAASS reduces apoptosis and pro-fibrotic effects in injured TECs. These effects are caused by hypoxia reoxygenation (H/R) or cisplatin treatment, as circAASS promotes mitochondrial homeostasis. Mechanistically, cytoplasmic circAASS functions as a competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA). It sequesters miR-324-3p, which increases the expression of PINK1, an important regulator of mitophagy. Additionally, nuclear circAASS directly interacts with the PGC-1α protein. This interaction inhibits its degradation through ubiquitin and facilitates post-translational modifications that enhance mitochondrial biogenesis. Restoring circAASS in I/R-AKI or CP-AKI mouse models improves both mitochondrial biogenesis and mitophagy, ameliorating pro-fibrotic effects of TECs, accordingly mitigating renal fibrosis.
Conclusion
In summary, our results indicate that circAASS plays a vital protective role in AKI by regulating mitochondrial homeostasis. This highlights its potential as a therapeutic target for AKI.

title: #1023 Association between baseline serum creatinine/cystatin C (SCr/CYS) ratio and adverse events in patients receiving cisplatin or carboplatin: a prospective cohort study
authors: Jiaxuan Lyu; Si Yuan Khor; Sherley Mejia; Katherine Specht; Tianqi Ouyang; Sachin J Shah; Jennifer Temel; Lesley Inker; Meghan Sise
abstract:
Background and Aims
Large discrepancies between serum creatinine (SCr) and cystatin C (CYS) have been used to identify frailty. title: #381 Conventional amphotericin B versus liposomal amphotericin B: effects of treatment with dapagliflozin on kidney function and hemodynamics
authors: Mariana Moura Nascimento; Desiree Bernardo; Ana Carolina de Bragança; Maria Heloisa Massola Shimizu; Claudia Ramos de Sena; Antonio Carlos Seguro; Rildo Volpini; Daniele Canale
abstract:
Background and Aims
Invasive fungal infections (IFI) are considered a major global public health issue and represent a significant cause of mortality. Amphotericin B (AmB) remains the gold standard for the treatment of IFIs. Despite its effectiveness, AmB is associated with some adverse effects including nephrotoxicity. Dapagliflozin, a selective SGLT2 inhibitor, is a novel antihyperglycemic drug originally developed for the treatment of diabetes mellitus type 2. However, the benefits of dapagliflozin seem to be multifactorial, mediated by a combination of natriuresis, diminished blood and intraglomerular pressure, tubuloglomerular feedback restoration, and reduced inflammation and fibrosis. Thus, the aim of the study was to evaluate whether prophylactic treatment with dapagliflozin mitigates nephrotoxicity induced by different formulations of amphotericin B.
Method
During a 10-day protocol, male Wistar rats received daily intraperitoneal injections (IP) of conventional amphotericin B or liposomal amphotericin B (10 mg/kg/day). The animals received dapagliflozin (1.6 mg/kg/day added to tap water, DAPA) or no treatment (tap water) and six groups were obtained as the following: control (C), received a standard diet; DAPA, received a standard diet and dapagliflozin treatment; c-AmB, received a standard diet + conventional amphotericin B IP; c-AmB+DAPA, received a standard diet + dapagliflozin treatment + conventional amphotericin B IP; l-AmB, received standard diet + liposomal amphotericin B IP; and l-AmB+DAPA, received standard diet + dapagliflozin treatment + liposomal amphotericin B IP. At the end of the protocol we evaluated mean arterial pressure (MAP) and renal blood flow (RBF), calculated renal vascular resistance (RVR) and assessed plasma cystatin C, phosphorus and magnesium. We also determined proteinuria, albuminuria, urinary excretion of phosphorus and magnesium. In addition, we evaluated renal tissue levels of KIM-1 by ELISA, and NPT2 and TRPM6 transporters by immunoblotting techniques. Data are expressed as mean ± SEM.
Results
Treatment with dapagliflozin normalized MAP and renal vasoconstriction, and improved renal function, evidenced by diminished KIM-1 and plasma cystatin C levels in c-AmB group. Furthermore, treatment with dapagliflozin showed lower proteinuria and albuminuria in c-AmB and l-AmB groups. Both formulations of AmB reduced phosphate and magnesium plasma concentration and augmented phosphorus and magnesium urinary excretion. These results were associated with reductions in renal NPT2 and TRPM6. Treatment with dapagliflozin ameliorated plasma phosphate, however, dapagliflozin was unable to improve urinary excretions of phosphorus and magnesium, as well as protein expressions of NPT2 and TRPM6. All results are described in Table 1.
Conclusion
Our results indicate that a liposomal amphotericin regimen combines a reduced toxicity with an increase in antifungal activity compared with conventional AmB. Nevertheless, tubular damage is a well known problem associated with liposomal amphotericin B. Treatment with dapagliflozin improved renal function and hemodynamics parameters in c-AmB group. Drug acquisition costs and the risk of nephrotoxicity are important factors in determining the cost-effectiveness of amphotericin B as empirical therapy in hospitalized patients. Therefore, prophylactic treatment with dapagliflozin and conventional amphotericin B provides an equally efficacious alternative to liposomal amphotericin B regarding nephrotoxicity. title: #962 Kidney involvement in severe Legionnaire's disease in intensive care
authors: Mickaël Bobot; Emile Charruyer; Romain Arrestier; François Arrive; Julien Demiselle; Pierre-François Dequin; Sami Hraiech; Gael Piton; Jean-Pierre Quenot; Jean-Christophe Richard; Noemie Resseguier; Guillaume Voiriot
abstract:
Background and Aims
Legionnaires' disease, caused by L. pneumophila, can cause severe pneumonia that can progress to acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), requiring intensive care. There are also extra-pulmonary complications, particularly renal, the mechanism, characteristics, risk factors and prognosis of which remain poorly described. Here, we describe the prevalence of associated renal involvement in a multicenter cohort of patients admitted to the ICU with severe legionellosis. Secondary objectives include identifying the risk factors associated with the onset of acute kidney injury (AKI) and studying its impact on the severity of Legionnaires' disease and patient prognosis.
Method
Multicenter retrospective cohort study in 39 intensive care centers in France between January 2012 and January 2024. Inclusion criteria were a diagnosis of Legionella pneumonia requiring invasive mechanical ventilation. Exclusion criteria were pre-existing chronic kidney failure. Data were collected from anonymized medical records, covering patient demographics, comorbidities, initial severity data, legionellosis-related data, blood and urine biology data, and follow-up data related to renal impairment.
Results
561 patients were included. The mean age was 61 years, with 73% men. The main comorbidities were smoking, alcohol abuse, obesity and arterial hypertension. Biantibiotherapy was administered in 87% of cases. Patients’ severity was high, with a mean SOFA at D1 of 7.9, 69% severe ARDS and 81% septic shock. The prevalence of AKI was 74% during ICU stay, with 44% requiring renal replacement therapy. Rhabdomyolysis (15%), hematuria (52%) and tubular proteinuria (mean 1.74 g/L) were frequently encountered. Rhabdomyolysis was an independent risk factor for AKI and use of RRT: aOR 3.72 [1.25; 11.02], P = 0.018 and aOR 3.69 [1.74; 7.82], P = 0.001, respectively. Use of EER was associated with significant excess mortality: aOR 2.49 [1.27; 4.87], P = 0.008, pLog-rank <0.001. Renal histology showed predominantly acute tubular necrosis lesions.
Conclusion
The prevalence of AKI appears higher in our population than for ARDS of all causes, with a high frequency of rhabdomyolysis, proteinuria and haematuria, in favour of kidney involvement specific to legionellosis. A history of chronic kidney disease, patients' initial severity and rhabdomyolysis were independently associated with the onset of AKI and the need for RRT. AKI and, especially, recourse to RRT were associated with a significant excess in mortality, whereas anti-legionella bi-antibiotic therapy was a protective factor.

title: #1284 Associations between lymphopenia and the development/recovery of acute kidney injury among patients hospitalized with respiratory virus infections
authors: Dingyi Wang; Guohui Fan; Xin Liu; Feiy Xu
abstract:
Background and Aims
We aimed to investigate the relationship between lymphopenia and acute kidney injury (AKI) in patients hospitalized with respiratory virus infections.
Method
Data were retrospectively collected from electrical medical records of patients hospitalized with severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), influenza or other respiratory virus infections from 2016 to 2023. Serial measurements of serum creatinine (Scr) and lymphocyte counts before AKI were collected. AKI was identified according to the KDIGO (Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes) guideline. Prolonged lymphopenia (<1.1 × 109/L) was defined as continuous lymphopenia lasting for ≥1 day before AKI diagnosis. Multivariable logistic regression models and Cox proportional regression models were conducted to evaluate associations between lymphopenia or blood counts ratios and AKI.
Results
A total of 3104 patients were analyzed, including 1945 infected with SARS-CoV-2, 597 with influenza, and 472 with other respiratory virus infections. AKI incidences were 18.0%, 23.3% and 16.3%, respectively. Scr was significantly negatively correlated with lymphocyte count in SARS-CoV-2 and influenza infections. Multivariable regression showed lymphopenia, especially prolonged lymphopenia, was significantly associated with AKI in all virus groups, especially in influenza. The risk magnitudes of monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR) on admission for AKI varied by different viral infections. Lymphopenia or not was not associated with AKI stages or AKI recovery.
Conclusion
Lymphopenia, especially prolonged lymphopenia, and NLR on admission were risk factors for AKI after respiratory virus infection, with the highest risk observed in influenza patients.

title: #1479 Macrophage TREM2 deficiency attenuates ischemic acute kidney injury
authors: Canlin Yang; Yan Liu; Shijie Yao; Miwen Zhang; Xiao Liang Zhang; Yi Wen
abstract:
Background and Aims
Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a severe syndrome with rapid kidney function decline, increasing the risk of chronic kidney disease (CKD) and end-stage renal disease (ESRD). Macrophages are involved in acute phase of AKI and contribute to AKI-CKD transition, however the mechanisms remain unclear. The triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 (TREM2), a significant regulator within macrophages, has diverse roles in diseases, such as modulating immune responses in neurodegenerative disorders and influencing tumor microenvironments in cancer. While studies have shown TREM2 knockout worsens kidney injury after obstruction or ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI), macrophage-specific TREM2 knockout have protective effects in the late stage of hepatic ischemia/reperfusion, highlighting the complex role of TREM2 in disease pathogenesis. Thus, elucidating the function of TREM2 in macrophages is crucial for understanding the AKI - CKD transition and identifying potential therapeutic targets.
Method
In-vivo and in-vitro experiments were done to study how macrophage TREM2 deficiency affects kidney repair after IRI. In-vivo, macrophage-specific TREM2 knockout (LysM-Cre+ TREM2fl/fl, TREM2 MKO) and wild-type (LysM-Cre− TREM2fl/f, WT) mice were made using CRISPR/Cas9. A unilateral renal IRI mouse model was established. Ischemic kidneys were collected at 1, 3, 7 days after AKI for histopathology, qRT-PCR to analyze kidney injury molecules, and western blot for signaling pathways. In-vitro, Raw264.7 cells had TREM2 expression reduced with lentivirus vectors. Normal and TREM2-knockdown cells were treated with LPS, and qRT-PCR measured inflammatory cytokine levels. Proteomics and RNA sequencing were used to find the underlying molecular mechanisms.
Results
Upon LPS induction in Raw264.7 and TREM2-kd Raw264.7 cells, compared with the normal group, the mRNA level of the inflammatory factor IL-6 was significantly decreased in TREM2-kd Raw264.7 cells (P = 0.0292), and the expression of iNOS in pro-inflammatory M1 macrophages was downregulated (P = 0.0273). In in-vivo experiments, there was no significant difference in the degree of tubular damage shown by renal pathology between MKO and WT mice after 1 and 3 days of IRI, while the renal tubular damage score was significantly lower at 7 days after IRI compared with WT mice. Genes involved in kidney injury in the kidneys demonstrated a similar pattern. Gene expression analysis showed no significant difference in the expression of renal injury-related factors between the two groups after 1 and 3 days of IRI. However, the expression of NGAL (P = 0.0090) and PAI (P = 0.0484) mRNA was down-regulated in the TREM2 MKO group after 7 days of IRI. Examination of apoptosis-related proteins Bax and Bcl2 in the IRI 7-day kidneys of TREM2 MKO and WT groups showed no differences. Proteomics and RNA sequencing analyses are currently underway.
Conclusion
TREM2 deficiency in macrophages promotes renal repair 7 days after renal IRI, which is inconsistent with the results of systemic TREM2 knockout. This discrepancy may be attributed to the differential effects of TREM2 in macrophages compared with other cell types. A comprehensive understanding of the role of macrophage TREM2 in the AKI-CKD transformation is essential. Currently, we are optimizing the IRI 14-day and 28-day models to further explore the role of macrophage TREM2 in this transformation. We anticipate that RNA sequencing and proteomics data will provide insights into how macrophage TREM2 exerts its renoprotective effects.

title: #736 Defective autophagy drives ferroptosis via mitochondrial ROS in diabetic kidney disease
authors: Sho Matsui; Takeshi Yamamoto; Yoshitaka Isaka
abstract:
Background and Aims
Ferroptosis is a regulated form of cell death triggered by excessive lipid peroxidation and plays a crucial role in the pathogenesis of acute kidney injury (AKI). While autophagy has been shown to drive ferroptotic cell death in cancer cells, the relationship between ferroptosis and the pathogenesis of diabetic kidney disease (DKD), a condition characterized by defective autophagy, is not clear. Here, we investigated whether autophagy modulates susceptibility to ferroptosis in proximal tubular epithelial cells (PTECs) under DKD conditions.
Method
We conducted the following investigations: (1) the association of ferroptotic stress and autophagy biomarkers in kidney biopsy samples from patients with DKD , (2) the impact of autophagy on ferroptosis in the context of ischemia-reperfusion (IR) injury toward DKD using ferrostatin-1 (Fer-1) in diabetic mouse models, including streptozotocin-treated type 1 diabetic mice and db/db type 2 diabetic mice, (3) the role of autophagy in ferroptosis in PTECs in vitro, (4) the mechanisms underlying the relationship between autophagy and ferroptosis in PTECs, with a focus on mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS).
Results
First, analysis of human renal biopsy specimens revealed impaired autophagy and lipid peroxide accumulation, as indicated by increased p62 and 4HNE expression respectively, in PTECs of the diabetic group. Notably, 4HNE expression was positively correlated with p62 accumulation in PTECs. Next, we assessed whether the susceptibility to IR-injury was affected by Atg5 deficiency (Atg5F/F; KAP) in non-diabetic and streptozotocin-treated type 1 diabetic mice. We observed that diabetes and dysregulated autophagy synergistically enhanced IR-induced AKI, which was ameliorated by ferrostatin-1 (Fer-1) treatment. These findings suggest that autophagy deficiency drives ferroptosis induced by IR injury. In db/db type 2 diabetic mice, severe tubular injury was observed following IR injury, but this injury was significantly attenuated by Fer-1 treatment. In addition, rapamycin-mediated improvement of autophagy in db/db mice suppressed IR-induced AKI, demonstrating that improved autophagy attenuates ferroptosis in DKD. Using primary PTECs isolated from Atg5 knockout (Atg5KO) mice, ferroptotic cell death and lipid peroxidation were augmented in Atg5KO cells under erastin (a ferroptosis inducer) treatment. Autophagy deficiency in these cells increased mitochondrial ROS and mitochondrial lipid peroxidation. Importantly, ferroptoric cell death was decreased in Atg5KO Rho0 cells (mitochondrial-DNA/RNA depleted cells), indicating that autophagy protects against ferroptosis by decreasing mitochondrial ROS.
Conclusion
Defective autophagy enhances susceptibility to ferroptosis in DKD by promoting mitochondrial ROS generation. These findings suggest that therapeutic strategies aimed at improving autophagy may mitigate ferroptosis-related injury in DKD.

Importantly, ferroptoric cell death was decreased in Atg5KO Rho0 cells (mitochondrial-DNA/RNA depleted cells), indicating that autophagy protects against ferroptosis by decreasing mitochondrial ROS.
Conclusion
Defective autophagy enhances susceptibility to ferroptosis in DKD by promoting mitochondrial ROS generation. These findings suggest that therapeutic strategies aimed at improving autophagy may mitigate ferroptosis-related injury in DKD.

title: #888 TREM2 macrophages ameliorate the transition from acute kidney injury to chronic kidney disease via a PI3K/AKT Signalling Pathway
authors: Yating Zhang; Le Wang; Yufei du; Siweier Luo; Yiming Zhou
abstract:
Background and Aims
Macrophages play a dual role in both contributing to renal injury and fibrosis as well as facilitating tissue repair. Recently, TREM2+ macrophages have been identified as key regulators of tissue inflammation and repair; however, their specific role in the AKI-CKD transition remains unclear. In this study, we investigate the effect of TREM2+ macrophage in AKI-CKD transition and explore the potential of TREM2-overexpression macrophage as therapeutic strategy for this disease.
Method
A unilateral ischemia-reperfusion injury (UIRI) mouse model was employed to study the AKI-CKD transition. Serum, urine, and kidney samples were collected on day 14. Serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen levels were measured by ELISA, while urinary albumin levels were assessed using Coomassie Brilliant Blue (CBB) gel staining. qPCR and Western blotting (WB) were used to evaluate gene and protein expression in kidney samples. Renal histology was assessed through H&E, PAS, Masson's Trichrome, and Sirius Red staining. Bone marrow-derived macrophages from wild-type (WT) and TREM2 knockout mice were isolated and subjected to hypoxia-reoxygenation (HR) treatment. Stable TREM2-overexpression macrophages were utilized to investigate their renal protective effects in the UIRI mice.
Results
In this study, we found that TREM2 macrophages play a strong protective role in the transition from AKI to CKD. The population of TREM2 macrophages was significantly increased in the UIRI-induced AKI-CKD transition mice. Knockout of Trem2 resulted in increased renal inflammation, exacerbated renal injury and fibrosis. In addition, we found that TREM2 expression enhanced macrophage phagocytosis but reduced the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines, resulting in lower levels of tubular cell apoptosis and fibrosis. RNA-seq analysis revealed that these effects of TREM2 were controlled by PI3K/AKT pathway. Notably, the kidney injury and fibrosis in the UIRI mice was effectively attenuated by cell therapy with TREM2-overexpressing macrophages.
Conclusion
Our study demonstrates that TREM2 macrophages play a protective role in the transition of AKI-CKD and targeting TREM2 may be a therapeutic strategy for this disease.

title: #2064 Targeting M2b macrophages by selenium nanomedicine for the treatment of lupus nephritis
authors: Haoran Lv; Hanzhi Liang; Yufei du; Le Wang; Yiming Zhou; Qinghua Liu
abstract:
Background and Aims
Excessive activation of macrophages has been identified as a key contributor to the pathogenesis and progression of lupus nephritis (LN). Development of effective and targeted therapeutic strategies to macrophages remains a significant challenge. In this study, we developed a selenium-based nanoparticle that could selectively target M2b macrophages in LN, with an emphasis on overcoming the limitations associated with traditional selenium formulations.
Method
Primary mouse macrophages were used to evaluate the toxicity, targeting specificity, and immune-modulatory effects of selenium nanoparticles. The effect of selenium nanoparticles on macrophage activation was examined by qPCR and Western blotting. Bulk RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq) was employed to identify the molecular pathways regulated by selenium nanoparticles. Finally, MRL/lpr mice were used to assess the therapeutic potential of selenium nanoparticles in vivo.
Results
Selenium nanoparticles are stable and biocompatible. By conjugating mannose to the nanoparticle surface, we enhanced the selective targeting of M2b macrophages both in vitro and in vivo, with increased retention time in the kidneys of lupus mice. Selenium nanoparticles effectively suppressed macrophage activation, leading to a significant reduction in the expression and secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines and chemokines, including TNF-α, IL-6, and CXCL9. Moreover, selenium nanoparticles attenuated reactive oxygen species (ROS) production and improved mitochondrial function in M2b macrophages, further supporting their potential as modulators of cellular oxidative stress. Mechanistically, selenium nanoparticles regulate M2b macrophage activation via the JAK1/JAK2-STAT1 signaling pathway that was achieved by upregulation of the antioxidant enzyme GPX1. In the lupus nephritis mouse model, selenium nanoparticles significantly improved renal function, preserved renal architecture, and reduced renal fibrosis, likely by inhibiting M2b macrophage-driven inflammatory responses.
Conclusion
In this study, we developed a novel selenium-based nanoparticle capable of selectively targeting and modulating M2b macrophage activation in lupus nephritis. By reducing ROS production and inhibiting the JAK1/JAK2/STAT1 signaling pathway through the upregulation of GPX1, selenium nanoparticles effectively attenuated the pathological progression of LN. Our findings highlight the therapeutic potential of this targeted nanoparticle approach and provide a promising strategy for the treatment of lupus nephritis by selectively modulating immune cell populations involved in disease pathogenesis.

title: #18 Role of roxadustat for prevention of severe contrast-induced acute kidney injury in rats
authors: Zeynep Kendi Celebi; Şevval Tarhan Aydınay; Bahar Akkaya; Hampar Akkaya; Didem Turgut; Damla Ors Sendogan; Metin Aldemir; Turan Çolak
abstract:
Background and Aims
Contrast induced acute kidney injury is third leading cause of acute kidney injury and has many adverse outcomes from prolonged hospitalization to death. Many studies have been conducted with different agents to prevent contrast induced acute kidney injury, but a preventive medication other than hydration and N-acetylcystein has not yet been found, that can be recommended by the guidelines.
Roxadustat (FG-4592) is a novel anti-anemia drug developed for patients with chronic kidney disease, which is a hypoxia-inducible factor stabilizer and induces endogenous erythropoietin production. Studies have shown that roxadustat has anti-inflammatory and anti-ischemic properties and prevents acute kidney injury in some experimental models.
In this study, we aimed to show the effect of roxadustat pretreatment in the prevention of contrast induced acute kidney injury.
Method
Thirty-six Sprague-Dawley rats were splitted to six groups at random; control group (1), roxadustat group (5 mg/kg (2) and 10 mg/kg (3)), contrast media group (4) and contrast media after roxadustat group (5 mg/kg (5) and 10 mg/kg (6)) were compared for the development of contrast induced acute kidney injury. After 3 days of pretest acclimatization rats received 5 and 10 mg/kg roxadustat intraperitoneally (group 2, 3, 5, 6). 5th day of the study contrast media was injected 15 ml/kg intravenously to the rats (group 4, 5, 6) Nephrectomy specimens were examined by two pathologists, with PAS for tubular changes, with Masson Trichrome for fibrosis, for HIF 1-alpha, CD73 and AIM2 for the activity and effect of roxadustat and caspase-3 for apoptosis. Blood specimens were obtained for hemoglobin, BUN and creatinine at 3rd and 7th day.
Results
BUN, creatinine, hemoglobin and platelet levels did not differ between groups at baseline an at 7 day. Although contrast induced acute kidney injury could not be demonstrated biochemically, histopathological findings of tubular damage of varying severity were observed in the rat groups receiving contrast. In groups 5 and 6, mild damage findings were observed more frequently compared to group 4, while no severe damage findings were observed. A dose-dependent increase in HIF1-alpha staining was observed in rats administered roxadustat. Mild HIF1-alpha staining was also observed in Group 4. Contrast media administration increased apoptosis which shown with caspase3 staining, but roxadustat administration decreased the frequency and severity of apoptosis in a dose-dependent manner. No difference was observed between the groups in AIM2 and CD73 staining.
Conclusion
Pretreatment with roxadustat resulted histopathologically less severe and less frequent contrast induced acute kidney injury in rats. HIF1-alpha increased with roxadustat administration, but the protection occurs other than AIM2/CD73 pathways, which protects kidney cells from ischemic injury.

title: #2068 Longer time on polymyxin-B direct hemoperfusion for sepsis control prevents kidney injury on day 28; a multicenter retrospective observational study (PMX-OPTIC)
authors: Hiroo Kawarazaki; Ryuta Nagamine; Kensuke Nakamura; Katsunori Mochizuki; Chizuru Yamashita
abstract:
Background and Aims
Evidence on polymyxin-B direct hemoperfusion (PMX-DHP) during septic shock is controversial. Kidney function is frequently impaired in septic shock and high mortality rates are reported in acute kidney injury. There is scarce data on the effects of PMX-DHP regarding kidney protection. In this study, we intended to clarify the impact of time on PMX-DHP and improvement in kidney function.
Method
This multicenter retrospective observational study (PMX-OPTIC study) gathered data from 24 ICUs in Japan. Each center registered 20 most recent consecutive cases of septic shock treated with PMX-DHP during 1/1/2015 to 31/12/2021. The dataset involved time on PMX-DHP only for the first session, so cases administered two or more sessions had to be excluded. We also excluded cases that died before day 28, and cases that were already on maintenance dialysis. The comparison was between long (PMX-L) versus short (PMX-S) time on PMX-DHP, divided by the median. The outcome (ΔeGFR) was the increase in eGFR on day 28 or discharge (post-eGFR) compared to the start of PMX-DHP (pre-eGFR). Since those cases with minimal kidney injury were prone to have no improvement in kidney function, we analyzed the relation for tertile sub-groups of pre-eGFR (eGFR-H, -M, -L). Continuous variables were expressed as medians with interquartile ranges. Multi-linear regression analysis was performed for relation between ΔeGFR and PMX-DHP duration time (PMX-L or -S) for the following three models: Model 1 was adjusted for age, sex, BMI. Model 2 was additionally adjusted for APACHE II scores and use of hemodialysis. Model 3 additionally accounted for infection focus, confirmation of gram-negative rods (GNR) in blood culture, and comorbidities.
Results
The initial data contained 480 cases of which 146 cases were enrolled after exclusion. The enrolled population was 75.0 (68, 80) years old, 61% male, and BMI 21.5 (18.5, 24.6) m2/kg. APACHE II score was 26.0 (20, 29), the major infection focus was gastrointestinal (66.4%), GNR in blood cultures dominated 42.7%, frequent comorbidities were malignant tumor (26.0%), diabetes mellitus (24.7%) and cardiac failure (21.2%). 56.9% received surgical interventions and 68.5% received hemodialysis together with PMX-DHP. Median time on PMX-DHP was 4.1(2, 14.2) hours and pre-eGFR was 33.7 (22.0, 53.1) ml/min/1.73 m2. The correlation between PMX-L and ΔeGFR in the eGFR-H and M subgroups were unremarkable through Models 1 to 3 (P > 0.05). However, in the eGFR-L group (eGFR <23.5 ml/min/1.73 m2), PMX-L demonstrated a significantly higher ΔeGFR in Models 1 to 3. The βcoefficient (p-values) in Model 1, 2, and 3 were as follows; 10.2 (0.042), 10.8 (0.022), 14.1 (0.048), respectively. Limitations are the exclusion of PMX-DHP cases that received two or more sessions of PMX-DHP, the small number of cases, and possible residual confounding due to the nature of the observational study.
Conclusion
Longer time on PMX-DHP for septic shock may improve kidney function in those with low eGFR.

title: #492 Depot-specific metabolic and thermogenic profiles in perirenal and renal sinus adipose tissue
authors: Maria J Pereira; Iris Argyri Mathioudaki; Amir Sedigh; Jan W Eriksson; Maria K Svensson
abstract:
Background and Aims
Kidney-associated adipose tissue depots, i.e., renal sinus (RSAT) and perirenal adipose tissue (PRAT), may contribute to metabolic, cardiovascular and chronic kidney diseases linked to obesity. The aim of this study was to characterize PRAT compared to RSAT and omental adipose tissue (OAT) by adipocyte size, glucose uptake, transcriptomics and immune cell fractions in healthy individuals.
Method
Adipose tissue biopsies were collected from healthy kidney donors (20 female, 20 male). Adipocyte glucose uptake and size were measured in isolated adipocytes. Transcriptomic profiling and immune cell composition estimates (RNA seq data), were performed to evaluate differences between PRAT and RSAT, using OAT as a benchmark.
Results
PRAT exhibited significantly larger adipocytes and higher insulin-stimulated glucose uptake than RSAT. 1113 significant differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified (PRAT: 571 down- and 542 upregulated) with enrichment of thermogenic and metabolic genes (UCP1, CIDEA, and CKMT1B) in PRAT and inflammation-related genes (NFKBIA, BIRC3, and IRF1) in RSAT. Pathway analysis highlighted activation of metabolic processes, including the TCA cycle and oxidative phosphorylation in PRAT contrasting to immune and inflammatory pathways in RSAT and OAT (see Fig. 1A–D). Immune cells gene signatures the depots: PRAT displayed an anti-inflammatory environment with transcripts associated with eosinophils and activated NK cells, whereas RSAT exhibited a pro-inflammatory profile associated with M0 macrophages.
Conclusion
Kidney-associated adipose tissue depots PRAT and RSAT exhibit distinct profiles. PRAT shows thermogenic and anti-inflammatory characteristics suggesting a protective metabolic role. RSAT inflammatory profile, more closely resembling OAT, may impact metabolic, cardiovascular and chronic kidney diseases. These findings highlight the heterogeneity of kidney-associated adipose tissue depots.

title: #2898 Treatment outcomes of liver cyst infection in patients with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease
authors: Charles Ronsin; François Jouret; Simon Ville; Bertrand Knebelmann; Julien Dang
abstract:
Background and Aims
Liver cyst infection (LCI) is a rare and severe complication of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD), and evidence-based data for optimal management is lacking.
Method
We conducted a multicentric retrospective study (from 2012 to 2024) to investigate the treatment and outcomes of LCI. LCI was either defined by (i) C-reactive protein levels ≥50 mg/L and suspicion at computed tomography scan, 18Fluorodeoxyglucose (18FDG) positron-emission tomography computed tomography (PET/CT), magnetic resonance imaging, or (ii) proven by cyst puncture. We studied the determinants of treatment failure (persistent infection with requirement for antibiotic therapy (ATBT) change, cyst drainage, hepatectomy), relapse (<2 months) and recurrence (>2 months) of LCI after ATBT discontinuation, using multivariate analysis.
Results
Sixty-two patients and 112 episodes were included. At least one microorganism was identified in 70/112 (63%) episodes, mainly Escherichia coli in 36/70 (51%) of cases. E. coli was resistant to 3rd generation cephalosporin, fluoroquinolone or cotrimoxazole in 13%, 16% and 34%, respectively. Treatment failure and relapse occurred in 30/112 (27%) episodes, including 5 episodes requiring cyst drainage and 1 episode requiring partial hepatectomy. Risk factors for treatment failure/relapses included an ATBT duration <14 days (OR = 39, IC 95% [3.56;427], P = 0.002) and a WBC count >15.000/mm3 (OR =13, IC 95% [2.27; 74.50], P = 0.003). When treatment failure and relapses were analyzed separately, WBC >15.000/mm3 was a risk factor for treatment failure (OR = 9.2, IC 95% [1.68; 50.42], P = 0.009) and ATBT duration <14 days was a risk factor for relapses (OR = 25, IC 95% [3.38; 192.33], P = 0.001). Recurrence occurred in 24/62 (38%) patients, within 1 year for 15 (24%) after the 1st episode. ATBT duration <28 days (OR = 9.22, IC 95% [2.19; 50.08], P = 0.04) and history of renal cyst infection (OR = 5.90, IC 95% [1.11; 37.74], P = 0.04) increased the risk of recurrence <1 year. Follow-up 18FDG-PET/CT was performed in 19 episodes within 64 [54–95] days post LCI diagnosis. Among them, 17 were followed at least 1 year after follow-up 18FDG-PET/CT: 6/8 (75%) and 3/9 (33%) patients with and without persistent liver cyst uptake, respectively, had relapse or recurrent LCI <1 year (P = 0.15). Neither fluoroquinolone nor dual ATBT reduced the risk of treatment failure/relapse or recurrence. No death was attributed to LCI.
Conclusion
Treatment failure/relapse or recurrence of LCI both occurred in one-third of cases, and are associated with a shorter ATBT duration <28 days.

authors: Julia Münster; Carolin Brigl; Constantin Aaron Wolff; Marco Klose; Kai-Uwe Eckardt; Ria Anne-Rose Schönauer; Jan Halbritter
abstract:
Background and Aims
Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) is one of the most common hereditary diseases, characterized by the progressive growth of renal cysts leading to chronic kidney disease and kidney failure [1]. Despite tremendous research efforts, with Tolvaptan, only one licensed medication is currently available for the treatment of ADPKD [2]. Tolvaptan is a vasopressin V2 receptor antagonist that has been shown to reduce the rate of renal cyst growth and preserve kidney function in ADPKD patients with rapid progression [2]. However, its long-term efficacy and tolerability in patients remain areas of active research. This study aims to evaluate the efficacy of Tolvaptan on kidney function, cyst growth and disease progression in patients with ADPKD, assessing a cohort of ADPKD patients who have received Tolvaptan as part of their treatment. Furthermore, we are seeking to identify responders and non-responders to Tolvaptan treatment and characterize differences between both groups.
Method
We are conducting this trial as a retrospective, observational, single-center study at the Charité Berlin. A total of 109 adult patients diagnosed with rapidly progressing ADPKD under Tolvaptan treatment for a minimum of 12 months were included. Participants laboratories, genetic diagnoses, and imaging records were acquired from as early as 2007 to assess disease progression before, during and after Tolvaptan treatment.
Results
The study cohort consists of 109 individuals with a mean age of 45 years and a sex distribution of (F:M) 43:66 (Fig. 1). In 76 of the 109 cases, a genetic diagnosis was obtained, showing that 80.2% of the genetically tested patients has a pathogenic variant in the PKD1 gene, further divided into 46 patients with a truncating and 15 patients with a non-truncating variant. Another 15.8% showed a pathogenic variant in PKD2, while 4% were diagnosed with a disease-causing variant in other genes, such as ALG9. The mean time of Tolvaptan intake was 44 months with 66 individuals (60.5%) still receiving Tolvaptan (Fig. 2). 22 patients (20.2%) had reached kidney failure at a mean age of 48 years which therefore resulted in ending their Tolvaptan treatment, while another 21 patients (19.3%) had to end their treatment due to side effects and drug intolerance (Fig. 1). The mean eGFR at the start of Tolvaptan treatment was 68 ml/min per 1.73 m2 (n = 107), with a difference observed between male and female patients (Male: 66 ml/min per 1.73 m2 vs. Female: 72 ml/min per 1.73 m2).
Conclusion
In a representative population of ADPKD patients taking Tolvaptan, we found that the majority (61%) tolerated the drug well over a mean period of 44 months. However, a substantial proportion of patients (39%) were unable to continue Tolvaptan long-term due to either kidney failure (20%) or drug intolerance (19%). As a next step, single patient eGFR-slopes and longitudinal imaging (delta TKV) will allow us to retrospectively divide patients into responders and non-responders to Tolvaptan treatment and enable identification of distinct traits. We believe that our project will contribute to further refine disease prognostication and improve the selection of patients that actually benefit from Tolvaptan treatment in a real-world scenario.

title: #2475 Angiotensin II induces mitochondrial oxidative stress in podocyte
authors: Tae-Sun Ha
abstract:
Background and Aims
Angiotensin II induces glomerular and podocyte injury via systemic and local vasoconstrictive or non-hemodynamic effects including oxidative stress. The release of reactive oxygen species (ROS) from podocytes may participate in the development of glomerular injury and proteinuria. We studied the roles of oxidative stress in angiotensin II-induced podocyte injury.
Method
Mouse podocytes were incubated in media containing various concentrations of angiotensin II and at different incubation times and transfected by Nox4 or negative control scrambled siRNA for 24 h. The changes of the intracellular and mitochondrial ROS production were measured using respective assays and observed by confocal imaging and western blotting according to the presence of angiotensin II.
Results
Angiotensin II increased NADH/NADPH oxidase 4 protein and expression in a transcriptional mechanism that was also reversed by probucol. In addition, the suppression of NADH/NADPH oxidase 4 by siRNA reduced the oxidative stress induced by angiotensin II. Angiotensin II also significantly increased the generation of superoxide anions and suppressed the superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity that were significantly recovered with probucol. Furthermore, angiotensin II increased the intracellular ROS levels in dose- and time-dependent manners that were also recovered with probucol.
The quantitative data of MitoSOX index demonstrated that mitochondrial superoxide production was significantly higher in angiotensin II -treated condition compared with that in untreated conditions with or without probucol at 24 h. When angiotensin II increased mitochondrial superoxide production by more than 2-fold, it was significantly recovered with probucol. We also found that cytoplasmic 8-oxo-dG immunoreactivity was significantly increased in angiotensin II -treated condition by 2-fold compared with that in untreated conditions with or without probucol at 24 h that was significantly recovered with probucol.
Conclusion
Our findings suggest that angiotensin II increased the generation of mitochondrial superoxide anions and ROS levels via the downregulation of the SOD activity and via the upregulation of NADH/NADPH oxidase 4 that were reversed by an antioxidant, probucol.

title: #468 Regulation of renal fibrosis via the RAGE pathway by miR-214 and host ncRNA in diabetic kidney disease
authors: Shinji Hagiwara; Jun Okabe; Maki Murakoshi; Hiroko Sakuma; Tomohito Gohda; Yusuke Suzuki; Mark Cooper; Phillip Kantharidis
abstract:
Background and Aims
Activation of the receptor for advanced glycation end-products (RAGE) and non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) contribute to the progression of diabetic kidney disease (DKD). However, the role of ncRNAs in the RAGE signaling pathway remains unclear. The aim of this study is to elucidate the role of ncRNAs in the context of RAGE signaling and its involvement in diabetic kidney disease DKD.
Method
Mesangial cells (MCs) derived from RAGE knockout (KO) and wild-type (WT) mice were cultured under high-glucose conditions to evaluate the expression of micro RNAs (miRs), ncRNAs, fibrosis, and inflammatory markers. Additionally, the effects of miR-214 administration on renal fibrosis were analyzed in a mouse model of DKD.
Results
The expression levels of miR-214 and the host ncRNA Dnm3os were significantly increased in RAGE KO MCs compared to WT MCs. Overexpression of miR-214 in MCs resulted in reduced fibrotic gene expression, while overexpression of Dnm3os increased fibrotic gene expression. DIAPH1, a RAGE adaptor molecule, was identified as a target gene of miR-214. Furthermore, a binding site between Dnm3os and Diaph1, distinct from the binding site of miR-214, was proposed, and in situ hybridization confirmed co-localization of Dnm3os and Diaph1 within the nucleus. Furthermore, administration of miR-214 to a mouse model of DKD demonstrated potent anti-fibrotic effects in renal tissues.
Conclusion
We show a novel mechanism involving miR-214 and Dnm3os as negative and positive regulators of fibrosis through the RAGE-DIAPH1 axis. The protective effects of miR-214 highlight its potential as a novel therapeutic agent for DKD.

title: #3011 Genetic testing in chronic kidney disease: clinical and genetic insights into autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease in a Chinese Cohort
authors: Kaiyue Wang; Lei Zhang; Peili Ji; Xiaoxiao Shi; Gang Chen; Yan Liu; Hua Zheng; Hang Li; Wei Ye; Peng Xia; Limeng Chen
abstract:
Background and Aims
Monogenetic diseases such as autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease (ADTKD), a rare but severe hereditary disorder, exemplify the diagnostic challenge due to its non-specific manifestations. This study aims to evaluate the utility of genetic testing in CKD patients and characterize features of ADTKD.
Method
We conducted genetic analyses on 171 individuals from 153 families with suspected hereditary kidney diseases (April 2022–August 2024). Inclusion criteria encompassed early-onset CKD, familial aggregation, extrarenal phenotypes, or unexplained CKD. Genetic diagnosis utilized Sanger sequencing, next-generation sequencing, and copy number variation (CNV) analysis following ACMG guidelines.
Results
The predominant phenotypes were hypokalemic tubulopathies with Gitelman syndrome (26.9%) and cystic nephropathies (14.0%). Diagnostic variants were identified in 79.1% of cases across 104 genes, primarily in SLC12A3 (12.9%) and PKD1 (9.3%).
The 17 ADTKD probands (10 females) included ADTKD-UMOD (n = 13), ADTKD-HNF1B (n = 2), ADTKD-REN (n = 1), and ADTKD-MUC1 (n = 1). Of the 16 identified genetic variants, there were 14 missense mutations, one frameshift deletion, and one CNV, including six novel UMOD variants. Most UMOD mutations were missense variants affecting EGF-like domains, D10C domain, and beta-hairpin region.
At diagnosis, patients presented with a mean age of 31.9 ± 8.1 years and eGFR of 57.9 ± 20.8 ml/min/1.73 m2, along with hyperuricemia (85%), renal cysts (54%), proteinuria (33%), and hypertension (31%). UMOD-subtype patients (n = 11) exhibited markedly elevated uric acid levels (mean 510.5 ± 156.1 μmol/L), with concurrent gout (36%) and urolithiasis (18%). Renal biopsies (n = 5) uniformly demonstrated chronic tubulointerstitial nephritis without typical features. Normalized uricemia was observed in 45% of patients following the urate-lowering intervention. During follow-up, two patients progressed to end-stage kidney disease at ages 40 and 61, while others showed a mean annual eGFR decline of 4.0 (0.25, 7) ml/min/1.73 m2.
Conclusion
This study highlights the high diagnostic yield of genetic testing in adult CKD patients by well-defined genetic testing criteria and optimizes resource allocation, which provides crucial insights for CKD management and prognostication.

title: #3031 Tailored kidney stone prevention improves metabolic risk factors and urinary crystallization risk indices and reduces renal colic and urological intervention rates
authors: Els Van De Perre; Florine Janssens; Dieter De Clerck; Wilfried Cools; Dominique Bazin; Christian Tielemans; Michel Daudon; Emmanuel Letavernier; Karl Martin Wissing
abstract:
Background and Aims
There is limited real-world data on the efficacy of combined prophylactic measures to prevent recurrent kidney stone formation.
Method
This single centre retrospective study evaluates the effect of combined, patient-tailored preventive measures on metabolic risk factors for kidney stone formation, urinary crystallization risk indices and renal colic and urological intervention rates in a real-life clinical setting.
Results
512 nephrolithiasis patients with a median follow-up of 13 months were evaluated. After prophylaxis introduction, the main metabolic risk factors urinary volume and urinary oxalate, calcium and citrate excretion improved significantly in patients presenting the specific risk factor at baseline (+666 ml/24 h for urinary volume, −11.1 mg/24 h for oxaluria, −2.35 mmol/24 h for calciuria and +881 μmol/24 h for citraturia, all P < 0.0001). Urinary volume and calciuria also improved in the total study population (+323 ml/24 h and
−0.47 mmol/24 h for urinary volume and calciuria respectively, both P < 0.0001). Relative urinary calcium oxalate supersaturation and Tiselius risk index improved significantly in the total study population (−1.64 and −0.33 respectively, both P < 0.0001). Finally, renal colic and urological intervention rates improved significantly (from 0.98 (95% CI 0.92 to 1.05)/1000 days at risk to 0.21 (95% CI 0.16 to 0.29)/1000 days at risk, P < 0.0001 for renal colic rate and from 0.31 (95% CI 0.27 to 0.35)/1000 days at risk to 0.25 (95% CI 0.19 to 0.33)/1000 days at risk, P < 0.0001 for urological intervention rate). The degree of control of the combination of the four main metabolic risk factors was significantly associated with a reduction of renal colic rate during follow-up.
Conclusion
Combined prophylaxis significantly improves metabolic risk factors and urinary crystallization risk indices resulting in a significant reduction of renal colic and urological intervention rates. Kidney stone formers should be treated by tailored prophylactic measures at a specialised kidney stone prevention clinic.

title: #3347 Renal magnesium handling in mouse model of Fanconi–Bickel syndrome
authors: Antonella Iannaccone; Antonio Miele; Iris Iuliano; Anna Iervolino; Yoko Suzumoto; Luciano D'apolito; Giovambattista Capasso; Francesco Trepiccione
abstract:
Background and Aims
Kidney plays a central role on the homeostasis of magnesium. The thick ascending limb (TAL) uptakes 40%–70% of Mg2+ via claudin-16 and claudin-19 complex, id the major segment for renal magnesium absorption. The DCT, reabsorb about 5% of the filtered Mg2+, but is the main regulatory site for serum Mg2+ concentration. The proximal tubule of the nephron reabsorbs approximately 10-20% of filtered amount of Mg2+ likely mediated by tight-junction proteins claudin-2 and claudin-12 driven by Na+/H+ exchanger 3 (NHE3)-mediated Na+ reabsorption. We have recently generated and characterized a mouse model with kidney-specific ablation of GLUT2 (Glut2Pax8Cre +), which recapitulate the renal phenotype of Glycogen storage disease XI, also known as Fanconi–Bickel syndrome. In the current study, we aimed at investigating the Mg2+ homeostasis in Glut2Pax8Cre + mice to unveil the molecular mechanisms on renal Mg handling associated with glycogen accumulation in PT and the effect of the SGLT2-inhibitors on renal Mg2+ handling.
Method
Urine samples were collected from male control mice (Glut2lox/lox; Pax8Cre/−) and GLUT2 cko (Glut2Pax8Cre +) mice with or without treatment with Dapaglifozin (DAPA) to evaluate the Mg2+ levels. Kidney tissues from control and cko mice were utilized for RNA extraction to perform RT-PCR analyses on CLDN16, CLDN19, TRPM6, TRPM7, SLC41A1, and CNNM2. To verify the expression of Claudin 16, immunofluorescence was performed on kidney tissues.
Results
Glut2 cKO mice exhibit a larger urinary Mg2+ loss compared to control mice. RT-PCR revealed that mRNA expression of CLDN16 were significantly increased in Glut2 cKO mice compared to controls. Immunofluorescence on renal tissues from ctr and Glut2 cKO mice further confirmed a similar localization of CLDN16 on the TAL. In addition, the Mg2+ transporters TRPM6 and TRPM7 expressed along the DCT did not present significant in mRNA abundance between the two groups. Since we have previously demonstrated that the treatment with dapagliflozin, a SGLT2-inhibitor, is able to rescue the phenotype of Glut2 cKO mice regarding, metabolic acidosis, albuminuria, phosphaturia and glycogen accumulation. We tested whether dapagliflozin could limit urinary Mg2+ loss in these mice. Dapagliflozin, effectively restored urinary Mg2+ loss at the control level.
Conclusion
Glut2 cKO mice could serve as a valid model to investigate the mechanisms behind the ability of SGLT2-inhibitors of increasing serum Mg2+ concentration. Here by showing an effect on magnesium excretion of dapagliflozin we could hypothesize that the SGLT2-inhibitors could act directly on proximal tubule Mg2+ transport. However, additional experiments are required to further elucidate the molecular mechanism.

title: #3348 Metabolic reprogramming and profibrotic behavior characterize tubular epithelial cells in Bardet–Biedl syndrome
authors: Antonio Villanova; Yoko Suzumoto; Giovambattista Capasso; Miriam Zacchia
abstract:
Background and Aims
Renal fibrosis is the final common pathway to all chronic kidney diseases (CKD), suggesting that in any context of kidney injury a biological switch leading to loss of epithelial functions and connective tissue expansion occur. Multiple line of evidence suggest that renal epithelial metabolic abnormalities precedes profibrotic behavior and predisposes to kidney damage. The present study analyzes the pathogenesis of kidney disfunction in the setting of Bardet–Biedl syndrome (BBS), a rare genetic disorder that is part of the ciliopathies group. BBS is characterized by a variety of clinical manifestations, including tubulointerstitial kidney disease. Our previous studies in inner medullary collecting duct (IMCD3) cells, where the Bbs10 gene has been deleted (IMCD3-Bbs10-/- cells), have demonstrated that BBS10 plays a critical role in mitochondrial function, glucose and lipid homeostasis. Moreover, IMCD3 Bbs10-/- cells exhibit altered cell proliferation. This study focuses on investigating the mechanism of mitochondrial dysfunction and cell proliferation in this context, to elucidate the mechanism of kidney disease in BBS and identify potential therapeutic targets.
Method
The generation of a stable Bbs10 gene knockout inner medullar collecting duct cell line was obtained with CRISPR/Cas9 technology (IMCD3-Bbs10-/- cells). Expression levels of key proteins involved in mitochondrial function, fibrosis, and cellular signaling such as, α-SMA, p70 s6 kinase, PI3 Kinase p85 and PINK1 were assessed through immunoblotting.
Results
We previously showed that BBS10 interacts in vitro with BAG2, which is known to stabilize PINK1 from proteasomal degradation. In IMCD3 Bbs10-/- cells we found reduced PINK1 expression, further suggesting impaired mitochondrial quality control due to defective Pink1-Parkin signaling. Additionally, both p70 s6 kinase and PI3 Kinase p85 levels were reduced in knockout cells, suggesting aberrant mTOR signaling. Moreover, IMCD3 Bbs10-/- cells showed increased α-SMA protein levels, indicating epithelial-mesenchymal transition.
Conclusion
This study highlights the presence of mitochondrial and metabolic abnormalities in renal epithelial cells in a model of BBS. The downregulation of PINK1 and disrupted Parkin signaling point to mitochondrial dysfunction, a key factor in cellular stress and kidney pathology. The observed downregulation of p70 s6 kinase and PI3 Kinase p85 suggests impaired mTOR signaling, which could impact cell metabolism and stress responses. Finally, increased α-SMA suggests a propensity to fibrosis. Further investigations are required to better understand the role of BBS10 in kidney disease and to identify potential therapeutic strategies for managing renal complications in BBS patients.

We previously showed that BBS10 interacts in vitro with BAG2, which is known to stabilize PINK1 from proteasomal degradation. title: #173 Description of a familial renal ApoCII amyloidosis associated with a p.Lys41Thr mutation
authors: Diane Marcoux; Thien Anh Ho; Lucie Bienfait; Frederic Bilan; Alexia Rinsant; Oumayma Hachani; Serge Treille de Grandsaigne; Frank Bridoux
abstract:
Background and Aims
Nasr et al. recently published the first series of 25 patients with hereditary renal apolipoprotein C-II amyloidosis (AApoCII). Twelve of them carried a APOC2(NM_000483.5):c.122A>C/p.(Lys41Thr) variant but only 3 had a family history of chronic kidney disease. We here describe the clinical presentation and outcome of a family including 3 siblings with hereditary renal ApoCII amyloidosis.
Method
The proband's kidney biopsy was analyzed by light microscopy with Congo red staining, immunofluorescence using an anti-ApoC2 conjugate (Abcam, Cambridge UK) and tandem mass spectrometry after laser microdissection. Exome sequencing was performed using Sureselect Human All exon V8 (Agilent technologies). We prepared libraries from 50 ng genomic DNA using Magnis Sureselect XT HS2 DNA reagent kit according to the manufacturer's protocol. DNA sequencing was conducted on a NextSeq2000 (flowcell P3, 2 × 150 bp reads). Variant calling and annotations was obtained by an in-house bio-informatic pipeline dedicated to routine molecular diagnosis.
Results
We describe a Belgian family of Sicilian origin without history of consanguinity. The parents immigrated from Italy in the sixties with their 6 children (Fig. 1). The mother died at age 80 without any chronic condition and the father at the age of 40 from a gunshot.
In 2005, patient II.4. (Fig. 1), aged 55 years, was referred to the nephrology department with a serum creatinine of 2.19 mg/dl and albuminuria of 2.2 g/24 h. A kidney biopsy showed diffuse glomerular amyloid deposits, which nature was not identified. His renal function slowly deteriorated, and he was started on chronic hemodialysis in 2013. He later died at home in January 2017.
In 2013, patient II.1., aged 68 years (Fig. 1) consulted with a serum creatinine of 1.9 mg/dl and proteinuria of 0.45 g/24 h. Her serum creatinine level raised from April 2012 (1.18 mg/dl) to October 2012 (1.57 mg/dl) and then stabilized until 2016 when a kidney biopsy was performed because of albuminuria of 1.6 g/24 h. Pathological studies showed renal glomerular and vascular amyloidosis, again without typing. She has been established on chronic hemodialysis since 2020.
In 2023, the proband (patient II.5.) (Fig. 1), aged 70 years, was referred for rapid increase in serum creatinine level (rising from 1.3md/dl in July 2022 to 1.7 mg/dl in August 2023 and 2.1 mg/dl in September 2023. Unlike his siblings, his albuminuria level was low (115.2 mg/g of creatinine. A kidney biopsy displayed diffuse glomerular amyloidosis. A fat pad and minor salivary gland biopsy were negative as extensive clinical workup (including cardiac evaluation) for other organ involvement. Renal parameters remained stable with serum creatinine of 2 mg/dl and albuminuria at 160 mg/g. Mass spectrometry analysis of the kidney biopsy identified high spectral counts for ApoCII, and immunofluorescence study confirmed glomerular staining for ApoCII. An exome sequencing revealed the presence of the p.Lys41Thr variant. Genetic testing in other family members is planned.
Conclusion
AApoCII associated with a p.Lys41Thr mutation is a rare form of renal limited autosomal dominant hereditary amyloidosis that manifests with progressive kidney disease and proteinuria. Combining mass spectrometry analysis of kidney biopsies with exome sequencing is a valuable strategy to rapidly establish the diagnosis of renal hereditary amyloidoses.

title: #825 Genotypic and phenotypic characteristics of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease in patients without a positive family history
authors: Tsielestina Poulli; Maria Konsta; Maria Varveri; Danai Palaiologou; Eirini Evangelou; Angeliki Poula; Niki Markou; Konstantina Kanellopoulou; Eleni Frangou; George Tsirpanlis
abstract:
Background and Aims
Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) is the most prevalent monogenic kidney disease and is typically inherited. However, a subset of patients presents without a documented family history (FH) of the disease. This absence of FH may result from challenges in accurately defining familial disease patterns or may reflect de novo mutations resulting in the disease. The genetic and phenotypic features of these patients remain poorly characterized. This study aims to evaluate the genetic and clinical features of ADPKD in this unique subgroup of patients.
Method
We evaluated ADPKD patients without a documented family history (FH) in comparison to those with a confirmed FH, all of whom were managed at the outpatient ADPKD clinic of our hospital. A total of 135 patients, encompassing both groups, underwent genetic analysis, including targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) of over 600 phenotypically relevant genes, Sanger sequencing, and multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification (MLPA). Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was conducted on 104 of the 135 adult patients, identifying the presence of more than 10 renal cysts in each individual. Among pediatric patients, those with a positive FH demonstrated at least one renal cyst on ultrasonography, while two without FH exhibited multiple renal cysts. Clinical data collection included detailed medical histories, laboratory investigations, and disease-specific assessments such as the PROPKD score.
Results
Among the 135 ADPKD patients studied, 90 (67%) had a confirmed family history, while 45 (33%) did not (22 female, 23 male; median age [IQR]: 41 [33–50] years). Genetic testing was negative in 6 (13%) patients without FH, while variants were identified in PKD1 (76%), PKD2 (4%), and other genes, including IFT140, SEC61B, and SEC63 (7%). In contrast, patients with a positive FH showed variant distribution rates of 67% in PKD1, 20% in PKD2, and 9% in other genes, with 4% testing negative (P = 0.04). Truncating PKD1 variants (14 nonsense, 10 frameshifts, 1 splicing, and 1 CNV large deletion) were detected in 26 of 34 (76%) patients without FH compared to 40 of 60 (67%) patients with FH (P = 0.4). Age at disease onset and hypertension diagnosis differed between groups. Patients without FH exhibited a later disease onset (median [IQR]: 30 [21–37] years) compared to those with FH (21 [14–31] years, P = 0.002). Hypertension diagnosis occurred at a mean age of 35.6 ± 14 years in patients without FH, compared to 31 ± 11 years in those with FH (P = NS). Hypertension was more prevalent in patients without FH, affecting 36 of 42 patients compared to 49 of 80 patients with FH (P = 0.005). Renal function and structural parameters also showed differences. Age-adjusted eGFR (median [IQR]) was lower in patients without FH (65 [45–104] ml/min) compared to those with FH (96.5 [59–120] ml/min, P = 0.04). Height-adjusted total kidney volume (htTKV) was higher in patients without FH (597 [428–972] ml/m) compared to those with FH (386 [270–654] ml/m, P = 0.01). Predicted time to end-stage renal disease (ESRD), calculated using the Irazabal MV et al. formula (JASN 2015), was significantly shorter for patients without FH (17 [10–37] years) compared to those with FH (26 [16–42] years, P = 0.04). Finally, PROPKD scores were higher in patients without FH (mean ± SD: 5.8 ± 2) compared to those with FH (4.9 ± 2, P = 0.05).
Conclusion
ADPKD patients without a documented family history demonstrated a more severe disease phenotype, which may be attributed to the higher prevalence of PKD1 variants in this group. Although the possibility of selection bias due to more frequent genetic testing in patients lacking a clear FH cannot be excluded, the observed severity of the phenotype likely contributes to the earlier recognition and diagnosis of the disease.

title: #1941 Development and validation of deep-learning model for diagnosing systemic acidemia from the electrocardiograms
authors: Won Ho Park; Minje Park; Giae Yun; Jung Nam An; Do Hyoung Kim; Hee Jung Jeon; Sung Gyun Kim; Eun Jung Kim; Jang Won Seo; Ja-Ryong Koo; Seon Ha Baek
abstract:
Background and Aims
Systemic acidemia critically impairs cardiovascular function and is typically diagnosed through arterial blood gas analysis, which may delay timely intervention. This study aimed to develop a deep learning model using electrocardiogram (ECG) data for rapid, non-invasive diagnosis of systemic acidemia.
Method
We developed and validated deep learning models to detect systemic acidemia, categorized by severity (mild: pH <7.35, moderate: pH <7.30, severe: pH <7.20), using 12-lead ECGs from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC)-IV database. The training, validation, and test datasets included 56.249, 1.429, and 1.446 ECG-pH samples, respectively. To investigate variations in the model's efficacy depending on the type of systemic acidemia, we carried out a subgroup analysis according to pCO2 and HCO3− levels.
Results
The models achieved high performance in detecting systemic acidemia, with the area under the receiver operating characteristic curves (AUCs) of 0.69, 0.73, and 0.82 for mild, moderate, and severe acidemia, respectively, in the testing cohort. No statistically significant differences in AUC were observed between the group with pCO₂ ≤45 mmHg and HCO₃⁻ <22 mEq/L and the group with pCO₂ >45 mmHg and HCO₃⁻ ≥ 22mEq/L, with p-values (DeLong's method) of 0.07, 0.07, and 0.25 for mild, moderate, and severe acidemia, respectively. The group predicted to be positive by the severe academia model showed a lower 30-day survival rate compared to the negative group (P < 0.05), supporting the clinical efficacy.
Conclusion
Deep learning offers a non-invasive method for diagnosing systemic acidemia in critically ill patients, enabling earlier intervention and improved patient care.
