title: #2961 DMX-200 does not induce a haemodynamic effect or an acute change in GFR and has a strong cardiovascular safety profile
authors: David Fuller; Alisha Smith; Robert Shepherd; Carl White
abstract:
Background and Aims
Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) is a major cause of glomerular disease that affects both adults and children and can rapidly progress to end-stage kidney disease. Lack of safe and effective treatment represents a significant unmet need for patients with FSGS. Change in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR slope) has been used as a key measure of treatment efficacy in clinical studies. However, when using eGFR as surrogate endpoint for kidney failure, treatments that exert haemodynamic effects or have an acute eGFR reductions complicate the estimation of long-term benefit. Therefore, it is important to establish if new interventions influence blood pressure and exert acute reductions in eGFR. DMX-200 (repagermanium) is a CCR2 pathway inhibitor that is currently in a Phase 3 pivotal trial (ACTION3, NCT05183646) in patients with biopsy-proven FSGS concomitantly receiving maximal tolerated angiotensin receptor blocker (ARB). Mechanistically, the inhibition of CCR2 is not anticipated to reduce blood pressure nor have an acute effect on GFR. The aim of this investigation was to establish whether DMX-200 has an acute effect on haemodynamics or eGFR.
Method
A post-hoc review of haemodynamic, eGFR and cardiovascular safety parameters was performed using data from two double blind cross over clinical studies NCT03627715 and NCT03649152 (ACTION2). In these studies, patients with FSGS (n = 8) or DKD (n = 45) that were receiving a stable dose of irbesartan 300mg were administrated DMX-200 (120 mg BID) or placebo for up to 12- or 16-weeks respectively.
Results
Administration of DMX-200 (120 mg BID) for up to 16-weeks had no noticeable effect on systolic blood pressure compared to placebo (mean change from baseline; Δ0.1 ± 12.4 mmHg versus Δ3.7 ± 10.8 mmHg respectively, n = 8). Similarly, no acute effect on eGFR has observed following administration of DMX-200 (120 mg BID) with a mean change from baseline eGFR; Δ3.9 ± 10.0 mL/min/1.73 m2, Δ2.1 ± 8.0 mL/min/1.73 m2 and Δ0.6 ± 6.2 mL/min/1.73 m2 at 1, 8 and 16-weeks respectively, n = 8). Creatine levels were also comparable following administration of DMX-200 or placebo for up to 16-weeks (mean change from baseline; Δ2.1 ± 16.3 µmol/L versus Δ−1.9 ± 19.2 µmol/L respectively, n = 8). Comparable results for blood pressure, eGFR and creatinine were observed in patients with DKD administered DMX-200 (120 mg BID) for up to 12-weeks. Confirming the cardiac safety of DMX-200, there were no significant effects on QT/QTc following administration of DMX-200 or placebo and adverse events reflected of the underlying disease and associated comorbidities.
Conclusion
DMX-200 is a CCR2 pathway inhibitor currently in a Phase 3 pivotal trial (ACTION3, NCT05183646) in adult patients with biopsy-proven FSGS. As anticipated, data from post-hoc analysis of Phase 2 studies indicate that DMX-200 does not induce a haemodynamic effect or acute change in eGFR. Notably, DMX-200 has a strong cardiovascular safety profile. These data support the design of ACTION3 where patients receive a stable maximally tolerated dose of an angiotensin receptor blocker prior to randomization.

title: #877 Efficacy and safety of telitacicept in IgA nephropathy: a preliminary report of the large single-center observational study
authors: Qian Chuyue; Li Jing; Sun Tao; Sun Mindan
abstract:
Background and Aims
IgA nephropathy (IgAN) is a common type of primary glomerulonephritis worldwide with nearly 40% of patient progresses to end-stage renal disease (ESRD) in 10-20 years. The most widely accepted hypothesis is known as the ‘multihit hypothesis’. B cells play an important role in producing galactose-deficient IgA1 (Gd-IgA1) and its autoimmune antibody, resulting in the deposition of IgA in the mesangium. B-cell activating factor (BAFF), also known as B-lymphocyte stimulator (BLyS), and a proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL) have been reported to play crucial roles in the activation of B lymphocytes. Telitacicept, a soluble humanized recombinant fusion protein that effectively neutralizes the activity of BLyS and APRIL had been demonstrated the ability to reduce proteinuria with adverse events similar to supportive care in a phase 2 clinical trial. Therefore, our project was aiming to conduct a large single-center observational study to explore the efficacy and safety of telitacicept in patients with IgAN compared with supportive therapy and glucocorticoid therapy.
Method
We are aiming to conduct a observational study of adults who had undergone renal biopsy at the First Hospital of Jilin University between October 2023 and December 2026 and were diagnosed with IgAN. Up to now, out of the initial pool of 243 patients, 159 were excluded based on specific criteria: (1) eGFR (CKD-EPI) <35 mL/min/1.73 m² (n = 39); (2) proteinuria <0.5 g/d (n = 10); (3) others (n = 109). So far, 84 eligible IgAN patients were enrolled in the project and 64 IgAN patients can be analysed due to the fllowed-up time. All patients received supportive care and were taking the maximally tolerated dose of angiotensin receptor blockers. The patients were divided into four groups according to the therapy: telitacicept (Group A, not enough cases now), telitacicept combined low-dose corticosteroids (Group B, n = 20), adequate-dose of glucocorticoids (Group C, n = 21) and angiotensin receptor blockers (Group D, n = 23). The efficacy was defined as a decrease in proteinuria of 50% or more. The research protocol underwent thorough scrutiny and received approval from the ethical committees of the First Hospital of Jilin University (approval number: 2024-1165).
Results
A cohort of 64 patients with IgAN were recruited with a follow-up duration of 12 weeks. All the clinical data has no significance among Group B, C and D. The median baseline proteinuria of Group B, C, D was 1.85 g/day, 1.34 g/day and 1.26 g/day respectively, while median baseline eGFR was 62.98 mL/min/1.73 m2, 82.26 mL/min/1.73 m2 and 78.44 mL/min/1.73 m2. Patients with higher proteinuria and lower eGFR are more likely to choose telitacicept. Renal biopsy data showed significance in T classification. The total efficacy among the three group also has no significance. Figure 1 showed the changing process of proteinuria and eGFR at week 4, week 8 and week1, indicates that telitacicept combined low-dose corticosteroids can reduce proteinuria and stabilize eGFR in patients with IgAN. However the adequate-dose of glucocorticoids seemed to keep urine protein at a lower level than telitacicept within 12 weeks, the long follow-up of our project may give the answer later.
Conclusion
Telitacicept can reduce the dose of corticosteroids and is no inferior to corticosteroid therapy in IgAN, the long-term kidney protection still needs to be confirmed.

title: #1216 40-year renal survival rate in patients with IgA nephropathy: Analysis of 1,121 patients at a single center
authors: Takayuki Fujii; Satoshi Suzuki; Noriko Terasaki; Junya Koshizaka; Takahiro Matsunaga; Nobuaki Yamauchi; Mayu Morimoto; Hiroaki Tanaka
abstract:
Background and Aims
IgA nephropathy was initially regarded as a benign kidney disease, but in the 1990s it was reported that 40% of patients progressed to end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) within 20 years, indicating that the renal prognosis is not favorable. Recently, UK Renal Registry showed that the risk of EKSD was high even if the time average proteinuria is below 0.44 g/g (CJASN 2023). In Japan, in addition to RAS inhibitors and steroids, tonsillectomy plus steroid pulse therapy has been widely performed since the 2000s, and has resulted in a good renal prognosis. We investigated the renal prognosis over the entire 40-year period and in each period stratified into four groups depending on the year of diagnosis of IgA nephropathy.
Method
We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of 1,121 cases diagnosed with IgA nephropathy by kidney biopsy at our hospital between 1977 and March 2023. We investigated the renal survival rate during the whole period of 40 years and in each era, dividing the time period into four groups: 1977–1990 (A), 1991–2000 (B), 2001–2010 (C), and 2011–2023 (D). Furthermore, among those 4 groups, we compared the renal survival rate using a Cox proportional hazards model with clinical data, histopathological findings, and treatment methods as covariates.
Results
The mean follow-up period was 11.2 years, 50% were male, age was 39 years, eGFR was 73 ml/min/1.73 m2, and proteinuria was 1.0 g/day. Renal survival rates using the Kaplan-Meier method were 74% at 20 years, 67% at 30 years, and 58% at 40 years. title: #3665 Glyoxylic acid induce crystalline nephropathy and hair-straightening products: a case report
authors: Ameni Slimeni; Sirine Bchir; Mouna Hamouda; Meriem Ben Salem; Nouha Ben Mahmoud; Manel Ben Salah; Ahmed Letaief; Habib Skhiri
abstract:
Background and Aims
Hair-straightening products containing glyoxylic acid have emerged as a potential cause of calcium oxalate nephropathy, a condition rarely reported in medical literature.
Method
We present a clinical case of acute kidney injury (AKI) linked to hair smoothing treatment in a young female patient, highlighting its diagnostic challenges.
Results
A 27-year-old woman with no prior medical history presented with symptoms of asthenia, nausea, epigastric pain, and bilateral lumbar pain. She reported reduced urine output. Physical examination was unremarkable, with stable hemodynamics and no peripheral edema. Laboratory tests showed severe AKI with serum creatinine at 456 µmol/L and urea at 9.6 mmol/L. Urinalysis revealed leukocyturia without proteinuria or hematuria. Serum electrolytes were within normal ranges, except for mild metabolic acidosis (bicarbonate 14.5 mmol/L). Abdominal ultrasound was unremarkable, ruling out obstructive causes.
Given the absence of systemic autoimmune markers (negative ANA, ANCA, and normal complement levels) and the lack of infectious signs, nephrotoxic exposure was suspected. The patient reported recent use of a hair straightening product containing “Brazilian Cacao Protein,” causing scalp irritation. Renal biopsy demonstrated interstitial edema with inflammatory lymphocytic infiltrates and intratubular calcium oxalate crystals under polarized light microscopy. Skin biopsy of the scalp confirmed epidermal necrosis consistent with chemical irritation.
Conclusion
Histopathological and urine sediment findings support the hypothesis that the pathophysiological mechanism involves dermal absorption of glyoxylic acid, subsequently metabolized into oxalate, inducing calcium oxalate crystallization. Similar cases was reported in Switzerland and France and this hypothesis was also confirmed in experimental murine models exposed to glyoxylic acid-based hair products.
Hair smoothing products containing glyoxylic acid represent an underrecognized cause of oxalate nephropathy, warranting regulatory review and public health intervention. Early recognition and prompt discontinuation of exposure are essential to prevent irreversible renal damage.

title: #7 The kidney failure risk equation in IgA nephropathy: external validation and model update
authors: Yngvar Lunde Haaskjold; Mariell Rivedal; Njål Gjærde Lura; Thomas Knoop; Øystein Solberg Eikrem
abstract:
Background and Aims
IgA nephropathy (IgAN) is the most prevalent glomerulonephritis and a leading cause of chronic kidney disease (CKD) globally. The disease's progression varies widely, so accurately predicting prognosis is crucial for identifying patients at risk of developing end-stage kidney disease (ESKD). Prognostic information is essential in patient counseling and could help decide appropriate treatment options. The 2024 KDIGO guidelines for CKD recommend using established CKD risk prediction tools to assess the risk for ESKD. The Kidney Failure Risk Equation (KFRE), developed in 2011 from a Canadian cohort, predicts the 2- and 5-year risk of ESKD in patients with eGFR <60 ml/min/1.73 m2 corresponding to chronic kidney failure stage 3. It has been externally validated using multiple international CKD cohorts involving over 700,000 patients. The tool includes four variables: age, sex, urine albumin/creatinine, and eGFR. It is easily accessible as an online tool. The International IgA Prediction Tool was developed in 2019. It can predict prognosis in IgAN for up to 6.7 years, and the current KDIGO guidelines recommend using it in patient counseling. However, the tool needs clinical and histopathological features from the Oxford classification to predict prognosis. In many patients with IgAN, detailed histopathological information might be unavailable due to few glomeruli in the diagnostic kidney biopsy. We, therefore, set out to externally validate the KFRE in an IgAN population.
Method
We used data from the Norwegian Kidney Biopsy Registry and patient records to identify 236 patients with biopsy-confirmed IgAN who had advanced to stage 3 chronic kidney disease. We used the published regression equation to derive the five-year prognostic index. We then assessed discrimination using cumulative dynamic receiver operating characteristics (ROC) analysis and the concordance index. Model calibration was evaluated by calibration curves, while goodness of fit was assessed by the Akaike information criterion (AIC). Recalibration was performed by updating the baseline survival from the validation cohort and performing regression on the prognostic index. An updated multivariable Cox model was derived using the same four variables and internally validated using boot-strapping methodology.
Results
170 (72%) of the patients were male, and the median age at CKD stage 3 was 48 years (IQR 34–59). The median urine albumin creatinine ratio was 71 mg/mmol (IQR 28–216). A total of 98 patients reached ESKD during the time of follow-up, while 20 patients died. The median follow-up time was four years (IQR 1–9). In total, 167 (71%) patients were treated with RAAS inhibitors, while 57 (24%) received immunosuppressive treatment. ROC analysis at five years presented an area under curve (AUC) value at 0.78, decreasing to 0.64 at 20 years (Table 1). Calibration curves revealed poor calibration at five and ten years by underestimating and overestimating ESKD-free survival in the low-risk and high-risk groups, respectively (Fig. 1). The AIC value was 860.61. Recalibration showed an improved calibration after five and ten years and improved goodness of fit (AIC: 838.21). Multivariable analysis revealed that eGFR and proteinuria were the prominent predictors. The new Cox model showed improved discrimination compared to the KRFE model, with AUC at 0.84 at five years, decreasing to 0.73 at 20 years (Table 1), and no signs of overfitting in internal validation, improved calibration (Fig. 1), and an improved AIC at 815.093.
Conclusion
Based on data from this cohort, the 4-parameter KRFE has acceptable predictive probabilities in patients with IgAN. However, it might be possible to improve model performance if the KFRE is adapted and updated for IgAN patients. One should be aware of the potential reduced predictive performance of generic CKD calculators in subgroups of patients.

title: #2565 End-stage kidney disease in people with ANCA-associated vasculitis: a systematic review of outcomes
authors: Andreas Kronbichler; Antonio Ramirez de Arellano; Juliette Cattin; Barnaby Hunt
abstract:
Background and Aims
Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis (AAV) is a group of rare autoimmune disorders characterized by inflammation of small blood vessels, and leads to damage of various organ systems, including the kidneys, respiratory tract, nerves and skin. Kidney involvement in AAV significantly increases both morbidity and risk of mortality, particularly when there is progression to end-stage kidney disease (ESKD). Management of kidney disease in people with AAV, particularly those at risk of losing kidney function entirely, remains an unmet need. This systematic review aimed to identify modern data on the cumulative incidence of ESKD in people with AAV, and how changes in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) impact the risk of developing ESKD.
Method
Literature searches of the PubMed, EMBASE and Cochrane Library databases were performed to identify studies that reported the incidence of ESKD in people with AAV. To ensure that high quality, modern studies were identified, searches were limited to studies published between 2019 and 2024, with at least 100 participants followed up for a minimum of 3 years. Data were extracted on the incidence of ESKD at each reported timepoint, as well as patient baseline characteristics, in the overall study population and in each reported sub-group. Data from identified studies were combined by calculating a pooled estimate of ESKD incidence, weighted by the number of study participants.
Where studies reported a relationship between eGFR and ESKD risk, additional data were extracted on the methods used to quantify the relationship, and the timepoints at which eGFR and ESKD incidence were measured. Hazard ratios (HRs) from univariate and multivariate Cox proportional regressions based on eGFR at diagnosis and at 6 months after diagnosis were combined in separate random-effects meta-analyses.
Results
A total of 43 studies reported incidence of ESKD in the overall study population, with notable heterogeneity in the reported results across studies and timepoints (Fig. 1). The cumulative incidence of ESKD ranged from 4.5% to 59.6% at 1 year of follow up, and from 9.4% to 51.4% at 10 years of follow up. Data were not sufficiently detailed to allow quantification of the relationship between patient characteristics and incidence of ESKD, but lower eGFR at study baseline was associated with increased risk of ESKD (Fig. 2). Race also appeared to be correlated with outcomes, with higher incidence of ESKD in Asian versus European or North American populations. The relationship was less clear between the type of AAV and ESKD incidence and no correlation was observed between ESKD incidence and age, gender or the Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score (BVAS). The pooled estimate of ESKD incidence across all studies was 13.7% after 1 year and 23.6% after 10 years.
The relationship between eGFR and ESKD risk was reported in 19 studies, which varied greatly in terms of patient characteristics, methods used, timepoints for data collection and units used in the analysis. The most commonly used method to quantify the relationship between eGFR and ESKD risk was Cox proportional regression analysis. Pooling the reported results indicated that a 1 mL/min/1.73 m2 increase in eGFR at diagnosis was associated with a 3 to 6% reduction in ESKD risk (HRs ranging from 0.94 to 0.97) depending on the approach used. The reduction in ESKD risk was slightly larger for a 1 mL/min/1.73 m2 increase in eGFR 6 months after diagnosis, ranging from 7% to 8% (HRs between 0.92 and 0.93).
Conclusion
The present systematic review indicates that the incidence of ESKD in people with AAV is approximately 14% at 1 year and 24% at 10 years. A 1 mL/min/1.73 m2 increase in baseline eGFR was associated with a reduction in ESKD risk by 3% to 6%, while an equivalent increase in eGFR at 6 months decreased ESKD risk by 7% to 8%. However, these estimates should be treated with caution as there was significant variation in study outcomes, likely due to heterogeneity in enrolled populations and study designs.

title: #2953 DMX-200 is effective in reducing urine monocyte chemoattractant protein 1 (MCP-1) levels in patients with FSGS without affecting plasma MCP-1 concentration
authors: David Fuller; Alisha Smith; Robert Shepherd; Carl White
abstract:
Background and Aims
Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) is a major cause of glomerular disease that affects both adults and children and can rapidly progress to end-stage kidney disease. Lack of safe and effective treatment represents a significant unmet need for patients with FSGS. Activation of the angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R) and the C-C motif chemokine receptor 2 (CCR2) have been independently implicated in the pathogenesis and progression of FSGS. High urine MCP-1 levels (the key endogenous ligand for CCR2) are associated with FSGS disease progression, and AT1R blockade is an existing supportive therapy for glomerular disease including FSGS. In addition, the AT1R and CCR2 receptors form a functional complex so inhibition of both receptors may provide an efficient and novel approach to FSGS treatment.
Several CCR2 inhibitors have previously entered clinical development. However, none have yet been approved. Notably, chemokine receptor tolerance has been observed for many CCR2 inhibitors, which may in part be driven by inhibitor mediated increases in plasma MCP-1 that directly counteracts CCR2 blockade. Indeed, studies of other CCR2 antagonists in diabetic kidney disease have observed a negative correlation between the change in urinary albuminuria and plasma MCP-1 levels.
DMX-200 (repagermanium) is a CCR2 pathway inhibitor currently in a Phase 3 pivotal trial (ACTION3, NCT05183646) in patients with FSGS concomitantly receiving maximal tolerated angiotensin receptor blocker (ARB). In vivo co-administration of DMX-200 and the ARB irbesartan demonstrated a synergistic reduction in proteinuria, macrophage infiltration, and podocyte loss compared with vehicle or antagonist alone. A subsequent Phase 2a cross-over study (NCT03649152) in n = 8 patients with biopsy-proven primary FSGS showed that the combination of DMX-200 and irbesartan was well tolerated with most patients experiencing a reduction in proteinuria (compared to placebo). However, the effect of DMX-200 on plasma MCP-1 levels has not been established. The aim of this study was therefore to investigate the effect of DMX-200 on urine and plasma MCP-1 levels in a post-hoc analysis.
Method
Urine from male Sprague-Dawley rats administered vehicle or DMX-200 and irbesartan was collected 12-weeks post subtotal nephrectomy and MCP-1 measured using rat MCP-1 ELISA. As part of ACTION2 (NCT03649152) urine and plasma samples were collected from patients following treatment with placebo or DMX-200 (120 mg BID) for 16-weeks. Samples were analyzed using a V-PLEX human MCP-1 immunoassay.
Results
In rats, administration of DMX-200 (30 mg/kg/day) and irbesartan (10 mg/kg/day) for 12-weeks reduced the urine MCP-1 concentration following subtotal nephrectomy compared to vehicle (P < 0.01, 2881 ± 162 pg/ml versus 4929 ± 631 pg/ml respectively). In patients with FSGS, the mean change from baseline urine MCP-1 following 16-weeks of treatment with DMX-200 (120 mg BID, and a maximally tolerated dose of irbesartan) was 0.85 (n = 8, 95% CI; 0.62 to 1.07) compared to 1.23 (n = 8, 95% CI; 0.81 to 1.63) for placebo. This corresponded to a between group difference of 37% (geometric mean 0.63 (95% CI; 0.07 to 1.18). In contrast, administration of DMX-200 (120 mg BID) and a maximally tolerated dose of irbesartan had no effect on plasma MCP-1 levels compared to placebo.
Conclusion
DMX-200 is a CCR2 pathway inhibitor currently in a Phase 3 pivotal trial (ACTION3, NCT05183646) in patients with biopsy-proven FSGS. Data from pre-clinical studies and post-hoc analysis of Phase2 measures suggest DMX-200 can reduce urine MCP-1 levels without increasing plasma MCP-1 (with corresponding reductions in proteinuria). This profile may be beneficial for the treatment effect of DMX-200 and supports its use in patients with FSGS. The effect of long-term administration of DMX-200 on urine and plasma MCP-1 will be analyzed as an exploratory endpoint in the ongoing ACTION3 trial.

title: #1156 Daratumumab-based regimens vs conventional clone-directed treatment in relapsed/refractory non-amyloid monoclonal immunoglobulin related kidney disease
authors: Maria Khrabrova; Vladimir Dobronravov
abstract:
Background and Aims
Anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody Daratumumab is known to be more effective in achievement of hematologic response (HR) in relapsed/refractory plasma cell clonal disease e.g. multiple myeloma and AL-amyloidosis comparing with conventional clone-directed treatment (CDT). Moreover, Daratumumab-based regimens demonstrated some benefits in relapsed/refractory renal AL-amyloidosis with higher rate of renal response (RR) reaching 50%–80%. However, the data on the Daratumumab effects in relapsed/refractory non-amyloid monoclonal immunoglobulin related kidney disease (mIgKD) are limited. The aim of the study was to check the hypothesis that Daratumumab-based regimens are more effective in relapsed/refractory non-amyloid mIgKD than traditional CDT including proteasome inhibitors, immunomodulatory drugs, cyclophosphamide, and dexamethasone.
Method
We included 37 patients with morphologically proven non-amyloid mIgKD with available follow-up (FUP) of at least 12 months. According to disease course and treatment modalities patients were divided on three groups including those who received: (i) only bortezomib-based regimens as frontline conventional CDT (group 1 “one line only,” n = 22) or due to relapsed/refractory disease were treated with (ii) more than one line of conventional CDT (group 2 “next lines,” n = 7) or (iii) Daratumumab-based regimens (group 3 “Dara group,” n = 8). Daratumumab was given in standard doses i.e. 16 mg/kg weekly 8 doses and then every other weeks 8 doses. Baseline clinical parameters of the groups and morphological spectrum of renal disease are presented in the Figs 1 and 2, respectively. HR was estimated according to currently accepted criteria. Decrease in 24 h proteinuria <3.5 g/by 50% from the baseline and <0.5 g at the FUP was determined as partial and complete RR, respectively. title: #1802 Development of the Nephrotic Syndrome Symptom and Impact Patient Reported Outcome (NephroSSI-PRO) measure for use in adults and adolescents with primary glomerulopathies
authors: Joshua Maher; Angela Hu; Sagar Nigwekar; Julie Lin
abstract:
Background and Aims
Understanding health-related quality of life through patient reported outcomes (PRO) instruments is important for assessing the effects of new therapeutics used to treat nephrotic syndrome (NS). To date, there are no validated PROs developed specifically for NS.
Method
The Nephrotic Syndrome Symptom and Impact Patient Reported Outcome (NephroSSI-PRO) tool was developed using: (1) a review of key literature, (2) concept elicitation (CE) interviews with patients with NS and clinicians, (3) instrument generation, and (4) cognitive interviews with patients with NS. The CE interviews were conducted with 4 clinicians with expertise in nephrology and among adults (aged ≥18 years) and adolescents (aged 12–17 years) with a diagnosis of NS caused by different etiologies, including focal segmental glomerular sclerosis, minimal change disease, membranous nephropathy, and IgA nephropathy. During cognitive interviews, items were modified as part of a patient feedback-based iterative process until the intended comprehension was achieved.
Results
Forty-five adult and adolescent patients were interviewed in total, across all concept elicitation and cognitive debriefing interviews. In the adult CE interviews, the most frequently reported symptoms were swelling in the feet/legs (n = 14/16), general tiredness (n = 13/16), change in appetite (n = 13/16), foamy urine (n = 12/16), and shortness of breath (n = 12/16), while impacts included emotional health, physical function limitations, sleep difficulties, and social/lifestyle limitations (n = 13/16). In adolescents the most frequently reported symptoms were tiredness/fatigue (n = 13/15), stomachache (n = 11/15), headache (n = 8/15), foamy/frothy urine (n = 7/15), swelling in face/eyes (n = 6/15), swelling in legs/ankles (n = 5/15), and change in appetite (n = 5/15), while the most common impacts were [negative] impact on schooling (n = 10/15), reduced ability to practice sports (n = 7/15), and [negative] impact on friendship (n = 7/15). A conceptual model was developed and used to generate a novel PRO instrument, the NephroSSI-PRO (Table 1). During the cognitive interviews, there were no significant challenges in understanding and relating to instrument instructions, items, and response options for adults or adolescents.
Conclusion
This is the first PRO instrument to evaluate the symptoms and impacts of NS in adult and adolescent patients, which has been cognitively validated. The authors aim for the NephroSSI-PRO to be a helpful tool for understanding the burden of NS as well as the effects of investigational treatments in a clinical context. The next steps involve the quantitative validation of the instrument, including empirically defining a scoring algorithm. This is planned to take place as part of Sanofi's Phase 2a RESULT study (NCT06500702).

title: #2200 Phospholipase A2 receptor antibody IgG and IgG4 subclass by TRFIA improves sensitivity and specificity in the diagnosis of primary membranous nephropathy
authors: Zhenling Deng; Yue Wang; Danxia Zheng
abstract:
Background and Aims
Primary membranous nephropathy (PMN) is a prevalent cause of nephrotic syndrome, often associated with circulating anti-phospholipase A2 receptor (PLA2R) antibodies, which can be detected using traditional ELISA methods. However, these methods have limitations, particularly in patients with PLA2R antibody values between 2 and 20 RU/ml, necessitating renal biopsy for accurate diagnosis. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic utility of time-resolved fluoroimmunoassay (TRFIA) for detecting serum anti-PLA2R IgG and IgG4 subclass to enhance sensitivity and reduce the need for invasive procedures.
Method
A total of 175 patients with serum anti-PLA2R antibody levels between 2 and 20 RU/ml were retrospectively analyzed, among which 121 patients were detected anti-PLA2R IgG and IgG4 by TRFIA. Clinical data and renal biopsy results were collected.
Results
The findings revealed that 52% (91/175) of patients had PMN, and the other 48% patients still need to be differentiated (Fig. 1). The positive detection rate of patients with PMN were14.3% for PLA2R-IgG and 34.1% for PLA2R-IgG4 by TRFIA, significantly improving diagnostic sensitivity compared to ELISA, especially PLA2R-IgG4. The positive detection rates of PLA2R-IgG4-TRFIA in 91 PMN with PLA2R-IgG-ELISA value of 2–7 RU/ml, 7–14 RU/ml and 14–20 RU/ml were 22.9% (11/48), 36% (9/25) and 66.7% (12/18), respectively (Fig. 2). Notably, PMN patients with positive PLA2R-IgG4-TRFIA exhibited distinct clinical characteristics, including higher age, lower albumin, TBIL, DBIL and C3.
Conclusion
In conclusion, the TRFIA method demonstrates enhanced sensitivity in detecting PLA2R antibodies, particularly the IgG4 subclass, which may facilitate more accurate diagnosis of MN and minimize the need for invasive renal biopsies. Future research should focus on validating these findings in larger cohorts and exploring the clinical implications of PLA2R subclass determination in kidney disease management.

title: #1286 Dextran sulfate sodium-induced colitis causes production of degalactosylated mucosal IgA and glomerular IgA-IgG deposition in HIGA mice
authors: Yukako Ohyama; Yudai Tsuji; Tadashi Fujii; Hiroyuki Tezuka; Takumi Tochio; Naotake Tsuboi; Kazuo Takahashi
abstract:
Background and Aims
IgA nephropathy (IgAN) is the most common form of glomerulonephritis. IgAN is exacerbated after upper respiratory tract inflammation and enteritis and associated with chronic inflammatory bowel diseases, such as Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis. There is a close association between mucosal-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT) and the pathogenesis of IgAN. IgA production in MALT is believed to interact with the mucosal bacterial flora. Recently, “short-chain fatty acids,” a metabolite of bacterial origin, has been reported to affect IgA production in MALT. Here, we used a dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced chronic colitis mice model with high IgA (HIGA) to show the effects of inflammation of gut-associated lymphoid tissue on the microbiota, short-chain fatty acids, and renal glomeruli.
Method
Fourteen-week-old female HIGA mice were randomly divided into two groups; control and DSS administration groups. DSS (36,000–50,000 kDa; MP Biomedicals) was dissolved in sterilized drinking water and administered in three cycles for seven days at 14 days interval and sterilized water was consumed during the remaining period. Histological scoring of colitis was performed as previously described. Intestinal microorganisms in the cecal contents were analyzed using 16s rDNA sequencing, and short chain fatty acids were measured using GC/MS. Serum and fecal IgA levels were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISA). IgA galactosylation and sialylation were analyzed by lectin ELISA using Ricinus Communis Agglutinin I (RCAI) and Sambucus nigra agglutinin (SNA). The glomerular deposition rates of IgA and IgG in renal specimens were measured using immunofluorescence.
Results
In the DSS group, all mice exhibited stool bleeding and significantly higher histopathological scores of colons than those in the control group (P = 0.0002). DSS administration changed the cecal microbiota and significantly decreased the propionate concentration (P = 0.0291). Mucosal IgA reactivity with RCAI and SNA was significantly lower than that with serum IgA even under normal conditions. DSS administration increased IgA secretion into the lumen of the intestinal tract and significantly decreased its reactivity with RCAI than that in the control (P = 0.0175). The glomerular deposition rates of IgA and IgG increased significantly in the DSS group (P = 0.0070 and P = 0.0175, respectively).
Conclusion
Mucosal IgA showed features of degalacto- and desialo-IgA compared to serum IgA under normal conditions. DSS-induced inflammation of the colon changed the microbiota and its metabolites, further reducing the galactosylation of mucosal IgA and inducing glomerular IgA-IgG deposition.

title: #2617 Advanced kidney models to better understand tacrolimus-induced nephrotoxicity
authors: Kate Liang; Elena Sendino Garvi; Gisela Slaats; Marianne Verhaar; Rosalinde Masereeuw; Anne Metje van Genderen
abstract:
Background and Aims
The use of tacrolimus as an immunosuppressive drug in organ transplant recipients is limited because of its nephrotoxic potential narrowing the therapeutic index. The exact mechanism remains poorly understood, although polymorphisms of the ABCB1 gene (encoding P-glycoprotein, P-gp) contribute to pharmacokinetic variability. Currently applied in vitro kidney models to unravel the toxic mechanisms have mainly focused on the proximal tubule cells as main target, whereas the use of animal studies and availability of clinical data are limited. Advanced in vitro models could allow for the generation of 3D models that better recapitulate kidney physiology and capture drug-induced response. To support this, we here describe an adverse outcome pathway (AOP) for tacrolimus-induced nephrotoxicity which was tested in two advanced in vitro models.
Method
An AOP describing key events (KEs) for tacrolimus-induced nephrotoxicity was developed based on current literature. The two kidney in vitro models used included an adult stem cell-derived kidney organoids “tubuloids” model mimicking the distal tubule segment after differentiation and induced pluripotent stem cell(iPSC)-derived kidney organoids mimicking the full nephron or after isolation using magnetic activated cell sorting mimicking the proximal tubule segment. To combine the outcomes of the AOP framework with our in vitro models, KE-related assays were developed to measure early kidney damage markers and apoptosis. Cells were exposed for 24 hours to tacrolimus (16–104 µM), with and without the addition of the P-gp inhibitor, PSC-833. Viability was assessed using Prestoblue and cell titer fluor. Intracellular tacrolimus concentrations were measured via LC-MS/MS. To study the effect of variations in P-gp genetic makeup on tacrolimus nephrotoxicity, CRISPR-Cas9 was used to develop ABCB1 mutant kidney organoids.
Results
The molecular initiating event of the AOP for tacrolimus-induced nephrotoxicity remains unidentified, but we could extract the following KEs: increased activation of nuclear factor kappa B (KE1), increased reactive oxygen species (KE2), oxidative stress (KE3), mitochondrial dysfunction (KE4), metabolic impairment (KE5), upregulation of TGF-beta (KE6), fibrosis (KE7), apoptosis (KE8), finally leading up to kidney failure (adverse outcome). The in vitro data showed that our tubuloid and kidney organoid models were sensitive to tacrolimus in a dose-response manner. Kidney injury molecule-1 and neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin mRNA expression was upregulated after exposure in the iPSC-derived organoids. P-gp inhibition with PSC-833 reduced viability in proximal tubule cells but not in distal cells, despite increased intracellular tacrolimus concentrations in both models. Further, heterogenous ABCB1 mutant models were successfully created, as confirmed by sanger sequencing and changes in relative ABCB1 gene expression as well as increased intracellular tacrolimus accumulation in kidney organoids. Nevertheless, sensitivity in ABCB1 mutant models decreased compared to wildtype organoids, suggesting a possible P-gp-linked compensatory mechanism.
Conclusion
Our results indicate that proximal tubule kidney cells respond differently to tacrolimus compared to distal cells. Future research will focus on the compensatory mechanisms in distal tubules and ABCB1 mutant organoids as well as identifying the initiating pathways of tacrolimus-induced nephrotoxicity. Advanced in vitro kidney models combined with the AOP framework offer a novel method for understanding tacrolimus-induced nephrotoxicity.

title: #2899 Subclinical renal tubular dysfunction in postmenopausal women exposed to low-level environmental cadmium
authors: Carlos Kunioka; Jonas Cruz; Vanessa Souza; Bruno Rocha; Fernando Júnior; Luís Belo; Maria Manso; Márcia Carvalho
abstract:
Background and Aims
Environmental cadmium (Cd) exposure is a significant public health concern due to its cumulative toxicity and long biological half-life. Cd primarily targets the kidneys, particularly the proximal tubules, where it accumulates and contributes to progressive renal dysfunction. Chronic exposure, often through dietary intake or inhalation in Cd-polluted areas, is associated with both tubular and glomerular damage [1]. This study aimed to investigate the dose-response relationship between dietary Cd exposure and renal tubular damage in postmenopausal women aged 50 and above, chronically exposed to low levels of Cd through their diet.
Method
A cross-sectional study in 380 postmenopausal women was conducted to assess early kidney tubular damage. Urinary Cd concentrations were used to estimate the body burden of Cd, while urinary β2-microglobulin (β2MG) served as a biomarker of tubular proteinuria. Urinary Cd analyses were performed by Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry (ICP-MS) equipped with Quadrupole Ion Deflector. Creatinine was measured using the Alkaline Picrate method; calcium (Ca), by the automated colorimetric method and β2MG by chemiluminescence. Studied variables were adjusted to urinary creatinine (creat) to standardize results. A level of significance of 0.05 was used for all statistical comparisons and associations.
Results
The median age (interquartile range) of patients was 60.0 (56.0–65.3) years and for body mass index (BMI) was 27.0 (24.4–30.1) kg/m2. All studied women were in the postmenopausal state. The median (interquartile range) for urinary Cd/creat was 0.30 (0.15–0.55) µg/g, and for β2-MG/creat was 90 (56–124) μg/g. Twenty-four women (6.3%) presented with a diagnosis of renal tubular damage, defined as a urinary β2-MG/creat ratio ≥300 μg/g. According to Brazilian reference ranges for urinary Cd2, 36 women (9.5%) presented Cd levels above P95 reference level; these participants also showed significantly higher β2-MG/creat (P = 0.002) and urinary Ca/creat (P = 0.036) levels when compared to those under P95. Urinary Cd levels (ln-transformed) correlated positively with β2-MG (rs = 0.374, P = 6.8 × 10−14; Fig. 1) and with Ca (rs = 0.261, P = 2.5 × 10−7). Furthermore, by performing multiple linear regression analyses, in a fully adjusted model (for age, BMI, smoking and chronic medication), Cd/creat (ln transformed) was independently associated with urinary Ca/creat (β = 1.229, P < 0.001) and β2-MG/creat (β = 1.399, P < 0.001).
Conclusion
In postmenopausal women, urinary Cd is an independent predictor of urinary β2MG and urinary calcium, even when β2MG levels are within the `normal' range. This finding supports the notion that low-level environmental exposure to Cd may adversely affect kidney health, contributing to subclinical tubular dysfunction.
Therefore, current thresholds for Cd exposure may underestimate the risk of renal dysfunction, particularly in vulnerable populations such as postmenopausal women. Enhanced monitoring and stricter environmental controls are warranted to mitigate the public health impact of Cd exposure.

title: #1709 Longitudinal follow-up of health-related quality of life indicators in glomerulonephritis treated with immunosuppressants
authors: Fiona Yeo; Jia Dong James Wang; Jason Choo; Cynthia Lim
abstract:
Background and Aims
Glomerulonephritis is a major cause of chronic kidney disease, especially among young adults. Patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) can allow nephrologists to understand and address patients’ perceptions of their health. We aimed to describe the patient-reported health-related quality of life (HRQOL) indices and their determinants among patients with active glomerulonephritis during their follow-up.
Method
This prospective cohort study included adults with active glomerulonephritis enrolled and followed-up between July 2020 and July 2021 at the Glomerulonephritis Disease Management Clinics, Singapore General Hospital. HRQOL was assessed at enrolment (baseline) and every 3 months for a year using interviewer-administered surveys: the patient reported outcome measurement informative system (PROMIS) and Short-Form Health Survey (SF-36). Socio-demographic and clinical data were collected from patient interviews and medical records. Longitudinal changes in HRQOL indices between baseline and Month 3 were analysed using a mixed-effects model incorporating time and adjusting for age, kidney function, and the Charlson Comorbidity Index.
Results
Sixty participants (mean age 45 ± 16 years) were enrolled. The most common diagnoses were primary podocytopathies (33%) and lupus nephritis (25%). The most common immunosuppressive therapies were prednisolone (65%), mycophenolate mofetil or sodium (47%) and calcineurin inhibitors (40%). The baseline, Month 3, Month 6, Month 9 and Month 12 surveys were completed by 60, 47, 27, 16, and 16 participants, respectively.
Mixed-effects analysis for changes in PROMIS domain scores over time found that the presence of oedema was associated with increased anxiety scores (β = 0.728, P = 0.03). Changes in the type of immunosuppressants reduced sleep disturbance scores (β = −0.663, P = 0.03).
In the analyses for changes in SF-36 domain scores over time, higher serum albumin levels were associated with improved physical functioning scores (β = 11.7, P = 0.04), while changes in the type of immunosuppressants improved social functioning scores (β = 17.1, P = 0.003).
Conclusion
Patient-reported HRQOL change during glomerulonephritis follow-up and treatment. PROMs can be integrated with individualized clinical care e.g. monitor for impact of therapeutic manoeuvres to address the physical, psychological, and social domains of HRQOL. Future studies should explore interventions to mitigate the psychological and functional burden experienced by patients with glomerulonephritis and evaluate the long-term impact of PROMs-driven care on patient outcomes.

title: #1812 Efficacy and safety of telitacicept in IgA nephropathy and IgA vasculitis nephropathy in children: a retrospective single-center study
authors: Jingyi Wu; Pei Chen; Lijun Liu; Sufang Shi; Jicheng Lv; Hong Zhang
abstract:
Background and Aims
IgA nephropathy (IgAN) and IgA vasculitis nephropathy (IgAVN) are common renal diseases in children, with limited treatment options available. Telitacicept, a dual-targeted fusion protein, has shown potential in treating these conditions. This study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of telitacicept in pediatric patients with IgAN and IgAVN.
Method
This was a retrospective, single-center study involving 10 pediatric patients (8 with IgAN and 2 with IgAVN) treated with telitacicept from January 2023 to January 2025. Patients received weekly subcutaneous injections of 80 mg or 160 mg of telitacicept based on body surface area. The primary efficacy outcomes included changes in 24-hour urinary total protein (24 h-UTP) and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). Secondary outcomes included changes in serum albumin (Alb), hemoglobin (Hb), urine red blood cell (RBC) count, and mean arterial pressure (MAP).
Results
During the follow-up period, the median 24 h-UTP decreased from 2.0 g at baseline to 1.0 g at 3 months (−41.5%) (P = 0.002) and further decreased to 0.7 g at 9 months (−58.0%). Median eGFR showed no significant changes as compared to baseline (P > 0.999). Serum Alb increased by 7.0 g/l (7.5%) at 9 months. Urine RBC count significantly reduced by 91.1% (P = 0.017) at 9 months. Most patients tolerated telitacicept well, with no patients discontinuing the treatment due to adverse events, and no serious adverse events were reported.
Conclusion
Telitacicept demonstrated a favorable safety profile in pediatric patients with IgAN and IgAVN, and was associated with clinically meaningful proteinuria reductions. Larger studies are needed to validate these findings.

title: #1961 Cystic kidney disease in X-linked Alport syndrome children
authors: Marina Aksenova; Marina Dobrynina; Olga Chumak
abstract:
Background and Aims
It is suggested that kidney cysts may be an incompletely penetrant phenotype of Alport syndrome. The aim of the study was to estimate the prevalence of cystic kidney disease and its association with kidney function in children with X-linked Alport syndrome (XLAS).
Method
Demographic, genetic, laboratory (proteinuria (Pr, mg/m2/day), eGFR (ml/min/1.73 m2), total kidney volume (TKV, cm3/m2)) data from 185 children (102M) with XLAS were analyzed.
Results
Renal cysts were revealed in 32 (17.3%): few cysts (≤3) in 25 (13.5%) and multiple cysts (>3) in 7 pts (3.8%). There were no genetic variants associated with cystic kidney diseases in 30 pts with WES, WGS data (2 pts had Alports’ genes panel). Missense variants in COL4A5 were reveled in 60.1% vs 50% pts without and with cysts respectively (P = 0.21). Kidney cysts were usually seen in boys (24.5% vs 8.4% in boys and girls respectively; P = 0.007), children with high proteinuria (41.5% vs 11.5% in Pr ≥ 500 and Pr < 500 mg/m2/day respectively; P < 0.001) and decreased eGFR (41.2% vs 8.3% in eGFR <90 vs eGFR ≥90 ml/min/1.73 m2 respectively; P < 0.001). Children with kidney cysts had lower eGFR then pts without cysts (69 ± 23 vs 108 ± 20 ml/min/1.73 m2; P = 0.02) and higher Pr (720[460;967] vs 93[20;405] mg/m2/day; P = 0.005). There was no significant difference between the groups of pts without and with cystic kidney in age (13.5 ± 2.3 vs 13.8 ± 2.5 yrs; P = 0.86), TKV (194 ± 40 vs 217 ± 43 cm3/m2; P = 0.84), urine level of β2-microglobulin (112 ± 25 vs 122 ± 20 ng/ml; P = 0.75) and TmP/eGFR (1.7 ± 0.2 vs 1.6 ± 0.12 mmol/l; P = 0.89).
Conclusion
Kidney cysts were found in 17.3% of XLAS children including polycystic kidneys in 3.8% of pts. No pathogenic variants were found in genes other than COL4A5. Cystic kidney disease in XLAS is associated with male gender and advance stage of nephropathy and most likely reflects the kidney disease progression.

title: #939 Proximal tubular multiciliated cells as prognostic markers in glomerular diseases
authors: Chun Soo Lim; Jeonghwan Lee; Jung Pyo Lee
abstract:
Background and Aims
Glomerular diseases encompass a wide range of kidney disorders with varying clinical courses, from rapidly progressive to chronic and irreversible. Despite advances in diagnostic tools, predicting outcomes remains challenging due to the heterogeneity of these diseases. Multiciliated cells (MCCs) have been observed in the proximal tubules of some patients with kidney diseases, but their clinical significance is unclear. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of MCCs in glomerular diseases and evaluate their potential as prognostic markers by analyzing their relationship with clinical outcomes.
Method
A total of 134 patients, including 126 with glomerular diseases and 8 controls, were included in the study. Kidney biopsy tissues collected between 2012 and 2021 were analyzed using immunohistochemistry to calculate the ratio of MCCs to proximal tubular epithelial cells. Baseline clinical characteristics and kidney disease outcomes, such as end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) and mortality, were collected. Statistical analyses, including Cox proportional hazard models, assessed the association between MCC ratios and clinical outcomes while adjusting for confounders such as age, sex, and baseline kidney function.
Results
MCCs were detected in patients with glomerular diseases, with a prevalence of 68.3%. The highest MCC ratios were observed in diabetic kidney disease (88.9%) and ANCA-associated glomerulonephritis (86.4%). Higher MCC ratios were associated with older age, male sex, increased proteinuria, and reduced estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). Survival analyses revealed that patients with higher MCC ratios had a significantly elevated risk of ESKD and death. Adjusted models confirmed that MCC ratios predicted ESKD (hazard ratio [HR] 1.413; 95% CI 1.012–1.972; P = 0.042) and composite outcomes (HR 1.401; 95% CI 1.028–1.909; P = 0.033).
Conclusion
Proximal tubular MCCs are prevalent in glomerular diseases and strongly associated with adverse outcomes, including ESKD and mortality. Quantifying MCCs in kidney biopsies may serve as a valuable prognostic tool, complementing clinical parameters. Further research is needed to validate these findings and explore the mechanistic role of MCCs in kidney disease progression.

title: #3308 Percutaneous kidney biopsy and the histopathologic patterns of kidney diseases in children
authors: Tuğçe Sümbüloğlu; Şenay Yıldırım; Pınar Erturgut; Ayça Esra Kuybulu; Rahime Renda; Nevin Semerci Koyun; Cagla Serpil Dogan
abstract:
Background and Aims
Kidney biopsy is the gold standard method for determining the diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis in children presenting with kidney disease.
Method
All patients who underwent percutaneous native kidney biopsy in the our pediatric nephrology clinic between January 2018 and June 2023 were included. Age at the time of biopsy, gender, laboratory findings, indications for kidney biopsy, and histopathological results were examined retrospectively.
Results
A total of 77 patients (female; n = 35, 45.5% and male; n = 42, 54.5%) were recorded. The mean age at the time of biopsy was 11.4 ± 4.8 years (11.9 ± 5.1 years in females and 10.9 ± 4.6 years in males). The most frequent indications were as follows; idiopathic nephrotic syndrome in 35.7%, nephritic syndrome in 8.7%, asymptomatic urinary pathologies (asymptomatic proteinuria and/or haematuria) in 16%, kidney involvement in systemic diseases in 11.6%, acute kidney injury in 24.4%, and other indications in 3.6%. According to histopathological diagnosis, primary glomerulonephritis (GN) was the most common histopathologic findings (50.6%), including minimal change disease in 3.9%, focal segmental glomerulosclerosis in 18.2%, membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis in 23.4%, acute postinfectious glomerulonephritis in 3.9%, crescentric glomerulonephritis in 1.3%. Kidney involvement in systemic diseases and tubulointerstitial nephritis were found in 11.6% (IgA vasculitis in 7 cases and lupus nephritis in 2) and in 11.1% of cases, respectively. Non-diagnostic findings and insufficient material were determined in 11.2% and 6.2%, respectively. Three patients (3.9%) had normal kidney histology, while two had chronic changes (2.6%). The only complication after biopsy was perirenal hematoma in 14.8% of the patients, which did not require surgical intervention.
Conclusion
The most common indication for kidney biopsy was nephrotic syndrome, and the most common histopathological diagnosis was membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis. Post-biopsy complication rate was low and limited to perirenal hematoma.

title: #315 Hypomagnesemia-induced proximal tubular injury and nephrocalcinosis in rats: insights into FHHNC pathophysiology
authors: Takamasa Iwakura; Atsushi Kitamura; Chiemi Ema; Hideo Yasuda
abstract:
Background and Aims
Patients with hypomagnesemia experience a more rapid decline in renal function compared to those with normomagnesemia [1]. Inflammation and oxidative stress are implicated in the pathophysiology of hypomagnesemia-associated kidney injury [2], though the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In humans, mutations in Claudin-16 and Claudin-19 genes result in chronic hypomagnesemia due to increased urinary magnesium excretion. This condition, mediated through bone resorption triggered by elevated parathyroid hormone (PTH), leads to progressive renal dysfunction with nephrocalcinosis, a hallmark of Familial Hypomagnesemia, Hypercalciuria, and Nephrocalcinosis (FHHNC) [3]. However, while Claudin-16 knockout mice exhibit hypomagnesemia without nephrocalcinosis or kidney injury, and Claudin-19 knockout mice have shown no reported renal injury [4], the exact mechanisms remain poorly understood. Previous studies in rats have demonstrated that a magnesium-deficient diet can induce renal tubular injury with calcification [5]. In this study, we investigated renal injury in a rat model of hypomagnesemia induced by a low-magnesium diet in greater detail.
Method
Rats were fed a low-magnesium diet, and renal injury was evaluated histologically. Serum magnesium and other electrolytes, as well as PTH levels, were measured.
Results
Histological analysis of kidney tissue revealed dilated tubules in the corticomedullary region. These dilated tubules were negative for the proximal tubule marker megalin but positive for the dedifferentiation marker vimentin and the proximal tubule injury marker Kim-1, indicating proximal tubule injury. Additionally, calcium deposition was observed in these tubules, as evidenced by positive von Kossa staining. Serum analysis revealed hypomagnesemia, hypophosphatemia, and elevated PTH levels. Magnesium sulfate supplementation improved both serum electrolyte abnormalities and histological changes (Fig. 1).
Conclusion
The rat model of hypomagnesemia-induced proximal tubular injury with calcification demonstrated pathological and serological findings similar to FHHNC. This model may provide valuable insights and opportunities for developing novel treatments for FHHNC.

title: #3222 Efficacy evaluation of Telitacicept in IgA nephropathy: a real-world study
authors: Yong Jiang; Ke Li; Niansong Wang; Ying Fan
abstract:
Background and Aims
IgA nephropathy (IgAN), the most common primary glomerular disease worldwide, progresses to end-stage renal disease (ESRD) in 30%–40% of patients. Despite its significant clinical burden, treatment options for IgAN remain limited. Recent advances in understanding disease mechanisms have led to the development of novel biologic agents, including Telitacicept, a recombinant fusion protein that targets the dysregulated B cell/plasma cell pathway by neutralizing B lymphocyte stimulator (BLyS) and A proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL). This dual inhibition suppresses B cell-mediated autoimmune responses, offering a promising therapeutic approach. A phase II clinical trial has demonstrated Telitacicept's efficacy and safety in IgAN; however, real-world data are lacking. This study was designed to evaluate the real-world efficacy and safety of Telitacicept in Patients with IgAN.
Method
This study included 20 patients with biopsy-confirmed primary IgAN treated at Shanghai Sixth People's Hospital between 2023 and 2024. The average follow-up duration was 208.85 ± 96.82 days. Inclusion criteria included 24-hour urine protein levels >0.65 g and an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) >30 mL/min/1.73 m². All patients received subcutaneous Telitacicept at a dose of 160 mg per week for at least three months. Changes in clinical parameters, including 24-hour urine protein and eGFR, were assessed at 3 months and at the end of the study compared to baseline. Telitacicept-related adverse events were systematically recorded during the treatment period.
Results
After 3 months of Telitacicept treatment, the median 24-hour urine protein significantly decreased from 1.025 g/24 h at baseline to 0.59 g/24 h (z = −1.979, p < 0.05), while the median eGFR showed no significant change (69.78 mL/min/1.73 m² vs. 62.17 mL/min/1.73 m², p = 0.135). At the study endpoint, the median 24-hour urine protein further declined to 0.585 g/24 h (z = −1.96, p < 0.05), and the median eGFR remained stable (69.78 mL/min/1.73 m² to 58.03 mL/min/1.73 m², p = 0.904). The treatment was well-tolerated, with no reported adverse events such as respiratory infections, urinary tract infections, or injection site reactions.
Conclusion
In this analysis of a small single-center cohort, Telitacicept demonstrated significant efficacy in reducing proteinuria and preserve renal function in patients with IgAN over both short-term (3-month) and long-term (≥6-month) treatment periods. Additionally, it exhibited an excellent safety profile, with no treatment-related adverse events observed. These findings support the further investigation and clinical application of Telitacicept in the management of IgAN.

title: #1196 Histological analyses of kidney legion in IgA model mice induced by nasal treatment of Porphyromonas gingivalis
authors: Yasuyuki Nagasawa; Ryota Nomura; Taro Misaki; Seigo Ito; Yuto Suehiro; Kensaku Shojima; Kana Suehara; Daisuke Matsuoka; Shuhei Naka; Michiyo Nakano; Ken Shinmura; Kazuhiko Nakano
abstract:
Background and Aims
IgA nephropathy (IgAN) is one of most common primary glomerulonephritis, whose pathogenesis had remained unclear. We had reported that C. rectus and T. denticola, kinds of major periodontal disease bacteria, in tonsils with IgA nephropathy patients were specific to IgAN patients compared with habitual tonsillitis (Nagasawa-Y et al., Plos One, 2014). We also reported Porphyromonas gingivalis (Pg) and Tannerella forsythia which belongs to red complex of periodontal bacteria had been detected higher in tonsils with IgA nephropathy patients than those in habitual tonsilitis (Nagasawa-Y et al., Int J. Mol. Sci. 2021). But, in this point there was no evidence that these periodontal bacteria could cause IgA like kidney lesion in mice model.
To confirm that nasal treatment of Pg and Staphylococcus salivalius (Ss) which was known as one of normal oral bacteria as disease control in mice could cause IgAN like kidney lesion in mice model.
Method
First, we evaluate the IgAN like kidney lesion using PAS staining and IgA immune-fluorescence staining with time course at day 14, 28, 42, 56 from the beginning of nasal treatment of Pg in C57Black/6 mice. And also, deposition of immune complex in mesangial region using electron-microscopy. Second, we evaluated kidney lesion using PAS staining and IgA immune-fluorescence at day 42 after nasal treatment of living or killed Pg and Ss.
Results
At day 14,28, 42, 56, IgA like kidney legion had been observed significantly higher in mice treated with nasal Pg administration than in control mice. At day 42, 56, IgA immune-fluorescence staining had been observed significant higher in mice with nasal Pg administration than in control mice. Immune complex had been confirmed in mesangial area by electron microscopy. Then, at day 42, both living and Pg could cause IgA nephropathy kidney lesion in PAS staining and in IgA immune fluorescence staining, while living and killed Ss caused these IgA like kidney lesion with lower prevalence (See Fig. 1)
Conclusion
Both living and killed Pg belonging to red complex of periodontal bacteria could cause IgA like kidney lesion.

title: #1535 Prognostic indicators after treatment in IgA nephropathy
authors: Byoung-Soo Cho; Sung Min Jung; Hyaejin Yun; Hyunsoon Lee; Won Hee Cho; Daeyong Kim
abstract:
Background and Aims
IgA nephropathy is one of the most common chronic glomerulonephritis and 30%–45% fall into CKD over a period of 20 to 25 years. Lots of therapeutic regimens are tried such as corticosteroids, ARB/ACEi, endothelin inhibitors, complement inhibitors, Anti-APRIL/BAF, SGLT2 inhibitors etc., however there is no cure as yet.(2024,ASN). Decreased proteinuria have long been regarded as surrogate marker of therapeutic effects, however our group showed even without proteinuria, pathologically improved cases were only 50% (2024,ASN). In order to find out the prognostic indicator we performed follow up biopsy after treatment and compare the urinary findings and pathologic findings
Method
From 2013 to 2019, 256 cases of IgA nephropathy were diagnosed as IgA nephropathy at our clinic. 246 cases took methylprednisolone (MP) pulse therapy, of which 104 cases who showed clinical improvement took follow up renal biopsy. Follow up renal biopsy findings were divided into 3 groups: group A: treated IgA nephropathy (no EDD, restoration of foot process). Group B: improved renal pathology (decreased amount of EDD, disappearance of crescents, restored epithelial foot processes etc.), group C: no significant pathological changes. One cycle of MP consists of MP (20-30 mg/kg, max 1 gm/day) for 3 consecutive days, depends on renal pathology by Lee's classification. We performed 3 to 17 cycles every 2 weeks.
Results
Male to female ratio were 52:52. Mean ages were 31.4 years old. Of the 246 cases who took MP pulse therapies 104 cases were performed follow up renal biopsy were performed who showed improved urinary findings. Follow up renal biopsy results were as follows: Group A were 35 cases, Group B 48 cases and Group C 21 cases. No patients relapsed during 8.4 years follow up in group A & B, however 2 cases were relapsed in group C.
Conclusion
In addition to clinical findings disappearance of EDD, disappearance of crescents, restoration of epithelial foot process should be regarded as cure in IgA nephropathy.
In group B and C: close monitoring at least every 3 months is mandatory to check relapse.
Follow up renal biopsy might be a mandatory procedure to confirm the treatment effects in IgA nephropathy.

title: #3271 Effect of immunosuppressive therapy with cyclosporine on arterial stiffness in patients with glomerulonephritis
authors: Adamantia Bratsiakou; Marios Papasotiriou; Areti Alafaki; Panagiota Perdiki; Georgia Andriana Georgopoulou; Anna Kanta; Evangelos Papachristou; Dimitrios Goumenos
abstract:
Background and Aims
Immunosuppressive treatment with cyclosporine has been the main therapeutic option in patients with glomerulonephritis, mainly with membranous nephropathy, in the past decades. Chronic administration of cyclosporine is associated with glomerulosclerosis and arterial hypertension. The aim of the present study was to determine whether cyclosporine administration could cause deterioration of arterial stiffness indices.
Method
In this prospective open label cohort study, we included 140 patients (93 males) with a medical history of primary or secondary glomerulonephritis, who were divided into three groups according to whether they had received cyclosporine during the study, in the past, or had never received cyclosporine as immunosuppressive therapy. Participants were followed as outpatients every three to six months for 2 years. During their visits, all the participants underwent central blood pressure (cBP) and pulse wave velocity (PWV) measurements with mobli-O-graph device, while basic laboratory testing was performed at each visit.
Results
Twenty patients (M:F = 12:8) were receiving immunosuppressive treatment with cyclosporine during the study, 31 (M:F = 21:10) had received cyclosporine in the past, while 90 patients (M:F = 60:30) had never received cyclosporine. The three groups did not differ in terms of mean age (52.1 ± 17.5 vs 57.7 ± 11.3 vs 52.9 ± 16.6 years, respectively, P = 0.288), the presence of diabetes mellitus, arterial hypertension, and heart failure. Accordingly, PWV was higher in the group receiving cyclosporine during the study compared to the group that had received in the past, while patients who had never received cyclosporine had the lowest PWV values ​​[8.5 (6.7–9.6) vs 8.0 (7.0–9.9) vs 7.5 (6.1–9.4) m/sec, respectively, P = 0.023]. Regarding cSBP, patients receiving cyclosporine during the study had a higher median value compared to those who had previously received or had never received cyclosporine; however, the difference was not statistically significant [120.3 (109.9–136.5) vs 117.3 (105.9–124.4) vs 118.0 (109.1–130.4), respectively, P = 0.120].
Conclusion
Immunosuppressive therapy based on cyclosporine, a popular treatment option especially for patients with membranous nephropathy, could worsen arterial stiffness indices.

title: #3725 Rituximab efficacy and safety in patients with glomerular diseases: a single centre experience
authors: Farid Ghalli; Nicholas Dalmon
abstract:
Background and Aims
Glomerulonephritis is an autoimmune glomerular inflammation that can lead to severe morbidity and mortality if left untreated. Conventional treatment for this condition involves the use of glucocorticoids and immunosuppressive drugs. In recent years, Rituximab has gained popularity as a treatment for several types of glomerular diseases. Rituximab is a monoclonal antibody that targets the CD20 protein expressed on the surface of B cells. Rituximab has shown promising results in the treatment of a variety of glomerular diseases, including minimal change disease, focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, membranous nephropathy, ANCA vasculitis, and lupus nephritis.
This work was performed to study the efficacy and safety of Rituximab in patients with different glomerular diseases managed with the drug in our renal unit.
Method
This work was conducted in 2022–2023, retrospectively collecting data of adult patients with different glomerular disease treated with Rituximab between January 2019 and October 2022 in a large teaching hospital in the United Kingdom. Data of patients were collected from the electronic patient records system and patient notes.
Results
A total of 83 patients were included in the analysis 40 Females and 43 Males. The mean age of all the patients was 56 years with range being 20–89 years. Patients had a range of glomerular diseases for which they were treated. The cohort of patients included patients with different glomerular diseases presenting with nephritic (28 patients) and nephrotic presentations (55 patients). Number of patients according to the disease : ANCA Glomerulonephritis (25), Membranous Nephropathy (18), Minimal Change Disease (15), Lupus Nephritis (10) , Focal Segmental Glomerulosclerosis (9), Immune Complex GN(3), and C1q Nephropathy (2) and mesangial proliferative glomerulonephritis (1).
Patients with nephrotic presentations had significant improvement in their Urinary Protein Creatinine Ratio (UPCR) (P = <0.001). There was also significant suppression of B cell load (P = <0.001).
We analysed patients presented with both nephritic and nephrotic presentations (81 patients) looking at kidney survival (2 patients excluded as they were on dialysis and had Rituximab for relapse with pulmonary haemorrhage). Only 7 patients (9%) progressed to end stage renal disease (ESRD) and dialysis suggesting Rituximab had (91%) success rate in preserving renal survival and preventing progression to ESRD and dialysis treatment.
The length of time B cells stayed suppressed (<1%) was analysed. B cells stayed suppressed for a significant amount of time longer than the six-month dosing schedule of Rituximab (P = <0.001). This suppression was significantly longer in males than females (P < 0.01).
The safety of Rituximab was also assessed. Patients received 263 doses during the study period. Fifteen adverse effects were recorded. Five patients sadly died during the study period. Of significance, one patient died due to COVID-19 infection and another one due to septic colonic perforation.
Conclusion
Rituximab was effective in preserving renal survival and stopping progression to ESRD in patients with the different studied glomerular diseases. It was highly effective in treating proteinuria and suppressing B cells for a significantly longer time than the known six-month period. This point at the possible use of longer dosing interval regimens for patients may be appropriate.
Rituximab is a safe drug to use in the patients with glomerulonephritis with clear efficacy in managing renal disease and a good safety profile.

title: #477 The role of antithrombin III deficiency in hypercoagulability of nephrotic syndrome: insights from a cross-sectional study
authors: Iryna Mykhaloiko
abstract:
Background and Aims
Nephrotic syndrome (NS), a clinical manifestation of glomerular diseases, is defined by significant proteinuria (>3.5 g/day), hypoalbuminemia, edema, and hyperlipidemia. Patients with NS are at a heightened risk of thromboembolic events, with incidence rates ranging from 3% to 44%, influenced by thrombosis localization and screening methods. The hypercoagulable state in NS arises from multiple mechanisms, including the urinary loss of natural anticoagulants such as antithrombin III (AT-III) and protein S, increased hepatic synthesis of coagulation factors, and impaired fibrinolytic activity. AT-III deficiency, commonly observed in NS, is attributed to its molecular similarity to albumin, resulting in parallel urinary losses. Despite its potential relevance, the contribution of AT-III deficiency to NS-associated hypercoagulability and its utility in guiding thromboembolic prophylaxis remain inadequately investigated.
This study aimed to evaluate the prevalence of AT-III deficiency in patients with primary glomerulonephritis (GN) and NS and to assess its correlation with markers of NS severity and hypercoagulability.
Method
A cross-sectional observational study was conducted involving 76 patients diagnosed with primary glomerulonephritis (GN) and nephrotic syndrome (NS) at the Ivano-Frankivsk Regional Clinical Hospital, Ukraine, during the period from 2022 to 2024. The inclusion criteria encompassed adults aged over 18 years, diagnosed with NS within the last month, and having eGFR greater than 60 ml/min/1.73 m². Patients with systemic vasculitis, diabetes, significant cardiovascular conditions, or active infections were excluded from the study. Serum levels of AT-III were quantified using a photometric assay with chromogenic substrates.
Results
Among the 76 patients, 62 (81.6%) were men, and 14 (18.4%) were women, with a median age of 45 years (IQR: 40–49). Normal AT-III levels (80–130%) were found in 24 patients (31.6%), while 52 patients (68.4%) had decreased AT-III levels (<80%). Patients with decreased AT-III levels demonstrated:
Correlation analysis showed:
No significant association was found between AT-III levels and histological variants of GN or platelet count, suggesting that AT-III deficiency and hypercoagulability are independent of the underlying glomerular pathology.
Conclusion
In this study, 68.4% of patients with primary GN and NS had reduced AT-III levels, which were associated with lower serum albumin, higher DPE, and increased ACR, highlighting the link between AT-III deficiency and NS severity.
No significant association was observed between AT-III deficiency and specific histological variants of GN, suggesting that the hypercoagulable state in NS may be independent of glomerular pathology. Elevated D-dimer and fibrinogen levels further support the role of AT-III deficiency in NS-associated hypercoagulability.

title: #691 Histological changes and a3ß1 integrin and MMP-1 expressions in early Fabry nephropathy in female patients
authors: Rodrigo Hagemann; Valeria Soares Pigozzi Veloso; Aline Santana; Regiane Da Cunha; Guilherme Miniskiskosky; Paulo Cézar Gregorio; Andréa E M Stinghen; Fellype Barreto
abstract:
Background and Aims
Fabry nephropathy (FN), characterized by proteinuira and progressive loss of renal function, may lead to ESKD and, consequently, to significant morbidity and mortality. Due to the skewed X inactivation, Fabry manifestations, including FN, may be overlooked in female patients. The α3β1 integrins are widely expressed in podocytes and enable their attachment to the glomerular basement membrane. Matrix metalloproteinase 1 (MMP-1) shows increased expression under conditions of tissue destruction. The aim of the present study was to evaluate the renal involvement, by laboratory and histological assessment, in female patients with Fabry Disease (FD) caused by a new mutation at diagnosis and compare the effects of enzyme replacement therapy.
Method
Longitudinal, analytical and prospective study. The index case was identified during screening for FD in a hemodialysis unit. Thereafter, family screening was performed. Female patients with proven diagnosis of FD were included in the study. Kidney biopsy was performed at diagnosis. Laboratory, kidney histology and immunohistochemistry were performed to assess FN. All patients needed to start enzyme replacement therapy (ERT), Agalsidase beta: 1.0 mg/Kg; e.o.w., due to Fabry manifestations. Data were analyzed using Chi-Square, Mann-Whitney tests and Spearman correlation
Results
In the period from March 2014 to December 2020, five female patients with FD (p.G35V) were treated with ERT. The median age at baseline was 30 (21.5 ± 47) years-old, while at the time of biopsy it was 30 (22 ± 47) and at the beginning of ERT it was 32 (22.5 ± 47). None of the patients had angiokeratoma, 60% had hypohidrosis and all patients had cornea verticillata and acroparesthesias. The median values for creatinine were 0.9 (0.7;0.9) mg/dL, for estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) were 96 (84; 114.5) ml/min, for 24 hours albuminuria 12 (5.9; 315.5) mg and for 24 hours proteinuria 0.22 (0.10; 0.48) mg. The light microscopy analysis showed a podocyte score of 3 (2.49; 3), global sclerosis of 0 (0.1), segmental sclerosis of 0 (0.1), pericapsular fibrosis of 4% (1.5; 8.5), intimal fibrosis of 1% (1; 1.5) and interstitial fibrosis of 5%. The electron microscopy analysis showed a podocyte inclusion score of 3 (2; 3.83). The presence of inclusion in parietal cells and distal tubules was found in 100% of patients. No patient showed inclusion in proximal tubule cells. Inclusion was also observed in the intimal/medial region of one patient, medial of another patient and undetermined in a third patient. The immunohistochemistry evaluation showed 29.42 (18; 64.55) of Integrin α3β1 in glomeruli and 27.32 (19.75; 48.65) in the proximal tubules). MMPI in fibrosis area was 21.27 (17.11; 66; 74) and in the perifibrosis area was 46.36 (25.85; 138.56). Statistically significant correlations were: MMP1 in fibrosis area and age at baseline (r = 0.9; P = 0.037), MMP1 in fibrosis area and Gb3 serum levels at baseline (r = 0.9; P = 0.037), GFR reduction and albuminuria (r = 0.9; P = 0.037), Integrin α3β1 in glomeruli and podocyt score (r = −0.89; P = 0.041) and Integrin α3β1 in the proximal tubules and podocyte score (r = −0.89; P = 0.041).
Conclusion
Kidney biopsies in women showed histological and immunohistochemistry changes of FN, even in the early stages of CKD and in the absence of high albuminuria. Therefore, kidney biopsy with α3β1 evaluation of the expression of integrins and MMP-1 might help to identify early stages of Fabry nephropathy.

title: #774 Reduced cumulative glucocorticoid toxicity in patients with minimal change disease treated with lower dose prednisolone and activated vitamin D: results from the ADAPT trial
authors: Tilde Kristensen; Anne Daugaard Thuesen; Ditte Hansen; Frank Mose; Rikke Borg; Ann-Maria Gramkow; Jon Waarst Gregersen; Marsela Resuli; Henrik Birn; Per Ivarsen
abstract:
Background and Aims
Minimal change disease (MCD) is traditionally treated with high-dose prednisolone, which is associated with significant adverse effects, and glucocorticoid-associated toxicity may lead to dose-dependent serious or permanent impairments. The toxicity of glucocorticoids can be estimated using a scale of more than 20 specific weighted items related to the adverse effects of glucocorticoids with higher scores indicating greater severity of toxicity. The Glucocorticoid Toxicity Index (GTI) has been validated as a construct [1]. We aimed to explore if a lower dose of prednisolone in MCD is associated with reduced glucocorticoid-induced toxicity and better quality of life.
Method
A Danish multicentre, prospective, open-label, randomized controlled trial examining the efficacy and safety of a lower dose of prednisolone (0.5 mg/kg/day) in combination with alfacalcidol (0.5 µg/day) in patients with biopsy-proven MCD and nephrotic syndrome when compared to standard higher-dose prednisolone (1 mg/kg/day). We calculated the differences in scores between baseline and specific time points as well as the cumulative worsening score (GTI CWS). These were calculated with and without LDL-cholesterol and BMI because nephrotic syndrome affects cholesterol metabolism, and body weight is often unreliable due to fluid retention. Quality of life was measured by the SF36 questionnaire.
Results
A total of 67 adults with MCD were included. The mean cumulative prednisolone dose was significantly lower in patients treated with lower-dose prednisolone and alfacalcidol (Table 1). The median GTI CWS (both including and excluding BMI and LDL) in the lower dose prednisolone and alfacalcidol group was significantly less than in the standard high dose prednisolone group, while no significant differences were observed in the differences in GTI scores compared to baseline (Table 1). Furthermore, there were no significant differences in the SF36 physical or mental component scores.
Conclusion
A significantly lower GTI CWS was observed in patients treated with a lower dose of prednisolone in combination with alfacalcidol compared to patients treated with the standard high dose of prednisolone. Across a variety of diseases with comparable cumulative doses of prednisolone, the GTI emerges as a plausible instrument for evaluating glucocorticoid toxicity. This evaluation is valuable in patients with MCD, who are often treated with high cumulative doses of prednisolone. Surprisingly, no variations were observed in the SF36 between the two treatment groups.
