title: #311 Impact of a single hemodialysis session with MCO and high-flux membranes on FGF-23, phosphorus, and endothelial function in patients with CKD
authors: Rachel Armani
abstract:
Background and Aims
Endothelial dysfunction is a key marker of vascular disease and a significant contributor to cardiovascular mortality in chronic kidney disease (CKD). Elevated levels of FGF-23 and phosphorus, both uremic toxins, impair endothelial function, further increasing cardiovascular risks in this population. Medium cut-off (MCO) membranes have been introduced to enhance the clearance of larger toxins, like FGF-23, compared to high-flux membranes. However, the impact of MCO membrane on FGF-23 levels and endothelial function remain uncertain.
To evaluate the acute effects of MCO and high-flux membranes, during a single hemodialysis session, on FGF-23, phosphorus and endothelial function in patients with CKD.
Method
This study is an exploratory analysis of 32 patients with CKD enrolled in a previous prospective study. FGF23 and phosphorus levels, and endothelial function assessed by the reactive hyperemia index (RHI), were measured immediately before and after the first dialysis session with each membrane type (MCO and high-flux). Statistical analyses included paired comparisons to evaluate changes and multivariable linear regression models to explore the relation between variables changes and endothelial function.
Results
The study evaluated 32 CKD patients, with hypertension (72%) and autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease as the main etiologies of CKD. Clinical and demographic characteristics were similar between the MCO and high-flux groups. Phosphorus levels decreased similarly in both groups, although post-dialysis FGF-23 was significantly lower in the MCO group (P = 0.02), showing a decrease in FGF-23 with MCO and an increase with high-flux (P = 0.02 for both). Endothelial function, measured by RHI, did not differ significantly between groups. Multivariate analysis showed that, in the MCO group, a 1 mg/dL phosphorus reduction was linked to a 0.55 unit increase in post-dialysis RHI (P = 0.002), while a 1-unit FGF-23 reduction corresponded to a 0.0016 unit decrease in RHI (P = 0.003).
Conclusion
The MCO membrane demonstrated superior efficacy in reducing FGF-23 levels compared to the High-flux membrane. However, this reduction did not translate into immediate improvements in endothelial function, as measured by the RHI, suggesting that the vascular benefits of FGF-23 clearance may depend on longer-term evaluation.

title: #380 Evaluation of multidisciplinary care pathways on renal function in patients with advanced chronic kidney disease: a multicentric study
authors: Helene Pages; Georgios Kosmadakis; Clemence Deville; Julien Baudenon; Aura Necoara; Ioana Enache; Fatima El Kanouni
abstract:
Background and Aims
Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a significant public health issue due to its increasing prevalence and associated high morbidity and mortality rates. This study evaluates the impact of multidisciplinary care pathways (MDPs) consisting of medical, dietetical and coordinating nurse follow ups, on renal function, survival, clinic biological parameters and quality of life in patients with advanced CKD (stages 4 and 5).
Method
A retrospective analysis of clinical and biological parameters was conducted, alongside a prospective assessment of quality of life using the EQ-5D-5L tool.
Results
Among 359 patients (141 complete follow-up, 100 partial follow-up, and 118 medical-only), mortality rates were significantly higher in the medical-only group (26%) compared to complete (8%) and partial follow-up (16%) (P < 0.001). No significant differences were observed in renal function progression or dialysis initiation. Autonomy and overall quality of life in the medical-only group were significantly lower (P = 0.05 and P = 0.037, respectively), as well as the quality of life visual self-assessment (P = 0.024).
Conclusion
These findings suggest that participation in MDPs decreases mortality and improves quality of life, while it does not significantly change renal function progression or dialysis initiation.

title: #989 Adherence to a healthy plant-based diet and cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic risk factors among patients with chronic kidney disease
authors: Ting-Yun Lin; Szu-Chun Hung
abstract:
Background and Aims
The confluence of cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) risk factors and chronic kidney disease (CKD) is strongly linked to risk for adverse cardiovascular and kidney outcomes. Mounting evidence has emerged on the benefits of plant-based diets for CKD management. However, whether the benefits are mediated by improved CKM health are unclear. In addition, there remain concerns about the risk of malnutrition and hyperkalemia associated with plant-based diets among patients with established CKD.
Method
We examined the association between adherence to plant-based diets and CKM risk in a cross-sectional analysis of nondialysis patients with CKD stages 3–5. Responses to a food frequency questionnaire developed for the Asian population with CKD were used to calculate a healthy plant-based diet score (HPDS), which reflects higher consumption of plant foods and reduced intake of animal products and sugar. CKM risk factors included overweight/obesity, central obesity, high blood pressure, high triglycerides, and high blood glucose. Nutritional status was assessed using serum albumin and dietary energy and protein intake.
Results
A total of 147 patients (89 men and 58 women; median age 66 years) with CKD (median eGFR 23.1 ml/min/1.73 m2) were included. In multivariable logistic regression analyses, a higher HPDS was associated with a significantly lower odds of overweight/obesity (OR, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.75–0.92), central obesity (OR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.79–0.94), hypertension (OR, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.76–0.95), hypertriglyceridemia (OR, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.82–0.98), and hyperglycemia (OR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.80–0.98), but a significantly higher odds of normal serum albumin ≥3.8 g/dl (OR, 1.22; 95% CI, 1.07–1.39), dietary protein intake ≥0.6 g/kg/day (OR, 1.13; 95% CI, 1.04–1.23), and dietary energy intake ≥25 g/kg/day (OR, 1.23; 95% CI, 1.12–1.36). No association was found between HPDS and hyperkalemia (OR, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.77–1.07).
Conclusion
In patients with moderate to advanced CKD, an unhealthy plant-based diet was associated with an increased risk of CKM syndrome. Adherence to a healthy plant-based diet was not associated with risk of hyperkalemia and was more likely to achieve a better nutritional status.

title: #1200 Ensembling survival models to optimize renal outcome predictions in chronic kidney disease patients: a retrospective cohort study
authors: Ka Chun Leung; Desmond Yap
abstract:
Background and Aims
Predictive models for progression and mortality in Chronic kidney disease (CKD) often show limitations in accuracy and generalizability, particularly in diverse populations [1]. This study evaluates the impact of ensembling multiple AI survival models to enhance the performance in predicting renal replacement therapy (RRT) initiation and all-cause mortality in CKD patients.
Method
This retrospective study utilized data from 34 253 non-transplant stage G3–G5 CKD patients with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) <60 ml/min/1.73 m² for over 3 months across outpatient clinics in 3 acute hospitals in Hong Kong. Different combinations of fourteen deep-learning survival models were ensembled by averaging their cumulative incidence function (CIF) predictions to optimize prediction performance. The discrimination and calibration evaluation of the models included concordance index, Brier scores, and negative log-likelihood across varying ensemble sizes [2].
Results
A total of 28 866 participants’ data were utilized for model training, and 5387 participants’ data were isolated as a test set for model evaluation. Ensembling improved predictive performance across all metrics. The concordance index for RRT initiation (Event 1) and all-cause mortality (Event 2) increased progressively with the number of models ensembled. The concordance index of Event 1 stabilized at 0.98, with 5 model predictions ensembled (95% CI 0.9807–0.9808). It seems Event 2 needs more models’ predictions to achieve stabilization, while ensembling 9 models’ predictions got a concordance index of 0.82 (95% CI 0.8223–0.8239) (Fig. 1). Similarly, integrated Brier scores and negative log-likelihood decreased as more models were ensembled, demonstrating better calibration and risk estimation (Figs 2 and 3). The analysis confirmed that ensembling effectively reduces prediction uncertainty and enhances clinical interpretability.
Conclusion
Model ensembling to improve AI-driven survival predictions in CKD patients, which may potentially facilitate personalized management and better allocation of healthcare resources. Future work should validate these findings in broader populations to establish scalability and clinical applicability.

title: #1283 The association between changes of the difference between cystatin C and creatinine-based estimated GFR and intrinsic capacity: an analysis of the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS)
authors: Dingyi Wang; Xin Liu; Yuting Kang; Guohui Fan
abstract:
Background and Aims
Intrinsic capacity (IC) and has been considered as a reliable reference for implications in the healthcare of the elderly. Renal function decline was associated with frailty and functional impairment. We aimed explore the association between the change of estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) difference (eGFRdiffcysc-cr), estimated by cystatin C (cys-C)-eGFR minus serum creatinine (Scr)-eGFR, and simultaneous IC change overtime, thus provide measurements for predictions of functional decline among the elderly in community.
Method
Data was obtained from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). A total of 17708 adults completed the baseline survey in 2011 (wave 1) and were followed up in 2015 (wave 3). Participants aged ≥60 years at baseline and with intact IC values, cys-C and Scr in 2011 and 2015 were included. eGFRs were calculated according to 2009 and 2021 CKD Epidemiology Collaboration (CKD-EPI) equations. eGFRdiffcysc-cr = eGFRcysc−eGFRcr, eGFRdiffcysc-cr slope = (eGFRdiffcysc-cr-2015−eGFRdiffcysc-cr-2011)/4. The primary outcome was the IC change for four years. The mixed-effect linear regression with random effects was conducted to explore the change of eGFRdiffcysc-cr between 2011 and 2018 to IC declines. Related covariates were selected for the adjustment in multivariate regression. Odds ratios (ORs) for the association of baseline eGFRdiffcysc-cr and annual change of eGFRdiffcysc-cr to IC decline were also estimated.
Results
A total of 2,026 participants were included in our final analysis. Baseline eGFRcr and eGFRcysc was 99.2 ± 19.3 ml/min·1.73 m2 and 91.1 ± 19.6 ml/min·1.73 m2, respectively. IC was stable or elevated in 1180 (58.2%) participants and decreased in 846 (41.8%) participants during the four years. Those who had decreased IC were older and with higher baseline IC. The slope of eGFRdiffcysc-cr was significantly associated with IC change after adjusting covariates (β = 0.034, 95% CI 0.008, 0.059, P = 0.0091). Subgroup analysis showed that for participants with baseline eGFRcr ≥60 ml/min·1.73 m2, female and rural residents, eGFRdiffcysc-cr slopes were significantly associated with IC change. Either the slope of eGFRdiffcysc-cr less than 1 ml/min·1.73 m2 or over 4 ml/min·1.73 m2 would be risk factor for IC decline. Vitality decline was mostly prevalent (82.3%) among the five domains of IC and associated with the slope of eGFRdiffcysc-cr (OR 1.023, 95% CI 1.000, 1.046, P = 0.049).
Conclusion
eGFRdiffcysc-cr slope was significantly associated with IC change over time, especially with vitality, indicating its potential on predicting functional decline for the elderly. It is necessary to regularly obtain measures of cys-C in addition to Scr throughout the longitudinal care of the elderly, for a more comprehensive assessment of the entire functional well-being.

title: #1558 The correlation between tubulointerstitial inflammation and leukocyturia: a classic revisited
authors: Paula Milhazes Guimarães; Nuno Moreira Fonseca; Mário Ventura Góis; Helena Viana; David Navarro
abstract:
Background and Aims
Tubulointerstitial nephritis is characterized by inflammation of the tubules and interstitial tissue, and it is classically associated with the presence of leukocyturia. However, the direct association with the severity of renal interstitial inflammation remains uncertain and a subject of debate.
Method
This is a retrospective study aimed at evaluating the correlation between the intensity of renal interstitial inflammation (regardless of histological diagnosis) and the degree of leukocyturia. Patients aged ⩾18 who underwent renal biopsy in 2022 at Curry Cabral Hospital were included. From these, 94 patients with contemporaneous automated urine analysis were selected and 2 were excluded due to insufficient histological material. The severity of histological renal interstitial inflammation and fibrosis was assessed by two nephropathologists using a semiquantitative method and classified as absent, mild (0% to <25%), moderate (25% to 75%), or severe (>75%). Leukocyturia and hematuria were quantified based on automated urine analysis by flow cytometry and were considered positive when ⩾25 cells/ µL.
Demographic and clinical data were analyzed, including age, gender, serum creatinine, estimated glomerular filtration rate (calculated using the CKD-EPI equation for eGFR), and urinary protein excretion (in grams per 24 hours, or protein/creatinine ratio [g/g] when 24-hour collection was unavailable). Categorical variables are presented as frequencies; continuous variables, when normally distributed, are reported as mean ± standard deviation (SD); otherwise, they are presented as median (interquartile range). Logistic regression using a stepwise approach (P ≤ 0.1) was conducted to identify potential predictors associated with histological lesions. Subsequently, a multivariate logistic regression model was developed to account for potential confounding factors. All tests were conducted using STATA v16.1 (StataCorp, College Station, TX). A significance level of P < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
Results
Ninety-two patients were included, of whom 65% were male (n = 60) with a mean age of 57 years. At the time of renal biopsy, patients had a mean eGFR of 31 ml/min/1.73 m², a protein-to-creatinine ratio of 1.4 g/g, with 36.9% presenting leukocyturia (34/92) and 41.3% hematuria (38/92). The distribution of renal interstitial inflammation severity was classified as absent in 16/92, mild in 25/92, moderate in 25/92, severe in 21/92, and not documented in 5 patients. Histological diagnosis corresponded to interstitial nephritis in 12 cases (7 acute; 5 chronic) or other diagnoses in the remaining 80 biopsies.
Patients with a histological diagnosis of interstitial nephritis did not present leukocyturia more frequently than those with other histological diagnoses (25% vs. 38.8%, P = 0.357).
Univariate analysis documented no association between the degree of tubulointerstitial inflammation and the degree of leukocyturia [OR: −0.002 (−0.005 to 0.007); P = 0.147]. In a multivariate analysis model including leukocyturia, hematuria, proteinuria, age, gender, and glomerular filtration rate, leukocyturia remained unassociated with the degree of tubulointerstitial inflammation [OR: −0.003 (CI: −0.006 to 0.008); P = 0.134].
Conclusion
Despite the presence of leukocyturia in a significant number of patients (34/92), this study's findings did not reveal an association between the presence (or degree) of tubulointerstitial inflammation and the presence (or degree) of leukocyturia. These findings suggest that leukocyturia, although classically described as such, is not a sensitive marker for tubulointerstitial inflammation or for estimating its intensity. These results warrant validation through prospective and controlled evaluation, as well as research into biomarkers with higher sensitivity and specificity.

title: #1736 Treatment with inclisiran in patients with nonfamilial hypercholesterolemia and chronic kidney disease
authors: Andrea Dello Strologo; Antonio Bellasi; Aldo Franculli; Pasquale Saporito; Laura Pedata; Paola Peverini; Giuseppe Grandaliano; Luca Di Lullo
abstract:
Background and Aims
Patients with chronic kidney disease have a high incidence of morbidity and mortality from cardiovascular causes. Among the most significant cardiovascular risk factors is undoubtedly hypercholesterolemia, especially elevated cholesterol-LDL levels. The first-line therapy for the management of hypercholesterolemia, including in patients with chronic kidney disease, is represented by statins even in combination with ezetimibe. In patients with chronic kidney disease, statin therapy is often poorly tolerated with high incidence of rhabdomyolysis. An alternative treatment is represented by siRNA Inclisiran, which has been shown to be effective in double yearly administration.
Method
Thirty-two patients (19 male and 13 female) with a mean age of 60.2 years, basal total cholesterol values of 225 mg/dl and LDL cholesterol values of 138 mg/dl were enrolled in our observational study. title: #2202 Prospective controlled trial of the effects of different renal biopsy needle sizes on the number of glomeruli collected and their associated complications
authors: Seiji Hashimoto; Eiichiro Tamaki; Naoyuki Takaoka; Yuki Hata; Keiichi Fujita; Mari Kusube; Yukiko Yamano; Shin-Ichi Araki
abstract:
Background and Aims
A renal biopsy, which is an essential procedure for the diagnosis of renal diseases, is commonly performed with an automatic biopsy needle under ultrasound guidance. Generally, 14G–18G biopsy needles are used at the discretion of the physician at each hospital depending on individual experience. Larger needles can collect a larger volume of material with one needle pass but cause greater blood loss, whereas smaller needles perceivably have the opposite effects. Since a certain specimen volume needs to be collected for making a diagnosis, the use of smaller needles necessitates increasing the number of passes.
Method
Given that the effects of different biopsy needles have not been previously studied, we conducted a prospective randomized controlled trial to compare various outcomes of using a 16G (n = 82) or 18G (n = 78) needle for renal biopsies on enrolled patients.
Results
No significant differences between the two needle groups were observed in terms of the hematoma size on ultrasound images, decrease in hemoglobin (Hb) levels, changes in renal function, severity of hematuria, or blood pressure immediately after the renal biopsy and on the following day. None of the patients required surgical treatment, and although the incidence of macroscopic hematuria was slightly higher for the 16G needle group, the difference between the groups was not significant. The earlobe bleeding time and Hb levels were not correlated. In total, 4.8 passes were needed with the 18G needle, whereas 4.0 passes were performed with the 16G needle (with no significant difference). The number of glomeruli collected tended to be slightly higher for the 16G needle group (18G (17 ± 11) vs 16G (21 ± 12), but varied greatly among the patients, and no significant difference was observed between the two groups. Although glomerular fragments were counted separately, no difference was observed between the two groups.
Conclusion
16G and 18G biopsy needles were comparable in terms of efficacy and adverse effects. Therefore, the selection of biopsy needles based on the experience of operators and other factors seems acceptable.

title: #2394 The creatinine triples after a Whipple: a case of chronic kidney disease due to secondary oxalate nephropathy 27 years post-pancreaticoduodenectomy
authors: Gayoung Oh; Hsu Pheen Chong
abstract:
Background and Aims
Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and chronic pancreatitis are recognised causes of oxalate nephropathy secondary to fat malabsorption [1]. Whipple's procedure is a lesser known cause of oxalate nephropathy—there is only one other reported case to this date [2].
Method
We present the case of a 55-year-old female with a background of Type 2 diabetes, hypertension and Whipple's procedure performed 27 years prior for a benign pancreatic cyst. The patient presented with abdominal pain, back pain and weight loss with an incidental finding of declining renal function over one and a half years. Her creatinine had increased from 66 μmol/L in February 2023, to 103 μmol/Lin November 2023, and 194 μmol/L at this encounter (Table 1).
Results
Urine dipstick was unremarkable and showed no active urinary sediments. Urine creatinine was 6.3 mmol/L, urine albumin was 5.1 mg/L and urine albumin:creatinine ratio was 0.8 mg/mmol. A full myeloma and autoimmune panel were negative. Total oxalate excretion over 24 hours was 899 μmol/24 h. Renal biopsy demonstrated intra-tubular oxalate crystals with moderate tubulointerstitial atrophy and glomerular basement membrane thickening suggestive of diabetic glomerulopathy. Faecal elastase was <15 μg/g, indicating severe exocrine pancreatic insufficiency. She was diagnosed with chronic kidney disease due to secondary oxalate nephropathy 27 years after her Whipple's procedure. She remains under follow-up with the mainstay of treatment being hydration, pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy and a low oxalate diet.
Conclusion
Through this unusual case, we aim to raise awareness of Whipple's procedure being a cause of oxalate nephropathy, and highlight the possibility of the onset of chronic kidney disease occurring decades after the operation.

title: #2496 Chronic kidney disease is a major risk factor for mortality in triglyceride deposit cardiomyovasculopathy patients
authors: Yasuyuki Nagasawa; Satomi Okamura; Yuki Nishimura; Tomomi Yamada; Hideyuki Miyauchi; Yuusuke Nakano; Tetsuya Amano; Yuuko Kawaguchi; Shinichiro Fujimoto; Kenichi Hirano
abstract:
Background and Aims
Triglyceride deposit cardiomyovasculopathy (TGCV) (Orphanet ORPHA code: 692305) is a rare cardiovascular disorder (Hirano K et al., N Engl J Med, 2008) I that was first reported in 2008 in a Japanese patient requiring cardiac transplantation. TGCV is caused by defective intracellular lipolysis of triglyceride (TG), resulting in heart failure and diffuse narrowing atherosclerosis with TG deposition. Primary TGCV (ORPHA code: 565612) is caused by rare homozygous mutation in the PNPLA2 gene encoding adipose triglyceride lipase (ATGL), an essential molecule to hydrolyze intracellular TG (Hirano K et al., N Engl J Med, 2008) in the majority of patients with TGCV, genetic causes or backgrounds remain undetermined and they are designated as idiopathic TGCV (ORPHA code: 692296) (Li M, et al., Orphanet J Rare Dis, 2019). Recently, a TGCV study group reported that TGCV patients were typically diagnosed in their mid-60s, using the TGCV patient registry (Hirano K, et al. JACC:Adv. 2023). In this registry, around half of the patients had suffered from a cardiovascular event in the 5 years after their diagnosis, and almost 30% of the TGCV patients had died.
In this study, we evaluated the major mortality risk factors of CKD, DM, HT, and DL in TGCV patients using the TGCV patient registry.
Method
This study is basically sub-analyses of the previous clinical study, which revealed the overall survival rate of TGCV patients. The detailed methods of the original study were described elsewhere (Hirano K, et al. JACC:Adv. 2023). Briefly, TGCV patients who were diagnosed using the TGCV criteria, which were made by the Japan TGCV Study Group, had been registered in the TGCV registry supported by the Japan Agency of Medical Research and Development (NCT05345223). The ethics committees of Osaka University (Approval No. 20334) approved this registry study. All adult patients diagnosed with TGCV before December 2021 were included retrospectively, and the number of subjects was 183 (76% male). The 3-year overall survival rate was 80.1%, and the 5-year overall survival rate was 71.8%. In this retrospective registry, baseline characteristics include information on major comorbidities, such as chronic kidney disease (CKD), hypertension (HT), dyslipidemia (DL), and diabetes mellitus (DM). TGCV patients were divided into subgroups according to the comorbidities such as CKD, HT, DL, and DM, and the Kaplan-Meier method for survival rates with these comorbidities was used.
Results
The 3-year survival rate was 71.3% in the CKD group and 91.7% in the non-CKD group, and the 5-year survival rate was 61.8% in CKD group and 84.4% in the non-CKD group. The Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed that CKD is a risk factor for mortality in TGCV patients (P = 0.006) (See Fig. 1). Although TGCV patients with CKD were older than those without CKD, Cox proportional hazard model analyses including age indicated that CKD has a significant association of the prognosis of TGCV patients (hazard ratio 2.33 [1.12–4.86], P = 0.024). DM, HT, and DL did not increase mortality in TGCV patients, although these risk factors were established in the general population.
Conclusion
CKD is a major risk factor for mortality in TGCV patients and thus should be paid attention to in these patients.

title: #2743 Clinical characteristics and prognosis of IgAVN in Chinese adult patients
authors: Minting Chen; Rongrong Hu; Zuoxian Hou; Yitao Lin; Wenling Ye; Wei Ye; Yubing Wen; Peng Xia; Limeng Chen
abstract:
Background and Aims
IgA vasculitis nephritis (IgAVN) in adults was less common than in children. We tried to identify the difference in clinical pathologic characteristics and prognosis in adult or child patients with IgAVN.
Method and Results
A total of 305 IgAV confirmed by renal biopsy from January 2012 to December 2023 in Peking Union Medical College Hospital were retrospectively enrolled with 82.6% adults, 52.8% male, and the onset age was 29 (19, 44 years). Compared to the children, the adult patients had less gastrointestinal involvement (abdominal pain, hematochezia, melena) than children (35.3% vs. 58.5%, P = 0.002), and more severe eGFR ( 88.0 (65.3, 113.4) vs. 128.9 (107.5, 140.0) ml/min/1.73 m2, P = 0.000), hypertension (21.8% vs. 11.3%, P = 0.012) and CKD (21.4% vs. 3.8%, P = 0.003), without significant difference in 24 h proteinuria, hematuria, and serum albumin. According to the International Society of Pediatric Nephrology (ISKDC) classification criteria ISKDC classification standard, the most subtype was IIIb, followed by 89.5 (58.0, 123.5) months, seven patients died, 26 (10.3%) progressed to ESRD, and 9 (3.6%) eGFR decreased by 50%. Cox regression showed base eGFR <60 (ml/min/1.73 m2), hypertension, proteinuria, and disease course were risk factors for the end event. The multivariate regression analysis indicated that renal insufficiency (HR 8.722 (4.174, 18.228), P = 0.000) and 24 h UP (HR 1.153 (1.052, 1.264), P = 0.002) at baseline increased the risk of endpoint events.
Conclusion
The prognosis of IgAVN in adults was poor need to pay more attention.

title: #2744 CKD with hyperuricemia vs CKD with wide plasma uric acid fluctuations—two different types of CKD both with rapid eGFR decline
authors: Hiroshi Tanaka
abstract:
Background and Aims
CKD patients are generally considered to be heterogeneous. Younger population can have their CKD as a result of glomerulonephritis, hereditary nephropathy, field workers under frequent dehydration, and so on. Contrarily, the elder population can have their CKD from many different causes such as arteriosclerosis, heart failure, and ethanol abuse. Many kidney diseases can have a rapid deterioration in eGFR even without proteinuria. The progression of CKD needs to be predicted on each patient basis but such prediction method is not readily available especially when proteinuria is absent.
Plasma uric acid (UA) level is known to be associated not only with gouty attacks and urolithiasis but also with CKD progression and higher cardiovascular mortality. The author has previously shown that CKD patients with wide fluctuations in plasma UA level are prone to have faster decline in eGFR [2024 ASN Kidney Week].
This study was done whether plasma UA level and/or its fluctuation might serve as a predictive marker for eGFR decline.
Method
A hospital-wide study with all the laboratory data for a period of 4 years and 2 months was conducted. All the patients with an age 18 or more in whom the eGFR slope was calculated over 731 days or more were included in the study.
Medians were used for each datum, including dipstick proteinuria and hematuria (both changed to numeric variables, e.g., 1+ to 1.0).
The survey population was divided into "High" and "Low" (the patients with the higher-than-median plasma UA levels vs the rest with the lower levels), as well as into "Wide" and "Stable" (those with the wider- vs the narrower-than-median fluctuations measured as coefficient of variation (CV)).
Statistical analysis was done with R 3.6.3 on Ubuntu, with packages including {mice} (imputation for missing values) and {randomForest} (random forest).
Results
A total of 6,585 patients were included in the study, with an age 65.1 (16.1) years, male:female 3,350:3,235, plasma uric acid 5.31 (1.42) mg/dL, and eGFR 68.9 (20.1) mL/min/1.73 m2.
Using "random forest" analysis, one of the multivariate analyses using machine learning, was performed in order to identify factors with the highest importance, i.e., with the largest changes in Gini indices. The factors with high importance in eGFR slope included plasma UA level fluctuation, eGFR, total cholesterol, haemoglobin, plasma UA, alanine transferase, and age, as a descending order of importance. Degree of proteinuria was found to have much less importance than the parameters above. UA fluctuation was found to have the largest contribution to eGFR slope among all.
The slope of eGFR was the fastest in "Low and Wide" group, then in "High and Wide" and "High and Stable," and the slowest in "Low and Stable" (−1.51, −1.45 , −1.32 and −1.26 mL/min/1.73 m2/yr, median).
Interestingly, "High & Stable" populations were found to be totally different from "Low and Wide" patients; the former, compared with the latter, were younger, less anemic, with better eGFR while higher serum creatinine, with elevated alanine transferase, and higher total cholesterol and serum albumin, shown by both the random forest analysis and t-tests (parameters above were all statistically significant).
Conclusion
Plasma UA can be an easy, useful marker to predict worse renal prognosis, as a stably high plasma UA level for younger generations as well as wider UA fluctuation for elderly population.

title: #2852 What changes can the use of the IEXPAC tool induce in the nurse consultation for advanced chronic kidney disease?
authors: Sergi Aragó Sorrosal; Lida Rodas
abstract:
Background
Patient-centered care includes therapeutic education, participation, information, and patient experience (XPA). XPA refers to the interactions of individuals throughout their disease process across various healthcare services, influencing their perceptions. Enhancing patient care improves self-management and fosters engagement in the continuum of their healthcare journey. Multiple tools are available to quantify XPA, the IEXPAC (Instrument to Evaluate Chronic Patient Experience) is a validated tool designed to assess the patient experience in chronic disease care. It focuses on three key dimensions: productive interactions, the new relational model, and patient self-management. Using 11 core and 4 optional Likert-scale questions, IEXPAC provides a comprehensive evaluation of patient-centered care, emphasizing shared decision-making, communication, and care continuity. In chronic kidney disease (CKD) clinics, IEXPAC enables the identification of areas for improvement, promoting enhanced patient satisfaction and engagement. This tool offers valuable insights to refine healthcare delivery and support self-care management for CKD patients.
Understanding XPA is not just important, but crucial in the context of advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD) and shared decision-making for renal replacement therapies (RRT). It's time to move beyond outdated concepts like satisfaction and focus on the patient's experience throughout their disease process.
Aims
Describe the results obtained using the IEXPAC questionnaire in a CKD unit. Define actions to implement in an CKD consultation based on XPA evaluation with the IEXPAC tool.
Method
This descriptive study of XPA was conducted at a tertiary hospital in January/February 2024. The study population included all patients who completed follow-up in the joint CKD consultation in 2023 and initiated RRT in the same year. Exclusion criteria were refusal to participate and inability to complete the questionnaire.
The IEXPAC tool, available online and in a phone version, was used. It assesses three dimensions: productive interactions, new relational models, and patient self-management. The questionnaire includes 11+4 Likert-scale questions. An independent interviewer administered the questionnaires in the CKD consultation.
The hospital's ethics committee approved the study, and verbal consent was obtained from participants.
Results
The sample included 66 patients, 60.6% male, with a mean age of 67.4 ± 15.7 years. Of these, 44% were prefrail, 33% were frail, and 28% required a caregiver.
RRT modalities: 65% hemodialysis, 3% home hemodialysis, 12% peritoneal dialysis, and 19% kidney transplantation (living/cadaveric donor). Patients completed 92% of the questionnaires. Global XPA score: 7.13 ± 0.86. Subscores: productive interactions 7.87 ± 4.2; new relational model 4.7 ± 2.2; patient self-management 8.19 ± 1.37.
Conclusion
The overall XPA score for CKD patients was satisfactory. However, the "new relational model" dimension scored the lowest, highlighting the need to strengthen peer-mentoring programs and integrate new technologies into XPA. Implementing these programs in CKD consultations is essential to address patient needs, including launching group classes with expert patients and incorporating access to technological tools.

title: #3170 “Early experience with specialist palliative care services in patients of advanced chronic kidney disease in India”

abstract:

CKD patients experience a significant symptom burden including pain, fatigue, depression, and reduced ability to perform daily activities which increase with advancing stage. Hemodialysis therapy, which, while life-extending, may not improve quality of life in those with co morbidities and in elderly. Conservative or palliative care, focuses on quality of life, is one of the pathways in management of CKD especially in advanced stages. It addresses the holistic needs of patients, including physical, emotional, and psychosocial aspects, but remains underutilized in advanced CKD. We studied our experience on the impact of conservative care and specialist palliative care referral service in advanced CKD.
AimsTrends of inpatient renal supportive care consultations initiated during the given study period.Renal supportive care interventions provided in the in-patient setting.Outcomes of the supportive care consultation.
Method
Inclusion and exclusion criteria: After institutional ethics committee approval case records of consecutive in-patients referred from nephrology department to the kidney supportive care unit between January 1, 2019, and December 31, 2023, were analyzed.
A structured study pro forma was used after removing the patient identifiers. Demography, healthcare-related factors, reasons for referral, interventions provided, and outcomes of inpatient kidney supportive care interventions were recorded. Those with incomplete records were excluded. Data was summarized on an excel sheet.
Results
Of 201 patients, mean age was 60 ± 15.58 years, with 139 (69.1%) males; 165 (82%), had end-stage kidney disease (ESKD), 36 (18%) had acute on chronic kidney disease (CKD). Of 201, 131 (65.2%) had diabetic kidney disease, 70 (34.8%) had CKD from other causes. Majority i.e. 190 (94.5%), were on maintenance hemodialysis (HD), 7 (3.4%) were not willing to undergo HD, and 3 (1.5%) were on peritoneal dialysis. Common co morbidities included ischemic heart disease (IHD) in 75 (37.3%), chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) in 3 (1.5%), cirrhosis of the liver (CLD) in 28 (13.9%), cerebrovascular accidents (CVA) in 20 (9.9%).

Conclusion
Specialist palliative care interventions in patients with advanced kidney disease had an impact on the management process. There is a case for integrating these services in the management of advanced CKD.

title: #3458 Efficacy and safety of aldosterone antagonists in heart failure patients with chronic kidney disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis of cardiovascular and renal outcomes
authors: Ifunanya Nnajiofor; Federico Napoli; Alanís Yael Szyferman; Clara Campoverde; Henrique Neves; Paula Dibo
abstract:
Background and Aims
Aldosterone antagonists, also known as mineral corticosteroid antagonists (MRAs), are a well-established treatment for patients with heart failure (HF) and have been shown to provide survival benefits. However, their use in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) has been limited due to safety concerns, and their efficacy and safety in this population remain unknown. Therefore, we performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the efficacy and safety of MRAs on cardiovascular and renal outcomes in HF patients with CKD.
Method
PubMed, Embase, Cochrane and ClinicalTrials.gov databases were searched for randomized (RCTs) and non-randomized controlled studies (non-RCTs) that compared MRAs to control (placebo and/or no aldosterone antagonist use) in HF patients with CKD and reported the outcomes of hospitalization for HF; cardiovascular death; myocardial infarction; hyperkalemia; worsening renal function; stroke; and all-cause mortality. Heterogeneity was assessed with I² statistics and a random-effects model was used for outcomes with high heterogeneity.
Results
Seven studies (5 RCTs) with 19,708 patients were included, of whom 9,001 (45.7%) received treatment with an MRA. The mean follow-up period ranged from 3 to 60 months. An analysis restricted to RCTs demonstrated that MRAs significantly reduced hospitalizations for HF (RR 0.74; CI 95% 0.65–0.85; P < 0.0001) and cardiovascular death (RR 0.80; 95% CI 0.71–0.90; P = 0.0003; Fig. 1) compared with controls. However, MRAs did not significantly reduce all-cause mortality (RR 0.82; 95% CI 0.63–1.06; P = 0.002). When combining data from all studies, MRAs were associated with a higher risk of hyperkalemia (OR 1.98; 95% CI 1.43–2.75; P < 0.00001; Fig. 2) and a non-significant increased risk of worsening renal function (OR 1.37; 95% CI 0.95–1.98; P = 0.09) compared with controls. No significant differences were observed between groups for the risk of myocardial infarction (RR 1.07; 95% CI 0.92–1.25; P = 0.40) or stroke (RR 1.01; 95% CI 0.82–1.26; P = 0.90).
Conclusion
MRAs effectively reduced heart failure hospitalizations and cardiovascular death in HF patients with CKD; however, their use is associated with an increased risk of hyperkalemia.

title: #12 Serum cystatin C: a novel biomarker for CKD detection—a meta-analysis
authors: Abdel Qader Abu-Salih; Rula Alshimi; Leen Abu-Salih; Mohammad Al Bdoor; Malik Abu Al-Rub
abstract:
Background and Aims
Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a major public health concern. Early and accurate diagnosis is crucial for effective management and improved patient outcomes. Serum cystatin C has been proposed as a promising biomarker for CKD, offering advantages over traditional serum creatinine-based methods. This meta-analysis aims to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of serum cystatin C for detecting CKD.
Method
A comprehensive literature search was conducted in public databases, including PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane, Embase, and Web of Science. Studies focusing on the sensitivity, specificity, and diagnostic odds ratio (DOR) of serum cystatin C in diagnosing CKD were included. Data were extracted and analyzed using a random-effects model. Heterogeneity was assessed and explored through subgroup analyses and meta-regression.
Results
A total of 25 studies involving 18,000 participants were included in this meta-analysis. The pooled sensitivity of serum cystatin C for diagnosing CKD was 88% (95% CI: 85–91%), and the specificity was 90% (95% CI: 87–92%). The diagnostic odds ratio was 50 (95% CI: 35–70), indicating high diagnostic accuracy. The area under the summary receiver operating characteristic (SROC) curve was 0.94 (95% CI: 0.92–0.96), confirming the robust diagnostic performance of serum cystatin C. For diabetic patients with CKD, the DOR was 60 (95% CI: 30–120), with sensitivity and specificity of 90% and 89%, respectively. Subgroup analysis revealed that serum cystatin C exhibited better diagnostic value in Western populations compared to Asian populations. Additionally, diagnostic accuracy was higher when serum cystatin C was measured using particle-enhanced nephelometric immunoassay (PENIA) compared to particle-enhanced turbidimetric immunoassay (PETIA).
Conclusion
This updated evidence, building on the last meta-analysis conducted in 2015, supports the high diagnostic accuracy of serum cystatin C for CKD. Its use as a diagnostic biomarker can facilitate early detection and management of CKD, ultimately improving patient outcomes.

title: #459 Clinical tools to stratify conservative kidney management patients with different care needs
authors: Sye Nee Tan; Swee Ping Teh; Shashidhar Baikunje; Ivan Wei Zhen Lee; Boon Cheok Lai; Lee Ying Yeoh
abstract:
Background and Aims
Personalized care in conservative kidney management (CKM) provides a person-centered care for patient who have opted for non-dialytic therapy. However, the illness trajectory of patients with chronic kidney disease G5 (CKD G5) on CKM can be unpredictable. Previous study suggested a sharp increase in symptom distress and health-related concerns in the 2 months before death. The objectives of this study were to identify clinical tools associated with mortality in patients on CKM, and to evaluate the concordance between preferred and actual place of death.
Method
This was a single-centre cohort study included 109 CKD G5 patients opted for CKM from April 2021 to September 2024. Baseline demographic, clinical, laboratory data, Clinical Frailty Score (CFS), Edmonton Symptom Assessment System Revised: Renal (ESAS-r: Renal), Resources Utilization Group–Activities of Daily Living scale (RUG-ADLs), Palliative Performance Score (PPS), and Karnofsky Performance Score (KPS) were collected. Logistic regression and survival analysis were performed.
Results
A total of 109 patients with CKD G5 opted for CKM included in this study with mean (±SD) age of the patients of 79.8 ± 7.3 years, 64.2% were female and 82.6% were Chinese. Primary cause of CKD G5 was diabetes mellitus (69.7%). Baseline mean estimated glomerular filtration rate CKD-EPI (eGFRCKD-EPI) was 10.3 ml/min with Charlson comorbidity index of 8.5, CFS of 4.6 and KPS of 67.3. Median total ESASr-Renal was 1, RUG-ADL was 4, PPS was 60, serum albumin was 38 g/L and haemoglobin was 9.6 g/dL. Sixty-two patients (56.9%) deceased during follow-up with a median survival of 11.9 months. After adjusting for the variables, baseline eGFR CKD-EPI remained the only significant predictor of mortality (Fig. 1). Patients with eGFRCKD-EPI ≤5 ml/min had a median survival of 4 months. PPS score of <50 showed a clear correlation with poorer survival estimate (Fig. 2). The advance care planning completion rate in this cohort was 60.5%. There was a moderate concordance between preferred and actual place of death, with 35.5% of the deceased patients passed away at home.
Conclusion
Baseline eGFRCKD-EPI is a significant predictor of mortality in CKM patients. PPS demonstrated utility in estimating survival and may aid in timely transition to hospice care. While home remains the preferred place for end-of-life care for most, fulfilling this preference remains challenging. This study highlighted the importance of early identification of patients at-risk and the need for personalized care plans in CKM. Recognition of these poor prognostic value may facilitate timely referral to hospice service.

title: #592 Comparative prognostic value of glomerular filtration rate, serum cystatin C, beta-2-microglobulin and albuminuria for death and chronic kidney disease progression
authors: Isis Cerezo Arias; Nicolas Roberto Robles Perez-Monteoliva; Barbara Cancho; Jorge Alberto Rodriguez Sabillon; Álvaro Álvarez López; Julián Valladares Alcobendas; Juan Lopez Gomez
abstract:
Background and Aims
Serum creatinine and albuminuria are the core of most CKD prediction and progression risk models. Several biomarkers have been introduced to improve these results such as beta-2-microglobulin (B2M) and cystatin C (CysC). Nevertheless, few clinical comparisons of these biomarkers are available. We have compared serum B2M levels with albuminuria, CysC levels, and the CKD-EPI GFR equations.
Method
A sample of 434 patients were studied: 234 males and 200 females, the mean age was 58.3 ± 15.0 years, and 33.4% have diabetes mellitus. In all patients, plasma B2M, CysC, creatinine, and urinary albumin excretion were analyzed. EGFR was calculated using CKD-EPI equations for creatinine, CysC, and creatinine-CysC. The risk of death and CKD progression was evaluated using ROC curves and Cox proportional hazards survivorship models.
Results
For mortality, the highest area under the curve (AUC) was for CysC (0.775, 0.676–0.875). The lowest sensitivity was shown by eGFR (creatinine) (0.298, 0.195–0.401, P < 0.001), eGFR (CysC) (0.216, 0.118–0.314, P < 0.001), and eGFR (creatinine + CysS) (0.218, 0.124–0.312, P < 0.001). For progression to advanced CKD, the highest AUC was for CysC (0.908, 0.862–0.954). The lowest sensitivity was shown by eGFR (creatinine) (0.184, 0.106–0.261, P < 0.001), eGFR (CysC) (0.095, 0.048–0.14, P < 0.001), and eGFR (creatinine+ CysC) (0.087, 0.040–0.134, P < 0.001). CysC, after age, was the second-best marker of life risk. Contrariwise, for CKD progression, CysC, and albuminuria were the best markers.
Conclusion
The best biomarker of mortality and risk of progression to CKD was CysC. Albuminuria and B2M were the next best options to be used. The lowest sensitivity was shown by estimated eGFR.

title: #754 Chemosensory function and food preferences among long term hemodialysis patients and correlation with nutritional status
authors: Aiswarya Kosaraju; Sandhya Suresh; Ramprasad Elumalai; M Jayakumar
abstract:
Background and Aims
Malnutrition frequently occurs in patients treated with chronic hemodialysis (HD), which in turn increases their mortality and morbidity. Disturbed sense of smell and taste, which has been reported in HD patients is associated with poorer nutritional status and increased mortality. The aim of the study was to investigate and compare the chemosensory function and food preferences among patients in long term HD with those of age – matched healthy controls and correlate it with the nutritional status of the patients. There is very few data published on this and in much smaller sample sizes.
Method
We performed a single center prospective randomized case control study on 50 patients undergoing HD and 50 age matched healthy individuals at Sri Ramachandra University, India over three months. We assessed the chemosensory function using Indian Smell Identification Test (INSIT) and Taste Drop Test (TDT). Food preferences in both the groups were assessed by a questionnaire over 44 items and was divided into 7 groups based on the category of foods. Malnutrition was assessed by the DMS (Dialysis Malnutrition Score) and body mass index (BMI). We only included patients who are more than 18 years and on HD for more than six months. Subjects with dementia, mental illnesses, less than one year after stroke, previous chemotherapy, or head/neck radiation therapy were excluded from both the groups.
Results
The baseline characteristics in the study showed 56% males and 40% females in cases and controls respectively with mean ages being 49.5 years and 52.7 years. The mean BMI was lower in cases (23.7) when compared with controls (28.3). The mean DMS in the control group was 13.44 (Normal) while cases had a significantly higher score of 25(moderate malnutrition). When compared to controls, 20%, 16%, and 38% of cases, respectively, did not appreciate the taste of sugar, salt, or tamarind, which was significant (p values of 0.001, 0.003, and 0.000). Similarly, 46%, 48%, and 32% of cases, respectively, had significant p values of 0.004, 0.003, and 0.008 for the inability to smell vanilla, rose, and pineapple. Fruits, vegetables and starches food groups were highly preferred by the cases. On the other hand, they showed little preference for meat, dairy and seafood which was significantly lower than the controls.
Conclusion
In HD patients, when compared to the controls, they had considerable impairment in their ability to smell and taste. The greatest impairment in taste was noticed for sour flavour, with just 62% of patients being able to recognise the taste, compared to 80% for sweet and 84% for salt. This, along with a significant degree of olfactory impairment has significantly affected the food preferences among the HD patients in our study who preferred vegetables over dairy. This also correlated with poorer nutritional status of the HD patients in terms on BMI and DMS score. They had significantly higher preference for fruits, dairy, snacks and starches compared to controls. Understanding each patients unique sensory preference can help individualise their diet more effectively, potentially improve their overall health and quality of life in HD patient.

title: #768 Collagen 1a1 depletion in podocytes increases proteinuria
authors: Chingchun Yang; Yu-Hsiang Chou; Shuei-Liong Lin
abstract:
Background and Aims
Glomerular disease is a major cause of acute kidney injury (AKI) and chronic kidney disease (CKD). The glomerular filtration barrier consists of the endothelium, the glomerular basement membrane (GBM), and podocytes. Damage to the glomeruli disrupts the filtration process, leading to either nephritic syndrome or nephrotic syndrome. Podocytes secrete type IV collagen, a key component of the GBM. However, whether podocytes secrete other collagens, such as collagen 1α1, and the role of collagen 1α1 in podocyte-associated glomerular diseases remain unclear. This study aims to investigate the role of collagen 1α1 in podocytes.
Method
We used Col1a1-GFPTg mice to identify the collagen-producing cell. Podocin-CreTg; Col1α1 floxed/floxed and Wt1CreERT2/+; Col1α1 floxed/floxed mice were employed to constitutively and conditionally knock out the Col1α1 gene in podocytes. Ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) was used as a model for AKI. We compared plasma levels of blood urea nitrogen (BUN), creatinine, and urine protein between littermate control mice and Col1α1 knockout mice under normal conditions and on day 7 after IRI.
Results
We discovered that podocytes are strong collagen-producing cells in both normal kidneys and IRI-affected kidneys. In Podocin-CreTg; Col1α1 floxed/floxed mice, knockout of the Col1α1 gene in podocytes did not result in abnormal plasma levels of BUN, creatinine, or increased proteinuria under normal conditions compared to littermate control. However, Col1α1 knockout in Wt1CreERT2/+; Col1α1 floxed/floxed mice led to significantly higher proteinuria compared to littermate controls. In the IRI model, higher proteinuria was observed at day 7 after IRI in Podocin-CreTg; Col1α1 floxed/floxed mice compared to littermate controls.
Conclusion
In Podocin-CreTg; Col1α1 floxed/floxed mice, Col1α1 knockout does not lead to increased proteinuria under normal conditions but does so in the IRI model. In contrast, Col1α1 knockout in Wt1CreERT2/+; Col1α1 floxed/floxed mice is associated with higher proteinuria. This increase may be attributed to damage to the glomerular filtration barrier, potentially linked to podocyte injury or dysfunction. The mechanisms underlying this phenomenon in Wt1CreERT2/+; Col1α1floxed/floxed mice require further investigation.

title: #922 Evaluating the nutritional accuracy and practicality of ChatGPT-generated recipes for CKD patients
authors: Sharon Rao; Lin-Chun Wang; Sheng-Han Yueh; Hanjie Zhang; Karin Bergling; Peter Kotanko; Len Usvyat; Linda Moore; Nancy Ginsberg; Frank Van Der Sande; Jeroen Kooman; Annabel Biruete
abstract:
Background and Aims
Adequate nutrition is fundamental to human well-being, particularly for patients with impaired kidney function. To address this, we began leveraging artificial intelligence—specifically, ChatGPT using the GPT-4o model (openai.com)—to assist in the development of personalized dietary recommendations for CKD patients. In previous work by Wang et al. (J Ren Nutr, 2024), the GPT-4 model demonstrated qualitative success in generating dietary recommendations for dialysis patients. However, quantitative analysis revealed notable limitations, and the recommendations had not been translated into actual prepared dishes, leaving their practical feasibility untested. This study aims to bridge that gap by preparing dishes based on the LLM's recommendations and evaluating them across multiple dimensions, including appropriateness for specific clinical profiles, palatability, and nutritional accuracy.
Method
Twenty virtual patients were created using Monte Carlo simulation; we provided the characteristics of three randomly selected patients diverse food preferences (Western, Chinese, and Mexican) to GPT-4o. GPT-4o generated three recipes for each virtual patient based on patient demographics, food preferences, laboratory data, clinical characteristics, and daily food budget. All nine dishes were made in a professional kitchen and rated based on the dishes’ appearance, taste, flavor, texture, portion size, and overall acceptability. We then entered the GPT-4o's-generated recipes into a USDA-approved nutrient analysis software (ESHA research, Salem, OR, USA) for comparison. For each recipe, individual ingredients, their weight and total quantity were cross referenced in the USDA Database for food amounts (fdc.nal.USDA.gov). Three renal dieticians were consulted to cross reference amounts and weights for each ingredient. A recipe card for each dish was generated following this to yield nutritional values for calories, protein, total fat, carbohydrates, phosphorus, potassium and sodium (Fig. 1). Once the nutritional analysis for each recipe was generated, a comparison was made between GPT-4o's nutrient estimation of calories, protein, total fat, carbohydrates, phosphorus, potassium and sodium and ESHA's nutrient analysis per dish.
Results
While ChatGPT's carbohydrate content estimation was relatively accurate, it underestimated calories by 36%, protein by 28%, and total fat, phosphorus, potassium, and sodium by around 50%. On the other hand, GPT-4o showed an overall improvement where it underestimated calories by 21% (mean: 78.7%; 95% CI: 50.3% to 107.1%), total fat by 36% (63.7%; CI: 46.1% to 81.2%), protein 24% (76.3%; CI: 57.6% to 95.0%), potassium 24% (mean: 75.7%; 95% CI: 54.1% to 97.3%), and overestimated phosphorus by 16% (115.7%; CI: 65.8% to 165.6%). The carbohydrate and sodium contents were satisfactorily accurate (difference within 10%). (Fig. 2). Scatterplots were also generated to compare GPT-4o-generated recipe values to ESHA values for each nutritional value. For instance, Chinese Udon noodles were an outlier in the sodium plot which was attributed to GPT-4o's recommendation for soy sauce – an ingredient high in sodium (Fig. 3). In terms of appearance, dieticians rated the recipes from GPT-4o between 4–5, taste was rated between 3–5, flavor and texture were rated largely around 4, portion size was rated between 4–5 (Fig. 4).
Conclusion
GPT-4o is a valuable tool for creating personalized nutrition plans for diverse patient groups. However, we recommend cross-checking the nutritional values of recipes with a validated database, such as ESHA, to ensure accuracy. While GPT-4o serves as an excellent starting point for dietitians, ingredient substitutions should align more closely with patients’ dietary needs. For instance, replacing Udon noodles with a healthier alternative like whole wheat noodles or replacing a low sodium soy sauce with fresh lemon or lime juice, and other healthier alternatives. This study underscores the need for continued refinement in AI-generated meal plans and highlights opportunities for collaboration between AI developers and healthcare professionals.

title: #1307 Association of albuminuria and POCUS in cardiorenal syndrome in a monographic nephrology consultation
authors: Zoila Stany Albines Fiestas; Axenia Babara; Jerson Andrés Alvarado Zelaya; Amelia Campos Sáenz de Santamaría; Mireia Pujol Saumell; Laura Karla Esterellas Sánchez; Paula Mora López; Ana Berni Wennekers; José Esteban Ruiz Laiglesia; Jorge Rubio Gracia; Ignacio Giménez López; Pablo Iñigo Gil
abstract:
Background and Aims
Albuminuria is defined as the loss of albumin in urine. It is an independent risk factor associated with cardiovascular disease. A urine albumin/creatinine ratio (CAC) >30 mg/g is considered pathological. Albuminuria is present in 40% of patients with chronic heart failure.
In this study, we explored the association of albuminuria with ultrasound congestion (evaluated by Point-of-Care Ultrasonography POCUS) in the follow-up of cardiorenal syndrome patients of a monographic nephrology consultation.
Method
A retrospective unicentric observational study was conducted on a database of patients evaluated in the cardiorenal pathology monographic consultation between June 2023 and June 2024 in a tertiary hospital.
Clinical data were extracted from electronic patient records. Microalbuminuria and the presence or absence of ultrasound congestion were evaluated in all patients.
We classified albuminuria according to the recommendations of the Kidney Disease Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) guidelines for chronic kidney disease. A1: CAC <30 mg/g (normal to mildly increased); A2: CAC 30–300 mg/g (moderately increased) and A3 CAC >300 mg/g (severely increased).
In POCUS, tissue congestion was assessed by lung ultrasound (LUS) using the 8-zone method; and venous congestion was assessed using Venous Excess Ultrasound (VexUS), evaluating the inferior caval vein and the anomalies on hepatic, portal and intrarenal venous Doppler. Mixed congestion was considered to be the simultaneous presence of tissue and venous congestion.
The correlation between microalbuminuria and ultrasound congestion was evaluated using Pearson's rank correlation coefficient for bivariate analysis, conducted with IBM SPSS®.
Results
74 patients were evaluated. Most were male (68%). The mean age of the patients evaluated was 77.89 ± 8.27 years. The majority (89.19%) of the patients evaluated in the consultation had type 2 cardiorenal syndrome.
The mean glomerular filtration rate estimated by CKD-EPI was 32.47 ml/min ± 10.65. The mean albumin creatinine ratio in urine was 78.90 ± 114.62 mg/g.
CAC >30 mg/g was found in 30 patients, among which 24 presented CAC 30–300 mg/g and 6 CAC >300 mg/g. 27 patients with CAC <30 mg/g and 14 with CAC 30–300 mg/g presented ultrasound congestion (Table 1). All patients with CAC >300 mg/g presented ultrasound congestion (1 tissue congestion, 1 venous congestion and 4 mixed congestion) (Fig. 1). We found a statistically significant correlation between CAC levels and ultrasound congestion (Table 2).
We found that most patients with CAC 30–300 mg/g and that all patients with CAC >300 mg/g presented elevated ProBNP levels (Fig. 2), too. A statistically significant correlation was found between CAC levels and ProBNP levels (Table 3).
Conclusion
In our experience, we found that CAC is a useful marker in the assessment of congestion in patients with cardiorenal pathology. Patients with higher levels of CAC mostly presented mixed ultrasound congestion.
We must not forget to include this parameter within the multiparametric assessment of congestion.

title: #1964 Validation of the IgA nephropathy prediction tool: a Portuguese center's experience
authors: Beatriz Cortez Ferreira; Pedro Fragoso; Beatriz Pedro Fernandes; Ana Galvão; Andreia Borges; Luís Rodrigues; Rui Alves
abstract:
Background and Aims
IgA nephropathy (IgAN) is one of the most common primary glomerulonephritis worldwide, significantly contributing to the global burden of chronic kidney disease (CKD). Its variable progression makes it challenging to identify patients at higher risk of CKD. The KDIGO 2021 guidelines emphasize the International IgAN Prediction Tool (IgAN-PT) as an important resource for assessing the risk of disease progression using clinical and histological data at the time of kidney biopsy. However, the applicability of this tool in the Portuguese population requires further study, as well as the prognostic value of certain histopathological features not included in the tool, such as crescent formation.
Method
We included all biopsy-proven IgAN cases from Centro Hospitalar Universitário de Coimbra between 1998 and 2018, with a minimum 5-year follow-up period. Clinical data collected at biopsy included age, sex, estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), blood pressure, and pharmacotherapy. Histological samples were classified according to the Oxford MEST-C score.
The primary outcome was defined as either progression to end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) or a 50% decline in eGFR within 5 years. Univariate logistic regression analysis was conducted, using the log-rank test for categorical variables and Cox regression for continuous variables. To validate our model, the area under the ROC (auROC) curve analysis was performed and optimal cut-offs with the Youden index were calculated. A multivariate logistic regression model was developed to assess the combined impact of the IgAN-PT and MEST-C score.
Results
A total of 93 patients (71% male) were included. Twenty-five patients (27%) developed the primary outcome: 15 reached ESKD, and 10 experienced a 50% reduction in eGFR.
The IgAN-PT accurately predicted the 5-year risk of progression to ESKD or a 50% decline in eGFR, with an odds ratio of 1.06 [95% CI (1.021–1.097), P = 0.002] and an auROC of 0.795 [95% CI (0.681–0.910)]. When combined with the MEST-C score, the predictive capacity of the model improved, achieving an auROC of 0.845 [95% CI (0.754–0.937)]. Importantly, although crescent formation is not included in the IgAN-PT, their presence is strongly correlated with worse outcomes showing a significant impact on disease progression (P < 0.001).
Our analysis also revealed key cut-off values for the 5-year risk of ESKD or a 50% reduction in eGFR, by calculating the Youden index. Regarding IgAN-PT, a score >12.39% was significantly associated with reaching the primary outcome. Additionally, levels of proteinuria > 1.4 g/24 h or an eGFR <79mL/min/1.73 m2 at biopsy were also predictive of poorer clinical outcomes over 5 years.
Conclusion
Our findings confirm that the IgAN-PT is a reliable tool for predicting disease progression in the Portuguese population, with improved accuracy when combined with the MEST-C score. We highlight that crescent formation, although not included in the prediction tool, emerged as a strong histological predictor of poorer outcomes. Moreover, we identified clinically relevant cut-off values for eGFR, proteinuria, and IgAN-PT scores that predict progression to ESKD or a 50% decline in eGFR at 5 years, emphasizing their potential in informing risk stratification and helping guide clinical management in IgAN.

title: #3368 The implementation of a multi-faceted cardio-renal service on heart failure and renal outcomes: a retrospective cohort study
authors: Arjun Virk; Aveen Mahmood; Hana Ahmed; Abdulrahman Nugod; Khaled Jallad; Abdalrahman Mohammed; Shabnam Buhary; Huda Mahmoud
abstract:
Background and Aims
Cardiorenal syndrome (CRS) is a complex set of conditions associated with increased mortality and multiple healthcare challenges that reduce the optimisation of therapeutic care.
Cardiorenal clinics (CRC) have emerged as a collaborative initiative between cardiologists and nephrologists to provide a multi-disciplinary approach to the optimal management of these individuals.
We describe the outcomes from the development of a cardiorenal service at a district general hospital, which includes weekly collaborative clinics with an attending cardiology and nephrology consultant, weekly multi-disciplinary team meetings with community heart failure (HF) nurses and secondary care pharmacy, cardiology and nephrology team members.
Method
This was a retrospective cohort study conducted to evaluate clinical outcomes in cardiorenal clinic service-users with CRS. Only service-users with a minimum of 12 months follow-up from the first clinic visit CRC were included. Data was collected by review of electronic clinic records and laboratory results.
Results
53 individuals with cardio-renal syndrome, 43% female (n = 23), 69.58 ± 14.38 years, current eGFR 29.74 ± 13.64 ml/min/1.73 m2.
72.5%, (n = 37) have HFrEF (heart failure with reduced ejection fraction), 67.5%, (n = 27) have severe HFrEF. 26%, (n = 14) of those with moderate and severe HFrEF demonstrated an improvement in ejection fraction across 12-months in response to treatment. Guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) was not prescribed in the following: beta-blockers (6.66%) and sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors (13.63%).
Annual delta estimated glomerular filtration rates (ΔeGFR) prior to CRC-service intervention were −6.12 ± 17.6 ml/min/1.73 m2, compared to the post CRC-service intervention ΔeGFR −1.9 ± 9.32 ml/min/1.73 m2 (P = 0.06).
The mean group weight declined across 12-months from 91.18 ± 26.6kg on initiation to CRC-service to 89.49 ± 25.10kg, P = 0.02. Greater annual declines in weight correlated with greater declines in annual-delta systolic blood pressure (BP) (r = 0.31, P = 0.02) and a tendency for greater declines annual-delta diastolic BP (r = 0.24, P = 0.08).
Furthermore, individuals on the CR-service intervention had a trend to have less admissions post intervention than prior, median admission rate dropped from 2 (IQR 1–4) to 1 (IQR 0–3), P = 0.07.
Conclusion
A multidisciplinary CRC model integrating nephrologists, cardiologists and community heart failure teams improved medication optimisation, weight reduction, renal function stabilisation and trend towards reduced hospital admissions over 12 months. These findings would support the role of CR-services in enhancing clinical outcomes in CRS patients and highlight the need for further prospective evaluation.

title: #3381 Predicting chronic kidney disease progression in elderly patients with acute kidney injury : a 10-year retrospective analysis
authors: Ilhem Ben Othman; Harzallah Amel; Meriam Hajji; Sahar Agerbi; Fethi Ben Hmida; Soumaya Chargui; Ezzeddine Abderrahim
abstract:
Background and Aims
Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a common condition in elderly patients, characterized by a rapid decline in kidney function, particularly in this vulnerable population, where AKI frequently progresses to chronic kidney disease (CKD). This progression, reported in up to 58.6% of cases, [1] carries significant clinical and socioeconomic consequences, including increased morbidity, prolonged hospital stays, and reduced quality of life.
Identifying predictive factors of CKD progression is crucial to improving outcomes. This study aims to analyze these factors in elderly AKI patients.
Method
A retrospective study including patients aged 65 years or older admitted to a nephrology department for AKI between 2012 and 2022. AKI was defined according to KDIGO 2012 criteria. Data on demographics, clinical and biological parameters, therapeutic interventions, and patient outcomes were collected. CKD progression was analyzed as a primary outcome. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of CKD evolution.
Results
Seventy-five patients were included, with a mean age of 72.9 ± 5.7 years and a male-to-female ratio of 0.59. title: #230 INShore: phase III, multicentre, randomised, open-label study of efficacy and safety of obinutuzumab vs MMF in patients with childhood-onset idiopathic nephrotic syndrome
authors: Julien Hogan; Jie Ding; Larry A Greenbaum; Malgorzata Mizerska-Wasiak; Kandai Nozu; Andreia Watanabe; Heather Boston; Debbie Chen; Ben Lanza; Patricia Lehane
abstract:
Background and Aims
Patients with childhood-onset frequently relapsing nephrotic syndrome (FRNS) or steroid-dependent nephrotic syndrome (SDNS) need approved therapies that sustain clinical remission and minimise glucocorticoid burden. Over the past decade, the effectiveness of B-cell–depleting monoclonal antibodies, primarily rituximab, for treating FRNS/SDNS has established the pathogenic role of B cells in this condition. Obinutuzumab, a type II anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody, depletes B cells more effectively than rituximab. The INShore study (NCT05627557, EU CT 2023-505140-19-00) assesses the efficacy and safety of obinutuzumab versus mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) among children and young adults (aged ≥2–25 years) with childhood-onset FRNS or SDNS.
Method
Participants in complete remission but at high risk of relapse are randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive obinutuzumab or MMF (Fig. 1). Intravenous obinutuzumab (1000 mg or 20 mg/kg for participants <45 kg) is infused on Day 1 and Weeks 2, 24 and 26; MMF (titrated by Week 4 to 1200 mg/m2/day) is given orally twice daily until Week 52, after which administration must be discontinued or tapered over the subsequent 3 months. Participants in either arm receiving oral glucocorticoids at randomisation follow a guided taper to achieve a target of 0 mg by Week 8. Participants and/or their caregivers assess urine protein via dipstick daily home monitoring. Relapse is confirmed by first morning void urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR) laboratory testing and is defined as: (1) UPCR ≥2 g/g, (2) dipstick urinalysis protein ≥3 for 3 consecutive days with the most recent UPCR >0.2 g/g or 3) dipstick urinalysis protein ≥3 on any single day with oedema and UPCR >0.2 g/g. The primary endpoint is the proportion of participants with sustained complete remission at 1 year, defined as first morning void UPCR ≤0.2 g/g at Week 52. Secondary endpoints include overall relapse-free survival, cumulative glucocorticoid dose, number of relapses and proportion of participants with sustained, complete remission at Week 76.
Results
INShore is fully enrolled with 85 participants across 32 sites and 9 countries. The study population comprises 30 (35.3%) females and 55 (64.7%) males; 23 (27.1%) Asian participants, 14 (16.5%) Black or African American participants, 47 (55.3%) white participants and 1 (1.2%) participant whose race is unknown; 38 (44.7%) have FRNS and 47 (55.3%) SDNS; 50 (58.8%) received prior non-steroid immunosuppressive therapy for the treatment of FRNS/SDNS. At baseline, mean (SD) age was 9.9 (4.39) years and serum albumin was 4.3 (0.42) g/dl; median [IQR] estimated glomerular filtration rate was 120.0 [110.0, 134.0] ml/min/1.73 m2 and UPCR was 0.0 [0.0, 0.1] g/g.
Conclusion
The successful enrolment and diverse demographics of the INShore study participants provide a robust basis for assessing the efficacy and safety of obinutuzumab versus MMF in managing childhood-onset idiopathic nephrotic syndrome. Full results of the INShore study will be available following the primary analysis, once all participants have completed 52 weeks in the study.

title: #250 Advancing coaching and telehealth for CKD Care: the ACT-CKD cohort study protocol
authors: Christoph Benjamin Niehus; Friedrich von Samson-Himmelstjerna; Benedikt Kolbrink; Kevin Schulte
abstract:
Background and Aims
Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a growing global healthcare challenge, affecting around 9 million people in Germany alone. Many patients do not receive adequate diagnostics and care, and barriers are expected to increase in the future. Furthermore, patients often lack disease knowledge and resources needed to make informed decisions about kidney-replacement therapy. The KDIGO guidelines for CKD highlight telemedicine as a potential solution to address these challenges. While early evidence highlights the promise of telehealth in CKD care, there is a clear need for further development and testing of innovative programs. Kidney+ is a novel hybrid telecoaching program designed to help CKD patients actively manage their health. The program combines telemedicine consultations—via chat, telephone or video—with a multidisciplinary care team of nurses, dietitians and patient peers. Patients receive guidance regarding healthy lifestyle habits, medication adherence, and self-sufficient decision-making regarding kidney replacement therapies. The ACT-CKD study aims to achieve three key objectives: (1) Build a detailed profile of the participants using the program. (2) Evaluate program effects regarding clinical parameters and patient-reported outcome measures. (3) Examine how participants engage with the program, their usage patterns, and their satisfaction with the telecoaching experience.
Method
The ACT-CKD cohort study will recruit patients with CKD attending a nephrology specialist and receiving the standard of care. Patients will access the Kidney+ program via its companion app. The study follows a longitudinal design over six months with a single-arm structure, conducting a pre/post-program analysis. To build a user profile, demographics, underlying diseases, laboratory values, and medication data will be analyzed. Evaluation of program effects will consist of clinical parameters such as blood pressure, body mass index, and laboratory changes as well as patient-reported outcome measures like quality of life (PROMIS-29), patient activation (PAM13), medication adherence (A14), lifestyle changes, disease knowledge, and preferred kidney replacement therapy. Regarding patient engagement with the program, analysis will focus on usage patterns and program satisfaction (adapted smartNTx). Based on an estimated medium effect size for most endpoints, a cohort of 100 participants has been determined as the required sample size. This calculation ensures sufficient power to evaluate the study hypotheses after six months of program participation.
Results
The study will follow a structured timeline, with data collection occurring at baseline and after six months of participation in the Kidney+ program. The primary analysis will focus on patient profile, program effects and usage patterns. Results will provide robust new insights into the impact and feasibility of the Kidney+ program, offering a foundation for further research and development in innovative telehealth solutions for CKD care. The findings are expected to raise further questions and open new pathways in hybrid telecoaching approaches. Regulatory approval is anticipated for Q1 2025, with recruitment planned from Q1 to Q2 2025. Results are expected by Q4 2025.
Conclusion
Nurse-led telecare has emerged as a promising approach for managing chronic diseases, offering significant potential for patients with CKD. However, comprehensive and well-structured programs tailored to this population with proven medical benefits remain scarce. The Kidney+ program aims to bridge this gap with an innovative, patient-centered telecoaching model designed to improve not only patient-reported outcomes but also clinically important features. The ACT-CKD study will evaluate the impact of the Kidney+ program, examining its effects on clinical and behavioral outcomes as well as user engagement. By addressing the pressing need for research into hybrid-care solutions for CKD, this study seeks to determine whether the program could serve as a cornerstone for future care models, easing the strain on an increasingly overburdened healthcare system.
