title: #2236 Creatinine muscle index (CMI) is independently associated with markers of Sarcopenia and mortality in chronic kidney disease
authors: Thomas McDonnell; Tom Phillips; Philip A Kalra; Simon Fraser; Rosamonde E Banks; Nicolas Vuilleumier; Maarten Taal
abstract:
Background and Aims
Sarcopenia is defined by the European Working Group on Sarcopenia in Older People (EWGSOP) as a progressive skeletal muscle disorder with an increased risk of falls, fractures, disability, and mortality. Sarcopenia is more prevalent in non-dialysis CKD than in age-matched controls and strongly linked to higher mortality. Since age and CKD stage poorly predict risk, reliable biomarkers are essential for identifying at-risk individuals. Indices combining serum creatinine and cystatin C (eGFR ratio and eGFR difference) have been explored. However, these have tended to perform worse in those with reduced eGFR, with few studies focusing on prevalent CKD populations and none assessing mortality outcomes.
Method
The National Unified Renal Translational Research Enterprise (NURTuRE)-CKD is a UK, prospective multicentre cohort study of adults with non-dialysis CKD. 2930 (1723 males, 1207 females) had paired creatinine and cystatin C levels measured in addition to muscle function testing in the form of hand grip strength tests (HGS) and timed up-and-go (TUG).
‘Creatinine muscle index’ (CMI), an estimator of glomerular filtration of creatinine and novel marker of muscle mass, was calculated in each person.
CMI mg/day per 1.73 m² = eGFRcys × serum creatinine (mg/dl) × 1 dl/100 ml × 1440 min/day.
The primary outcome was the relationship of CMI to:
1. All-cause mortality (ACM) before initiating kidney replacement therapy (KRT). Assessed via Cox proportional hazards, per 100 mg/day per 1.73 m².
2. Sarcopenia, classified by applying the EWGSOP2 criteria. HGS was used to identify persons with ‘probable sarcopenia’ (<27 kg for males and <16 kg for females). Assessed via logistic regression.
Both regression analyses controlled for white ethnicity, age, body mass index (BMI), Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI), coronary artery bypass graft (CABG), hypertension uACR and CRP.
Secondary analysis examined the relationship of CMI to continuous variables of HGS, TUG, and functional status by the Karnofsky Performance Score (KPS) and Health-related quality of life (QOL), calculated by the 5-level EuroQol-5D (EQ-5D-5L) via Pearsons correlation coefficient.
To account for variations in muscle mass/function, the cohort was split by sex and examined in sex specific tertiles.
Results
806 (27.5%) were sarcopenic at baseline, and over the median 50 months (41.2, 55.9), 527 (18%) people died pre-KRT. Table 1 presents the cohort's baseline demographic, clinical, and outcome characteristics stratified into sex-specific tertiles of CMI. For both males and females: Age and all co-morbidities (except hypertension), CRP and ACR increased across the lower tertiles of CMI. For both men and women, rates of sarcopenia and mortality increased with decreasing CMI as did health-related quality of life indices (EQ-5D-3L) and functional status (KPS).
In the fully adjusted model, 100 mg/day per 1.73 m² increase in CMI was associated with a HR of 0.83 (95% CI: 0.77 to 0.89) for ACM in males and 0.74 (95% CI: 0.64 to 0.85) in females. Similarly, for sarcopenia, the OR per 100 mg/day per 1.73 m² increase in CMI was 0.72 (95% CI: 0.67 to 0.79) in males and 0.81 (95% CI: 0.73 to 0.91) in females.
The correlation of CMI to secondary outcomes can be seen in Fig. 1. In both men and women, increasing CMI was positively correlated with HGS, EQ-5D-3L, and KPS, and negatively correlated with TUG.
CMI was superior to the creatinine-cystatin C ratio (eGFRcys/eGFRcr) and the difference (eGFRcys–eGFRcr) for predicting ACM and sarcopenia.
Conclusion
People with CKD are at an increased risk of sarcopenia, which is associated with higher mortality and reduced quality of life. Identifying those at greatest risk is crucial for implementing targeted interventions to reverse sarcopenia. Here we show for the first time in a prevented CKD population that CMI product of eGFR, cystatin C, and serum creatinine, reflecting creatinine generation and excretion, is independently associated with ACM and confirm its relationship to muscle function, a measure of sarcopenia. CMI could be used as a practical tool to identify individuals with sarcopenia and elevated mortality risk to direct care.

title: #2598 Impact of empagliflozin on metabolic profile, anthropometric indices, and renal function in chronic kidney disease patients with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease
authors: Rakhimjon Tursunbayev; Sherzod Abdullaev; Muzaffar Asomov; Ranokhon Igamberdieva
abstract:
Background and Aims
Increased life expectancy and living conditions have contributed to an increase in comorbidities and metabolic disorders. 25%–30% of the adult population suffers from non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), while chronic kidney disease (CKD) affects 10%–15%. The aim of the study was to evaluate the impact of empagliflozin on the metabolic, anthropometric and kidney parameters in CKD patients with coexisting NAFLD.
Method
The study involved 41 patients, including 25 women and 16 men. Patients aged 38 to 75 years, the average age was 67.5 years. Patients were divided into main (23 patients) and control groups (18 patients). The study did not include patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus, eGFR less than 30 ml/min/1.73 m2, patients over 85 years old, viral hepatitis, storage diseases (Wilson disease, hemochromatosis), drug-induced and alcoholic liver pathologies. NAFLD was diagnosed according to the 2016 EASL-EASD-EASO guidelines. The study covered 25 patients (60.9%) with CKD stage 3a and 16 patients (39.1%) with CKD stage 3b. Platelets, aspartate aminotransferase (AST), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), albumin, creatinine, body mass index (BMI), waist circumference, ultrasound examination of the liver and kidneys, hepatic steatosis index (HSI), NAFLD fibrosis score, ALD/NAFLD index (ANI), glomerular filtration rate (GFR) were studied in patients before and after the study. Antihypertensive, hypoglycemic drugs were continued according to standard therapy. Patients of the main group were prescribed empagliflozin 10 mg/day in addition to standard therapy. The duration of the study was 16 weeks. 1 patient was excluded from the study due to genital candidiasis. As the last point of the study, an improvement in laboratory, instrumental and anthropometric parameters was obtained.
Results
After the end of the study the main group of patients demonstrated significant improvements across multiple parameters. Platelet count increased from 244.9 × 109/l to 318.1 × 109/l (by 23.1%), albumin from 36 g/l to 45 g/l (by 20%), AST from 38 mmol/l to 30 mmol/l (by 21.1%), ALT from 41 mmol/l to 32 mmol/l (by 21.9%), creatinine decreased from 114.2 μmol/l to 88.1 μmol/l (by 22.9%). Anthropometric indices also improved: BMI improved from 34.23 kg/m2 to 27.6 kg/m2 (by 19.4%), waist circumference from 119 cm to 97 cm (by 18.5%). Liver ultrasound findings indicated a reduction in hepatosis severity, decreased from grade 1.64 to grade 1.33 (by 18.9%). Key NAFLD biomarkers also improved: HSI index from 44 to 34.8 (by 21%), NAFLD fibrosis index from −0.58 to −0.55 (by 5.2%), ANI from −89.9 to −94.8 (by 5.2%). eGFR increased from 37 ml/min/1.73 m2 to 48 ml/min/1.73 m2 (22.9%). In contrast, patients in the control group did not show significant changes in laboratory, instrumental, or anthropometric parameters.
Conclusion
The study demonstrated that the use of empagliflozin in chronic kidney disease patients coexisting with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease is associated with improvements in the metabolic, anthropometric parameters, and has a nephroprotective effect. However, additional large-scale and long-term studies are required to further elucidate the therapeutic benefits of empagliflozin and to determine its definitive impact on CKD and NAFLD outcomes.

title: #3125 Proteomic insights into the molecular mechanisms of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) using mIMCD3 cells
authors: Raquel Martínez Pulleiro; Ana Maria Barcia de la Iglesia; Laura Núñez González; Susana Bravo; Noa Carrera Cachaza; Catarina Allegue Toscano; Miguel Garcia Gonzalez
abstract:
Background and Aims
Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) is the most common hereditary kidney disease, primarily caused by mutations in the PKD1 (80%) and PKD2 (15%) genes. Other cases are either genetically unresolved or due to mutations in less common cystic genes. Individuals with ADPKD develop renal cysts progressively, leading to kidney function loss and the need for renal replacement therapy. Despite scientific advances, challenges remain, such as diagnostic and therapeutic limitations and a lack of understanding of the disease's molecular pathogenesis. Our objective was to conduct a comprehensive proteomic analysis of a monoclonal cell line to gain insights into the molecular mechanisms of ADPKD.
Method
Protein samples from monoclonal WT mIMCD3 cells and three Pkd1 KO mIMCD3 cell clones were analyzed. Cells were cultured, and proteins were extracted using RIPA buffer. The proteomic analysis was conducted by the Proteomics Platform of the Health Research Institute of Santiago de Compostela. It involved LC-MS/MS and protein identification and quantification. Results include qualitative analysis (Data-Dependent Acquisition, DDA) and quantitative analysis (Sequential Window Acquisition of All Theoretical Mass Spectra, SWATH). DDA provides a comprehensive list of identified proteins, while SWATH includes quantified proteins common across conditions. Data was filtered to include proteins with a p-value <0.05 and a fold change >1.5. Bioinformatic tools like STRING, Heatmapper.com, and GraphPad Prism 10 were used for data analysis. mIMCD3 cell cycle was analyzed by flow cytometry.
Results
PCA showed clear clustering of KO and WT groups. SWATH identified 334 differentially expressed proteins: 165 upregulated, 118 downregulated, and 51 exclusive to KO. DDA detected 765 proteins, with 291 shared between techniques.
STRING enrichment analysis was applied to all dysregulated, upregulated, and downregulated proteins. Gene Ontology terms revealed insights into mitochondrial metabolism and RNA-related processes. Upregulated proteins highlighted mitochondrial changes, while downregulated proteins were linked to diverse metabolic processes. Subcellular location enrichment aligned with biological processes, showing mitochondrial and RNA-related terms. Tissue expression enrichment did not find kidney-related terms but identified other organ systems.
In terms of metabolism in Pkd1 KO mIMCD3 cells, glycolysis showed two glycolytic proteins differently regulated with opposite behaviors, making it difficult to determine alterations. Fatty acid oxidation was upregulated in Pkd1 KO cells. The TCA cycle was challenging to interpret due to varied enzyme activities. Oxidative phosphorylation had many upregulated proteins, indicating high energy demand, and Pkd1 KO cells were able to use oxygen under the used conditions, contrary to what has been described for ADPKD.
Regarding stress and apoptosis, there was an increased stress state, particularly in the mitochondria. Pro-apoptotic proteins were upregulated, while anti-apoptotic proteins were downregulated.
The cellular status studied by flow cytometry showed that WT cells exhibited a population with a Gaussian distribution, while mutants had a bimodal distribution. The cell cycle profile indicated a decrease in S phase cells and an increase in G2/M phase cells in mutants, suggesting genetic instability.
Conclusion
The proteomic study of mIMCD3 cells finds the mitochondria and the mitochondrial metabolism to be the most enriched terms based on the dysregulated proteins between Pkd1 KO and WT cells. Pkd1 KO cells show altered population size distribution and cell cycle, indicative of genetic instability.

title: #3247 Hyperkalemia: treatment and associated costs in Argentina
authors: Marcelo Taylor; Noelia Sforza; Sofia Paz; Francisco Pinto; Marina Fiorella Tabares
abstract:
Background and Aims
Hyperkalemia (HK) is defined as an elevated level of serum potassium in the blood, a condition frequently observed in populations with pathologies such as arterial hypertension, diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular disease and chronic kidney disease. This elevation has health consequences and is a barrier to optimizing cardio-nephroprotective treatment. However, in Argentine practice it is underestimated and there is high tolerance to high values. There is no updated clinical practice guide for its approach and its economic implications have not been assessed. Hyperkalemia (HK) is defined as an elevated level of serum potassium in the blood, a condition frequently observed in populations with underlying pathologies and whose problem crosses various specialties, occurring more frequently in patients with hypertension, diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular disease and chronic kidney disease. This elevation has health consequences and is a barrier to optimizing cardio- nephroprotective treatment. However, in Argentine practice it is underestimated and there is high tolerance to high values. There is no updated clinical practice guide for its approach and its economic implications have not been assessed. Objectives: To identify the approach and estimate the direct and indirect medical costs and resources used annually for the management of HK in Argentina in all subsectors: public, social security and private sector.
Method
The study was carried out in three phases; first, a literature review was conducted in order to model the economic burden of hyperkalemia in a questionnaire validated by experts. Second, the Delphi Panel method was used to obtain a comprehensive understanding of resource utilization in the management of HK. This approach allowed for variations and nuances between different subsectors of the health system to be considered. The Delphi Panel consisted of six experts and involved two rounds of iterative questions.
Finally, a micro costing was performed to estimate the cost of HK in the different health subsectors of Argentina. Costs were analyzed in dollars (USD) at the official exchange rate at the time (November 2023)
Results
The presence of HK presents an average additional cost per patient of approximately 6,280 dollars per year, which includes diagnosis, treatment (outpatient and hospital), follow-up and associated events. Costs of diagnosis, treatment (outpatient and hospital), follow-up and adverse events (AE) of three hyperkalemia profiles were identified and estimated: acute (HKA), recurrent (HKR) and on dialysis (HKD). The average cost per patient per year in each profile for the entire health system was USD 5,700, USD 8,217 and USD 4,924 respectively. The main cost that describes its economic burden is AE (predominantly cardiovascular events). The events with the greatest economic impact were: arrhythmias, cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events. According to the panel, this could be associated with the fact that the dominant treatment strategy reported is the suspension of iRAAS (ACE inhibitors, ARBs and MRAs), which could be interpreted as a therapeutic crossroads between HK correction vs. cardiovascular and renal protection in these patients, and therefore, it could explain the presence and frequency of these three events. They explain 81%, 56% and 80% for HKA, HKR and HKD, respectively.
Conclusion
HK is associated with an average incremental cost per patient of USD 6,280. 73% of this is explained by AEs and 18% by hospital treatment. This study could contribute to a consensus on good practices regarding HK.

According to the panel, this could be associated with the fact that the dominant treatment strategy reported is the suspension of iRAAS (ACE inhibitors, ARBs and MRAs), which could be interpreted as a therapeutic crossroads between HK correction vs. cardiovascular and renal protection in these patients, and therefore, it could explain the presence and frequency of these three events. They explain 81%, 56% and 80% for HKA, HKR and HKD, respectively.
Conclusion
HK is associated with an average incremental cost per patient of USD 6,280. 73% of this is explained by AEs and 18% by hospital treatment. This study could contribute to a consensus on good practices regarding HK.

title: #3302 SEARCH project: early diagnosis of chronic kidney disease in Argentina. Initial results
authors: Marcelo Taylor; Guillermo Javier Rosa Diez; Hernan Trimarchi; Ricardo Heguilen; Dora Aguero; Oscar Gaston Alvarez; Enrique Aliciardi; Noelia Sforza; Adriana Penalba; Raúl Vigil; Lara Mariscal
abstract:
Background and Aims
SEARCH is an educational campaign for health professionals about the early diagnosis of CKD. It involves the generation of material, educational talk and promotes a change in medical practice by reporting the estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) automatically (CKD-EPI Formula or MDRD4) at each request of serum creatinine (Cr).
Aims: Presentation of the results at 6 months of the implementation of this educational campaign in 10 health institutions, both public and private in 6 Argentine provinces.
Method
the number of determinations of urea, Cr, microalbuminuria (albuminuria/creatininuria in spontaneous urine or 24 h), eGFR, eGFR <60ml/min and the number of visits to Nephrology were collected at baseline and at 3, 6 and 12 months. Data were analyzed with a closure date of June 2024.
Results
In the first three cut-off points a total of 68264 creatinine measurements and 6681 nephrological consultations were recorded. At baseline, a median of 1805 (interquartile range [IQR]: 755–2730) urea and 2037 (720–3244) Cr measurements were recorded. The median number of microalbuminuria determinations was 57 (26–261). At baseline, 21 eGFR calculations were reported and a median of 154 (56–264) referrals to Nephrology were recorded. After the implementation of the program, an increase in the determination of urea and Cr was verified (3539 [1809–4450] and 3614 [1855–4643], respectively). The number of microalbuminuria determinations increased to 158 (64–343). An increase in the number of eGFR reports was observed at 3 and 6 months (19666 and 20438 records, respectively; P = 0.001 vs. baseline). Reporting of patients with eGFR < 60 mL/min increased significantly (2456 and 3000 records at 3 and 6 months, in that order; P = 0.003 vs. baseline). 13.6% presented values of eGFR was <60 ml/min. Referrals to Nephrology increased non-significantly at 6 months (median: 246; 198–468).
Conclusion
The implementation of SEARCH was associated with an increase in the determinations of renal function parameters in the real world, with significant differences between 3 and 6 months for the calculation of eGFR, proteinuria and early detection of patients with early stages of CKD. 13.6% of patients in the overall population had an eGFR <60 ml/min.

title: #3627 Predictive value of blood cellular indices for thromboembolic events in end-stage renal disease
authors: Martin Arceo; Fakiha Siddiqui; Vinod Bansal; Debra Hoppensteadt; Jawed Fareed
abstract:
Background and Aims
In end-stage renal disease (ESRD), uremic toxin buildup triggers chronic inflammation, immune dysfunction, and oxidative stress, collectively increasing thromboembolic risk. Blood cellular indices—such as the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR)—have emerged as key biomarkers of systemic inflammation and endothelial dysfunction, correlating with elevated risks of stroke, pulmonary embolism (PE), myocardial infarction (MI), and deep vein thrombosis (DVT). This study evaluates the predictive power of NLR, SII, and PLR for thromboembolic events in patients with ESRD.
Method
Blood samples were collected from 112 ESRD patients at Loyola University Medical Center. Blood cellular indices were derived from these samples, and incidences of thromboembolic events—including stroke, PE, MI, and DVT—were recorded via retrospective chart review. Linear regression analyses assessed the predictive power of NLR, SII, and PLR.
Results
Linear regression confirmed NLR as the strongest predictor of stroke (R² = 0.211, β = 0.376, 95% CI = 0.015–0.031, P < 0.001) and a moderate predictor of PE (R² = 0.087, β = 0.231, 95% CI = 0.004–0.015, P = 0.002). SII also demonstrated moderate predictive power for stroke (R² = 0.193, β = 0.298, 95% CI = 9.26 x 10−5–2.105 × 10−4, P < 0.001), while PLR had a weaker but still significant relationship (R² = 0.165, β = 0.238, 95% CI = 4.189 x 10−4–0.001, P < 0.001).
Conclusion
Our analysis demonstrates that NLR was the strongest predictor of stroke in ESRD patients, with significant associations also observed for SII and PLR. NLR additionally displayed predictive value for PE, although comparatively weaker than stroke. These findings highlight the role of blood cellular indices in enhancing risk stratification for thromboembolic events in patients with ESRD, thereby reducing morbidity and mortality. Future research with larger cohorts is needed to validate these findings and better define the role of blood cellular indices in risk stratification.

title: #2436 The association between cognitive impairment and brain imaging changes in chronic kidney disease and the impact of physical activity on this relationship: a systematic review
authors: Louise Ryan; Jonathan Law; Julia Brettschneider; Ponnusamy Saravanan; Indranil Dasgupta
abstract:
Background and Aims
Cognitive impairment is common in people with chronic kidney disease (CKD). Abnormalities in brain imaging are also highly prevalent in people with CKD with white matter hyperintensities (WMH), decreases in brain and lobar volumes and cerebral micro-bleeds being the most common changes. Physical activity prevents cerebral atrophy and increases hippocampal volume in the general population and has been shown to have the potential to make a clinically significant, positive impact on cognitive impairment in CKD. Despite several studies addressing the degree to which cognitive impairment and brain imaging abnormalities are correlated in CKD, this relationship has not clearly been defined. We conducted this systematic review to answer 2 questions: firstly, in adults with non-dialysis dependent CKD (NDDCKD), what is the association between brain imaging abnormalities on MRI and cognitive function? Secondly, does physical activity alter the relationship between cognition and brain imaging abnormalities in adults with NDDCKD?
Method
This study was conducted in line with the PRISMA guidelines. A systematic search of 4 medical databases (Embase, MEDLINE, Scopus and CENTRAL) was conducted to identify relevant articles. The population of interest was people with NDDCKD. Kidney transplant recipients were excluded. Published randomised controlled trials, quasi-experimental trials, cohort studies and case control studies in English were eligible for inclusion. There was no timeframe restriction.
Results
Ten articles relating to 9 studies were included (1,230 participants) in the review of question 1. Seven of these studies were cross-sectional while 2 were cohort studies. Four studies described the outcomes in people with ND CKD5 while the remainder spanned from CKD stage 1 to ND stage 5. Seven of the nine studies showed a positive correlation between cognitive impairment and changes in brain MRI in people with CKD. The outcomes of the studies addressing the relationship between brain volumes and cognitive function (4 positive, 2 negative) and that of white matter changes and cognitive function (2 positive and 2 negative) are outlined in Table 1. Two studies found an association between changes in functional MRI brains and cognitive impairment including changes in characteristic path length and global and local efficiency. No studies were found that addressed question 2.
Conclusion
There was a trend towards an association between decreased brain volumes and changes in functional brain MRI with cognitive impairment in CKD. No study was found which addressed the impact of physical activity on this association.

title: #2661 Interplay between polymorphism in the EDNRA gene and endothelin-1 concentration in the blood of patients with chronic kidney disease
authors: Milena Ściskalska; Magdalena Król-Kulikowska; Miroslaw Banasik; Marta Kepinska
abstract:
Background and Aims
The important role of endothelin-1 (ET-1) in inflammation, fibrosis and podocyte dysfunction was proven. ET-1 can influence on glomerular filtration barrier via ETA receptor (ETAR) activation, what contributes to podocyte apoptosis and renal tubular damage. The role of ET-1 in chronic kidney disease (CKD) was proven. The aim of this study is to evaluate the concentration of ET-1 in the blood of healthy individuals (n = 80) and patients with diabetics kidney disease (n = 70). Additionally, this study analyzed the impact of the rs5333 polymorphism in the EDNRA gene on ET-1 concentration in the studied population.
Method
The rs5333 polymorphism in the EDNRA gene was determined using the PCR-RFLP method, while ET-1 levels in plasma were measured using a commercial ELISA test. The statistical analysis of the obtained results was performed using the STATISTICA 13.3 package. The Kruskal-Wallis H test was used to determine significant differences between the studied subgroups.
Results
A significant increase in ET-1 concentration in the group of patients with CKD compared to healthy individuals was found. Higher ET-1 concentrations were observed in healthy men compared to healthy women. In contrast, in the patient group, higher concentrations of this peptide were found in women compared to men. In the group of women with CKD with the T/T genotype, a significantly higher ET-1 concentration was observed compared to women with CKD with the T/C genotype for rs5333 polymorphism in the EDNRA gene
Conclusion
Chronic kidney disease increases the concentration of ET-1 in the blood. Male gender significantly affects endothelin-1 levels in healthy individuals. The T/T genotype for SNP rs5333 in the EDNRA gene predisposes women with CKD to elevated ET-1 levels in the blood.

title: #2908 Vadadustat combination with ferric citrate, compared to either agent alone, protects against inflammation-induced anaemia and anaemia-induced by chronic kidney disease
authors: Steven Burke; Debie Hoivik; Anna Zuk
abstract:
Background and Aims
Anaemia of chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a major unmet medical need. Vadadustat, a hypoxia-inducible factor prolyl hydroxylase inhibitor (HIF-PHI), approved for the treatment of anaemia of dialysis-dependent CKD, stimulates endogenous erythropoietin (EPO) production, increasing haemoglobin (Hb) and haematocrit (HCT). Ferric citrate is a source of iron and is used as a treatment for iron deficiency anaemia. The objectives of these studies were to determine if the co-administration of vadadustat with a well-absorbed oral iron preparation such as ferric citrate would have additive effects on anaemia correction.
Method
The experiments were conducted in the peptidoglycan polysaccharide (PGPS) rat model of inflammation-induced anaemia, and the rat model of adenine-induced CKD (n = 10/group). Primary treatments included both vadadustat and ferric citrate alone and in combination, with appropriate controls. Recombinant human EPO (rhEPO) was used in some experiments as a comparator.
Results
In the PGPS rat model of inflammation-induced anaemia, the coadministration of vadadustat and ferric citrate caused a statistically significant increase in serum iron and transferrin saturation (TSAT) and a statistically significant decrease in total iron binding capacity (TIBC) compared to when vadadustat or ferric citrate were given alone. There were also increases in Hb, HCT, percent reticulocytes, mean corpuscular volume (MCV) and mean corpuscular haemoglobin (MCH) levels. Regarding inflammation, the combination of vadadustat and ferric citrate treatment decreased white blood cell counts in a statistically significantly manner and this was associated with decreases in neutrophil and lymphocyte counts, haptoglobin, IL-6, IL-15, C-reactive protein, ankle diameter and paw weight. Similarly, in the rat model of adenine-induced CKD, there was a statistically significant increase in serum iron levels in the rats given vadadustat in combination with ferric citrate compared to the rats given ferric citrate or vadadustat alone or in rats given rhEPO either alone or in combination with ferric citrate. Consistent with the serum iron data, the combination of vadadustat and ferric citrate resulted in increases in TIBC, serum iron saturation percent, Hb, HCT, MCV and MCH levels. Serum levels of IL-6, FGF-21, and myostatin, markers of inflammation, did not differ statistically across groups.
Conclusion
Collectively, these data suggest vadadustat in combination with oral iron provides greater improvement in anaemia related parameters in models of inflammation-induced anaemia and CKD than when either agent is given alone.

title: #507 Correlation of homocysteine levels with lipid profile and coronary heart disease in chronic kidney disease patients on hemodialysis—preliminary findings
authors: Maria Sofra
abstract:
Background and Aims
Patients with end-stage chronic kidney disease (ESRD) exhibit disturbances in protein and amino acid metabolism and elevated homocysteine levels. The latter has been implicated as an independent risk factor for cardiovascular events in these patients. The aim of the present study is to correlate homocysteine levels with lipid profile and cardiovascular events in these patients.
Method
In this study 50 patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) on hemodialysis for >6 months, 30 men (60%) and 20 women (40%) were included. The mean age of the patients was 67.6 years ± 13.21 and the main underlying diseases were hypertensive nephrosclerosis (n = 15, 30%) and diabetic nephropathy (n = 11, 22%). Patients were divided into two groups according to the presence or absence of coronary artery disease (CAD) and based on receiving or not antilipidemic treatment and folic acid. Serum homocysteine levels were correlated with normal laboratory values, total cholesterol, triglycerides, HDL and LDL cholesterol levels.
Results
Homocysteine levels were found elevated in 70% of patients. Over the course of a year, an upward trend of homocysteine levels was observed regarding normal values (1st measurement: 21.8%, 2nd measurement: 26.6%, 3rd measurement: 29.6%). Men appeared to have higher homocysteine levels than women, but the difference was not statistically significant (P = 0.17). Homocysteine levels were found to be elevated in patients without CAD compared to those with CAD (P = 0.04). A positive correlation between homocysteine levels and total cholesterol (P = 0.01), LDL (P = 0.007) and CRP (P = 0.02) was observed in both CAD and non-CAD patients. In addition, homocysteine levels in patients receiving antilipidemic treatment were higher than in patients not receiving it (P = 0.04). There was no statistically significant difference in homocysteine levels between patients receiving or not receiving folic acid (P = 0.94).
Conclusion
Homocysteine levels were found to be elevated in a high percentage of patients but surprisingly there was no statistically significant equivalence with CAD while the correlation with cholesterol and LDL cholesterol levels was statistically significant in both groups. Our findings are contradictory based on classical knowledge, and due to the fact that are preliminary with a relatively small number of patients, further study is necessary in order to confirm our findings.

title: #2671 Relationship of the `kidney failure risk equation' with disease progression and cost in chronic kidney disease stages 3–5
authors: Ayşe Müge Holoğlu; Ezgi Aysu Şahin Mavi; Necla Ozer; Irem Ozarli; Gorkem Celebi; Guldehan Haberal; Arda Erdut; Hacı Hasan Yeter; Tolga Yıldırım; Şeref Rahmi Yilmaz; Bulent Altun; Mustafa Arici
abstract:
Background and Aims
Chronic kidney disease (CKD) significantly impacts healthcare systems and economies. The kidney failure risk equation (KFRE), developed in 2011, predicts the risk of progression to kidney failure more accurately. KFRE may guide better management of healthcare resources and is increasingly used in practice. The primary objectives of this study were to estimate the risk of progression to end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) in patients diagnosed with stage G3-G4 CKD using KFRE and to examine the impact on healthcare resource utilization.
Method
This single-center, retrospective observational study was conducted in the Department of Nephrology at Hacettepe University Hospitals. Patients aged 18 years and older, with an estimated glomerular filtration rate between 15-60 mL/min/1.73 m² and who were regularly followed up from 2014 to 2019 were included in the study. Patients with missing data at the time of admission, pregnancy status, malignancy, and history of renal replacement therapy were excluded, and a total of 822 patients were included in the study. 4- and 8-variable KFRE were calculated. Stage G3 and G4 CKD patients were analyzed in all risk categories as low, intermediate, and high risk according to KFRE. The term “end stage kidney disease-free survival” (ESKD-fs) was used to report the survival rates of patients who did not undergo dialysis and/or kidney transplantation. Hospital resource use and costs were evaluated separately in all risk categories.
Results
In stage G3 patients, according to the 4- and 8-variable KFRE, the 5-year ESKD-fs rate was significantly higher in low-risk patients compared to those in the intermediate- and high-risk groups (P < 0.001 and P < 0.001, respectively) (Figs 1 and 2). In stage G4 patients, according to the 4- and 8-variable KFRE, the 2-year ESKD-fs rate was significantly higher in low-risk patients compared to those in the other risk groups (P < 0.001 and P < 0.001, respectively) (Figs 3 and 4). In addition, according to the 4-variable KFRE classification, the median annual outpatient treatment cost in stage G3 patients was found to be $121 in the high-risk group, $98 in the intermediate-risk group, and $94 in the low- risk group (P = 0.017). According to the 4-variable KFRE classification for patients with stage G3, the median annual hospitalization costs were $622 in the high-risk group, $447 in the intermediate-risk group, and $433 in the low-risk group (P = 0.025). According to the 8- variable KFRE classification, the median annual hospitalization costs in patients with stage G3 were $628 in the high-risk group, whereas they were $478 and $423 in the intermediate- and low-risk groups, respectively (P = 0.045). Furthermore, according to the 4- variable KFRE for patients with stages G3 and G4, the median annual hospitalization numbers were significantly higher in the high-risk group (P < 0.001 and P = 0.006, respectively).
Conclusion
This study demonstrated that KFRE models accurately predict the 2- and 5-year risk of progression to ESKD in patients with stage 3–5 CKD. We demonstrated that patients with stage G3 CKD, who are at higher risk of progression to renal failure according to KFRE, have higher hospital outpatient and hospitalization costs compared to patients in the low-risk category. Effective application of KFRE emerges as a powerful tool for early diagnosis and cost-effective management of at-risk patients.

The term “end stage kidney disease-free survival” (ESKD-fs) was used to report the survival rates of patients who did not undergo dialysis and/or kidney transplantation. Hospital resource use and costs were evaluated separately in all risk categories.

In stage G3 patients, according to the 4- and 8-variable KFRE, the 5-year ESKD-fs rate was significantly higher in low-risk patients compared to those in the intermediate- and high-risk groups (P < 0.001 and P < 0.001, respectively) (Figs 1 and 2). In stage G4 patients, according to the 4- and 8-variable KFRE, the 2-year ESKD-fs rate was significantly higher in low-risk patients compared to those in the other risk groups (P < 0.001 and P < 0.001, respectively) (Figs 3 and 4). According to the 4-variable KFRE classification for patients with stage G3, the median annual hospitalization costs were $622 in the high-risk group, $447 in the intermediate-risk group, and $433 in the low-risk group (P = 0.025). According to the 8- variable KFRE classification, the median annual hospitalization costs in patients with stage G3 were $628 in the high-risk group, whereas they were $478 and $423 in the intermediate- and low-risk groups, respectively (P = 0.045). This study demonstrated that KFRE models accurately predict the 2- and 5-year risk of progression to ESKD in patients with stage 3–5 CKD. Effective application of KFRE emerges as a powerful tool for early diagnosis and cost-effective management of at-risk patients.

title: #3185 Insights into the adoption of consensus guidelines for hyperkalemia management in Spain: a national, multicenter, descriptive analysis
authors: Andrea Diez; Nicolás Fernandez; María Garcia; David Ollero; Elsa Alepuz Gilabert; Eloy Gutiérrez; Rodrigo Lombraña; Laura Rama; Amaia Ugarte de Miguel; Barbara De la Lama Lara; Alberto Jimenez; Miren Sequera Mutiozabal
abstract:
Background and Aims
Hyperkalemia is a recurrent, life-threatening electrolyte imbalance requiring rapid intervention. The latest Spanish Consensus Document on the Management of Hyperkalemia published in 2023 outlined recommendations for improving its management. In this analysis, we assessed the perception of nephrologists and other specialists who manage this condition as regards the adoption of these guidelines in Spain.
Method
A national, multicenter, descriptive analysis was conducted with nephrologists and specialists in cardiology, internal medicine, and geriatrics involved in hyperkalemia management. Participants were presented with eight questions evaluating clinical practices based on the recommendations of the Consensus Document, divided into the categories of 'knowledge' and 'management'. These questions were discussed at 27 medical meetings held in Spain between November 2023 and December 2024.
Results
A total of 122 nephrologists and 186 professionals from the aforementioned specialties participated. Almost three-quarters of nephrologists (73.2%) and 72.3% of the other specialists declared adequate knowledge of hyperkalemia classification. Nevertheless, only 30.3% of nephrologists and 21.9% of the others reported a second episode of hyperkalemia in 30%–40% of patients with heart failure and/or chronic kidney disease. Regarding management, 70.8% of nephrologists and 70.4% of the other specialists prioritized adding potassium binders for mild hyperkalemia when the patient is receiving optimal therapy, and 90.8% of nephrologists and 70.8% of the other specialists participating in this analysis considered using new antihyperkalemic agents at discharge to prevent recurrence. However, only 25.7% of nephrologists and 22.3% of the other specialists agreed with the recommendation to maintain renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system inhibitor (RAASi) treatment with no adjustments. Despite this, 79.8% of nephrologists and 84.8% of the others perceived that the recommendation to reintroduce it upon discharge was considered by clinicians. Regarding treatment initiation, 15.7% of nephrologists and 14.6% of the other specialties reported that they start antihyperkalemic agents at potassium levels of 5–5.5 mEq/L. Additionally, only 17.9% of nephrologists and 20.7% of the other clinicians indicated adherence to the recommendation not to discontinue antihyperkalemic treatment once normokalemia is reached. Finally, 32.5% of nephrologists and 18.4% of the others lacked access to new antihyperkalemic agents, and 35.2% of nephrologists and 55.9% of the other specialists had no access to updated management protocols.
Conclusion
There is a high level of awareness regarding the consensus document on the management of hyperkalemia. However, notable gaps remain in the implementation of key recommendations, particularly regarding RAASi therapy and the use of antihyperkalemic agents. Encouragingly, there is a gradual shift towards improved management practices, such as having a RAASi reintroduction or titration plan. Standardizing and optimizing hyperkalemia management has the potential to significantly improve patient cardiorenal outcomes while reducing healthcare costs.
The authors presented this communication on behalf of AstraZeneca Medical team involved in ‘Aktuando Juntos’ program.

title: #1000 Assessment of metabolic risk of exposure to lithogenic factors and prevention of development of nephrolithiasis in children
authors: Shamansurova Elmira; Abdurazakova Shirin; Isakhanova Nigora; Yorkin Rasulev
abstract:
Background
Among all urological pathologies, nephrolithiasis (N) is in second place, second only to infectious pathologies of the urinary tract. Among all patients in urological departments of hospitals, the proportion of N varies within 30%–50%.
Aims
to identify risk factors for the development of nephrolithiasis in children and to create a prognostic matrix for a comprehensive risk assessment.
Method
In order to determine the influence of various factors on the risk of developing nephrolithiasis in children, we formed 3 groups of patients from the examined children: Group I—57 children (26 boys and 31 girls), average age—4.51 ± 3.83 years with a diagnosis of urolithiasis, Group II—32 children (21 boys and 11 girls), average age 4.66 ± 2.81 years with a diagnosis of chronic tubulointerstitial nephritis (TIN). Group III—31 children (16 boys and 15 girls), average age—4.58 ± 2.19 years with crystalluria (oxalate—74.19%, urate—6.45%, mixed—19.36. For the purpose of statistical comparison of the obtained indicators of the children studied in the work, we formed a control group (CG) of practically healthy 8 boys and 22 girls aged 2–7 years, average age—4.40 ± 1.57 years. We conducted a study of the anamnesis of the patients studied, the frequency of occurrence of certain parameters.
Results
The analysis of the frequency of the studied and compared nuances of the anamnesis of the examined children, their mothers, including the number of pregnancies and its course, childbirth, medications received by the pregnant woman and the already born child, the mother's comorbid background, the presence of a burden in parents and their relatives for H., as an aspect of heredity, and other compared parameters allowed us to further assess the strength of the influence of each of them on the formation and rate of development of H, taking into account different "stages" of pathology between the studied groups. The data showed that mothers of children in group I had a higher frequency of early and late gestosis, they more often took GCS and vitamins during pregnancy, suffered from diabetes mellitus and obesity, more often gave birth to premature babies and with the help of cesarean section, less often breastfed, children of this group more often suffered from rickets, diseases of the urinary system and gastrointestinal tract, more often received AB, pro- and prebiotics. In many respects it is similar to groups I and III, but we can only assess the influence of similar frequencies of possible risk factors by statistical analysis of these and other indicators of all studied groups in a comparative aspect.
Analysis of the data obtained during the study allowed us to develop a methodology for assessing the probability (predicting) of the occurrence of crystalluria and H in children. We compiled a prognostic matrix, which, based on anamnestic data, allows us to identify a risk group for the development of H in children.
Then, in accordance with the standards, we calculated risk subranges in 3 intervals: low (106.9–371.8), medium (371.9–636.7) and high (636.8–952.7) probability of the risk of developing HL and threshold values ​​of prognostic coefficients as the boundaries of risk groups (Table 1).
Individual prediction of the development of complications allows us to anticipate the development of urolithiasis, which implies a change in eating habits and water consumption, and, if the prognosis is unfavorable, supplementing the above with treatment and preventive measures.
Conclusion
Individual prognosis can be used in a screening manner by studying only the most significant strong laboratory indicators and assigning them points, the sum of which will determine the risk group of a particular child.

title: #1800 Cardiorenal relationships: correlation analysis of the effect of metabolic syndrome components on renal and cardiac function in heart failure patients with mid-range ejection fraction
authors: Muzaffar Asomov; Gulchehra Atakhodjayeva; Olimkhon Sharapov; Rakhimjon Tursunbayev; Ranokhon Igamberdieva; Saodat Ulmasova
abstract:
Background and Aims
An independent inverse relationship was found between eGFR <60 ml/min/1.73 m2 and an increased risk of death, cardiovascular outcomes, and hospitalization. The incidence of new cardiovascular complications is 4.8% in patients with stage 2 CKD and almost doubles in stages 3–4. The risk of developing adverse cardiovascular outcomes in patients on dialysis or in kidney transplant recipients is tens of times higher than in the general population. Aim was to study the nature of the relationships between the glomerular filtration rate (GFR), carbohydrate and lipid metabolism parameters (glucose, TG), body mass index (BMI), blood pressure (BP) and parameters of systolic and diastolic function of the left ventricle (LV) in patients with HFmrEF with different representations of metabolic syndrome (MS) components.
Method
97 male patients with chronic heart failure (CHF) of ischemic genesis, functional class (FC) II–III according to NYHA, aged 40–60 years, with a history of myocardial infarction from 6 months to 5 years were examined. Depending on the presence of MS components, 3 groups of patients were identified: Group I (n = 70), patients without MS (CHF FC II—38, CHF FC III—32 patients); Group II (n = 67) patients with various combinations of dyslipidemia (HDL-C <1.03 mmol/l; LDL-C >3.0 mmol/l) with abdominal obesity (AO), hypertension and hypertriglyceridemia (HTG) (CHF FC II—35, CHF FC III—32 patients); Group III (n = 60) patients with various combinations of dyslipoproteinemia (DLP) and type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM2) with AO, hypertension and hypertriglyceridemia (HTG) (CHF FC II—26, CHF FC III—34 patients).
According to the classification of CHF (ESC 2016), depending on the level of ejection fraction (EF), all examined patients with CHF were also divided into subgroups: with normal (preserved EF)—EF ≥50% (HFpEF) and mid-range EF (gray zone)—EF = 40%–49% (HFmrEF). Thus, in group I of patients with CHF without MS, 42 had preserved EF and 28 patients had mid-range EF, in group II, 39 patients had preserved EF, 28 patients with CHF mid-range EF, and in group III, 28 had preserved EF and 32 had mid-range EF.
All examined patients (HFmrEF, EF 40%–49%) were divided into three groups: without MS (group I), with MS (group II), and with MS in combination with T2DM (group III). The following parameters were assessed: eGFR (using the calculation formula or creatinine clearance), TG, glucose, BP, BMI, and echocardiography parameters (EF, IVRT, E/A ratio, RE/RA). Correlation analysis was performed to identify significant relationships between cardiac and renal parameters.
Results
In the group without MS (I), statistically significant inverse relationships were found between eGFR and TG, glucose, BMI (r = –0.46 to –0.49; P < 0.01) and positive relationships with EF (r = 0.58; P < 0.01) and endothelial-dependent vasodilation (r = 0.69; P < 0.001). In the presence of MS (group II), the most pronounced positive correlation of eGFR with EF (r = 0.72; P < 0.001) and negative relationships with BP (r = –0.42; P < 0.01) and BMI (r = –0.39; P < 0.05) were observed. In combination with MS and T2DM (group III), the strongest negative relationships of eGFR with TG (r = –0.63; P < 0.001) and glucose (r = –0.74; P < 0.001) were recorded, as well as a positive correlation with the LV diastolic function index (RE/RA) (r = 0.49; P < 0.01).
Conclusion
(1) The parameters of cardiac (systolic and diastolic) and renal function are closely interrelated with the components of MS (hypertriglyceridemia, arterial hypertension, hyperglycemia, obesity). (2) Deterioration of metabolic status (especially when combined with type 2 diabetes) is accompanied by a significant decrease in eGFR and an increased risk of cardiorenal complications, which should be taken into account in the treatment and dynamic monitoring of patients with HFmrEF.

title: #2054 Observation of the therapeutic effect of finerenone, a novel non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist, in patients with non-diabetic CKD
authors: Fang Li; Jing Han; Wenjing Zhang; Jia Lv; Zhigang Wang; Huixian Li; Jin Li; Jie Feng; Wanhong Lu; Jiping Sun
abstract:
Background and Aims
Finerenone, a non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA), has anti-fibrotic and anti-inflammatory properties. Two clinical studies have demonstrated that finerenone can slow the progression of chronic kidney disease (CKD) and decrease cardiovascular events in CKD linked with diabetes. However, studies assessing CKD patients without diabetes are scarce. Further research is required to determine the safety and effectiveness of finerenone in the real-world setting for this demographic.
Method
This retrospective, single-center real-world study assessed non-diabetic CKD patients >18 years old administered finerenone at Xi'an Jiao Tong University's First Affiliated Hospital between January 2023 and August 2023. The primary study indicators were estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), 24-hour urine protein, serum potassium (sK+), and serum albumin. Follow-up for six months was performed to assess finerenone's safety and effectiveness.
Results
(1) 78 patients proved eligible. The effective rate was 61.5% (n = 48) and the average age was 41.53 ± 12.54 years, including 50 (64.1%) men. Totally 34 (43.6%) cases had cardiovascular disease. After treatment, the average age of the 48 effective cases was 44.33 ± 12.75 years, with 31 (64.6%) males and 20 (41.7%) cardiovascular disease cases. (2) Among effective patients, the average 24-hour proteinuria was 1.71 ± 0.32 g/d, and the average eGFR was 88.34 ± 4.48 ml/min/1.73 m2 at baseline. After treatment, the average 24-hour proteinuria was significantly decreased, the average eGFR briefly decreased, the average sK+ fluctuated only slightly, and the average serum albumin gradually increased. At 3 and 6 months after finerenone initiation, average proteinuria levels were 0.64 ± 0.14 g/d (P = 0.002) and 0.55 ± 0.14 g/d (P < 0.001), average percentage changes from baseline were −63% and −68%, respectively; mean eGFR were 82.09 ± 4.69 ml/min/1.73 m2 (P = 0.016) and 87.05 ± 6.21 ml/min/1.73 m2 (P = 0.759), respectively. The average sK+ were 4.23 ± 0.07 mmol/L, 4.46 ± 0.07 mmol/L (P = 0.003), 4.41 ± 0.08 mmol/L (P = 0.041), at baseline and 3 and 6 months, respectively. The average serum albumin were 39.17 ± 0.93 g/L, 41.80 ± 0.70 g/L (P = 0.005), 42.24 ± 0.70 g/L (P = 0.003) at baseline and 3 and 6 months, respectively. (3) The half of IgAN cases (n = 20) achieved proteinuria relief. (4) During finerenone treatment, combination with RASi alone, SGLT2i alone or RASi + SGLT2i resulted in higher efficacy versus cases not administered these drugs (effective rates of 64%, 60%, 63% vs 50%, respectively), but the difference was not statistically significant (χ² = 0.664, P = 0.952). (5) Adverse effects were minimal.
Conclusion
Finerenone can effectively decrease proteinuria in patients with non-diabetic CKD, with little impacts on eGFR and sK+. Its efficacy does not depend on concurrent use of RASi and SGLT2i. It is expected to confer proteinuria remission in IgAN. However, given the limited sample size, more comprehensive prospective studies and real-world research are needed to corroborate the results of this study.

title: #2629 Decoding the CKD-MASLD connection in diabetes: a prospective study
authors: Luciana Marc; Adelina Mihaescu; Lazar Chisavu; Nicu Olariu; Oana-Marina Schiller; Adalbert Schiller
abstract:
Background and Aims
Chronic kidney disease (CKD) and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) are widespread comorbidities in individuals with type 2 diabetic mellitus (T2DM), significantly raising morbidity and mortality rates. These conditions share overlapping pathophysiological mechanisms, including persistent low-grade inflammation, insulin resistance, oxidative stress, and dysregulated lipid metabolism, which collectively aggravate disease development and systemic consequences. Although the individual effects of CKD and MASLD in T2DM patients are well-documented, their specific interaction remains insufficiently explored. This study aims to evaluate the relationship between CKD and MASLD in a cohort of patients with T2DM.
Method
We conducted a prospective study involving 91 T2DM patients with confirmed MASLD, recruited from the Nephrology Clinic at Pius Brânzeu Clinical Emergency County Hospital, Timișoara, Romania, between January and December 2023. CKD was diagnosed and staged according to KDIGO 2024 guidelines, which included eGFR (CKD-Epi) and urine albumin-creatinine ratio (UACR). MASLD was identified utilizing FibroScan® with transient elastography (TE) and the controlled attenuation parameter (CAP). At enrollment, all patients were tested for CBC, renal function (urea, creatinine), fasting glucose, HbA1c, liver enzymes, lipid profile (total cholesterol, HDL, LDL, triglycerides), and UACR. Serum creatinine levels were rechecked after three months to confirm real CKD. The patients were divided into two groups: CKD (n = 55) and non-CKD (n = 36). The statistical analyses included t-tests, Mann-Whitney U tests, and Pearson correlation.

Given the limited existing research on this association, our findings offer a foundation for future studies to investigate and validate this relationship.

title: #2919 Risk factors for albuminuria in patients with previously undiagnosed chronic kidney disease—AURA registry data
authors: Mikhail Batyushin; Gregory Arutyunov; Alexander Arutyunov; Ekaterina Tarlovskaya; Dmitry Polyakov; Roman Bashkinov; Marina Trubnikova; Tatiana Batluk; Evgenii Melnikov; Elizaveta Gordeychuk; Anastasiia Ermilova
abstract:
Background and Aims
Albuminuria (AU) is a laboratory marker included in the diagnostic criteria for chronic kidney disease (CKD) according to KDIGO recommendations. However, in real-world clinical practice use of this marker is less widespread compared to the calculation of glomerular filtration rate (GFR).
To identify risk factors for albuminuria in patients with previously undiagnosed CKD.
Method
AURA (NCT05690009) is a real-world clinical practice registry covering 34 regions of the Russian Federation. It included 4,531 patients older >40 years without previously verified CKD or type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus. The AU level was determined once using test strips at the time of patient enrollment in the registry. The threshold value for AU was set at 20 mg/L. To develop the model demographic data (age and sex) and information on chronic diseases from medical records were analyzed.
Results
AU <20 mg/L was identified in 1,592 patients (35.1%), while AU ≥20 mg/L was found in 2,939 patients (64.9%). A multivariate model revealed that the presence of AU ≥20 mg/L was significantly influenced by age, metabolic syndrome, prediabetes, cardiovascular pathology, chronic cystitis, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) (Fig. 1).
ROC analysis of the multivariate risk prediction model for AU ≥20 mg/L in patients with previously undiagnosed CKD demonstrated satisfactory predictive value: area under the curve (AUC) of 61.5%, sensitivity of 66.0%, and specificity of 51.3%.
Conclusion
Data analysis from the AURA registry demonstrated that diagnostically significant AU in patients with previously undiagnosed CKD was significantly associated with age, cardiovascular diseases (myocardial infarction, atrial fibrillation), metabolic syndrome, prediabetes, chronic cystitis, and COPD. For older patients and those with these conditions, AU testing, including test strips, serves as an early CKD screening method, which can optimize medical care delivery and enable timely nephroprotective measures.

title: #804 Evaluation of sequential romosozumab-denosumab therapy for osteoporosis in maintenance hemodialysis patients
authors: Rie Kiyosumi; Kana Koinuma; Yuka Nodaira; Naofumi Ikeda
abstract:
Background and Aims
The risk of fractures in dialysis patients is approximately 5–6 times higher than in the general population. Osteoporosis significantly impacts the activities of daily living (ADL) and prognosis of dialysis patients. Despite the evident need for treatment, managing osteoporosis in these patients is challenging due to limited medication options, cautious administration requirements, and contraindications. As a result, treatment tends to be conservative and lacks well-established protocols.
This study evaluated the efficacy of sequential therapy combining romosozumab, a humanized monoclonal antibody targeting sclerostin, and denosumab, a human monoclonal antibody targeting RANKL. Romosozumab was administered in the first year to promote bone formation, followed by denosumab in the second year to inhibit bone resorption. We measured changes in bone mineral density (BMD) and bone metabolic markers to evaluate the effects of this treatment approach.
Method
From April 2019 to December 2024, 23 maintenance hemodialysis patients from our institution were enrolled in this study. The cohort included 3 males and 20 females, with a median age of 74.6 years (range: 47–88) and a median dialysis history of 11.8 years (range: 2–29). The inclusion criteria required no history of cardiovascular complications within the past year and no difficulty in calcium (Ca) management.
Patients received romosozumab, administered monthly for the first year, followed by denosumab, administered every six months during the second year. BMD of the lumbar spine and femoral neck was measured every three months using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA). Serum whole-parathyroid hormone (whole-PTH), corrected calcium (Ca), and phosphorus (P) levels, and bone metabolic markers such as tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase-5b (TRACP-5b), bone-specific alkaline phosphatase (BAP), and type I procollagen N-terminal propeptide (P1NP)—were measured monthly. Pre-treatment values, averages at the end of the first and second years, and values at 24 months were compared to evaluate the outcomes of the treatment.
Results
A comparison between pre-treatment and 24-month measurements revealed significant improvements in BMD. Lumbar spine BMD increased from 68.4 (44–96) at baseline to 80.7 (49–110) at 24 months (P < 0.001). Femoral neck BMD also improved significantly, increasing from 54.6 (37–68) at baseline to 56.1 (35–74) at 24 months (P = 0.012) (Fig. 1).
During the one-year romosozumab phase, lumbar spine BMD increased from 74.4 (63.4–92.5) to 86.8 (71.1–98.1) during the denosumab phase (P < 0.001). Similarly, femoral neck BMD improved from 57.3 (49.7–63.7) to 61.0 (52.1–64.9) (P < 0.001) (Fig. 2).
Bone metabolic markers also showed significant reductions in the second year. Whole-PTH decreased from 85.0 (64.0–136.1) pg/mL in the first year to 65.6 (41.3–80.2) pg/ml in the second year (P < 0.001). TRACP-5b decreased from 318.8 (211.8–440.3) mU/dl to 152.2 (117.5–253.5) mU/dl (P < 0.001). BAP decreased from 15.8 (11.9–18.7) μg/L to 9.32 (7.8–11.4) μg/L (P < 0.001), while P1NP decreased from 302.9 (217.9–470.5) ng/ml to 145.1 (91.9–253.9) ng/ml (P < 0.001) (Fig. 2).
The continued improvement in bone resorption markers observed during the denosumab phase suggests that the bone-forming effects of romosozumab, followed by the bone resorption inhibitory effects of denosumab, may have contributed to sustained improvements in bone mineral density.
Conclusion
Sequential therapy with romosozumab and denosumab demonstrates potential as a promising treatment strategy for osteoporosis in maintenance hemodialysis patients. By combining romosozumab's bone formation-stimulating effects and denosumab's bone resorption-inhibiting effects, this approach may significantly improve bone mineral density and stabilize bone metabolism in this high-risk population. While further studies are required to confirm its long-term efficacy and safety, this therapy offers a promising option for managing osteoporosis in hemodialysis patients.

title: #3474 1 year follow up of bone density markers in patients dialyzed with a citric acid-vitC containing dialysate versus acetate dialysate
authors: Ioanna Lampropoulou; Antigoni Martika; Dimitrios Salvaridis; Mirtsa Kalbazidou; Dimitrios Apostolou; Sofia Spaia
abstract:
Background and Aims
The substitution of acetate with citrate, as a stabilizer, in hemodialysis fluid induces hemodynamic stability, producing less hypotension and inflammation and improves nutritional status [1]. It also modifies several parameters of bone mineral metabolism as it lowers preHD ionic calcium and elevates PTH levels [1]. Plasma vitamin C is positively associated with the lumbar spine bone mineral density (BMD) in young and early middle-aged men [2]. It is also considered to reduce erythropoietin supplementation needs through elimination of inflammation [3, 4]. However, impact of long-term use of citrates- VitC dialysate has not been described.
Method
We randomized 48 stable hemodialysis patients to receive either citrate-VitCD or acetateD as a stabilizer in hemodialysis fluid and checked them prospectively for 12 months. BMD, CKD-MBD markers, electrolytes, HCO3−, dialysis adequacy and hemoglobin were compared at start, 6 months and 12 months of observation. Medication and adverse events were recorded.
Results
There was no difference between two groups in demographic characteristics, biochemical parameters and BMD markers (Tscore femur-spine, Zscore femur-spine) on time 0, 6, 12 months. However, BMD markers deteriorated irrespective of the dialysate type during the follow up year. In patients on citrate-VitCD, Tscore spine and Tscore femur worsened on 6 months and stabilized on 12 months (Tspine0 vs Tspine6, P = 0.003, Tspine6 vs Tspine12 P = 0.17 and Tfemur0 vs Tfemur6, P = 0.0005, Tfemur6 vs Tfemur12, P = 0.014 respectively). As for patients on acetateD, Tscore spine and Tscore femur also worsened (Tspine0 vs Tspine6, P = 0.268 Tspine6 vs Tspine 12, P = 0.01 and Tfemur0 vs Tfemur6, P = 0.03, Tfemur6 vs Tfemur2, P = 0.9 respectively). Ratio ESA/Hb did not differ between two groups during the follow-up period. No adverse events were recorded.
Conclusion
In the present cohort use of citate-vitC dialysate did not seem to improve Bone Density Markers. In both groups, osteopenia deteriorated following the same pattern at the end of the follow-up year. Contrary to previous reports ionized calcium levels were unaffected from the use of citrate-vitCD in the long term. Dialysis adequacy was similar between the two groups. Likewise, erythropoietin supplementation needs did not alter during this time. In the absence of long-term studies, our results are valid and indicative of real-world impact of citrate-vitC dialysate.

title: #3868 Impact of medium cut-off dialyzer membrane and dietary modification on serum p-cresyl sulfate and indoxyl sulfate levels: a randomized controlled trial
authors: Tjaša Herič; Tjaša Vivoda; Špela Bogataj; Jernej Pajek
abstract:
Background and Aims
Online hemodiafiltration (ol-HDF) with a high-flux dialyzer membrane is currently considered the gold standard for chronic hemodialysis, but its efficacy compared to the newer medium cut-off (MCO) membrane in reducing protein-bound uremic toxins (PBUTs) remains unclear. P-cresyl sulfate (PCS) and indoxyl sulfate (IS) are key PBUTs associated with cardiovascular toxicity and increased mortality in end-stage renal disease. Their levels are influenced by residual kidney function and diet, with bacterial metabolism in the colon playing a major role. Previous studies suggest that increased fiber and short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) intake may lower PCS and IS levels, but data are limited. We hypothesize that combining MCO membrane use with dietary modifications enhances PBUT removal by improving toxin clearance and reducing intestinal production. This study aimed to assess the impact of this approach on serum PCS and IS levels compared to ol-HDF.
Method
A prospective, randomized, controlled interventional study was conducted with 62 chronic hemodialysis (HD) patients between February 2021 and June 2022 at the Department of Chronic Hemodialysis, University Medical Center Ljubljana, Slovenia. Two weeks after standard bicarbonate HD (BHD), patients were randomized to hemodialysis with MCO membrane (EXP group) or ol-HDF with a standard "high-flux" (HF) dialyzer membrane (CON group). After 4 weeks, both groups were supplemented by a change in the diet with increase of the daily intake of dietary fiber by 19 g and addition of a SCFA propionate in the dose of 1g daily for 8 weeks. Two main outcomes were serum concentrations of PCS and IS. Measurements were taken at baseline (after 2 week wash-in period, T0), after 4 weeks of the first intervention phase (MCO vs. ol-HDF; T1), after 8 weeks of second intervention phase (fiber and SCFA supplementation; T2) and finally, after 4 weeks of wash-out period with BHD (T3).
Results
From 62 participants, 52 completed the study (63.5% men, 65.6 ± 11.2 years, Charlson comorbidity index 5.8 ± 2.2), with 24 in the EXP group and 28 in the CON group. In the CON group, serum concentrations of PCS (in μmol/L) were 34.2 ± 18.0 (T0), 35.8 ± 18.5 (T1), 33.2 ± 17.2 (T2) and 38.6 ± 19.9 (T3). Serum concentrations of IS (in μmol/L) were 34.0 ± 13.4 (baseline), 34.4 ± 14.0 (T1), 31.5 ± 10.3 (T2) and 39.6 ± 20.9 (T3). In the EXP group, serum concentrations of PCS were 30.6 ± 16.3 (T0), 33.1 ± 17.3 (T1), 32.3 ± 17.4 (T2) and 34.8 ± 20.8 (T3). Serum concentrations for IS were 38.7 ± 14.2 (T0), 38.9 ± 14.6 (T1), 42.0 ± 15.8 (T2) and 40.6 ± 16.1 (T3). After the analysis of repeated measures, a statistically significant interaction was found between time and group for IS (P = 0.005). Post-hoc analysis revealed a significant difference within the CON group between T2 and T3 (P = 0.003). When comparing both groups, we found a statistical significance between CON and EXP in T2 for IS (P = 0.006). During the study, we observed that only 46% of patients adhered well to their fiber intake, defined as consuming at least 14 g of fiber per day. Furthermore, compliance was higher in the CON group (n = 16) compared to the EXP group (n = 8).
Conclusion
The findings of this study indicate that both hemodialysis methods are equally effective in eliminating PCS and IS. However, the combination of diet modification with ol-HDF resulted in a significant reduction in serum IS concentrations, whereas no such effect was observed when combined with an MCO membrane. This reduction in the control group can likely be attributed to their substantially better compliance with fiber and SCFA intake. Furthermore, the significant increase in IS concentrations following fiber discontinuation in the CON group reinforces the beneficial impact of dietary modifications on IS levels. In contrast, no significant effect of dietary intervention was observed on serum PCS levels. To validate these findings and optimize treatment strategies, further research with a larger sample size, extended dietary intervention, and improved compliance is warranted.

title: #1671 Inhibiting progression of abdominal aortic calcification by vitamin K2 in dialysis patients
authors: Hiroya Menjo; Tanaka Tomoki; Ryousuke Umeda; Shun Minatoguchi; Shigehisa Koide; Hiroki Hayashi; Midori Hasegawa; Naotake Tsuboi
abstract:
Background and Aims
Vitamin K plays a crucial role in preventing vascular calcification by activating matrix Gla-protein (MGP). Maintenance dialysis patients often present with low vitamin K nutritional status, and Mönckeberg's arteriosclerosis is a characteristic feature in this population. In light of this, our study aimed to evaluate the impact of vitamin K2 on abdominal aortic calcification in this demographic.
Method
We conducted a 12-center, open-label, randomized controlled trial in Japan over two years. From April 2014 to April 2022, 207 maintenance dialysis patients were enrolled and randomly assigned, with stratification by age, sex, dialysis vintage, presence of diabetes, serum inorganic phosphorus levels, and bone mineral density (BMD) (cutoff at 70% of the young adult mean, YAM). The intervention group received a daily dose of 45 mg menatetrenone, while the observation group received standard dialysis care and were restricted from using vitamin K supplements (Fig. 1). The primary outcome was the relative change in Agatston score (rcAS) in the abdominal aorta, a measure of vascular calcification, which was evaluated using a linear mixed-effects model (LMM) with time, group, and their interaction (time × group) included as fixed effects. T-tests with Kenward-Roger adjustment compared group contrasts at each time point. The secondary outcomes included the difference in the relative change of AS at two years, tested by the Wilcoxon rank-sum test, and the trend of desphospho-uncarboxylated (dp-uc) MGP (inactive form of MGP), osteocalcin (OC), and undercarboxylated osteocalcin (ucOC), tested by the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. A food frequency questionnaire (FFQ) was also performed to assess vitamin K intake, which was then evaluated for its impact on the outcomes.
Results
During the study, 46 patients were lost to follow-up. We analyzed the remaining 161 patients, divided into 77 in the intervention group and 84 in the observation group. Baseline characteristics for both groups were as follows: the average age was 67 ± 12 years and 66 ± 12 years, respectively; the proportion of male patients was 64.8% and 61.9%, respectively; the median duration of dialysis was 6.0 years (3.0, 13.0) and 5.0 years (2.0, 10.5), respectively; and daily vitamin K intake was 141 ± 110 μg/day and 139 ± 118 μg/day, respectively, for the intervention and observation groups. The Agatston score at baseline and at two years were 1,870 (619, 4868) and 2,287 (838, 5597) in the intervention group, respectively, compared to 1,818 (547, 3961) and 2,291 (1097, 4618) in the observation group. LMM analysis revealed significant effects for both time (P < 0.001) and the interaction between time and group (P = 0.012). This indicates that the time effect on rcAS differed between the groups. At two years, the difference in rcAS between the groups was statistically significant, with an estimated mean difference (standard error) of 28.5% (10.2) and a P-value of 0.006 (Fig. 2). In secondary analyses, rcAS at two years was significantly lower in the intervention group (P = 0.046, which, along with the primary outcome, strongly supports the hypothesis that vitamin K2 ameliorates the progression of abdominal aortic calcification. Additionally, both dp-ucMGP and ucOC levels decreased significantly only in the intervention group over the two-year period (P < 0.001 and 0.023, respectively), suggesting improvements in factors related to vascular calcification and bone metabolism through vitamin K2 administration. Notably, these effects appeared independent of dietary vitamin K intake, as estimated from the FFQ.
Conclusion
The progression of abdominal aortic calcification in maintenance dialysis patients is suppressed by vitamin K2 administration, and this effect is independent of dietary intake.

title: #1779 MSC exosomes inhibit peritoneal fibroblast transdifferentiation by entering fibroblasts via CD44-EGFR binding
authors: Fang Yu; Xiaoyue Wang; Jia Chen; Qingli Cai; Kehong Chen; Yani He
abstract:
Background and Aims
Peritoneal fibrosis (PF), a serious complication of peritoneal dialysis (PD), has limited treatment options. Recent studies show that fibroblast transdifferentiation into myofibroblasts is key in this process. Our previous research has revealed that the mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) exosomes have the potential to alleviate peritoneal fibrosis. Our research aims to determine if MSC exosomes can attenuate PF by impeding fibroblast transdifferentiation.
Method
We extracted primary MSCs using whole bone marrow culture and MSC exosomes using ultracentrifugation. The exosomes were then characterised using electron microscopy, nanoparticle tracking analysis and nanoflow detection. A PF model was established using C57BL/6 mice, which were divided into a control group (saline), a peritoneal fibrosis group (2.5% PDF+LPS) and an exosome-treated group (2.5% PDF+LPS+Exos). The mice were euthanised and the peritoneum removed to detect peritoneal fibrosis after 6 weeks. In addition, a 2.5% PDF+LPS-induced cell injury model was established using primary mouse fibroblasts and mouse fibroblast cell lines. Exosome tracking was performed ex vivo and in vivo using the DiI fluorescent dye method. The ex vivo experiments were performed to detect fibroblast transdifferentiation by immunofluorescence, qRT-PCR and western blot. The key membrane proteins mediating the ability of exosomes to target fibroblasts were analysed by 4D proteomics, biosignature analysis and live cell workstation.
Results
In vivo, the PF group exhibited higher peritoneal fibroblast and myofibroblast markers than controls, indicating these two cells drive peritoneal thickening and fibrosis. The PF+Exos group had reduced peritoneal thickening, lower TGF-β1 levels, and decreased myofibroblast markers compared to the PF group. In vitro, MSC-Exos treatment reversed fibroblast transdifferentiation, reduced the pro-fibrotic fibroblast phenotype, and lowered TGF-β1 expression. These results indicated that MSC exosome could effectively reverse 2.5% PDF+LPS-induced fibroblast to myofibroblast transdifferentiation and thus inhibit peritoneal fibrosis. To determine if exosomes can enter submesothelial fibroblasts and exert biological effects, a DiI fluorescent dye assay was used for exosomal tracing in vivo and in vitro. In a PF mouse model, immunofluorescence showed co-expression of fibroblast markers and DiI, indicating exosome entry into fibroblasts. In vitro, mouse fibroblasts co-cultured with DiI-Exos showed active exosome absorption, peaking at 48 hours. These results suggest that MSC-Exos can cross the peritoneal mesothelial layer to affect submesothelial fibroblasts. We explore how exosomes target fibroblasts, using 4D proteomics to analyze 5619 fibroblast and 162 exosomal proteins. It identified 522 fibroblast and 16 exosomal membrane proteins, with seven interacting proteins found via STRING software. The protein-protein interaction network showed that EGFR and CD44 proteins were key nodes. Protein-protein interaction analysis in Pymol showed a structural basis for CD44 and EGFR binding, with multiple hydrogen bonds. Co-IP results validated their binding. Inhibition of CD44 or EGFR significantly reduced and delayed DiI exosome entry into fibroblasts, as shown by in vitro exosome tracer assay and living cells workstation. These findings suggest that CD44-EGFR binding aids MSC-exosome entry into fibroblasts.
Conclusion
In conclusion, we have identified that MSC exosomes enter peritoneal fibroblasts via CD44-EGFR binding, subsequently inhibiting fibroblast transdifferentiation and thereby mitigating peritoneal fibrosis during peritoneal dialysis. Our findings propose a novel cell-free therapeutic approach for the treatment of peritoneal fibrosis and provide a theoretical foundation for potential clinical applications.

title: #87 Comparative analysis of predictive criteria for unassisted maturation of AVF using post-operative ultrasound measurement: UAB vs NKF-KDOQI
authors: Seok Joon Shin; Sang Hun Eum; Hoon Suk Park
abstract:
Background and Aims
The study aimed to assess the predictive performance of the University of Alabama at Birmingham (UAB) criteria versus the NKF-KDOQI guidelines in determining the likelihood of unassisted arteriovenous fistula (AVF) maturation. Additionally, we aimed to investigate how the predictive performance of these criteria differs between upper arm AVFs and forearm AVFs.
Method
We retrospectively analyzed the age, gender, BMI, and comorbidities of chronic kidney disease patients who underwent AVF creation and were followed up from January 2017 to March 2021 at a single medical center. Additionally, we examined the types of AVFs, the success of the first cannulation, and postoperative AVF ultrasound measurements.
Results
Among a total of 560 patients, unassisted maturation of AVFs was confirmed in 68.6% of cases. Specifically, the unassisted maturation rate for upper arm AVFs was 70.2%, which was higher than the rate of 66.8% observed for forearm AVFs. While the positive predictive value for the overall unassisted maturation of AVFs was higher for NKF-KDOQI at 0.85 compared to UAB's 0.77, UAB demonstrated superior negative predictive value at 0.57. Evaluating the predictive abilities of both criteria through Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve analysis, UAB (AUC = 0.643 (95% CI 0.602–0.684)) outperformed NKF-KDOQI (AUC = 0.56 (95% CI 0.532–0.589)) in predicting unassisted maturation of overall AVFs. Notably, when predicting unassisted maturation for forearm AVFs, UAB (AUC = 0.654 (95% CI 0.593–0.715)) demonstrated superiority over NKF-KDOQI, whose predictive ability (AUC = 0.517 (95% CI 0.494–0.540)) approached random chance.
Conclusion
In conclusion, the UAB criteria demonstrated superiority in predicting the overall unassisted maturation of AVFs compared to the NKF-KDOQI guideline. This trend was particularly pronounced in the case of forearm AVFs, where the predictive ability of NKF-KDOQI criteria for unassisted maturation was found to be close to random chance.
