title: #1306 Effect of erythropoiesis-stimulating agent types on malignancy in hemodialysis patients
authors: Jun Young Do; Seok Hui Kang
abstract:
Background and Aims
Since erythropoiesis stimulating agent (ESA) types vary in their affinity for receptors, investigating their association with malignancies could offer valuable insights. This study aims to evaluate the effect of ESA types on malignancy incidence in hemodialysis (HD) patients.
Method
This retrospective study analyzed data from 33 960 HD patients, who underwent 4th and 5th HD quality assessments. Participants were divided into 3 groups: short-, intermediate-, and long-acting groups. The onset of any malignancy was defined as the date of the first diagnosis based on ICD-10 codes for the 12 most common malignancies. Patient survival assessed for those with a first diagnosis of any malignancy during follow-up.
Results
The short-, intermediate-, and long-acting groups comprised 26 006, 6 448, and 1 506 patients, respectively (over ∼75 mo follow-up). The 5-year malignancy-free rates were 88.4%, 88.2%, and 87.0% for short-, intermediate-, and long-acting groups, respectively (P = 0.024 for short/intermediate-acting vs. long-acting group). Univariable and multivariable analyses showed higher malignancy risk in the long-acting group, especially in males, older individuals, and those on higher ESA doses. We performed analyses using a balanced cohort after propensity score weighting. The balanced cohort also confirmed higher malignancy risk in the long-acting group, while survival rates remained unaffected by ESA type.
Conclusion
Our population-based cohort study reveals an association between long-acting ESAs use and the incidence of any malignancy, with a particularly strong influence on high-dose users. This suggests that avoiding long-acting ESAs may be advisable for patients at high risk of malignancy.

title: #1311 Association between ultrafiltration variability and clinical outcomes in patients undergoing hemodialysis
authors: Seok Hui Kang; Jun Young Do
abstract:
Background and Aims
Traditionally, high ultrafiltration volume (UFV) is well-known to affect the cardiovascular system, increasing the risk of various cardiovascular diseases or mortality. Research on the clinical significance of UFV variability is generally very limited. Therefore, this study aims to evaluate the effect of UFV variability on clinical outcomes in maintenance hemodialysis (HD) patients using a population-based cohort.
Method
In our retrospective study, datasets from patients who underwent periodic HD quality assessments and their claims data were analyzed. Overall, 50,583 patients were included in this study. The UFV variability was calculated using the residual standard deviation derived from a within-subject linear regression model with six UFV values for each patient. Participants were divided into the four quartile groups based on the UFV variability: first quartile (1Q), second quartile (2Q), third quartile (3Q), and fourth quartile (4Q).
Results
The number of patients in 1Q, 2Q, 3Q, and 4Q was 12,646, 12,646, 12,646, and 12,645, respectively. The 5-year patient survival rates in the 1Q, 2Q, 3Q, and 4Q were 68.3%, 67.9%, 66.4%, and 65.8%, respectively. Multivariable analysis showed that the hazard ratio (HR) for all-cause mortality was highest in the 4Q group among the four groups. We also evaluated the association between cardiovascular events, atrial fibrillation, or dementia and UFV variability. Multivariable Cox regression showed that the Q4 group had greater HR for cardiovascular events or atrial fibrillation than the 1Q and 2Q groups. Additionally, the Q1 group had lowest HR for dementia among the four groups. Spline curves also showed similar trends with those from Cox regression.
Conclusion
Our study demonstrated an association between high UFV variability and various clinical outcomes, particularly all-cause mortality and dementia. These findings suggest that UFV variability could be a useful optional indicator for predicting prognosis, in addition to UFV or ultrafiltration rate. However, owing to the various limitations of this study, further research is needed to confirm this association more definitively.

title: #544 Effect of serum albumin levels at the time of peritoneal dialysis initiation on technique survival period and outcome
authors: Hiroki Uchida; Akiko Kudo; Takeshi Nakata; Akihiro Fukuda; Hidetoshi Kikuchi; Eiji Uchida; Makoto Arima; Naoya Fukunaga; Hirotaka Shibata
abstract:
Background and Aims
There are some factors for peritoneal dialysis (PD) failure include patient-related factors such as age, peritonitis occurrence, and residual renal function, as well as treatment-related factors like dialysis prescription and modality. Hypoalbuminemia during PD treatment is also reported as a PD technique failure factor, however the effect of hypoalbuminemia at PD initiation on technique survival period and outcome are unclear. This study investigated the relationship between hypoalbuminemia at PD initiation (Alb <3.0 g/dL) and technique survival period and reasons for failure.
Method
Multi-center retrospective cohort study was conducted, and 277 patients who initiated PD between January 2007 and December 2017 were observed until March 2024. Patient characteristics at initiation, including reasons for end-stage renal disease, age, sex, Alb, eGFR, Hb, and urinary protein were extracted from medical records. Factors for technique survival period were analyzed using Cox proportional hazard models, and the result revealed the hypoalbuminemia (Alb <3.0 g/dL) as a significant technique failure factor. We divided patients into two groups based on albumin levels (≥3.0 g/dL, <3.0 g/dL) to analyze whether PD technique survival period and the reasons for PD failure differ depending on albumin level. In this study, PD technique failure was defined as transfer to hemodialysis or death.
Results
A total of 277 patients were follow-up from three PD centers, of them 8 patients were excluded due to transplantation. The remaining 269 patients were included in this study. Mean PD technique survival period was 40.8 months. Multivariate analysis using Cox proportional hazard models, adjusted for age, sex, and diabetic nephropathy, showed that hypoalbuminemia (Alb <3.0 g/dL) were most strongly associated with PD technique survival rate (HR 1.585 [CI 1.109, 2.264]). Comparing the two groups (hypoalbuminemia group: 67 patients, Alb ≥3.0 g/dL group: 202 patients), the hypoalbuminemia group showed significantly lower PD technique survival rate (log-rank test P < 0.0001; Fig. 1) and shorter mean PD period (27.2 vs 45.3 months, P < 0.0001). Patient characteristics between two groups were as follows: age (68.6 vs 61.9 years, P < 0.0001), male sex (65.4 vs 66.8%, P = 0.707), Alb (2.6 vs 3.5 g/dL, P < 0.0001), Hb (9.0 vs 9.7 g/dL, P = 0.0005), eGFR (6.8 vs 6.0, P = 0.0210), urinary protein (5.4 vs 3.3 g/gCr, P = 0.0004), and diabetic nephropathy (55.2 vs 33.2%, P = 0.0013). The hypoalbuminemia group was significantly older, had advanced anemia, and a higher prevalence of diabetic nephropathy. Comparing the reasons for PD failure between two groups, there was no significant differences in PD-related infections or volume overload. However, the hypoalbuminemia group had significantly higher number of PD failure for death (n = 23, 34.9% vs Alb ≥3.0 g/dL group n = 34, 18.1%, P = 0.0050), and cardiovascular disease (CVD) was the most common reason for death (n = 9, 39.1%).
Conclusion
Among patient characteristics at PD initiation, hypoalbuminemia was most strongly associated with PD technique survival period. The hypoalbuminemia group also showed significantly higher mortality, especially due to CVD, compared to the Alb ≥3.0 g/dL group. PD patients with hypoalbuminemia at initiation need to be careful about technique failure not only due to infection or volume overload, but also technique failure for CVD. Therefore, it is necessary for better prognosis to correct hypoalbuminemia, including diabetes management to decrease urinary protein.

Among patient characteristics at PD initiation, hypoalbuminemia was most strongly associated with PD technique survival period. title: #1808 Denosumab versus bisphosphonates for medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw and recurrent clinical fractures among Japanese patients on haemodialysis: a target trial emulation
authors: Tatsunori Toida; Tatsuyoshi Ikenoue; Ryoji Tominaga; Ryohei Inenaga; Akihito Fujita; Masataka Taguri; Noriaki Kurita
abstract:
Background and Aims
The cardiovascular safety and fracture prevention effectiveness of denosumab versus bisphosphonates has been previously studied among dialysis patients [1].
However, evidence regarding the risk of medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ) and clinical fractures remains insufficient. This study aimed to evaluate the comparative safety and effectiveness of denosumab versus bisphosphonates in this population.
Method
This cohort study emulated a target trial using the DeSC Healthcare Comprehensive Japanese Administrative Claims Database. Eligible participants were patients on maintenance haemodialysis with osteoporosis or fragility fractures who were newly prescribed denosumab or bisphosphonates between March 2019 and August 2023. The safety outcome was the incidence of MRONJ, while the effectiveness outcomes included clinical fractures, analysed separately for first and recurrent fractures.
Hazard ratios (HRs) for MRONJ and first fractures were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models, while recurrent fractures were analysed using the Anderson-Gill approach. Inverse probability of treatment weighting was applied to account for confounding by indication.
Results
A total of 2,119 observations were included (denosumab: 674; bisphosphonate: 1,445). The mean age was 78.8 years in the denosumab group and 78.4 years in the bisphosphonate group. Females comprised 56.9% and 51.5% of the respective groups, and the history of osteoporotic fractures was higher in the denosumab group (38.7% vs. 28.3%). Although the incidence of MRONJ was rare, it was higher in the denosumab group compared to the bisphosphonate group (HR: 2.10, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.60–7.30).
Conversely, denosumab use was significantly associated with a lower risk of both first and recurrent clinical fractures compared to bisphosphonates (HR for first fractures: 0.69, 95% CI: 0.48–0.99; HR for recurrent fractures: 0.67, 95% CI: 0.47–0.95).
Conclusion
Among patients on haemodialysis, denosumab should be prescribed with consideration of both the increased risk of MRONJ and its superior effectiveness in preventing recurrent fractures compared to bisphosphonates.

title: #1466 Ca-sensing receptor agonists can improve taste sensitivity in hemodialysis patients
authors: Eri Imai; Ririko Murata; Ainori Hoshimoto; Rina Hisada; Makiko Harano; Emi Anno; So Hagiwara; Shuzo Kaneko
abstract:
Background and Aims
Hemodialysis patients often experience dysgeusia, which has various causes and lacks an established treatment. Calcium-sensing receptors (CaSR) are expressed on the tongue, and may play a potential role in enhancing taste sensitivity (reported as “Kokumi”). CaSR agonists are used to treat secondary hyperparathyroidism (2HPT) in patients with end-stage kidney disease, but no studies have examined the effect of CaSR agonists on taste in dialysis patients.
Methods
This study is a single-center prospective observational study. Outpatient maintenance hemodialysis patients scheduled to newly initiate treatment with a CaSR agonist for 2HPT were enrolled in this study. (1) A comparison of taste thresholds was conducted between 12 hemodialysis patients with 2HPT (2HPT-HD) at our hospital prior to starting treatment with etelcalcetide, and 8 healthy controls (HC); (2) In the 2HPT-HD patients, taste thresholds were compared before and 3 months after starting etelcalcetide treatment. Ten of the 12 2HPT-HD patients were zinc deficient, and they were given zinc supplementation one week before the taste threshold test, prior to starting etelcalcetide treatment. Taste threshold testing was performed using the whole-mouth method, and thresholds for sweet, sour, bitter, salty, and umami were scored (each score 0–4, total score 0–20) using the Burghart Taste Strips.
Results
The background of the 12HPT-HD patients was as follows: 8 males, 7 with a history of diabetes, an average dialysis duration of 44 months, and median age 69 years, and ranged from 50 to 80 years. The 8 HC were 4 males, with a median age of 49 years, ranging from 26 to 78 years. The HC tended to be younger, although this was not statistically significant. None of the 2HPT-HD patients reported subjective dysgeusia in the questionnaire form survey, but in the taste threshold test, there were 6 patients with a score of 9 or less, which is judged to be a decrease in taste sensitivity. (1) The total score was significantly lower in 2HPT-HD patients than in HC (10.3 vs. 15.0, p = 0.002) (Fig. 1), with significant differences observed for sweet, bitter, and sour tastes (p = 0.028, 0.033, and 0.039, respectively); (2) In the 2HPT-HD, the total score significantly improved from 10.3 to 13.0 (p = 0.012) after 3 months of etelcalcetide treatment (Fig. 2), particularly for sour taste (p = 0.021), while no change was observed for salty taste.
Conclusion
CaSR agonists may improve taste sensitivity in hemodialysis patients. Furthermore, many dialysis patients have potentially reduced taste sensitivity, which should be considered in dietary counseling.

title: #1981 Antihypertensive therapy improves cardiovascular outcomes in patients on hemodialysis: an updated meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
authors: Maria Varveri; Christodoula Kourtidou; Ioannis Kontogiorgos; Eirini Leptokaridou Mourtzila; Garyfallia Varouktsi; Eleni Georgianou; Vasilios Vaios; Konstantinos Leivaditis; Vassilios Liakopoulos; Panagiotis Georgianos
abstract:
Background and Aims
Large observational studies have shown a paradoxical reverse association between blood pressure (BP) and risk of all-cause mortality in hemodialysis patients, raising concerns on whether hypertension is truly an independent risk factor in this population. The available randomized controlled trials that evaluated the efficacy of antihypertensive therapy in hemodialysis patients have been few, have included small sample sizes with insufficient number of cardiovascular events and have provided contradictory results. Accordingly, the aim of this meta-analysis is to explore the effect of active treatment with antihypertensive drugs relative to placebo on cardiovascular outcomes and all-cause mortality in the hemodialysis population.
Method
We searched MedLine/PubMed and Cochrane Central databases from inception through June 2024 aiming to identify RCTs comparing the efficacy of antihypertensive treatment relative to placebo or no add-on therapy in patients on hemodialysis. RCTs were eligible, if they were designed to explore treatment effects on fatal or non-fatal cardiovascular events as a primary efficacy outcome.
Results
A total of 9 RCTs incorporating data from 2,340 hemodialysis patients met the prespecified inclusion/exclusion criteria and were inserted in quantitative data synthesis. As compared with placebo or no add-on therapy, active treatment with antihypertensive drugs was associated with a 27.8% reduction in the risk of fatal or non-fatal cardiovascular events using a fixed-effects model [relative risk (RR): 0.722; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.618–0.845] and with a 34.7% relative risk reduction using a random-effects model (RR: 0.653; 95% CI: 0.502–0.849). In addition, relative to placebo or no add-on therapy, active treatment with antihypertensive medications was associated with a 29.4% reduction in the risk of death from any cause using a fixed-effects model (RR: 0.706; 95% CI: 0.592–0.843) and with a 35.6% reduction using a random-effects model (RR: 0.644; 95% CI: 0.469–0.833).
Conclusion
This updated meta-analysis of RCTs shows that among patients on hemodialysis, deliberate BP lowering with the use of antihypertensive medications is associated with significant reductions in the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events and all-cause mortality.

title: #2779 Improvement in uncomfortable dialysis-related symptoms such as daytime itching, nighttime itching, restless legs and leg muscle cramps by switching from HD to OHDF through enhanced removal efficacy of medium-molecular-weight substances
authors: Emi Kihara; Kazuko Arita; Hiroaki Oda
abstract:
Background and Aims
Uncomfortable complaints frequently observed in maintenance hemodialysis (HD) patients, such as pruritus, restless legs syndrome (RLS), burning feet, leg muscle cramps, and insomnia, contribute to a decline in the quality of life (QOL) for these patients. One of the effects of on-line hemodiafiltration (OHDF) is the improvement of uncomfortable complaints by increasing the removal rate of α1-microglobulin. The purpose of this study is to investigate whether changing from conventional HD to OHDF enhances the removal efficiency of small-middle molecular weight substances and large-middle molecular weight proteins, subsequently improving dialysis-related symptoms in dialysis patients.
Method
This study involved 24 HD patients (21 males and 4 females) with a mean age of 63 ± 12 years and an HD duration of 78.6 ± 74.3 months, including 11 patients with diabetes and 13 without diabetes. All participants were receiving pharmacological treatment, including Nalfurafine hydrochloride (2.5 µg/day), Clonazepam (0.5 mg/day), and Shakuyakukanzoto extract (6.0 g/day). During HD and at 0, 1, 2 and 3 months after transition to OHDF, the serum albumin and blood urea nitrogen concentrations, the removal rates of β2-microglobulin and α1-microglobulin were measured. The associations between these parameters and dialysis-related symptoms, including daytime itching, nighttime itching, restless legs and leg muscle cramps were investigated. The severity of the subjective symptoms was assessed using a Visual Analogue Scale (VAS), with 0 indicated no symptoms, 1 indicated mild symptoms, 2 indicated moderate symptoms, 3 indicated moderate to severe symptoms and 4 indicated severe symptoms.
Results
There were no significant differences in the BUN removal rate and KT/V between HD and HDF. The serum albumin concentration at 2 months after the transition from HD to HDF was lower than that during HD. The β2-microglobulin and α1-microglobulin removal rates at 0, 1, 2 and 3 months after the transition from HD to HDF were significantly higher than those during HD (Table 1).
After the transition from HD to OHDF, all symptoms, including daytime itching, nighttime itching, restless legs, and leg muscle cramps, significantly improved (Table 2). Furthermore, 13 out of 24 patients were able to reduce or discontinue medications.
Conclusion
Transition from HD to OHDF resulted in a slight decrease in serum albumin concentrations; however, no significant decline in Kt/V was observed, and the marked reduction in the removal rates of small to middle-weight substances was not evident. The removal efficiencies of β2-microglobulin and α1-microglobulin significantly improved, consequently the overall patients experienced an improvement in dialysis-related symptoms. Therefore, HDF treatment has demonstrated the potential to enhance the QOL for dialysis patients suffering from uncomfortable dialysis-related symptoms.

title: #78 Skeletal muscle density measured in L3 computerized tomography is a prognostic marker in patients initiating hemodialysis
authors: Yunkyeong Hwang; Suyeon Han; Hwajin Park; Yu Ah Hong; Yoon-Kyung Chang
abstract:
Background and Aims
Among dialysis patients, those with sarcopenia exhibit poorer clinical outcomes compared to their non-sarcopenic counterparts. Accordingly, the evaluation of sarcopenia in dialysis patients is essential for predicting prognosis and assessing quality of life. CT imaging allows for the analysis of body composition using pre-existing scan data and is widely employed as a biomarker of sarcopenia in oncology, geriatric, and surgical populations. It is particularly useful for predicting surgical complications and mortality risk. The third lumbar vertebra (L3) level is a representative anatomical landmark for assessing skeletal muscle mass. Measurements at this level using single-slice CT imaging provide an efficient and representative estimation of total body muscle mass, making it a critical tool for the evaluation and management of sarcopenia. This study aims to evaluate skeletal muscle mass and quality using CT imaging in patients initiating dialysis and to investigate their association with all-cause mortality in this population.
Method
This is an observational retrospective single-center study including 458 CKD patients initiating maintenance hemodialysis who underwent abdominal CT at Daejeon St. Mary Hospital between January 2018 and December 2023. Abdomen CT scan was taken within 1 month before or after the commencement of dialysis. Patients were enrolled if they were aged 18 years or older. We assessed the all-cause mortality of patients until October 2024. Single-slice transverse CT images at L3 were determined to quantify skeletal muscle mass and density. Image analysis was conducted with ImageJ (version 1.54). Skeletal muscle area was measured by using a threshold for Hounsfield Unit of −29 to +150 for skeletal muscle according to Gomez-perez tutorial.
Results
The patients with skeletal muscle density below the derived cut-offs had worse survival compared to the patients with skeletal muscle density above those cut-offs. The results showed that SMD had a significant positive correlation with male sex (r = 0.389, P < 0.001), height (r = 0.391, P < 0.001), albumin (r = 0.312, P < 0.001), and PNI (r = 0.317, P < 0.001). Conversely, SMD showed a significant negative correlation with age (r = −0.474, P < 0.001) and BMI (r = −0.119, P = 0.008). A multivariable linear regression analysis was subsequently performed, focusing on factors that were significant in the simple regression analysis. Importantly, this analysis revealed that male sex (β = 0.341, P < 0.001), age (β = −0.364, P < 0.001), BMI (β = −0.297, P < 0.001), and albumin (β = 0.242, P < 0.001) were not only significant but also independently and critically associated with SMD.
Conclusion
Our research verified that skeletal muscle density from L3 CT scan are strong predictor of mortality in initial hemodialysis patients. What is unique about our study is that our study subject took CT at initial hemodialysis state while most of the other studies focus on non-dialysis or maintenance hemodialysis patient as the subject of the study. Age and sex showed a strong correlation with SMD. Aging, female is independent risk for low SMD. BMI has a negative correlation with SMD. Creatinine, which is also secreted by muscles, showed a correlation with SMD, as higher SMD was associated with higher creatinine levels. In our study, decreased albumin was also associated with reduced SMD.

title: #626 Association between peritoneal uric acid clearance, inflammation, and peritoneal membrane function in normouricemic patients undergoing peritoneal dialysis
authors: Natalia Stepanova; Victoria Driianska; Andriy Rysyev; Lyudmyla Snisar; Ihor Poperechnyi; Vyacheslav Filonov
abstract:
Background and Aims
Elevated uric acid (UA), a byproduct of purine metabolism, is known to contribute to oxidative stress and inflammation. In patients undergoing peritoneal dialysis (PD), efficient clearance of UA is crucial for regulating systemic UA levels. However, the potential effects of UA on the peritoneal membrane function remain unclear. This study investigates the relationship between peritoneal uric acid clearance (pUACl), markers of systemic and intraperitoneal inflammation, and the peritoneal membrane function measured by peritoneal transport status, ultrafiltration (UF) rate and peritoneal Kt/V. We hypothesized that increased pUACl in normouricemic PD patients could exacerbate intraperitoneal inflammation and impair peritoneal membrane function.
Method
A total of 120 patients aged 50 (38-64) years with a dialysis vintage of 36 (17-60.5) months, who had been undergoing continuous ambulatory PD for at least 3 months before enrollment, were included in this cross-sectional study. Key parameters measured included serum, urine, and dialysate uric acid (UA) concentrations, weekly peritoneal (pUACl), urinary (uUACl) and total UA (tUACl) clearances, creatinine clearance (CrCl), peritoneal UF rate and Kt/V, interleukin-6 (IL-6), monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1) in serum and dialysate, and serum C-reactive protein (CRP) levels. Weekly pUACl was calculated using the following formula:
Data were presented as medians with interquartile ranges (Me [25th–75th percentiles]) and analyzed using the Kruskal-Wallis test. Correlations between variables were assessed using Spearman's test, and logistic regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with a peritoneal Kt/V <1.7.
Results
The median serum UA levels and pUACl were significantly lower in women compared to men: 283.3 (248.9–304.5) vs. 315.7 (272.0–333.5) μmol/L (P < 0.0001) and 30.1 (23.4–42.8) vs. 36.4 (32.7–47.3) L/week/1.73 m² (P = 0.008), respectively. Moreover, pUACl were significantly lower in patients with high peritoneal transport status compared to high-average and low-average transporters: 26.7 (20.6–34.5) vs. 32.2 (24.8–41.3) vs. 38.5 (35.1–47.2) L/week/1.73 m², respectively (P = 0.01). title: #3193 Investigation of the gastrointestinal tract with capsule endoscopy in patients undergoing renal replacement therapies
authors: Andreas Smyrlis; Konstantia Kantartzi; Konstantinos Mimidis; Vasileios Papadopoulos; Pelagia Kriki; Marios Theodoridis; Efthimia Mourvati; Evaggelia Charitaki; Triantafyllia Bounta; Anna Chalkidou; Stylianos Panagoutsos
abstract:
Background and Aims
Gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding is common among patients on renal replacement therapies. Endoscopic examination of the upper and lower GI tract often fails to identify hemorrhagic lesions in anemic ESRD patients. The aim of the present study was to investigate the gastrointestinal mucosa and the lesions caused by end-stage renal disease as well as to evaluate the obscure gastrointestinal bleeding (OGIB) in patients with ESRD undergoing renal replacement therapies at our department.
Method
This is a single center observational study of 54 patients undergoing RRT for > 6 months. Of them, 48 patients were on hemodialysis and 6 patients on peritoneal dialysis. Patients underwent capsule endoscopy. We studied the transit time of capsule as well as the and small bowel preparation with laxatives in contrast to simple fasting as well as the Rhemitt score. Also we compare the transit time of the capsule in with or without: diabetes, liver disease, previous GI bleeding and bowel preparation. We recorded demographic, laboratory parameters, comorbidities, parameters related to anemia and history of gastrointestinal bleeding as well as medication. We compare Rhemitt score between hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis patients, with or without heart failure, with or without previous GI bleeding and with or without the use of heparin, clopidogrel or PPIs. We used univariate analysis and multiple logistic regression, to identify factors that promote gastrointestinal mucosal lesion and unexplained gastrointestinal bleeding (OGIB).
Results
There were significant differences in Rhemitt Score between the groups. Hemodialysis patients had higher rebleeding tendency Rhemitt score than peritoneal dialysis patients (P = 0.008). Patients with heart failure had worse Rhemitt score (P = 0.041) than patients without HF, patients with previous GI bleeding had worse Rhemitt score (P = 0.039) than patients without GI bleeding. There was statistically significant difference in the Rhemitt score regarding anticoagulant-antiplatelet treatment of patients and especially low molecular weight heparin (P = 0.023) and clopidogrel (P = 0.008). At last, patents on PPIs had worse Rhemitt score (P = 0.041) than patients without PPIs. (Table 1). Also there were significant differences in transit time between the below groups: Transit time was affected by diabetes mellitus (P = 0.024), liver disease (P = 0.012), previous GI bleeding (P = 0.028) and preparation with laxatives (P = 0.036). Transit time between hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis patients did not differ. Also, the duration of renal replacement therapy did not affect transit time, Rhemitt score or endoscopic findings. (Table 2).
Conclusion
End-stage renal disease causes damage to the gastrointestinal tract that affects the therapeutic management of patients and puts their lives at risk because it contributes to the high probability of rebleeding.

title: #1486 Analysis of the survival rate of patients on kidney replacement therapy in a large city: a multicenter prospective cohort observational study
authors: Konstantin Vishnevskii; Ekaterina Parshina; Alexander Zemchenkov
abstract:
Background and Aims
A detailed comparison of the efficacy of combined interventions in long-term treatment is challenging, if not impossible, to conduct in controlled trials due to ethical constraints. This gap can be addressed through pragmatic research or registry analysis.
Method
Data from eleven-year registry of KRT (n = 1516 new patient with full data) in a major city was utilized to assess mortality risk factors in the modern dialysis population, where dialysis intensity (including hemodiafiltration mode) and correction of anemia were not constrained by resource limitations.
The numerical boundaries for categorical risk factors were selected based on sensitivity evaluation.
Results
The overall five-year survival rate was 60.4% ± 1.5%. In adjusted Cox regression the mortality risk factors associated with dialysis start included: age (increased by 1% per year), underlying diagnosis, baseline GFR values below 5.3 ml/min/m², or 3.6 ml/min/m² (+41% and +55%, respectively), phosphatemia above 1.78 mmol/L (+58%), and lower than 1.13 mmol /L (+38% ), calcemia outside target range (increase +57%, if below, and +120%, if higher), sodium levels above 141 mmol/l (+62%), albumin levels below 36 mg/dL (+22%), and urgent dialysis start (defined as absence of permanent vascular access at first session) and IDWG (+23%, per 1 % increase in IDWG—as mean over 3–15 month period)—for all factors P < 0.01.
The Cox regression analysis evaluated the interaction of calcium and phosphate levels. In comparison with the combination of target ranges, the greatest risk was associated with a combination of hyperphosphatemia and hypercalcemia (3.10), although the proportion of such patients was small (5.6%). In normocalcemia, hypo- and hyperphosphatemia were associated with similar risks (1.85 vs. 1.71)—all P < 0.001; the latter combination was the most frequent (43.7%), more than combination of target ranges (31.4%).
The interaction between baseline eGFR levels and ultrafiltration rate (UF) during HD sessions was assessed using Cox regression analysis. A particularly high mortality risk (+126%, P < 0.001) was linked to a combination of eGFR below 5.4 mL/min/m² and an UF rate exceeding 10 mL/hour/kg (n = 378).
Compared to combination of high baseline eGFR and low UF rate (n = 477), the exceeding the recommended limits of UF rate in patients with relatively preserved kidney function resulted in a 78% increased mortality risk (P < 0.001; n = 561), Compared to a combination of high baseline eGFR and low UF rate (n = 477), exceeding the recommended limit of UF in patients with relatively preserved kidney function resulted in an 78% increase in mortality risk (P < 0.001; n = 561); for patients with negligible eGFR and a low UF, the risk increase was 51% (P = 0.011, n = 100).
Table 1 shows risk factors associated with a hard outcome during follow-up (after index period).
When multiple regression analysis of the baseline albumin level and its changes over follow-up were included in the model, the significance of the baseline albumin level was lost. A favorable scenario was an increase in albumin levels, which was associated with a 14% reduction in OR (P = 0.003), and observed in only 15% of patients, compared to those with stable albumin levels.
Delivered Kt/V (1.54 ± 0.11) and hemoglobin levels were not significant in the context of current practice. The median Hb level was 110 (102–118) g/l; 63.2% of the monthly measurements corresponded to the target range of 100–120 g/l. The median EPO dose was 5250 (3200–6600) IU. In the unadjusted analysis, only a decrease from the target range (100–120 g/l) was associated with a borderline increase in the risk of death (OR 1.107; (95% CI 1.000–1.226), P = 0.050). Similarly, there was no association between Kt/V and mortality risk.
Conclusion
The analysis of survival in KRT registry identified key factors determining hard outcomes in modern dialysis settings. These include both the initial characteristics of patients at the start of KRT and long-term quality indicators for dialysis, as well as unfavorable scenarios regarding the dynamics of key parameters for dialysis quality.

title: #1985 Ambulatory pulse wave velocity as a predictor of all-cause death risk in patients receiving peritoneal dialysis: a prospective observational study
authors: Georgia Vareta; Panagiotis Georgianos; Vasilios Vaios; Ioannis Kontogiorgos; Evangelia Geropoulou; Konstantinos Leivaditis; Evangelia Ntounousi; Elias Balaskas; Pantelis Zebekakis; Vassilios Liakopoulos
abstract:
Background and Aims
Novel devices are now available to enable the recording of central hemodynamic parameters and arterial stiffness indices in ambulatory conditions. The prognostic significance of ambulatory pulse wave velocity (PWV), a marker of arterial stiffness, in end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) patients undergoing long-term peritoneal dialysis (PD) remains unknown.
Method
In this prospective observational study, 140 stable ESKD from 3 PD centers of Northern Greece were included. At baseline, all patients underwent assessment of PWV over a 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring with the oscillometric device Mobil-O-Graph device (I.E.M. GmbH, Stolberg, Germany). Subsequently, these patients were prospectively followed for the evaluation of the risk of death from any cause. The value of 24-hour ambulatory PWV as a predictor of all-cause death risk was assessed using univariate- and multivariate-adjusted Cox regression hazard models.
Results
The study included 140 PD patients (86 males) with a median age of 65 (18-89) years. Over a median follow-up period of 25 months [interquartile range (IQR): 13–47], 38 patients (27.1%) died. In Kaplan-Meier survival analysis 24-hour ambulatory PWV appeared to be of prognostic significance, with all-cause mortality being higher in patients with 24-hour ambulatory PWV ≥9.35 m/s (Log Rank p value = 0.013). In univariate Cox regression analysis, patients with higher 24-hour ambulatory PWV at baseline had a 1.87-fold higher risk of all-cause mortality during the follow-up period [hazard ratio (HR): 1.87; 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.13–3.09]. However, after adjustment for several confounding factors (age, mode of PD, diabetic status, history of pre-existing cardiovascular disease, blood pressure medication use, hemoglobin and serum albumin levels at baseline, residual kidney function) 24-hour ambulatory did not remain an independent of survival (HR: 0.70; 95% CI: 0.30–1.61).
Conclusion
The present study shows that among ESKD patients undergoing long-term PD, 24-hour ambulatory PWV, as assessed with the Mobil-O-Graph device, is not an independent predictor of all-cause death risk after adjustment for multiple risk factors. Whether this marker can enable the better stratification of cardiovascular risk in the PD population requires examination in future studies.

title: #3338 A novel peritoneal dialysis catheter insertion technique to reduce catheter migration
authors: Hyung Duk Kim
abstract:
Background and Aims
Peritoneal dialysis catheter tip location is important to prevent catheter dysfunction. This study evaluates a new surgical technique aimed at preventing peritoneal dialysis catheter migration.
Method
Medical record review was conducted involving 35 patients who underwent peritoneal dialysis catheter insertion. 19 patients received the modified surgical approach by anchoring the upper segment of the catheter's inner cuff to the posterior rectus sheath, while 16 were treated with the conventional method. The adjustment directs the force applied to the catheter towards the abdominal wall, potentially stabilizing its position. We compared the outcomes of this method with traditional placement techniques in a single institution setting. Immediate postoperative kidney-ureter-bladder (KUB) radiography confirmed correct placement of the catheter tips within the pelvic cavity for all patients.
Results
Two-week postoperative KUB assessments revealed that 8 out of the 16 patients in the traditional group experienced catheter tip migration outside the pelvic cavity. In contrast, all 19 patients treated with the new technique maintained intra-pelvic positioning of the catheter tips. Among the eight patients with migrated catheters in the conventional group, seven experienced spontaneous recovery without catheter dysfunction, while one required a guidewire intervention due to catheter dysfunction.
Conclusion
These findings suggest that anchoring the peritoneal dialysis catheter to the posterior rectus sheath may effectively prevent catheter migration, thereby reducing the risk of catheter dysfunction and the need for subsequent interventions. Further studies with larger sample sizes and longer follow-up are necessary to confirm these preliminary results and to establish this method as a standard practice in peritoneal dialysis catheter placement.

title: #88 Effectiveness of a boosting mRNA COVID-19 vaccine dose among hemodialysis patients during the Omicron era
authors: Jong-Woo Yoon; Young-Ki Lee; Hayne Cho Park; Ajin Cho
abstract:
Background and Aims
Previous vaccine effectiveness studies in the hemodialysis population have mainly focused on the Alpha and Delta variant periods, demonstrating that two doses of mRNA COVID-19 vaccines provide substantial protection against severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection and severe outcomes. However, evidence regarding the effectiveness of a boosting mRNA vaccine dose in hemodialysis patients during the Omicron era remains limited.
Method
We conducted a retrospective cohort study of maintenance hemodialysis patients in South Korea who received either two or three doses of mRNA COVID-19 vaccines between January 16, 2022, and April 16, 2022. Data regarding vaccination status, SARS-CoV-2 infection, and COVID-19–related hospitalizations and deaths were identified through the National Health Insurance Service. The RT-PCR–confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection, hospitalization, and death were evaluated as outcomes. A Cox proportional hazards model was used to estimate hazard ratios (HR) after adjustment for age, sex, region, insurance status, and Charlson Comorbidity Index.
Results
A total of 66,654 individuals (mean age 65.7 ± 12.8 years; 60.5% male) were included. At baseline, 11,314 (17%) had completed two vaccine doses, whereas 55,340 (83%) had received three doses. Compared with two-dose recipients, those who received three doses had a 10% lower risk of SARS-CoV-2 infection (HR 0.90, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.86–0.93), a 20% reduction in COVID-19–related hospitalization (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.68–0.93), and a 56% reduction in 30-day mortality following infection (Hr = 0.44, 95% CI 0.37–0.51, Fig. 1). Both BNT162b2 and mRNA-1273, when administered as a third dose, significantly decreased the risks of SARS-CoV-2 infection, COVID-19-related hospitalization, and death.
Conclusion
During the Omicron period, three-dose mRNA COVID-19 vaccination was associated with lower rates of SARS-CoV-2 infection and severe COVID-19 outcomes among maintenance hemodialysis patients compared with two-dose regimens. Our results highlight the importance of ongoing booster strategies in hemodialysis patients to further reduce COVID-19–related morbidity and mortality.

title: #753 Association of combined hypomagnesemia and hypouricemia with mortality risk in hemodialysis patients: a cohort study
authors: Yun-Ting Huang; Ming-Yan Jiang; Chih-Chiang Huang
abstract:
Background and Aims
Low magnesium (Mg) levels are associated with higher mortality in hemodialysis (HD) patients, while the relationship between uric acid (UA) levels and mortality remains inconclusive. Previous studies have examined Mg and UA separately, but their joint association with mortality is unexplored. This study investigates the association of combined hypomagnesemia and hypouricemia with mortality in patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis.
Method
This retrospective cohort study included 444 adult patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis for at least 3 months at a tertiary hospital. Patients were categorized into five groups based on quintiles of serum magnesium (Mg) levels and further stratified into lower (≤7 mg/dL) and higher (>7 mg/dL) uric acid (UA) levels. The cohort was followed for up to 2 years to assess outcomes.
Results
In a cohort of 444 hemodialysis patients (mean age: 62 ± 12 years; 56.3% male), serum Mg levels averaged 2.5 ± 0.4 mg/dL, with 42% exhibiting hypermagnesemia (>2.5 mg/dL). UA levels ranged from 1.2–11.5 mg/dL (median: 7.0 mg/dL), with 98.6% of patients within normal or hyperuricemic ranges. A linear relationship between serum Mg and albumin levels was observed (r = 0.26, P < 0.001). Patients with combined the lowest Mg and lower UA exhibited low nPCR (normalized Protein Catabolic Rate), pre-albumin, and hemoglobin levels, along with high hs-CRP (high-sensitivity C-reactive protein). Survival analysis showed that this group had the highest mortality risk (HR: 2.356, 95% CI: 1.26–4.38), and the association was attenuated after adjusting for serum albumin.
Conclusion
Our findings suggest that combined hypomagnesemia and hypouricemia are associated with increased mortality in hemodialysis patients, largely driven by malnutrition and elevated inflammation. Further research is needed to confirm these results and explore interventions aimed at improving survival in this population.

title: #3483 Outcomes of sirolimus-coated balloon angioplasty for arteriovenous fistula stenosis: a prospective registry analysis from a single center
authors: Ru Yu Tan; Suh Chien Pang; Chee Wooi Tan; Alvin Tng; Apoorva Gogna; Kiang Hiong Tay; Hsien Tsung Tay; Charyl Yap; Tze Tec Chong; Chieh Suai Tan
abstract:
Background and Aims
Arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) are critical for hemodialysis in patients with end-stage renal failure (ESRF), but stenosis remains a significant challenge, often leading to reduced patency and increased intervention rates. Traditional treatment methods, such as plain balloon angioplasty, have limitations concerning long-term patency. Drug-coated balloons aim to improve vascular outcomes by reducing restenosis rates. This study aims to the efficacy of sirolimus-coated balloon angioplasty for AVF stenosis:
Method
Patients who received sirolimus-coated angioplasty for AVF stenosis from a single centre were prospectively followed-up for 12-months. Primary, primary-assisted, and secondary patency rates of AVF over a 12-month were analyzed.
Results
The cohort comprised 40 patients with an average age of 66.3 years, predominantly male (65%) and of Chinese ethnicity (82.5%). The majority of patients presented with significant comorbidities, including hypertension (92.5%) and diabetes (77.5%). At six months, the target lesion primary patency rate was 74.6% (95% CI, 62.7%–88.8%), which decreased to 45.9% (95% CI, 33.1%–63.7%) at 12 months. Circuit access primary patency was 65.2% (95% CI, 51.5%-–82.4%) at six months and declined to 34.2% (95% CI, 21.7%–53.9%) at 12 months. Despite these decreases, the primary assisted patency remained high, with rates of 94.6% (95% CI, 87.6%–100%) at six months and 83.5% (95% CI, 72.3%–96.5%) at 12 months. Remarkably, secondary patency was maintained at 100% throughout the 12-month follow-up.
Conclusion
These findings suggest that sirolimus-coated balloon angioplasty is a promising intervention for maintaining AVF patency, offering high rates of primary assisted and secondary patency in a challenging ESRF population.

title: #2091 Cancer mortality in patients with kidney failure: insights from the Korea Clinical Data Utilization Network (K-CURE) database
authors: Chang Seong Kim; Hong Sang Choi; Hyejin Park; Su Hyun Song; Sang Heon Suh; Eun Hui Bae; Seong Kwon MA; Soo Wan Kim
abstract:
Background and Aims
The population with cancer is associated with an increased risk of death. However, the impact of cancer on mortality among individuals with kidney failure remains unclear. We investigated cancer-related mortality in patients with kidney failure, stratified by various types of cancer.
Method
A total of 1,307,680 participants who were newly diagnosed with cancer identified from the Korea-Clinical Data Utilization Network for Research Excellence (K-CURE) database between 2013 and 2019. We analyzed data from 7,719 patients with preexisting kidney failure before cancer diagnosis and compared their mortality risk with patients without kidney failure using multivariable Cox proportional hazard models.
Results
The mortality rate was significantly higher in the kidney failure group (196.6 vs 91.1 per 1,000 person-years). Adjusted hazard models indicated that preexisting kidney failure was associated with an increased risk of mortality all cancer types after adjusting for comorbidities and treatment modalities (adjusted hazard ratio [AHR] 1.75, 95% CI 1.70–1.81). Among specific cancer types, breast, uterine, ovarian, pharyngeal, and thyroid cancers showed the highest mortality risks, with thyroid cancer presenting the greatest risk (AHR 4.96, 95% CI 3.73–6.60). Furthermore, interaction analyses revealed higher AHRs for mortality in localized cancers compared to regional and distant stages.
Conclusion
Preexisting kidney failure significantly increases the mortality risk among cancer patients, particularly in those with localized disease stages and specific types of cancer. This underscores the importance of developing tailored management strategies for this vulnerable population.

title: #2219 Development of a predictive model for nafamostat mesylate dosing in hemodialysis
authors: Shin Yeong Lee; Hwa Jeong Kim; Jin Sug Kim; Kyung-A Choi; Jeong Min Yoon; Moon-Jeong Seo; Kyun-Sang Lee; Ji-Yung Lee; Ah-Ran Choi; Kyoung Hwa Seo; Sung Min Ko
abstract:
Background and Aims
Nafamostat mesylate, an anticoagulant with a short half-life, is useful in hemodialysis for patients with a high risk of bleeding. Research on the appropriate dosage of nafamostat has been insufficient. This study aims to develop a dosage prediction model using data from patients adequately anticoagulated with nafamostat.
Method
We retrospectively analyzed medical records from 12 centers affiliated with Yeolin Medical Foundation over an 8-month period. We evaluated coagulation records from dialysis membranes and vein chambers and cases demonstrating adequate coagulation were included. Candidate predictor variables were evaluated using bootstrapping and stepwise regression to determine feature importance. Several predictive models were developed, and the best model was selected based on RMSE and adjusted R² metrics.
Results
Data from 88 patients and 308 cases were analyzed, with an average nafamostat dose of 21.90 ± 6.82 mg/hr. The top four important features were oral anticoagulant use, dry body weight, age and hemoglobin. The Stepwise 70% model wich used top 12 variables showed the best prediction with an RMSE of 4.11 (95% CI: 4.06, 4.15) and an adjusted R² of 0.49. In the multivariate linear regression results using the best model, variables such as oral anticoagulant use [coeff. −14.20, 95% CI (−18.28, −10.12), P value <0.001] and age [−0.13, 95% CI (−0.19, −0.08), <0.001] were associated with a decrease in nafamostat dosage. Conversely, variables such as dry body weight [0.15, 95% CI (0.09, 0.22), <0.001] and hemoglobin [1.13, 95% CI (0.51, 1.76), <0.001] were associated with an increase in nafamostat dosage.
Conclusion
The nafamostat dosage prediction formula derived from the Stepwise 70% model enables individualized dosage calculations. However, further studies for model improvement and external validation are required due to the retrospective nature of this study. Body weight, age, oral anticoagulant, and hemoglobin should be considered when determining the dose of Nafamostat.

title: #2842 Benefits of exercise in octogenarians on hemodialysis
authors: Lida Rodas; Sergi Aragó Sorrosal; Anna Yuguero
abstract:
Background
The aging population has increased the number of older adults with chronic kidney disease in advanced stages who require hemodialysis (HD) therapy. Octogenarians constitute a vulnerable group due to the frequent presence of comorbidities, sarcopenia, and functional limitations. However, physical exercise, as demonstrated in this study, not only improves the quality of life but also contributes to the preservation of physical functionality and the mitigation of cardiovascular and metabolic complications in octogenarians on hemodialysis. This finding offers hope for the future of geriatric care, even in complex clinical conditions.
Aims
To evaluate the feasibility and impact of intradialytic physical activity programs on functional performance in patients over 80 years of age undergoing hemodialysis. The study aims to assess changes in physical parameters, including 4-meter walking speed and the 5 sit-to-stand test (5STS), before and after implementing a structured exercise regimen. Additionally, it seeks to explore the potential benefits of exercise in improving quality of life and maintaining physical functionality in this vulnerable population, considering the challenges of sarcopenia and frailty.
Method
This is a 12-month prospective study of 15 patients, the mean age being 84 years, 80% women, on a chronic hemodialysis program, three sessions per week, 5 hours per session. The baseline and 12-month physical assessments include cardiorespiratory fitness, a 4-meter walk test (4MWT), and muscle strength with 5 sit-to-stand repetitions (5STS). The time to complete the test is recorded with a stopwatch. Safety measures, including supervision by trained staff and immediate cessation if fatigue, dizziness, or instability occurs, were strictly adhered to, ensuring the well-being of the patients.
Intradialytic exercise strategies include low intensity cycling using pedal exercisers, adjusted for individual endurance, performed for 30 minutes during the first two hours of dialysis; resistance exercises with elastic bands targeting major muscle groups, focusing on 1–2 sets of 8–10 repetitions. All activities are supervised by trained staff, with vital signs monitored throughout. These interventions aim to enhance physical function while ensuring patient safety and adherence. Safety measures include immediate cessation of exercise if any signs of fatigue, dizziness, or instability occur and the presence of trained staff to provide immediate assistance if needed.
Results
The adherence to the program was high (80.8%). After the intervention, the two main variables were evaluated. Overall, increases in walking speed (higher values in m/s) were observed, indicating improvements in functional capacity, there was no statistically significant difference with a p 0.57 and 5STS p 0.32. Intra-subject differences ± 95% CI between procedures were 0.02 ± 0.05m s for velocity and 6.9 ± 29.8 for a 5STS, which were considered trivial. There were no intradialytic complications.
Conclusion
Intradialytic physical exercise in octogenarian patients did not show significant differences in the physical tests evaluated, possibly due to the limited capacity to adapt to exercise associated with sarcopenia and the small sample size. However, the implementation of intradialytic exercise programs remains a relevant tool to improve the quality of life of patients with advanced chronic kidney disease on dialysis. Although changes in functional parameters were modest, this study provides a realistic view of the potential of exercise to contribute to maintaining physical function, reducing the impact of frailty, and promoting patient participation in their care process.

title: #92 Weekly patterns of emergency department visits, hospitalizations, and mortality in patients with end-stage kidney disease: a Korean nationwide registry analysis
authors: Young-Ki Lee; Hayne Cho Park; Jong-Woo Yoon; Ajin Cho; Kyung Don Yoo
abstract:
Background and Aims
Previous studies have shown that patients with end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) undergoing thrice-weekly hemodialysis may experience higher mortality following their longest dialysis-free interval, often referred to as the “post-weekend effect.” However, there is limited information on the weekly patterns of emergency department (ED) visits and outcomes in ESKD patients compared with those who have normal kidney function (non-CKD).
Method
We conducted a retrospective analysis of data from the National Emergency Department Information System (NEDIS) in South Korea from January 2019 to December 2021. The ED visits, hospitalizations, and in-hospital mortality were assessed on a daily basis. Logistic regression analyses were used to assess weekly pattern after adjustment for demographic and clinical factors, including the Korean Triage and Acuity Scale (KTAS). In total, 159,456 ED visits by ESKD patients and 21,547,014 ED visits by non-CKD patients were included in the analysis.
Results
Compared with the non-CKD group, ESKD patients were older, had a higher proportion of males, and presented with more severe conditions at ED admission. A distinct weekly pattern emerged among ESKD patients showing the highest ED visit rates on Monday (19.9%) and Tuesday (15.8%) compared to non-CKD patients on Sunday (19.1%) and Saturday (16.2%) (Figure). Hospitalization rates were substantially higher among ESKD patients (66.5%) compared to those of non-CKD patients (21.3%), peaking on Wednesday (67.2%) and Thursday (67.4%). Moreover, ESKD patients had a higher in-hospital mortality rate (9.2%) compared with non-CKD patients (5.1%), particularly on Wednesday (9.7%) and Thursday (9.4%).
Conclusion
Our findings indicate that ESKD patients exhibit pronounced weekly patterns in ED visits, hospitalizations, and mortality compared with non-CKD patients. Notably, ED visits among ESKD patients were highest on Monday and Tuesday, whereas hospitalization and mortality peaked on Wednesday and Thursday.

title: #2141 Machine learning analysis of clinical determinants affecting gut microbiota in hemodialysis patients: a longitudinal study
authors: Ping-Hsun Wu; Chan Hsu; Po-Yu Liu; Teng-Hui Huang; Yi Wen Chiu; Mei-Chuan Kuo; Shang-Jyh Hwang; Yi-Ting Lin
abstract:
Background and Aims
Gut microbiome diversity influences clinical outcomes in haemodialysis patients, yet the long-term impact of clinical factors on microbiome composition remains unclear. This study investigated how patient characteristics, medications, and clinical parameters affect gut microbiome diversity in haemodialysis patients over three years using machine learning analysis.
Method
We conducted a longitudinal study (2017–2020) of 41 haemodialysis patients, collecting gut microbiome samples at baseline and follow-up. Individual clinical data was extracted monthly from electronic health records throughout the observation period. Microbiome diversity was measured using the Shannon index. Long short-term memory (LSTM) neural networks analysed factors affecting diversity changes, with integrated gradients identifying key predictors. Linear regression examined antibiotic exposure timing and alpha diversity relationships.
Results
LSTM models identified antibiotic exposure as the strongest predictor of microbial diversity changes (validation MAE: 0.107, RMSE: 0.131). Beta-lactams showed the highest feature importance in both LSTM and age/sex-adjusted linear regression models. Species analysis revealed significant compositional differences between beta-lactam treated and untreated groups, particularly in Bacteroides vulgatus and Sutterella wadsworthensis abundance.
Conclusion
Antibiotic exposure, particularly beta-lactams, significantly impacts gut microbial diversity in haemodialysis patients. Our LSTM model effectively predicts microbiome changes, offering insights for antibiotic stewardship in this population.

title: #963 Psychological symptoms among hemodialysis patients in Thailand and their impact on health-status
authors: Parnreutai Chaiyasat; Pongsathorn Gojaseni; Reutairat Chaiyasat
abstract:
Background and Aims
End-stage kidney disease (ESKD) is a rapidly increasing global health burden. The prevalence of psychological issues among individuals with ESKD has increased, potentially impacting clinical outcomes. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of depression and anxiety among hemodialysis patients in Thailand and to investigate their effects on physical functional scale.
Method
The study population consisted of 766 dialysis patients from eight facilities across Thailand. The assessment tools used were the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HAD) and the SF-36, Thai edition.
Results
The findings revealed a high prevalence of psychological conditions, with rates for anxiety and depression standing at 24.8% and 28.5%, respectively. title: #1119 The association between residual urine output and quality of life in hemodialysis patients
authors: Hyun Lee Ko
abstract:
Background and Aims
The preservation of urine output and improvement of quality of life (QoL) are clinically crucial challenges in dialysis patients. However, systematic research on the relationship between urine output and quality of life remains limited. Therefore, this study aims to analyze the correlation between urine output and QoL, as well as to identify the factors that influence this relationship.
Method
A cross-sectional study was conducted with 97 dialysis patients. Twenty-four-hour urine output collected on non-dialysis days and QoL assessed by EQ-5D-5L value were divided into two groups based on their median values (520 mL/day and 0.82, respectively). Statistical analysis consisted of chi-square tests for group comparisons, followed by univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses. Results were presented as odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI).
Results
Of the 97 participants, 37 had no urine output (0 mL/day), while 60 had residual urine output, evenly divided between ≤520 mL/day and >520 mL/day. Participants with higher urine output demonstrated significantly shorter dialysis vintage, lower ultrafiltration rates, and lower serum potassium levels (Table 1). Higher urine output was associated with better reported QoL, with a significant difference (P = 0.028) observed in the group with urine output >520mL/day (Fig. 1). Both univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses revealed that participants with urine output >520 mL/day had significantly higher odds of better QoL compared to those with no urine output (Or = 3.833, 95% CI: 1.410–11.102, P = 0.010; and Or = 18.305, 95% CI: 2.520–175.757, P = 0.007, respectively) (Table 2).
Conclusion
This study demonstrates a significant association between urine output and QoL in hemodialysis patients. Our findings suggest that strategies to preserve residual urine output may contribute to improved QoL in this population. However, longitudinal studies are warranted to establish causality and further elucidate these relationships.

title: #1949 Timing of transition to peritoneal dialysis (PD) and its impact on bacteremia risk in PD patients
authors: Sara-Jane Chan; Marjorie Foo; Htay; Mathini Jayaballa; Khin Zai Li Lwin; Elizabeth Oei; Chieh Suai Tan; Angela Wang
abstract:
Background and Aims
End stage kidney patients opting for PD as choice of modality can either start PD with a PD catheter or with interim hemodialysis (HD) via a tunnelled vascular catheter before transitioning to PD. This study examined how the timing of the transition to PD influences patient outcomes.
Method
This single-center retrospective cohort study included adult PD patients from 2005 to 2015, classified into three groups: PD-first (started directly on PD), Rapid PD Transition (interim HD with PD catheter insertion within ≤2 weeks), and Delayed PD Transition (interim HD with PD catheter insertion between >2 weeks and ≤6 months). The study investigated how the timing of PD transition affected the risk of bacteremia.
Results
The study included 807 PD patients, comprising 257 in the PD-first group, 169 in the Rapid PD transition group, and 381 in the Delayed PD Transition group. Compared to the PD-first group, the Delayed PD Transition group had higher rates of diabetes and cardiovascular disease and, a greater proportion of patients not seen by a nephrologist before dialysis. Patients in the Delayed PD Transition group had significantly higher odds of bacteremia compared to the PD-first group (adjusted odds ratio (AOR) 2.08; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.46–2.99; P < 0.001), whereas no such association was observed in the Rapid PD Transition group (AOR: 1.45; 95% CI: 0.93–2.26; P = 0.10) Additionally, the time to the first episode of bacteremia was shorter in both the Rapid PD Transition group (adjusted hazard ratio (AHR) 1.60, 95% CI 1.10–2.33; P = 0.01) and Delayed PD Transition group (HR 1.97, 95% CI 1.46–2.67; P < 0.01) compared to the PD-first group.
Conclusion
Patients with Delayed PD Transition were significantly associated with an increased risk of bacteremia and a shorter time to its onset compared to those who initiated PD with PD catheter. Future multicenter studies are needed to confirm these findings.

title: #2519 Long-term treatment with medium cut-off dialyzer increase muscle mass in hemodialysis patients
authors: Jung Eun Lee; Hoon Young Choi; Hyeong Cheon Park
abstract:
Background and Aims
Sarcopenia, characterized by progressive loss of muscle mass and function, is a prevalent complication in hemodialysis (HD) patients, significantly impacting morbidity and quality of life. Uremic toxics, oxidative stress as well as systemic inflammation contribute to muscle degradation. Short-term treatment with medium cut-off (MCO) dialyzers have demonstrated potential in increasing muscle while maintain fat tissue in maintenance HD patients, This study aimed to investigate long-term effects of MCO dialyzer in muscle mass and serum albumin in maintenance HD patients.
Method
We performed a randomized prospective study with 77 HD patients, divided into MCO dialyzer group (MCO, n = 39) and high-flux dialyzer group (HF, n = 38) (31 males, mean age 64.8 ± 12.2 years) from dialysis units of Gangnam Severance hospital and Yongin Severance hospital, Korea. Measurements of body weight, height, bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA), and various biochemical parameters were taken at baseline and 12 months.
Results
Both group showed a slight decline in albumin levels, with a slightly greater drop in MCO group, but the difference was not statistically significant (−0.10 vs −0.19, p-value 0.065). Beta2-microglobulin levels increased in the HF group but slightly decreased in the MCO group (2.59 vs −0.51, p-value 0.025). The appendicular skeletal mass index (ASMI) that reflects skeletal muscle mass amount remained stable in the MCO group but declined in the HF group (−0.81 vs 0.27, p-value 0.049]. Kappa and Lambda free light chain level decreased in both group but were reduced greater in MCO group than in HF group at 12 months(−17.96 vs −74.89, p-value 0.008; −29.01 vs −54.23, p value <0.001).
Conclusion
Long-term use of MCO dialyzer may improve muscle mass by reducing toxic middle molecules. These findings suggest that the potential role of MCO dialyzers in preventing sarcopenia in maintenance HD patients. Further large-scale studies are needed to confirm these benefits.

title: #2805 Importance of intrinsic membrane dysfunction as a predictor of survival in peritoneal dialysis
authors: Claudia Muñoz Martínez; Byron Chiliquinga Morales; Leonardo Calle Garcia; Carmen Martin Varas; Carlos Santos Alonso; Pablo Luis Sánchez Garrote; Paulo Garcia Gutierrez; Maria Nieves Losada; Pía Orellana; Maria Jose Fernandez-Reyes Luis
abstract:
Background and Aims
The absolute dip of dialysate sodium concentration (ΔDNa) (Na Dialysate at the start of the PET—Na Dialysate at 60 min) is an expression of sodium sieving. Intrinsic membrane dysfunction has recently been defined as ultrafiltration failure (UFF) with a low sodium differential (ΔDNa <5 mEq/l), irrespective of the type of transport at the start of peritoneal dialysis. However, it is not known whether this dysfunction is intrinsic and whether it conditions patient prognosis.
Our main objective was to determine whether variations in ΔDNa condition UF capacity and patient survival from the outset. A second objective was to see if this dysfunction was maintained over time.
Method
We included 58 incident patients in our centre (age: 60.6 ± 14.4 years; 74% male; 15.5% diabetic) between 2009–2023 who underwent 3.86%-PET ΔDNa in the first 8–12 weeks. We recorded dialysis regimen and daily UF (dUF defined as the mean daily UF of the previous 2 months). We analysed survival. Subsequently we performed a sub-analysis with 30 patients who continued on the technique to see if there were changes in kinetics at one year.
Results
There is a large variability between baseline kinetic parameters [D/Pcr: 0.68 ± 0.09; standard UF (sUF): 805 ± 242 ml and ΔDNa: 10.5 ± 3.8 mEq/L]. Patients were followed for 24 ± 19 months. Mean dUF was 393 ± 316 ml and diuresis was 1662 ± 736 ml. 51.7% patients were on CAPD from baseline, 24% used icodextrin and only 8.67% used 2.27%-glucose exchanges. In linear regression analysis for sUF, D/PCr and ΔDNa were independent risk factors. In the linear regression analysis for dUF, the only independent risk factor was ΔDNa, with no influence of the type of technique (CAPD/APD) or the use of icodextrin.
Lower ΔDNa, not D/Pcr or sUF, was associated with worse survival (P = 0.039). In the Cox analysis, when age was introduced as a confounder, the predictive value for mortality disappeared. There was a nearly significant correlation between ΔDNa and age (R = −0.25, P = 0.053). Worse survival was observed in the Kaplan Meier analysis in patients with ΔDNa <6 mEq/L (P25) (Fig. 1).
In the 30 patients who underwent 3.86%-PET ΔDNa at 1 year, we observed no change in ΔDNa (10.5 ± 3.8 vs 10.6 ± 5.7 mEq/L, n/s).
Conclusion
The great variability of ΔDNa in basal kinetics is confirmed, conditioning from the beginning the UF capacity, independently of permeability and technique. This is an inherent characteristic of the patient. We observed an effect on survival both as a continuous variable (Cox) as well as in patients with ΔDNa <6 mEq/L. As there is an almost significant correlation with age, studies with a larger population are needed to confirm this. It is important to perform baseline kinetics with 3.86%-PET and measure ΔDNa in order to classify, from a pathophysiological point of view, patients at high risk of membrane dysfunction and individualize their prescription.

title: #3664 BRIGHT-HD—Brazil research investigation on public health gain comparing survival between hemodialysis and hemodiafiltration
authors: Eduardo Paiva; João Chang; Elaine Arantes; Aline Cordeiro; Sandra Reis; Douglas Andrade; Rafaela Rossi; Rafael de Lima; Whelington Rocha; Andrea Magalhães; Cynthia Borges; Rosilene Motta
abstract:
Background and Aims
High-flux online hemodiafiltration (OL-HDF) appears to be associated with better survival than hemodialysis (HD). In Brazil, OL-HDF is only affordable for patients with private health insurance. Although observational studies have shown a survival advantage with OL-HDF, even in Brazil, it is unclear whether this benefit would apply to patients without private health insurance. We compared overall and cardiovascular mortality between OL-HDF and HD in patients treated exclusively by the Public Health Care system.
Method
This is an observational cohort study that included adult patients on maintenance dialysis between September 1st, 2022 and December 1st, 2024. The main outcome was all-cause mortality. Secondary outcome was cardiovascular mortality. Fine-gray sub-distribution hazard models were used to evaluate survival in the presence of a competing event (kidney transplant and recovery of renal failure).
Results
Patients on HD (n = 321) and OL-HDF (n = 48) were similar in age, race, sex and vascular access. Patients on HD were more likely to have diabetes (54.0% vs. 29.2%, P = 0.001) and underwent higher hours/week on dialysis (11.2 ± 1.8 vs. 10.5 ± 1.6 h, P = 0.006). In an adjusted Fine and Gray model, the hazard of death for patients on OL-HDF was 68% lower than that for patients on HD and the risk of death in patients with an arteriovenous fistula was 55% lower compared to patients to those with a catheter (Fig. 1). Cardiovascular mortality was not different among groups.
Conclusion
These findings indicate that OL-HDF is associated with higher overall survival compared to HD, even for patients without private health insurance.

title: #1547 Association between acid-base disorders at dialysis initiation and mortality: a multicenter prospective cohort study in Japan
authors: Hideaki Shimizu; Yoshihiro Nakamura; Sho Sasaki; Daijo Inaguma
abstract:
Background and Aims
Among patients with advanced chronic kidney disease metabolic acidosis is the most common acid-base balance abnormality. Other types of acid-base balance abnormalities, such as metabolic alkalosis, are also important and should not be overlooked. However, there are no prior studies on the association between acid-base disorders at dialysis initiation and mortality. The aim of this study was to investigate the relationship between the type of acid-base disorders at dialysis initiation and mortality in a Japanese population.
Method
This study was a multicenter prospective cohort study. The data was collected by the Aichi Cohort study of Prognosis in Patients newly initiated into dialysis (AICOPP) in which 18 Japanese tertiary care centers participated. The study enrolled 1,524 patients who were newly introduced to dialysis (the patients started maintenance dialysis between October 2011 and September 2013). Of all participants, 1,149 patients were eligible for the study. After descriptive statistics, a multivariable adjusted Cox hazard models were used to evaluate mortality based on the type of acid base disorder. The types of acid base disorder were divided into five categories: normal, high anion gap metabolic acidosis (HAGMA), HAGMA with metabolic alkalosis, non-anion gap metabolic acidosis (NAGMA) and metabolic alkalosis.
Results
Among 1,149 patients (mean age, 68 years; 67% male), 841 (73.2%), 142 (12.4%), 87 (7.6%), 45 (3.9%) and 34 (3.0%) patients were classified as HAGMA, HAGMA with metabolic alkalosis, normal, NAGMA and metabolic alkalosis, respectively.
During a median follow-up period of 3.5 years (mean: 3.3 years), a total of 284 patients (25.8%) died.
Compared to normal, metabolic alkalosis tended to have a higher all-cause mortality rate, but it was not statistically significant (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR, 1.35; 95% CI, 0.69–2.63]). On the other hand, HAGMA (aHR, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.64–1.51), HAGMA with metabolic alkalosis (aHR 0.80; 95% CI, 0.69–2.63), NAGMA (aHR 0.80; 95% CI, 0.37–2.63) showed a risk similar to normal.
Conclusion
In our study, metabolic alkalosis at the initiation of dialysis tended to be higher risk of mortality compared to normal. Although the difference was not statistically significant, this may be attributed to the smaller sample size with metabolic alkalosis. Further research with larger sample sizes is necessary to clarify the impact of metabolic alkalosis on survival outcomes.

title: #579 Sarcopenia, frailty, and malnutrition in hemodialysis patients: an emerging clinical challenge
authors: Altagracia Elisa Bello Ovalles; Aránzazu Pardo Ruiz; Antonio Manuel Gil Paraíso; Celia Garijo Pacheco; Esther Najera Galarreta; Marta Artamendi Larrañaga; Jorge Francisco Sanchez Iglesias; Miguel Villa-Valdés; Laura Sahdala Santana; Emma Huarte Loza
abstract:
Background and Aims
Sarcopenia, defined as the loss of muscle mass and strength, is closely associated with aging and chronic diseases. The diagnostic criteria, as updated by the European Working Group on Sarcopenia in Older People (EWGSOP2), emphasize identifying reduced muscle mass accompanied by impaired function. Various diagnostic techniques, including magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA), are widely employed.
The aim of this study is to describe the nutritional, sarcopenic, and frailty profiles of patients undergoing chronic hemodialysis (HD) at San Pedro Hospital, Logroño. descriptive cross-sectional study, employing validated surveys to assess malnutrition (MIS), sarcopenia (SARC-F), functional capacity (Lawton and Brody), frailty (FRAIL), and long-term mortality based on patient comorbidity (Charlson Comorbidity Index).
Method
This descriptive cross-sectional study evaluated the nutritional, sarcopenic, and frailty profiles of patients on chronic HD at San Pedro Hospital, Logroño. Validated surveys, including the Malnutrition Inflammation Score (MIS), the SARC-F for sarcopenia, the Lawton and Brody scale for functional capacity, the FRAIL scale for frailty, and the Charlson Comorbidity Index, were employed to assess the population.
Sarcopenia was further evaluated using handgrip strength as an indicator of muscle strength and the phase angle (PA) measured through single-frequency bioimpedance analysis (50 Hz). The inclusion criteria encompassed patients undergoing HD for over three months and those without acute inflammatory conditions.
The study population was categorized based on the presence of sarcopenia, as determined by a positive SARC-F screening. Clinical, analytical, and impedance data were compared between the sarcopenic and non-sarcopenic groups.
Results
The study included 39 patients, of which 33% were women and 66% were men, with a mean age of 65 years. The mean scores for the SARC-F, FRAIL, MIS, and Charlson Comorbidity Index were 2.4, 2.05, 8.6, and 4.28, respectively.
Regarding nutritional status, as assessed by the MIS, 24% of the patients were categorized as having normal nutritional status (MIS <6), 55% as mildly malnourished (MIS = 7–12), and 21% as moderately to severely malnourished (MIS = 13–18). Sarcopenia, defined as a SARC-F score ≥4, was present in 53.8% of patients, while 46.2% were categorized as non-sarcopenic (SARC-F <4). title: #3205 Axillary loop arteriovenous grafts as a rescue from vascular access failure: long-term results at a single facility
authors: Manabu Asano; Hitoshi Iwabuchi; Kengo Horie; Takashi Iijima; Kenichi Oguchi
abstract:
Background and Aims
Vascular access (VA) is mandatory for hemodialysis patients. Normally, arteriovenous fistula in forearm or upper arm is considered the standard VA. However, there are a certain number of cases in which autologous blood vessels are degraded and arteriovenous (AV) grafts is the only option. Among these, we have ranked the axillary loop AV grafts as the final VA in upper limb. We report the current status of axillary loop AV grafts at our facility and efforts to maintain long-term patency of these.
Method
Among 5741 cases of VA treatment at our facility over the 10-year period from 2015 to 2024, the patients who had axillary loop AV grafts were surveyed. We examined patient background, type of grafts used, implant length, VA complications and radiological/surgical intervention details to sustain function and patency rate. The primary patency period was defined as time from surgery to the first therapeutic intervention, also the ssecondary patency period was defined as time until VA function was abolished. The patency rate was calculated using the Kaplan-Meier method.
Results
Forty-eight patients were identified who had undergone axillary AV graft placement. The mean age was 68 years (range from 43 to 90), 30 (62.5%) were women, 20 (41.7%) were diabetic, and the mean dialysis vintage was 155 months. Forty-five patients (93.8%) have already received some access surgeries. The mean number of prior VA surgeries was 4.0 (between 1 and 11). Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) grafts were used in all patients as follows : Advanta VSTM 4—6 mm in 2 cases, Advanta VXT™ 4-6 mm in 10 cases, GOREⓇPROPATENⓇ 4–6 mm in 9 cases, LifeSpanⓇ 4–7 mm in 7 cases and Flixene™ 4–6 mm in 20 cases. In our method, the axillar artery was used for inflow access and the basilic or axillary vein was used for outflow access. The mean graft length was 29.9 cm (ranged from 18 to 40). Early VA complications within 30 days after surgery were observed in 19 cases (venous outflow tract stenosis in 10 cases, thrombosis in 8 cases, central venous stenosis in 1 case). Late complications appeared in 23 patients (venous outflow tract stenosis in 16 cases, thrombosis in 3 cases, central venous stenosis in 2 cases, infection in 2 cases). VA salvage was performed in 41 cases, of which 37 underwent radiological intervention (includes 17 cases of thrombus aspiration and 15 cases of stent placement for outflow tract stenosis) and 4 underwent surgical intervention (thrombectomy in 1 case, graft removal due to infection in 2 cases, and closure due to severe heart failure in 1 cases). The mean follow-up period was 22.7 months. The primary and secondary patency rates were 14.4/75.3% at 1-year, 3.9/59.8% at 3-year, and 3.9/49.3% at 5-year, respectively.
Conclusion
We consider axillary loop AV graft as the final internal VA in absolutely desperate hemodialysis patients. If early VA complications could be avoided through diligent screening and maintenance, further long-term patency may be expected.
