title: #2026 The effects of interventions synbiotics on serum metabolic profiles in hemodialysis patients.
authors: Evgeny Shutov; Stepan Bolshakov; Seda Keroglyan; Anna Chibikova; Sofia Mariasina; Uliana Bulgakova; Vasily Vasil'ev; Sergey Sorokoletov
abstract:
Background and Aims
The study of the metabolites in patients with CKD on hemodialysis, is of great interest due to the involvement their in the development of typical complications (cardiovascular diseases, vascular calcification, infection s and so on), and deciding the appropriate treatment. The resulted metabolic disturbances associated with the severity of the disease mirror the phenotype of an organism and provide a detailed understanding of the metabolic processes involved in a disease. In addition, the use of synbiotics (probiotics and prebiotics) can significantly affect the intestinal microflora and metabolites.
The patients included in the study were clinically stable (men and women) with HD for at least 6 months before the study. The patients underwent a standard haemodialysis procedure 3 times a week. The aim of this study was to investigate the blood metabolic profile in patients on hemodialysis and the effect of the treatment with with “Maxilac”, a synbiotic drug on the blood metabolic profile.
Method
In our study we included 22 patients, age 53 ± 12.4 years (12 f/10 m), who received hemodialysis at our nephrology center. The study of metabolites included 2 stages before taking “Maxilac” and after two months. Blood samples were analyzed using 1H-nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy focusing on low-molecular-weight metabolites. We used standard statistical methods and OPLS-DA analyses employing the MetaboAnalyst 5.0 platform.
Results
A total of 55 metabolites were identified in serum samples from hemodialysis patients with CKD. The t-test demonstrated statistically significant changes in several metabolites after “Maxilac” treatment, including threonine, hippurate, myoinosotole, xanthosine, carnitine, acetone, aspartate, formate, proline, creatinine, 2-oxoisocaproate, lactate (Fig. 1). The oPLS-DA statistical analysis score plot is presented in the Fig. 2 with component changes including 15 metabolites with significant changes in concentration before and after “Maxilac” treatment. These metabolites included threonine, formate, acetone, xanthosine, aspartate, acetate, proline, myoinositol, inosine, 1-methylhystidine, carnitine, lactate, 2-oxoisocaproate, dimethylamine, 3-methyl-2-oxovalerate. These findings indicate that “Maxilac” therapy induces specific metabolic alterations in patients on hemodialysis, predominantly impacting amino acid, purine, and glucose metabolism.
Conclusion
The use of “Maxilac” in patients on hemodialysis leads to an improvement in the metabolic profile.

title: #2945 Fragility fractures in end-stage chronic kidney disease (CKD) population: patient-related and CKD-related factor analysis—a single-center experience
authors: Gianmarco De Luca; Giuseppe Grandaliano
abstract:
Background and Aims
Chronic kidney disease (CKD) stands as a prevalent global health concern, and mineral and bone disease are among the most impactful consequences. A severe complication arising from mineral and bone disease is the occurrence of fragility fractures, which disproportionately affect individuals with CKD compared to the general population. The prevalence of these fractures impacts both survival rates and quality of life. The aims of this study are analyzing and identifying patient-related risk factors and CKD-related risk factors to contribute to the development of preventive measures for fragility fractures for this population.
Method
A retrospective, single-center observational study was conducted, encompassing patient data from the years 2021 to 2023. Registry data were recorded, including patient-related and CKD-related data. Patients were interviewed about traumatological history, and their answers were recorded. Logistic regression analysis was employed to investigate the association between independent variables and dependent variables.
Results
Eighty-four patients, with a mean age of 64.3 ± 15.2 years and a male percentage of 58.3%, were included in this study. Among them, 19.5% exhibited smoking habits. The mean Charlson Comorbidity Index was 3.06 ± 1.21. All patients were diagnosed with end-stage chronic kidney disease, with mean durations of 208 months from the diagnosis and 84.5 months from the beginning of dialysis. The logistic regression analysis, adjusted for age, sex, and CCI, revealed that smoking habits play a significant role as a risk factor for fragility fractures in lower limbs (p: 0.011). The incidence of fragility fractures increases directly proportionally to the time since diagnosis (p-value: 0.021) and the beginning of dialysis treatment (p-value: 0.001)
Conclusion
Among patient-related factors, smoking habits seem to significantly affect lower-limb fracture rates (P < 0.05), whereas among CKD-related factors, time since CKD diagnosis and time since the beginning of dialysis treatment are directly related to higher risks of fragility fractures. No relevant correlations emerged in the studied treatments, except for a reduction in proximal femur fracture occurrence when patients underwent a combined treatment of a calcimimetic and a vitamin D analog.

title: #3268 Cognitive decline in hemodialysis patients : a prospective cross-sectional study analysing sociodemographic and clinical determinants
authors: Siri Chandana Gangasani; Ram Prasad Elumalai; Sandhya Suresh
abstract:
Background and Aims
Cognitive impairment is a prevalent but underdiagnosed complication in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) undergoing hemodialysis (HD). Cognitive decline in hemodialysis patients impacts treatment adherence, quality of life, and long-term health outcomes.
The Addenbrooke's Cognitive Examination-III (ACE-III) is a widely used, standardized cognitive assessment tool designed to evaluate five key cognitive domains: attention, memory, fluency, language, and visuospatial skills. It provides a comprehensive score out of 100, with higher scores indicating better cognitive function. The ACE-III is particularly effective in identifying cognitive impairment across various conditions, including dementia, mild cognitive impairment, and other neurodegenerative diseases. Its detailed evaluation of different cognitive domains makes it highly suitable for detecting subtle cognitive deficits in chronic illnesses like chronic kidney disease.
This study aims to evaluate the prevalence and determinants of cognitive impairment in hemodialysis patients and to explore its association with sociodemographic and clinical factors. The findings may pave the way for targeted interventions that can improve patient outcomes.
Method
A prospective cross-sectional study was conducted on 175 patients undergoing hemodialysis in a tertiary care centre from south India. Data on sociodemographic factors (age, education level, and gender), clinical characteristics (dialysis vintage, comorbidities), and cognitive scores (ACE-III) were collected.
Statistical analyses were performed to evaluate correlations between cognitive scores and variables such as age, education, and dialysis vintage. Inclusion criteria focused on patients actively undergoing hemodialysis, excluding those with viral serology positivity, malignancy, or on peritoneal dialysis.
Results
Cognitive impairment was highly prevalent in the cohort, with 76.8% of patients scoring below the expected ACE-III threshold. Key findings include:
1. Age and cognitive scores:
Cognitive performance declined significantly with age. Patients aged ≤40 years had a mean ACE-III score of 91 ± 4, while those >60 years scored 62 ± 5 (P = 0.0003). A moderate negative correlation was observed between age and cognitive scores (r = −0.38, P = 0.002).
2. Education and cognitive reserve:
Higher education levels were strongly associated with better cognitive scores. Graduates scored 88 ± 3, whereas patients with a high school education averaged 65 ± 8 (P = 0.0004). A positive correlation (r = 0.52, P = 0.001) confirmed the effect of education on cognitive reserve.
3. Dialysis vintage:
Patients with shorter dialysis vintage (<24 months) demonstrated significantly higher scores (84 ± 6) compared to those with a vintage >72 months (61 ± 7, P = 0.001). A negative correlation (r = −0.26, P = 0.004) suggested that prolonged exposure to hemodialysis exacerbates cognitive decline.
4. Cognitive domain analysis:
Memory (mean score: 15 ± 3) was the most affected domain, while language (mean score: 22 ± 2) and fluency were comparatively preserved. Patients with longer dialysis vintage showed deficits in memory recall and logical reasoning.
Conclusion
The study reveals a high prevalence of cognitive impairment in hemodialysis patients, with age, education, and dialysis vintage emerging as significant determinants. These findings underscore the need for targeted interventions to address cognitive decline, such as Neurocognitive Rehabilitation, Optimized Dialysis Protocols, Lifestyle and Nutritional Support, Psychosocial Interventions. By integrating cognitive assessments like the ACE-III into routine hemodialysis care and implementing these interventions, healthcare providers can improve patient adherence, reduce hospitalization rates, and enhance the overall quality of life for chronic kidney disease patients.

title: #3747 Multi-stream data analysed by machine learning experiments confirmed factors influencing dialysis tolerability and patient recovery time: BP, pulse, dialysis vintage, age
authors: Mariusz Kusztal; Jakub Stojanowski; Olczyk Piotr; Joachim Beige; Krzysztof Letachowicz; Tomasz Gołębiowski
abstract:
Background and Aims
Aim of this study was to assess multi-stream data collected during dialysis session onpatient-related outcomes (PROs), especially dialysis tolerability and patient recovery time. Hemodialysis patient's lab results (electrolytes, hemoglobin, URR, Kt/V), real time dialysis machine-measured parameters, intradialytic weight gain, temperature, demographics were multi-stream variable analysed by machine learning experiments.
Method
Symptom Monitoring on Renal Replacement Therapy-Hemodialysis (SMaRRT-HD), a 14-item PRO app on Samsung tablets were used in recall period to assess symptom severity (eg cramps, dizziness, headache) in 60 patients during 400 HD sessions. Ten dialysis (Fresenius 5008) machine-generated data (TMP, AV line pressures, Qb, UF rate, BP, HR) stored on LAN server in academic dialysis centre.
Results
Lastly, we used a full set of 240 HD sessions from 58 chronic dialysis patients in multiple machine learning experiments. The sessions were split into training and test data sets, which let us build models that can predict how well the procedure will work. We paid particular attention to accurately representing treatment days before and after a longer weekend break.
Treatment tolerance: The RF classifier model classified patients based on the input parameters: systolic and mean blood pressure at the end of the procedure, as well as heart rate. It achieved an accuracy of 94.29%, precision of 0.95, sensitivity of 0.94, Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 0.89, and area under the curve (AUROC) of 0.95.
We used a regression model with a support vector machine (SVM) to determine how long a patient needs to rest after hemodialysis. It was based on the type of dialysis, the patient's age, their baseline MAP, and their pulse at the end. The model had a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.0515, a mean squared error (MSE) of 0.031, and a root of mean squared error (RMSE) of 0.176.

title: #379 Correlation of the Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index (GNRI) with other indicators of nutrition in chronic hemodialysis patients
authors: Georgios Kosmadakis; Aura Necoara; Nathalie Ramade; Fanny Fuentes; Clemence Deville; Julien Baudenon; Ioana Enache; Fatima El Kanouni
abstract:
Background and Aims
The GNRI (Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index1) is an index used in geriatrics to predict the risk of complications and mortality associated with malnutrition. It considers serum albumin levels and the ratio of current weight or BMI to the ideal theoretical weight/BMI. The aim of this study was to evaluate this index in a population of metabolically stable chronic hemodialysis patients aged >60 years and associate it with other nutritional markers.
Method
The studied patient cohort was divided in two groups based on their Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index (GNRI) scores: Gr 1 with GNRI score <97 and Gr 2 with GNRI ≥97. We registered the anthropometric, clinical and biological data of the study population.
Results
One hundred seventy-seven patients (102M-75F) undergoing chronic hemodialysis were included Table 1). There were no differences in age, muscle mass estimated by bioimpedance analysis, potassium levels, phosphorus levels, and nPCR between the groups. However, there were significant differences between the two groups concerning the primary disease. Gr 1 presented with a higher prevalence of diabetes and cardiovascular comorbidities. Additionally, Gr 1 presented with lower handgrip strength (Mean ± standard deviation in kg, 19.79 ± 9.37 vs 26.83 ± 11.63, P = 0.05), lower fat mass index estimated by bioimpedance analysis (Mean ± standard deviation in kg/m2, 7.31 ± 4.55 vs 15.24 ± 6.47, P < 0.001), and higher CRP levels (Mean ± standard deviation in mg/l, 22.27 ± 23.49 vs 8.13 ± 10.14, P < 0.001).
Conclusion
In conclusion, the GNRI, an easily calculated tool for nutritional assessment, is associated with important nutritional status parameters in chronic hemodialysis patients.

title: #2704 Investigating the impact of magnesium levels on Adragão score in hemodialysis patients
authors: Beatriz Cortez Ferreira; Gonçalo Canhão; Sofia Sá Guimarães Cerqueira; Nuno Oliveira; Ana Galvão; Rui Alves
abstract:
Background and Aims
The Adragão score is a widely used validated tool for assessing cardiovascular mortality risk in hemodialysis (HD) patients. In the general population, hypomagnesemia is strongly associated with increased mortality and cardiovascular events through mechanisms such as endothelial dysfunction, vascular calcification, and inflammation. However, the evidence regarding this relationship in HD patients remains very little, and no definitive magnesium cut-off values have been identified to predict poorer outcomes. This study aimed to evaluate whether a relationship exists between serum magnesium levels and the Adragão score in chronic HD patients while adjusting for other factors that may influence magnesium levels.
Method
This retrospective observational study included all patients from the regular hemodialysis program at ULS Coimbra on an outpatient basis between June 2023 and June 2024. Serum magnesium levels were measured and Adragão scores were calculated for each patient to assess their cardiovascular risk. Patients’ medications that could affect magnesium levels were also evaluated, particularly acetylsalicylic acid (ASA) and metamizole, which are known to increase magnesium levels, and proton pump inhibitors (PPIs), which may decrease magnesium levels. To evaluate the relationship between magnesium levels and the Adragão score, logistic regression analysis was performed, adjusting for the influence of these medications.
Results
A total of 49 patients (48.9% male) were included. The median Adragão score was 3 and the median magnesium levels were 2.3 mg/dL. 34.7% of patients were medicated with magnesium-increasing drugs (such as ASA and metamizole) and 57.1% with magnesium-decreasing drugs (such as PPIs). All patients had standard magnesium in the dialysate (1m Eq/L).
The logistic regression analysis revealed that patients with magnesium levels equal or greater than 2.6 mg/dL had a lower risk of presenting an Adragão score equal or greater than 3 (P = 0.032). The association between magnesium levels and the Adragão score remained significant even after adjusting for medications that could influence magnesium levels, such as ASA, metamizole, and PPIs.
Conclusion
In chronic HD patients, higher serum magnesium levels (≥2.6 mg/dL) were associated with a reduced risk of a higher Adragão score. This association remained robust after adjusting for medications that influence magnesium levels. This suggests that higher magnesium levels may be beneficial in reducing cardiovascular risk in HD patients. Although this is a small sample, and further research is needed to explore the therapeutic implications of magnesium in this population, these findings suggest that maintaining elevated magnesium levels (≥2.6 mg/dL) may provide cardiovascular benefits in HD patients. Additionally, this enhances the role of magnesium as a possible cardiovascular risk marker in this population, especially in settings with limited access to radiological imaging.

title: #3094 Benefit of central concentrate delivery system for healthcare workers in hemodialysis unit: a questionnaire survey
authors: Sua Lee; Seokjin Hwang; Soyoung Lee
abstract:
Background and Aims
The central concentrate delivery system (CCDS) is a hemodialysis system as centralizes the preparation of dialysate with concentrate solutions for multiple patients and distributes it to each hemodialysis machines. However, there was a lack of research conducted from the perspective of the healthcare workers. Therefore, this study revealed the benefit of CCDS for healthcare workers in hemodialysis unit.
Method
Among the dialysis hospitals currently using CCDS, questionnaires were sent to 60 dialysis facilities whose address and contact address were confirmed.
Results
Responses from 35 institutions were received and analyzed. Of the institutions that responded, 21 (60%) were primary healthcare facilities, 4 (11%) were secondary healthcare facilities, and 7 (20%) were tertiary institutions. The average usage period of CCDS across all facilities was 8.1 ± 4.2 years. The most common reasons for introducing CCDS were for reducing healthcare workers’ work loading and creating a comfortable environment. Economic feasibility was second reason for introducing CCDS. In terms of healthcare workers’ workload after the implementation of CCDS, none of the respondents reported that the workload had deteriorated. 65% of respondents reported that their workload had improved, and 12% reported a substantial decrease. This indicated that overall, the workload has significantly reduced. When asked if they had ever had an infection-related problem in dialysis system, 2 of the 35 institutions surveyed reported, had an infection problem while using CCDS, and the remaining institutions reported no infection problem.
Conclusion
The CCDS can be helpful for labor-saving and environmentally friendly in hemodialysis units without increasing infection-related problem. Further study is needed to determine the effect and safety of CCDS.

title: #3209 Inflammatory profile of incident hemadialysis patients: role of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors
authors: Tania Monzón Vázquez; Ana Yurena Sánchez Santana; Ernesto Francisco Valga Amado; Patricia Perez
abstract:
Background and Aims
Incident patients on chronic hemodialysis have a high prevalence of inflammation. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) drugs have shown a protective effect on cardiovascular risk, and it is postulated that they may also have a role against inflammation. Therefore, their use in incident patients on hemodialysis is increasing.
Method
A retrospective cohort study was conducted, assessing incident hemodialysis patients in the northern area of Gran Canaria January to December 2024. Patients with DM1 were excluded.
The immunity-inflammation systemic index (SII), neutrophil-lymphocyte (NLR), platelet-lymphocyte (PLR) and C-reactive protein (CRP) baseline data and treatment were obtained.
The inflammatory ratios were analyzed in 4 groups according to the presence or absence of type 2 diabetes mellitus and treatment with SGLT2i.
Results
62 patients were included. The average age was 70.5 ± 14.86 years. 24.2% were women. The median SII was 760.53 (q25–q75: 473.82–1245.58).
A statistically significant decrease in SII was observed in the group of diabetic patients who had SGLT2i treatment compared to diabetics without that treatment (Kruskal-Wallis, P = 0.012). In addition, although not reaching statistical significance, SII was lower in diabetic patients with SGLT2i compared to non-diabetics treated with these drugs (Table 1).
Conclusion
In our sample, type 2 diabetic mellitus patients treated with SGLT2i had lower SII values ​​than patients without treatment with SGLT2i.

title: #770 Real-world practice of palliative care for advanced cancer in patients on maintenance hemodialysis
authors: Nanami Kida; Toshitaka Morishima; Hirota Kida; Yoshiharu Tsubakihara; Isao Miyashiro
abstract:
Background and Aims
The management of medications in hemodialysis (HD) patients with cancer requires meticulous evaluation of the metabolic pathways. Consequently, in practice of palliative care for advanced cancer, HD patients may have difficulty in controlling renal metabolic drugs, leading to suboptimal pain control. Nonetheless, the specific status of palliative care for advanced cancer in HD patients have been documented only through limited case reports and remain insufficiently elucidated. The aim of this study is to elucidate real-world palliative care strategies for advanced cancer in HD patients by comparing with those implemented in non-HD patients.
Method
In our study, patients diagnosed with stage III or IV cancer were identified from the cancer registry data collected from 69 hospitals in Osaka Prefecture, Japan, between January 2019 and December 2021. To obtain more detailed information on treatment and pharmaceutical intervention, we integrated these data with Japan's Diagnosis Procedure Combination (DPC) data, resulting in the creation of a consolidated dataset. From this dataset, information on maintenance HD, the practice of palliative care, and the use of opioid analgesics—such as morphine sulfate, morphine hydrochloride, hydromorphone, oxycodone, fentanyl, and tramadol hydrochloride—was extracted. The patient characteristics, cancer types, the practice of palliative care, and the use of opioid analgesics were analyzed and compared between patients on maintenance HD and the non-HD.
Results
Among 57,917 patients diagnosed with stage Ⅲ or Ⅳ cancer, 377 patients (0.7%) were identified as receiving maintenance HD. The median age was 73 years (interquartile range: 68–79) for HD patients and 73 years (66–80) for non-HD patients, with no significant difference (P = 0.411). A higher proportion of HD patients were male compared to non-HD patients (78.8% vs. 61.2%, P < 0.001). There was no significant difference of cancer type between the two groups. HD patients had a higher prevalence of the practice of palliative care compared to non-HD patients (14,3% vs 10.4, P = 0.020). There was no significant difference in use of opioid analgesics (76.1% vs 72.7%, P = 0.462). However, regarding the opioid types, HD patients had a higher prevalence of fentanyl (65.3% vs 59.1%, P = 0.024) and tramadol hydrochloride (23.6% vs 14.2%, P < 0.001) use, and a lower prevalence of morphine hydrochloride (4.2% vs 8.2%, P = 0.004) and hydromorphone (1.9% vs 3.9%, P = 0.043) use compared to non-HD patients. There was no significant difference in use of morphine sulfate (0% vs 0.9%, P = 0.054) and oxycodone (13.3% vs 14.0%, P = 0.766).
Conclusion
In cancer patients with stage Ⅲ or Ⅳ, HD patients received a greater implementation of palliative care practices compared to non-HD patients. Although the use of opioid was comparable, the selection of drug types differed. Our findings indicate that HD patients received comprehensive palliative care through the use of pharmacological drugs targeting non-renal metabolic pathways.

title: #815 “Is assisted peritoneal dialysis a valid alternative in dependent patients undergoing renal replacement therapy techniques?”
authors: Edduin Miguel Martín Izquierdo; Alejandro Alonso Bethencourt; Samuel Abrante; Orlando Siverio Morales; Manuel Luis MacÍa Heras
abstract:
Background and Aims
Assisted peritoneal dialysis (APD) is a home dialysis treatment option for patients with terminal CKD and dependent patients. Its use has been widespread worldwide for more than four decades, allowing fully or partially dependent patients to perform home therapy with the objective of delaying or replacing other renal replacement therapy (RRT) alternatives.
The objective of our study is to describe the profile of APD patients in our center.
Method
Retrospective, observational, descriptive study that analyzed patients in APD in our center during the last 5 years.
Demographic characteristics, causes of CKD, time on PD, characteristics of the caregivers, occurrence of complications as well as average time on the technique were analyzed.
Results
34 patients were analyzed in APD, of which 20 were men, with a mean age of 73 years. Diabetic nephropathy was the most common cause of CKD. 67.4% were on automated PD and the rest on continuous outpatient PD, with a mean time spent on the technique of 16 months. The most frequent cause of dependence was cognitive and mobility deficit. At the beginning of follow-up, the average Charlson Index was 9 points. The main caregivers were children (43%), spouse (37%) and others (20%).
The most frequent causes of abandonment of the technique were death and transfer to hemodialysis. The rate of peritonitis during the study period was analyzed, being 0.15 patient-year, similar to the rest of the patients in our unit.
Conclusion
We consider that APD is a PD modality that must be adapted to the needs and demands of patients and their caregivers, being a feasible option although generally underused.
According to our results, the evolution and complications are similar to the rest of the patients in our program, although an optimal model of training, education and quality monitoring of these patients would be necessary.

title: #1049 50 years demographic change in the Okinawa dialysis study (OKIDS) registry (1971–2020)
authors: Kunitoshi Iseki
abstract:
Background and Aims
Dialysis therapy has been saving lives in patients with end-stage renal disease. In Okinawa, Japan, the first hemodialysis (HD) clinic was opened in June 1971. We previously reported the 30-year demographics of the Okinawa dialysis study (OKIDS) registry (1971–2000; Kidney Int 61;668–675, 2002). However, recent trends from 2001 to 2020 were not examined. The registry filed all resident dialysis patients who survived at least one month of scheduled HD, peritoneal dialysis (PD), and renal transplantation. Completeness of follow-up is expected due to the isolated islands and cooperation with all dialysis facilities. The aims were to describe the trends of incidence and mortality rate of dialysis patients. We examined the standardized incidence ratio (SIR) and standardized mortality ratio (SMR).
Method
All chronic dialysis patients both HD and PD who were residents of Okinawa were registered. By reviewing medical records both paper and electric, we excluded those who were suspected of acute kidney injury treated by HD, died within one month after starting HD, and non-residents of Okinawa. Dialysis facilities increased from 51 in 2000 to 84 by the end of 2020. The population has increased from 1.32 (2000) to 1.46 (2020) million. Primary renal disease was grouped into six categories as chronic glomerulonephritis (CGN), diabetes mellitus (DM), nephrosclerosis (NScl), polycystic kidney disease (PKD), systemic lupus nephritis (SLE), and others. Causes of death were classified as infection, withdrawal (cancer, cachexia, stopping dialysis), cardiac, sudden death, cerebrovascular disease, and others. Outcomes were determined by January 1, 2021, as alive on dialysis, died, and received renal transplantation. We recorded the last dialysis dates in those who moved outside Okinawa and lost follow-up before the end of 2020. SIR was calculated concerning the incidence of 2020 and SMR to the population in Okinawa each year. The hazard ratio (95% confidence interval) of death was calculated after adjusting for sex, age at the start of dialysis, and diabetes mellitus in every 5-decade (reference: start year of dialysis 1971 to 1980).
Results
A total of 15,928 patients were examined. We excluded those with insufficient data (n = 8), those with less than 18 years (n = 93), and those who followed less than 1 month after starting dialysis (n = 124). Outcomes such as death, alive on dialysis on January 1, 2021, and receiving renal transplantation were determined in 15,703 patients. The numbers of death, alive on January 1, 2021, and renal transplantation were 9,747 (62.1%), 4,733 (30.1%), and 633 (4.0%), respectively. There were 147 (0.9%) patients moved outside Okinawa and 443 (2.8%) lost follow-up. Compared to 2020, for both men and women, the standardized incidence ratios (SIR) have not increased since 2000. Hazard risk (HR) and 95% confidence interval (CI) of death were calculated after adjusting for sex, age at the start of dialysis, year of start of dialysis, and diabetes mellitus. The prognosis was significantly improved when compared to that of 1971–1980 as the adjusted HR (95% CI) was 0.79 (0.71–0.89) in 1981–1990, 0.63 (0.56–0.71) in 1991–2000, 0.53 (0.47–0.59) in 2001–2010, and 0.43 (0.38–0.49) in 2011–2020, respectively. Compared to the general population in Okinawa, SMR in both men and women decreased steadily since 2000. The SMR in 2000 (2020) was 4.49 (2.83) in men and 6.68 (3.75) in women, respectively.
Conclusion
SIR is decreasing and SMR has improved significantly. However, SMR is still high as ≥2.0.

Dialysis facilities increased from 51 in 2000 to 84 by the end of 2020. The population has increased from 1.32 (2000) to 1.46 (2020) million. Primary renal disease was grouped into six categories as chronic glomerulonephritis (CGN), diabetes mellitus (DM), nephrosclerosis (NScl), polycystic kidney disease (PKD), systemic lupus nephritis (SLE), and others. Causes of death were classified as infection, withdrawal (cancer, cachexia, stopping dialysis), cardiac, sudden death, cerebrovascular disease, and others. Outcomes were determined by January 1, 2021, as alive on dialysis, died, and received renal transplantation. Conclusion
SIR is decreasing and SMR has improved significantly. However, SMR is still high as ≥2.0.

title: #1073 Itching in dialysis rooms: multicenter survey on medical staff and patients
authors: Stefano Possenti; Federico Alberici; Bernardo Lucca; Federica Mescia; Rocco Gargiulo; Alice Guerini
abstract:
Background and Aims
Itching is one of the most common symptoms in uremic patients. Uremic pruritus associated with uremia (CKD-AP) is particularly relevant in patients with chronic kidney disease undergoing renal replacement therapy through hemodialysis. Recent data (DOPPS, phases 4–6, 2009–2018) show a prevalence of CKD-AP around 70%, with 37% of patients describing itching as a moderate to extreme intensity disorder (1). The presence of itching is associated with an increased risk of infections and reduced therapeutic compliance, leading to higher hospitalization rates and mortality (1). Moreover, it has a significant psychological impact, reducing sleep quality, deteriorating overall quality of life in personal, relational, social, and work aspects, and fostering the onset of depressive states (4). Despite these facts, CKD-AP remains an underdiagnosed problem and is rarely addressed with standardized and shared diagnostic/therapeutic criteria.
Method
We conducted a survey in 5 centers in Northern Italy regarding itching in hemodialysis, involving both medical staff and patients. The survey consists of 3 questions for the medical staff and 3 for the patients (Fig. 1). The identification of the itching symptom among patients was done using the Q-20KDQOL-SFTM1.3 questionnaire with a scale from 1 to 5. Medical staff were asked to answer their questions before conducting the survey on all patients undergoing chronic hemodialysis at their center.
Results
The survey involved 29 doctors directly engaged in hemodialysis activities and 803 chronic hemodialysis patients. The estimated prevalence of itching among patients, as perceived by the doctors, was as follows: 17/29 between 0 and 10%, 6/29 between 11% and 20%, 4/29 between 21% and 30%, 0/29 between 31% and 40%, and 2/29 over 40%. 79% of the doctors did not have a protocol for managing itching (available in only one center). 27/29 doctors (97%) manage the problem independently, and 2 doctors (3%) refer to another specialist (dermatologist) (Fig. 2). Among the patients, the itching reported was as follows: 500/803 (62%) level 1, 178/803 (22%) level 2, 66/803 (8%) level 3, 29/803 (4%) level 4, 30/803 (4%) level 5. In total, 125/803 (16%) had significant itching (≥3); of these, 3/125 (2%) reported the symptom once a month, 20/125 (16%) once a week, 54/125 (43%) almost every day, 33/125 (26%) every day, and 15/125 (12%) multiple times a day. 87/125 patients (70%) did not report a correlation between itching and dialysis; 14/125 (11%) felt improvement after dialysis, and 24/125 (19%) felt worsening (Fig. 3).
Conclusion
The survey shows significant variability among doctors in identifying itching and the absence of specific multidisciplinary protocols to address it. Among patients, a significant itching prevalence of 16.5% is found, with 38.4% of cases occurring almost daily. No correlation with dialysis seems to be evident.

title: #1420 Assessment of hydration status according to the percentage of relative overhydration (AVROH) due to electrical bioimpedance in patients of the CEDIMAT hemodialysis unit, period January–July 2024, Dominican Republic
authors: Melissa Reyes Veras
abstract:
Background and Aims
Determination of dry weight in hemodialysis is essential for effective dialysis. Hydration status is assessed using clinical indicators such as weight gain, hypertension, and hypotension, but overhydration may remain undetected until 4–5 liters of fluid accumulate, increasing morbidity and mortality. Electrical bioimpedance is a non-invasive, economical method to assess body composition and hydration status, detect overhydration or dehydration early, reduce antihypertensive medication use, preserve residual kidney function, lower cardiovascular risk, and improve quality of life.
This study aims to analyze and compare the hydration status of hemodialysis patients using electrical bioimpedance, focusing on relative overhydration (AvROH = OHpre/ECW × 100). Values greater than 15% are associated with increased morbidity and mortality. The goal is to support its routine use in clinical practice to optimize water balance management, reduce risks linked to overhydration, and establish a foundation for future research at our center and other hemodialysis units nationwide.
Method
An observational, descriptive, retrospective, cross-sectional study was conducted with 85 patients from the CEDIMAT hemodialysis unit (January–July 2024). Sociodemographic variables (age, gender), body composition (BCM from Fresenius), and clinical parameters (blood pressure, hemoglobin, albumin, serum sodium) were analyzed.
Results
Of the population, 72.94% (n = 62) had AvROH ≥15% (overhydrated group) and 27.06% (n = 23) had AvROH <15% (normohydrated group). Both groups were predominantly male (71% and 69.57%, respectively), with a mean age of 63 years in the overhydrated group versus 68 years in the normohydrated group. No significant differences were observed in hemoglobin or serum sodium levels. However, serum albumin was lower in the overhydrated group (3.9 g/dL vs. 4.4 g/dL). Lean tissue index (LTI) and fat tissue index (FTI) were also lower (12.0 vs. 12.4 kg/m² and 11.0 vs. 13.7 kg/m², respectively). Blood pressure levels were higher in the overhydrated group (163/84 mmHg vs. 155/81 mmHg).
Conclusion
The study found a high prevalence of relative overhydration (72.94%) in the hemodialysis population, underscoring the need for effective hydration monitoring. Overhydrated patients were younger, with lower serum albumin, LTI, and FTI levels, linking overhydration to poor nutrition. Higher blood pressure in this group suggests a connection to hypertension.
These findings emphasize regular bioimpedance monitoring in hemodialysis. The study supports future research and interventions to reduce morbidity and mortality, including hydration protocols, nutritional evaluations, hypertension management, and strategies to boost lean mass. Training healthcare professionals is crucial to improve overhydration management and patient outcomes.

title: #1594 Demographic and clinical profile of dialysis patients in Brazil DaVita Kidney Care: a comparative analysis with global trends in chronic kidney disease epidemiology
authors: Bruno Zawadzki; Rogerio Da Hora; Fernanda Coelho; Marcelo Lopes; Danilo Cunha; Bruno Vieira; Eric Correa; Fabio Reis; Priscila Sampaio; Ana Vieira; Cristina Pinto
abstract:
Background and Aims
Chronic kidney disease (CKD) affects approximately 850 million people worldwide, with dialysis being a critical life-sustaining therapy. Understanding patient demographics is essential for optimizing care strategies. DaVita Kidney Care (DKC Brazil) delivers comprehensive renal care, and analyzing its patient data provides valuable epidemiological insights. Offering a broader perspective on national and global trends in kidney health, this study compares the demographic and clinical characteristics of patients from DKC Brazil's December 2024 BI database with data from the Brazilian Dialysis Census (SBN 2023), the ISN Global Kidney Health Atlas (2023), and the Lancet 2024 review.
Methods
We used data from DKC Brazil's Power BI database (December 2024) and compared it with the Brazilian Dialysis Census (SBN 2023) and international benchmarks to gain insights into local and global trends in kidney care. We included the following variables in the analysis: age, gender, dialysis modality (HD, HDF, PD), regional disparities in access to care, and time on dialysis. Descriptive statistics and percentage comparisons were used to assess variations in epidemiological patterns and identify key trends.
Results
Conclusion
The demographic and clinical profile of DKC Brazil's dialysis patients (Dec 2024 data) aligns closely with national patterns (SBN Census 2023) but shows distinct differences from global benchmarks (ISN Atlas 2023 & Lancet 2024). Key takeaways:
Age and gender distributions are consistent with national and global trends. HDF remains underutilized in Brazil, highlighting the need for increased adoption. Significant regional disparities persist, requiring policy interventions for equitable dialysis access. Brazil retains a high proportion of chronic dialysis patients, unlike low-income countries with high dropout rates. These findings highlight the need to expand HDF implementation, enhance regional access to care, and conduct further research on long-term dialysis outcomes in Brazil.

title: #1626 Association of serum selenium and zinc levels with anemia parameters and ESA response in different dialysis modalities
authors: Ayşe Şeker; Can Huzmeli
abstract:
Background and Aims
Chronic kidney disease (CKD) affects approximately 10% of adults worldwide, with trace element imbalances being common complications. These elements play crucial roles in oxidative stress and anti-inflammatory processes, with their deficiencies potentially contributing to malnutrition.
Anemia represents one of the most common and prognostically significant complications in CKD. While erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESAs) have revolutionized renal anemia treatment, reduced ESA response remains a significant challenge associated with increased mortality in end-stage renal disease patients.
This study aimed to evaluate selenium and zinc levels in pre-dialysis, hemodialysis (HD), and peritoneal dialysis (PD) patients and investigate their relationship with anemia parameters and erythropoiesis-stimulating agent (ESA) response.
Method
A cross-sectional study was conducted with 298 patients (98 hemodialysis, 92 peritoneal dialysis, and 108 pre-dialysis). Patients in the pre-dialysis group consisted of patients with stage 3 and 4 CKD. Demographic data, laboratory parameters including selenium, zinc, hemoglobin, and erythropoietin resistance index (ERI) were analyzed.
Continuous variables were analyzed using Mann-Whitney U test or independent samples t-test based on normality distribution. Correlations were assessed using Spearman's correlation coefficient.
Results
Analysis of trace element levels revealed distinct patterns across treatment modalities. Selenium concentrations demonstrated significant variation between groups, with peritoneal dialysis patients showing markedly lower levels (52.05 μg/L) compared to both hemodialysis (58.97 μg/L) and pre-dialysis patients (59.50 μg/L) (P < 0.001). In contrast, zinc levels were found to be highest in hemodialysis patients (0.83 mg/L), showing significant elevation compared to both peritoneal dialysis (0.76 mg/L) and pre-dialysis (0.78 mg/L) groups (P = 0.005). Laboratory analysis of nutritional and inflammatory markers showed that pre-dialysis patients maintained significantly higher albumin levels compared to both dialysis groups, while CRP levels were notably elevated in hemodialysis patients.
Correlation analysis revealed significant relationships between trace elements and various clinical parameters. Selenium demonstrated a moderate positive correlation with albumin (r = 0.408, P < 0.001), suggesting its potential role in nutritional status. Additionally, selenium levels showed positive associations with hemoglobin (r = 0.189, P = 0.001) and negative correlations with ESA response index (r = −0.159, P = 0.034), indicating its possible involvement in erythropoiesis regulation. Zinc levels exhibited similar patterns, showing positive correlations with albumin (r = 0.231, P < 0.001) and dialysis adequacy as measured by Kt/V (r = 0.206, P = 0.004). Both trace elements demonstrated inverse relationships with inflammatory markers, particularly CRP (selenium: r = −0.165, P = 0.005; zinc: r = −0.163, P = 0.005).
Conclusion
Our findings suggest that selenium and zinc levels vary significantly across different dialysis modalities. Selenium levels showed significant correlations with anemia parameters and ESA response, suggesting a potential role in erythropoiesis. The strongest correlation between selenium and albumin levels indicates that nutritional status may be an important factor in maintaining adequate trace element levels.
The variations in trace element levels across different treatment modalities highlight the need for personalized approaches to supplementation strategies. Our comprehensive comparison across pre-dialysis, hemodialysis, and peritoneal dialysis patients provides unique insights into how different renal replacement therapies might influence trace element status.

title: #2191 Turbulent topography: managing individuals with renal disease during the conflict of genocidal proportions against Gaza, Palestine
authors: Jomana Ghaith; Israar Ulhaq; Junaid Sultan; Huda Mahmoud
abstract:
Prior to the conflict of genocidal proportions, there were approximately 1000 to 1500 Gazans with end-stage-renal-failure (ESRF) requiring hospital haemodialysis across multiple dialysis units. As a consequence of the military aggressions against healthcare establishments, the siege on humanitarian and medical aid, these individuals have been disproportionately, negatively impacted.
Due to the destruction of many renal healthcare services, 593 Gazans requiring hospital haemodialysis utilise 24 dialysis machines at Al-Aqsa hospital dialysis unit in southern Gaza. Due to the rationing of renal-replacement-therapy (RRT), dialysis sessions’ length and frequency have been significantly reduced. Often, individuals are disconnected early to accommodate more critically ill patients, admitted with pulmonary oedema or hyperkalaemia.
Furthermore, the creation and management of definitive access has been significantly hindered due to the damaged healthcare infrastructures and those requiring RRT commencement or suffer fistula failure are initiated on RRT via semi-permanent lines. Unsurprisingly, there has been an increase in the incidence of line-related infections and central stenosis. Additionally, fistulas are at an added risk of dehydration-related thrombosis and traumatic injury.
Majed Abu Maaheel was one such individual, he was Palestine's first Olympian, a coach, a runner and a father of five. He died aged 61, because he was unable to access dialysis due to disrupted power supplies secondary to the siege. An unnecessary and preventable death. Similarly, other displaced individuals on ESRF, living in tents, were unable to access dialysis and without the necessary anticipatory medications suffered significantly in the last weeks, days and hours of life secondary to severe uraemic symptoms.
The aggressions on healthcare services and restrictions on medications have led to a colossal breakdown in primary-care services and a rise in individuals attending the emergency department with newly diagnosed end-stage-renal-failure due to undiagnosed and/or untreated hypertension and diabetes. Hypertensive emergencies presenting with systolic blood pressure readings greater than 220 mmHg leading to pulmonary oedema and cerebral haemorrhage are multiple times a week occurrence. Life-threatening and life-taking hyperkalaemia is an alternate-day happening.
Managing the significant escalation in critically ill patients is further challenged by the lack of necessary medical paraphernalia to deliver basic, not even standard or good care. On a daily occurrence there is no access to ECG leads or paper, portable chest X-rays or standard bloods: albumin, troponin, ketones. No access to calcium gluconate or potassium binders.
Irrespective of the conflict, the most vulnerable in society must be protected. Healthcare services, personnel and service users must be protected as part of preserving international humanitarian law and man-made healthcare catastrophes of this nature must not be permitted to happen again.
The forward solution is for Gazan renal patients is unimpeded medical missions, humanitarian and medical aid to help restore healthcare services and facilities, with a view to restoring dialysis units, interventional radiology and transplant services.

title: #2494 Peritoneal dialysis in patients with cardiorenal syndrome: a systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis
authors: Maria Gabriela Guimaraes; Luiz Carlos Passos; Pandora Fonseca; Fernanda Tapioca; Alleh Nogueira; Nicole Felix; Thiago Reis; Paulo Novis Rocha
abstract:
Background and Aims
Peritoneal dialysis (PD) may be a gentler option for dialysis in patients with cardiorenal syndrome (CRS). We aimed to evaluate overall mortality and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) in patients with CRS undergoing PD.
Methods
We searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library for studies evaluating PD in patients with CRS with >3 months follow-up. We applied a random-effects model to overall proportion ratios (OPRs) for binary outcomes and mean differences (MDs) for continuous outcomes, with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Statistical analyses were performed using R software (v 4.3.1).
Results
We included 29 observational studies comprising 1940 patients. The follow-up period ranged from 5 months to 6.5 years. The OPR for mortality was 56.2 (95% CI 46.4–65.6 events, I2 = 89.1%; Fig. 1A). Among individuals with end-stage kidney disease (ESKD), the OPR was 57.2 (95% CI 37.0–75.2, I2 = 95.3%) compared to 55.8 (95% CI 44.7–66.4, I2 = 80.1%) in those without ESKD, showing no significant difference between these subgroups (P = 0.90). We found a mean improvement in LVEF of 3.67% post-PD (CI 0.80–6.53, P = 0.01, Fig. 1B).
Conclusion
In this meta-analysis of longitudinal cohort studies investigating patients with CRS undergoing PD, all-cause mortality was high but PD was associated with a modest yet unexpected improvement in LVEF.

We included 29 observational studies comprising 1940 patients. The follow-up period ranged from 5 months to 6.5 years. The OPR for mortality was 56.2 (95% CI 46.4–65.6 events, I2 = 89.1%; Fig. 1A). In this meta-analysis of longitudinal cohort studies investigating patients with CRS undergoing PD, all-cause mortality was high but PD was associated with a modest yet unexpected improvement in LVEF.

title: #2650 Changes in serum bisphenol S (BPS) concentrations in dialysis patients: impact of switching from hemodialysis (HD) to on-line hemodiafiltration (OHDF) and changing the dialysis membrane from polyethersulfone (PES) to polysulfone (PS)
authors: Kazuko Arita; Emi Kihara; Takehiro Tanabe; Hiroaki Oda
abstract:
Background and Aims
BPS, utilized as a substitute for bisphenol A in the manufacture of dialyzers, is classified as an endocrine disruptor; however, its effects on dialysis patients remain unclear. The aim of this study is to investigate the changes in serum BPS concentrations in patients undergoing HD when switching from HD to OHDF, and when changing the dialysis membrane from PES, which contains BPS, to PS, which is free from BPS.
Method
This study involved 24 outpatients undergoing HD with PES membranes for their dialyzers (20 males and 4 females; 11 patients with diabetes and 13 without; average age 63 ± 12 years; average duration of HD 78 ± 74 months). All participants underwent a transition from conventional HD to pre-dilution OHDF using 40 liters of replacement dialysate. Among them, 12 patients (10 males and 2 females; 7 with diabetes and 5 without; average age 62 ± 12 years; average duration of HD 78 ± 59 months) continued using PES membranes during OHDF. In contrast, the remaining 12 patients (10 males and 2 females; 4 with diabetes and 8 without; average age 63 ± 13 years; average duration of HD 80 ± 80 months) had their dialysis membrane changed from PES to PS concurrently with the change in dialysis method. The alterations in serum concentrations of BPS, total protein (TP), albumin (Alb), total cholesterol (TC), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), triglycerides (TG), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), alkaline phosphatase (ALP), the removal rates of β2-microglobulin and α1-microglobulin, blood glucose, red blood cell (RBC) count, hemoglobin and white blood cell (WBC) count before and after the changes in dialysis method and membrane were compared. Statistical significance was assessed using the paired t-test, with P < 0.05 considered significant.
Results
The serum BPS concentration and the removal rate of α1-microglobulin did not exhibit significant changes in patients who continued to use PES membrane dialyzers after transitioning from HD to OHDF. Conversely, in patients who switched from PES membrane dialyzers to PS membrane dialyzers while changing the dialysis method from HD to OHDF, serum concentrations of BPS and TG significantly decreased, while the removal rate of α1-microglobulin and the serum HDL-C concentration were significantly elevated. Furthermore, the removal rate of β2-microglobulin showed significant improvement in all patients following the transition from conventional HD to OHDF (Table 1).
Conclusion
Pre-dilution OHDF using 40 liters of replacement dialysate demonstrated high efficacy in the removal of medium-middle molecular weight substances, while its ability to eliminate small molecular weight substances is comparable to that of conventional HD. Consequently, even after changing the dialysis method from HD to OHDF while continuing to use PES membranes, the serum concentration of BPS in dialysis patients did not decrease. Given the small molecular weight of BPS (MW 250.27), there is no advantage in removing BPS by switching from HD to OHDF. However, OHDF significantly removed medium-middle molecular weight substances, such as β2-microglobulin (MW 11,800), compared to HD. In patients who continued to use PES membranes after transitioning from HD to OHDF, the removal rate of α1-microglobulin (MW 33,000) did not improve due to the relatively small pore size of the selected PES membranes, which was designed to prevent albumin leakage, thereby resulting in lower permeability for large to middle-sized molecules. Additionally, the lipid profile of dialysis patients improved when switching from conventional HD using PES membrane dialyzers to OHDF with PS membranes. By changing the dialysis membrane from PES, which contains BPS, to PS membranes that do not contain BPS, a significant reduction in serum BPS concentrations was observed in dialysis patients, thus protecting them from exposure to endocrine-disrupting substances. Further investigations to delineate the precise role of BPS-free dialyzers in the treatment of patients undergoing dialysis are warranted.

title: #2856 Quality management in dialysis: dialysate flow optimization and resource use in DaVita Brazil Kidney Care
authors: Bruno Zawadzki; Ana Vieira; Cristina Pinto; Danilo Cunha; Eric Correa; Fabio Reis; Fernanda Coelho; Marcelo Lopes; Priscila Sampaio; Rogerio Da Hora; Fernando Cunha; Paulo Oliveira
abstract:
Background and Aims
Hemodialysis relies heavily on water and energy resources, making sustainability a critical consideration. As global concerns about environmental impact grow, strategies to minimize resource use while maintaining clinical outcomes are essential. Standardized protocols that combine sustainability and clinical effectiveness are key to advancing quality management in dialysis. While a dialysate flow of 500 mL/min has been the standard for decades, modern dialyzers suggest higher flows offer limited benefits. Adapted Flow technology adjusts dialysate flow proportionally to blood flow, aiming to optimize resource use without compromising dialysis efficiency. This study evaluates whether implementing an Adapted Flow protocol influenced dialysis adequacy, measured by Kt/V, and water consumption in Brazil.
Methods
A retrospective analysis was conducted in dialysis clinics operated by a single organization across all regions of Brazil. Clinics were included if they exclusively used machines with Adapted Flow and had been part of the network for at least 90 days by October 2023. The protocol, disseminated in July 2024 and fully implemented by September 2024, emphasizes maintaining a Kt/V target of ≥1.3 while reducing resource consumption. It standardizes Adapted Flow with a fixed 1.2× ratio to optimize dialysate delivery and outlines steps to improve Kt/V when below target, including adjustments to blood flow, session duration, dialyzer selection, and vascular access assessment. If these measures are insufficient, a multidisciplinary review is recommended rather than increasing dialysate flow. Kt/V data were collected for Q4 2023 (pre-implementation) and Q4 2024 (post-implementation). Weighted and simple averages, medians, and ranges of Kt/V were calculated, and the Wilcoxon signed-rank test was applied to assess differences. Water consumption data, when available, were compared between quarters using descriptive statistics and percentage changes. Analyses were performed using Python (version 3.9).
Results
Fifty-two dialysis clinics met the inclusion criteria, distributed across Brazil's five regions: 4 in the north, 6 in the northeast, 7 in the central-west, 28 in the southeast, and 7 in the south. Among 28 clinics with available data, water consumption decreased from 97,041 m³ in Q4 2023 to 82,458 m³ in Q4 2024, reflecting an 11% reduction and saving 14,583 m³ of water. During the same periods, dialysis sessions increased from 250,485 in 2023 to 255,960 in 2024. The total Kt/V values analyzed were 22,322 in 2023 and 22,679 in 2024. The weighted mean Kt/V was 1.79 in Q4 2023 and 1.77 in Q4 2024. Median Kt/V values were 1.63 and 1.66, respectively. No statistically significant differences were observed in Kt/V between the periods (P = 0.354).
Conclusions
The observed reduction in water consumption, despite an increase in dialysis sessions, supports the successful implementation of the Adapted Flow protocol across multiple clinics. Dialysis adequacy, as measured by Kt/V, remained stable, suggesting resource optimization can be pursued without compromising patient care. These findings highlight the potential for dialysis services to align clinical outcomes with environmental sustainability, emphasizing the value of standardized protocols in advancing quality management and ecological responsibility. Further studies are needed to explore long-term impacts on clinical and sustainability outcomes.

title: #3225 Integrating telemedicine into peritoneal dialysis: a holistic model for palliative care in advanced CKD
authors: Paolo Luca Maria Lentini; Giorgio Laudadio; Brenda Menegazzo; Claudia Benedetti; Valeria Fuso; Ilenia Filippi; Daniela Cremasco; Sofia Andrighetto; Federica Vienna; Graziella Berlingò; Antonino Previti
abstract:
Background and Aims
Patients with advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD) and a limited life expectancy face significant challenges in accessing high-quality care. Peritoneal dialysis (PD) as a palliative therapy has demonstrated potential to improve symptom management. This study highlights the role of telemedicine in enhancing automated peritoneal dialysis (APD) care, enabling remote monitoring, and optimizing healthcare resources
Method
A retrospective analysis was conducted on 6 patients with advanced CKD and an estimated life expectancy of more than 6 months, enrolled in a telemedicine-integrated APD program. All patients underwent APD supported by telemonitoring and teledialysis systems, which provided real-time tracking of dialysis performance and patient status. Key metrics analyzed included hospital admissions, number of healthcare services provided, Charlson Comorbidity Index, and Rein score. Teledialysis (TD) was performed using a combination of two integrated systems:
Daily monitoring of PD sessions was conducted through Sharesource© (Vantive SRL), while clinical evaluations and training were performed using the eVISUS System® (T4MED, Italy)
Results
The integration of telemedicine significantly improved clinical outcomes and resource efficiency. The average age of patients was 81.2 years, with a mean Charlson Comorbidity Index of 16.5 and a mean Rein Score of 9. Hospital admissions were minimized to an average of 1.8 per patient, while the average number of healthcare services provided was 5.8 per patient. Patients and caregivers expressed satisfaction with the ease of access to healthcare professionals and the reduction in logistical burdens. [Table 1 and Fig. 1]
Conclusion
Telemedicine enhances the delivery of automated peritoneal dialysis for palliative care, offering an innovative approach to managing complex patients with advanced CKD. By reducing hospitalizations and optimizing service delivery, telemedicine represents a cost-effective and resource-efficient model for palliative nephrology care.

title: #3227 National home hemodialysis (HHD) survey about organization of care and medical practices in France
authors: Maxence Ficheux; David Attaf; Hafedh Fessi
abstract:
Background and Aims
There is a renewed interest in HHD with mainly short daily session schedules and rarely long nocturnal sessions (LNHD). Data on medical practices and care organization of HHD programs are scarce. Benabed A et al. [Néphrologie&Thérapeutique 2017;13:18–25] described patients, practice and outcomes in low flow dialysate HD. KIHDNEY cohort study described practices at European level. In 2024, we decided to conduct a national survey to describe HDD practices and care organization: this is the objective of our “home survey” about organization of care and medical practices in HHD.
Method
Questionnaire sent in April 2024 to french nephrologists of all dialysis centers without selection via a secure e-platform. The questionnaire covers (1) characteristics of nephrologists and centers, (2) reasons for not offering or offering HHD, (3) patient profiles, (4) recruitment and training program and (5) organization of centers. Only doctors' claims are collected, no patient data is collected. We present here interim results (January 2025) of this survey which will be closed in May 2025.
Results
70 nephrologists respondents to date (see Fig. 1). 86% of respondents have a HHD program. 14% don't have such program (economically not profitable, lack of medical evidence, lack of personal motivation, delegation to third-party center). The respondents are from public hospitals (49%), private clinics (11%) and dialysis associations (34%). HHD programs are heterogeneous: 25% dedicated to HDD, 34% to home (HD+ PD), 17% to home + in center HD, 22% without dedicated structure. Number of HHD patients per center is low : all modalities combined 92% of respondents have between 0–10 patients. HHD is offered mainly based on medical evidence (82%) and demand from patients (58%). Patient acceptance rate for HHD varies from 1% to 25% for 82% of respondents: refusals expressed due to “treatment introduced at home", fear of puncture, personal lifestyle choices, technical complexity. Conversely, HHD acceptance factors are quality of life, autonomy of care, geographic mobility. Age of HHD patients is 26–50 y. (38%), 51–75 y. (61%). Male gender = 60%. Comorbidities are type 2 diabetes (52%), obesity (37%), coronary artery disease (34%). Preferred indications are Young age, autonomous patient, heart failure, hyperphosphatemia. Exit modes from HHD modality are mainly renal transplantation (RT) and in center HD, Exceptionally PD or hybrid modality PD/ HDD. The Modality preceding HDD is often Self-dialysis / in center HD / CKD ND and rarely RT and PD. 75% of respondents have a HDD recruitment program for “dialysis initiation” (93%) and “urgent start program” (62%). Role of nephrologists in HHD programs is equally shared: All doctors follow all patients, one doctor follows all patients, Each doctor follows his patients. Only 10% of nurses are participating in HHD program in full time. 26% of respondents claim advanced nurses practitioners involved in HHD program.
Conclusion
These are interim data with probable return from experienced centers (selection bias?). These initial data indicate low number of HDD patients per center, absence of a barrier related to the doctor in this survey, expected causes of refusal (fear of puncture, technical and organizational complexity), expected preferential indications and a HDD mainly from AVF but the KTC is prescribed. These data encourage to continue the survey until May 2025 in order to have more information on the prescriptions and the structures/organization of HDD programs.

title: #3259 Intradialytic clearances and reduction ratios for middle molecular weight uremic toxins and protein-bound uremic toxins: comparison of hemodiafiltration with asymmetric cellulose triacetate vs hemodiafiltration with helicoidal polysulfone during a 6-month follow-up
authors: Marco Ferrarini; Niccolò Morisi; Giuseppe Di Chiaro; Giuseppe Oliviero; Ylenia Cancelli; Giulia Ligabue; Fabio Olmeda; Lucia Stipo; Silvia Giovanella; Gabriele Donati
abstract:
Background and Aims
Polysulfone (PS) is to date the most used and versatile material for hemodialysis membranes. The features of permeability and resistance of this material allow its use in hemodiafiltration (HDF) with few alternatives. Asymmetric cellulose triacetate (ATA) is a new dialysis membrane, suitable for HDF which represents a substitute in case of hypersensitivity to PS. The CHORALS study evaluates the intradialytic performances of ATA membrane compared to the widespread PS membrane in hemodiafiltration. The filter efficacy is evaluated through the removal of middle molecular weight toxins (MMUT) and protein-bound uremic toxins (PBUT).
Method
Twenty anuric HD patients with AVF and blood flow >300 ml/min were transitioned from HD to post-dilutional HDF. Patients were either equally assigned to ATA arm (filter Solacea 22H, Nipro) or to PS arm (FX100, Fresenius). Assigned convective volume was calculated on body surface area. Toxin depuration was focused on β2 Microglobulin (β2M), κ light Chains (Lκ) and Lambda light Chains (Lλ) for MMUT removal and P-Cresyl (PC) and Indoxil Sulphate (IS) for PBUT removal. Kinetics of removal were assessed at the first session after transition to HDF and after 6 months of follow-up. In both cases, we performed a continuous sampling of the spent dialysate to establish the concentration of toxin removed over a treatment of at least 210 minutes. Blood toxin determinations were corrected by hemoconcentration. Blood and spent dialysate samples, collected at hourly time points, were used to calculate intradialytic clearance (K) and reduction ratio (RR).
Results
In both sessions and for both filters K remains stable during treatment for all tested molecules except for B2M. Little to no differences were found in the comparison between sessions. Besides B2M K and Lκ K, which are significantly higher for PS membrane with good reproducibility, other toxins do not show relevant differences in their performance. In both dialysis sessions, the whole treatment RR for Lκ in PS was significantly higher than ATA but not for the other MMUT and PBUT (Table 1). During treatment, B2M instantaneous K varies significantly with a peak between the first and the third hour of treatment. Inversely, all other molecules show a very stable K over time for both tested filters, especially for Lκ. This reflects on the standard deviation of the all-time K distribution in which all measured K were depicted pooled (Fig. 1). Alongside MMUT, all-time IS K for PC is significantly higher than ATA, although this was not confirmed in both considered sessions. Besides these few differences in performance between filters, PBUT global RR remains unaffected in both sessions.
Conclusion
Considering that instantaneous total K does not significantly vary over time for the majority of tested toxins in both filters tested, we can exclude an impairment of the function of both filters tested. B2M clearance rises during treatment, especially for PC in which this trend is significant. This phenomenon, observed in both sessions, couldn't be related to adsorption as K is calculated on the dialysate side. Since K remains stable, hourly RR decays in response to the decrease of the toxin gradient over time between blood and dialysate. This pattern is well represented by all considered toxins, with the slope of the RR decay seemingly dependent on the K. ATA shows significantly lower B2M and Lκ clearance, but this doesn't affect B2M RR due to high variance. Besides differences in Lκ depuration, filter RR are equal.

title: #3833 Access to hemodialysis in Haiti, a low-income, conflict-affected country
authors: Judith Exantus; Ana Catalina Alvarez-Elías; Xiaoling Ye; John Larkin; Len Usvyat; Peter Kotanko
abstract:
Background and Aims
Low-resource countries face significant challenges in providing kidney replacement therapies (KRT), particularly for patients with end-stage kidney disease (ESKD). ESKD patients in Haiti, a country affected by ongoing armed conflicts, face even greater struggles regarding access to KRT. Port-au-Prince, the country's capital, has a population of 1.2 million as of 2021, with at least 65% of residents over the age of 18 years. The reported average annual salary is equivalent to $1,760 USD, with 69% of the population living in extreme poverty with less than $1 USD per/day. Despite the absence of formal registries, a recent population-based study estimated a 2% prevalence of chronic kidney disease (CKD), defined as an eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m² [Nicholas S Robert et al. CJASN 2023, PMID 37081617]. Currently, neither peritoneal dialysis nor kidney transplantation are available, leaving hemodialysis (HD) as the only available option of KRT. In Port-au-Prince, seven centers provide HD. Given the difficult circumstances, no comprehensive overview of HD resources exist. We attempted to mitigate this knowledge gap by collecting data from some of the HD centers located in Port-au-Prince.
Method
We developed a short questionnaire using Microsoft Forms, consisting of 16 questions. Between September 1, 2024, and January 15, 2025, the questionnaire was distributed via mobile phones to the primary nephrologists and internists at healthcare centers around Port-au-Prince that offer HD. The questions focused on gathering information about the HD equipment, patient demographics, and available human resources. Center identifiers were anonymized. Responses were extracted into an Excel file and analyzed descriptively.
Results
We are reporting four of seven HD centers in Port-au-Prince, three private and one public. Currently, the three private centers provide HD treatments. An armed conflict has forced the fourth center to close since physical access was no longer possible (see Table 1). The three accessible centers each have a median of six functional HD machines, with a median of 13 patients per center. The youngest patients have a median age of 18 years. The cost per HD session at private centers is $200 USD, while at the currently closed public center, it is $20 USD, as the Health Ministry covers the remaining costs. Two of the private centers offer erythropoiesis-stimulating agent (ESA) treatment. The number of weekly HD sessions depends on patient's ability to pay, most patients receive twice weekly HD. The most common vascular access is the arteriovenous fistula (AVF), though jugular and femoral catheters are also regularly used. Overall, the three functional centers report an average patient duration on HD of 12 months. Internal medicine doctors and nurses are the primary healthcare providers.
Conclusion
With an estimated adult population of 780,000 in Port-au-Prince and a previously reported chronic kidney disease (CKD) prevalence of 2%, at least 15,000 adults in the metropolitan area may have CKD. Our partial report reveals a total of 18 machines across three out of four HD centers in Port-du-Prince, the most populated area in Haiti. Given this limited capacity, meeting the needs of the Haitian ESKD patients seems far from achievable. Pediatric patients, in particular, face even fewer opportunities for KRT, neither for acute nor chronic conditions. Urgent action is needed, including data collection and the establishment of registries, to better understand the disease burden in Haiti, especially within the context of an ongoing armed conflict. Support from international non-governmental organizations (NGOs) is crucial to address this significant unmet need.

title: #3523 Percutaneous ethanol injection therapy (peit) for refractory secondary hyperparathyroidism in hemodialysis patients unfit for surgery: safety and efficacy evaluation
authors: Nikolaos Papadakis; Ioannis Petrakis; Dimitra Ligerou; Kleio Dermitzaki; Eleni Drosataki; Marinos Mitrakos; Andreas Antonakis; Georgios-Alexandros Kavvadias; Konstantina Kydonaki; Christos Pleros; Ariadni Androvitsanea; Kostas Stylianou
abstract:
Background and Aims
Secondary hyperparathyroidism (SHPT) in hemodialysis patients is associated with increased mortality, fracture risk, and vascular calcifications. For patients who are ineligible for surgery and resistant to medical therapy, percutaneous ethanol injection therapy (PEIT) may serve as a feasible alternative for managing SHPT. This study evaluates the effects of PEIT in a cohort of dialysis patients with resistant SHPT who were unable to undergo surgery.
Method
This prospective study included patients who underwent PEIT after providing informed consent. The procedure was performed using a PEIT needle (HS Hospital Service S.p.A, Italy) following confirmation of parathyroid adenomas via Sestamibi Tc99m scintigraphy. Adenoma volume was assessed using a LOGIQ Book XP ultrasound system (GE Healthcare, MI, USA). Under sterile conditions, 95% ethanol (v/v) was injected into the adenomas. Laboratory data were extracted from medical records. Statistical analysis was conducted using Student's t-test for dependent samples in SPSS 20 (IBM, USA), with significance set at P < 0.05.
Results
A total of 45 dialysis patients (24 male) with a mean age of 54 years (SD: 14) underwent PEIT. The mean initial serum PTH level was 1086 pg/mL (±722), and the mean adenoma volume was 1.23 cm³ (±1.15). The mean total ethanol infusion volume was 2.66 mL (±2.5), and each patient received an average of 3 PEIT sessions (±1.37). A strong positive correlation was observed between adenoma volume and total ethanol infusion volume (R = 0.61, P < 0.001). Two months post-PEIT, patients exhibited a sustained reduction in serum PTH levels at a mean of 472 pg/mL (±347), (Student's t-test = 2.79, P = 0.007, medium effect size d = 0.72, Fig. 1). No major complications were reported.
Conclusion
PEIT is a safe and effective treatment option for selected hemodialysis patients with resistant secondary hyperparathyroidism who are unable to undergo surgery.

title: #45 Impact of load and movement on arteriovenous fistula flow
authors: Cynthia Borges; Thelma Vicente; Adriana Antônio; Fernando Nakagawa; Thiago Diaz; Eliane Xavier; Rosilene Motta
abstract:
Background and Aims
Arteriovenous fistula (AVF) is the preferred vascular access for hemodialysis. Whether acute arm movement impacts arteriovenous fistula (AVF) blood flow is unknown.
Method
In this cross-analysis, we evaluated AVF blood flow using an ultrasound device at resting and after 3 muscle movements for proximal (elbow flexion, shoulder adduction and abduction) or distal AVF (fist extension and flexion, fingers squeeze), without and with a 2 kg load.
Results
We included 23 patients, 53 ± 13 yrs, 14% men, 26.1% with diabetes, on dialysis for a median time of 5.2 months. At resting blood flow in proximal and distal AVF were 4355 (2470, 7233) ml/min and 2286 (2063, 2442) ml/min, respectively. There was no significant difference between blood flow at resting and any movement without and with load in either proximal or distal AVF (P > 0.05 for all comparisons).
Conclusion
Acute arm movement with or without load does not significantly alter the blood flow of mature AVF. These results demystify the general belief that patients should avoid AVF arm movement.

title: #1219 Efficiency of different medium cut-off membranes in maintenance hemodialysis
authors: Gurkan Yurteri; Ahmet Murt
abstract:
Background and Aims
Retention of larger middle molecules is a factor for increased mortality in maintenance hemodialysis patients. With their unique architecture, medium cut-off (MCO) membranes provide the benefit of removal of middle and large middle molecules. Such property of hemodialysis with MCO membranes removing an expanded set of molecules adds the name of expanded hemodialysis (HDx) to this modality. HDx may be comparable to post-dilution hemodiafiltration (HDF) for large middle molecules removal. Furthermore, HDx may be more favorable than HDF as this modality results in less albumin loss than HDF. This study aimed to analyze the removal of middle molecule β2-microglobuline and larger molecules IL-6 and TNF-alfa after switching from high-flux dialyzers to MCO membranes in a group of maintenance hemodialysis patients. Two different MCO dialyzers (Nipro-Elisio™-17H and Baxter-TheranovaTM-B400) are also compared with each other.
Method
Maintenance hemodialysis patients who have been dialyzed thrice weekly with high-flux membranes for more than a year were eligible to be involved in the study. Those who had active infections, malignancies, bleeding diathesis or received any immunosuppressive agents in the last 6 months were excluded from the study. After receiving patients’ informed consent, high-flux membranes were switched to one of the MCO dialyzers. Allocation to one of the MCO dialyzers was decided with a lottery. Patients received HDx thrice weekly for a month. Ultrafiltration was adjusted according to dry weight of the patients. At the end of one month, patients’ dialysis adequacy, average heparin dose, complete blood count, electrolytes, parathormone, C-reactive protein, cholesterol, ferritin, albumin, β2-microglobuline, IL-6 and TNF-alfa levels were compared with the day when high-flux membranes were switched to one of the MCO membranes.
Results
The study included 60 patients, 29 used Elisio™-17H and 31 used TheranovaTM-B400 membranes. Patients were 58.7 ± 13.4 years old and their dialysis vintage was 65.8 ± 58.6 months. At the end of one month with MCO membranes, a statistically significant decrease in β2-microglobuline levels (33.8 ± 9.3 mg/L vs 30.3 ± 7.3 mg/L; P = 0.02) was observed. There was also a significant tendency of decreasing low density lipoprotein (LDL) levels (71.5 ± 30.3 mg/dL vs 61.1 ± 29.5 mg/dL; P < 0.01). However, albumin loss was also significant with decreased levels at the end of one month with MCO membranes (38.1± 2.9 g/L vs 36.9 ± 3.2 g/L). Comparisons of other parameters can be found in Table 1. In addition, a switch to MCO dialyzers resulted in more clotting episodes in extracorporeal circuit and higher heparin doses had to be used (3768.5 ± 1287.5 vs 3972.2 ± 1438.7 IU; P < 0.01). When changes in these parameters were compared between two different MCO dialyzers, there was no statistically significant differences.
Conclusion
MCO dialyzers provide the benefit of better removal of middle-sized molecule such as β2-microglobuline. However, more albumin loss and circuit clotting may be observed with these membranes and necessary precautions should be taken in order to increase the efficiency of using these dialyzers.
