title: #2625 Impact of sarcopenia on hospitalization and mortality in patients on maintenance hemodialysis
authors: Eman Nagy; Samar Karawya; Ahmed Mohammed Abd El Wahab; Rasha Elzehery; Samar Tharwat; Alaa Sabry
abstract:
Background and Aims
Sarcopenia refers to the loss of muscle mass and is a multi-factorial and prevalent complication among patients on maintenance hemodialysis (MHD). This study aimed to investigate the impact of sarcopenia on one-year hospitalization and mortality in these patients.
Method
This prospective observational study was conducted on patients on MHD, with and without sarcopenia, from December 2021 to December 2022. Sarcopenia was diagnosed based on the presence of low muscle mass, assessed by quadriceps muscle ultrasound, and low muscle strength, assessed by handgrip strength. Sociodemographic and medical data, including the duration of hemodialysis (HD) and comorbidities, were collected. Anthropometric measurements, including body mass index, mid-arm circumference, and triceps skinfold thickness, were recorded. Routine laboratory data, including white blood cell count, hemoglobin, serum calcium, phosphorus, creatinine, albumin, total iron binding capacity (TIBC), and intact parathyroid hormone, were collected from patient records. Carotid intima media thickness (CIMT) was measured using carotid duplex. Patients were followed for one year for hospitalization and mortality.
Results
The study included 50 patients with sarcopenia and 37 without. Twelve patients (14%) died during the study period. There was no significant difference in one-year mortality between patients with and without sarcopenia (41.7% vs. 58.3%, P = 0.948). Additionally, one-year hospitalization rates showed no significant difference between patients with and without sarcopenia (13.5% vs. 10.9%, P = 0.713). Non-surviving patients were significantly older than surviving patients (59.5 vs. 46 years, P = 0.022). The duration of HD was significantly longer in non-surviving patients compared to surviving ones (11 vs. 7 years, P = 0.001). Blood hemoglobin, TIBC, and serum albumin levels were significantly lower in non-surviving patients compared to surviving ones (P = 0.033, P = 0.031, and P = 0.003, respectively). CIMT was significantly greater in non-surviving compared to surviving patients (0.92 vs 0.80 mm, respectively, P = 0.015) [Table 1]. Binary logistic regression of mortality revealed that the duration of HD was the only significant predictor of mortality (OR = 1.317, P = 0.025) [Table 2].
Conclusion
Older age, longer HD duration, low blood hemoglobin, low serum albumin, low TIBC, and greater CIMT were significantly associated with mortality. However, sarcopenia appeared to have no impact on one-year hospitalization or mortality. Multicenter studies with larger patient populations and longer follow-up periods are recommended.

Sarcopenia was diagnosed based on the presence of low muscle mass, assessed by quadriceps muscle ultrasound, and low muscle strength, assessed by handgrip strength. Sociodemographic and medical data, including the duration of hemodialysis (HD) and comorbidities, were collected. title: #2707 Comparison of methods for determining Kt/V
authors: Celso Felipe Mazariegos Campos; Herbert Ferrer Cuesta
abstract:
Background and Aims
An important part of monitoring patients on kidney replacement therapy (KRT) is to assess whether the delivered dose is adequate in order to improve short- and long-term results. Many parameters can be used to assess the quality and effectiveness of hemodialysis (HD), however, the determination of Kt/V is indicated and recommended by the KDOQI guidelines for the adequacy of HD in chronic patients. The aim of this study was to determine the correlation and concordance between Kt/V conventional by method Daugirdas second-generation single-pool formula and Kt/V by method online of Diamax machine.
Method
A descriptive study was carried out in HD patients. The following criteria were included: over 18y age, had started KRT more than 3 months ago, with a nutritional assessment from the previous month, were present on the day of laboratory sample collection and had the correct information on the Diamax HD machine monitor. Patients who underwent treatment on a Surdial HD machine, did not have laboratory results due to clotted samples or processing problems, and those who had not completed treatment due to complications were excluded. During the medical visit, the data entered into the Diamax machine were verified to be correct, taking into account the patient's age, height and dry weight, the latter based on the last nutritional assessment; these data are used by the machine's software to determine the volume of distribution, using the Watson formula. The data collection form was then filled out, taking into account the aforementioned data, the scheduled time of each treatment, the ultrafiltration (UF) volume and the Kt/V calculated by the Diamax machine system. Before starting the treatment and at the end of it, samples were taken to determine the pre- and post-HD serum urea nitrogen level, used in the second generation Daugirdas formula, with which the measured Kt/V was obtained.
Results
64 patient were analyzed, age mean 53.3 ± 13.3 y., the majority of patients being male (73.4%), a mean BMI of 25.8 ± 4.7 kg/m2 classified as overweight and a mean total body water content using the Watson formula of 37.3 ± 6.2 liters. In most cases the etiology of CKD is unknown (47%). Regarding HD treatment data, the majority of patients have permanent access to a native AVF (77%), the median UF was 2650 ml, a mean interdialytic weight gain of 5.8 ± 2.6 pounds was documented, treatments were performed with a median blood pump speed of 350 ml/min, a median treatment time of 3.5 hours, and a median filter size of ELISIO H15®. Laboratory data, a mean hemoglobin (hgb) of 10.6 ± 1.7 g/dl and a mean hematocrit of 34.5 ± 6.3% were obtained, with 69% of patients having target hgb levels above 10 g/dl. Regarding urea nitrogen, a mean of 66.3 ± 18.9 mg/dl was obtained pre-HD and a median of 19.3 mg/dl post-HD, obtaining a mean URR of 69.6 ± 5.8%, Kt/V median 1.3 (IQR 1.2, 1.4) Diamax machine and 1.6 (IQR 1.3, 1.7) Daugirdas formula, this represents 80% and 94% of patients above the 1.2 target respectively. When performing an analysis comparing patient sex and type of vascular access, it was found that there are no differences between men and women when analyzing whether the Kt/V value is at target ≥1.2, however there is a tendency to higher values in female patients versus male patients (p: 0.001), also with the URR (p: 0.001); with respect to the type of vascular access, there is a significant difference in favor of patients who present as access an AVF, whether native or prosthetic, versus patients with a catheter, whether temporary or permanent. Regarding the hgb target >10 g/dl, no differences are found in either the patient's sex or the type of vascular access. Spearman correlation coefficient was established, it was found positive-moderate relationship and significant (r: 0.57, p: >0.001) (Fig. 1); however concordance Bland-Altman analysis, was found Diamax method underestimate Kt/V value 11% (−0.2) (Fig. 2), although this bias is not systematic (p: 0.33).
Conclusion
determinate Kt/V by method online of monitor Diamax could not be a substitute of standard method by Daugirdas second-generation single-pool formula, however it can be useful for a fast and constant evaluation of dialysis dose.

title: #2715 Evaluation of the effect of hemodialysis on serum uric acid levels and the association with cardiovascular diseases in patients with chronic kidney disease
authors: Stella Kushnirenko; Liubov Savytska; Yurii Kalantarenko; Oksana Lysianska
abstract:
Background and Aims
Hyperuricemia, characterized by elevated serum uric acid (SUA) levels, is associated with a number of diseases, including chronic kidney disease (CKD) and end-stage renal disease (ESRD).
The aim of this study was to assess the prevalence of hyperuricemia in CKD patients on hemodialysis (HD), to evaluate the effect of HD on SUA levels, and to determine the association with cardiovascular diseases.
Method
A cross-sectional study was performed involving 52 ESRD patients from two outpatient dialysis centers. SUA levels were measured, and data on HD adequacy over the past six months, preservation of water excretion kidney function, and interdialytic weight gain over the past month were analyzed. Statistical data processing was performed using the χ²-test, mean comparison, and regression analysis.
Results
The mean age of the patients was 56.50 ± 13.35 years, with 29 males (56.9%) and 22 females (43.1%). The prevalence of hyperuricemia, using the common cut-off point of 360 µmol/L, was 57.69%, including 58.06% in males and 57.14% in females. The mean dialysis vintage was 12.50 ± 62.22 months. None of the patients received urate-lowering therapy.
Using the χ² criterion, a statistically significant difference in the prevalence of hyperuricemia (Fig. 1) was found depending on dialysis vintage (p 0.029), with peak values observed at the initiation of renal replacement therapy and after five years (61.54%). All patients with a dialysis vintage of 24–36 months had hyperuricemia, whereas the lowest hyperuricemia prevalence was observed in the 12–24-month group (16.67%), and no patients in the 36–60-month group had elevated SUA levels.
Based on a minimum SUA value of 113 µmol/L and a maximum of 544 µmol/L, four quartiles were identified: Q1—SUA level from 113 to 309.5 µmol/L; Q2—SUA level from 309.5 to 374.0 µmol/L; Q3—SUA level from 374.0 to 420.75 µmol/L, and Q4—SUA level from 420.75 to 544 µmol/L.
Statistically significant differences were found in the prevalence of prior acute cerebrovascular events (ACVE) or myocardial infarction (MI) depending on a SUA level (p 0.029) in CKD patients. The highest prevalence (50.0%) was observed in Q1, suggesting a higher prevalence of prior ACVE or MI in ESRD patients with relatively low SUA levels. High SUA levels in Q4 were not associated with an increased frequency of prior ACVE or MI (7.69%), which could contradict the expected association between hyperuricemia and cardiovascular risks. However, the primary limiting factor in this situation is the maximum SUA value of 544 µmol/L, which does not allow for a complete assessment of this association.
A regression analysis was also performed to assess the effect of dialysis vintage (R² 0.003; p 0.703), mean KT/V (R² 0.001; p 0.853), and interdialytic weight gain (R² 0.025; p 0.265) on the SUA level. The results showed that none of the included factors had a significant effect on the SUA level. This may indicate that the SUA level in HD patients may be determined by other factors not included in this study, such as dietary habits, concomitant medication therapy, except urate-lowering drugs, genetic factors, etc.
Conclusion
Further studies are needed to identify factors influencing the SUA level and to determine safe SUA levels in CKD patients on HD.

title: #2721 A safety and survival analysis of sequential systemic anticancer treatment in patients with end-stage kidney disease and metastatic renal cell carcinoma
authors: Tomaž Milanez; Vinay Srinivasan; Bostjan Seruga; Janja Ocvirk; Miha Arnol; Edgar Jaimes
abstract:
Background and Aims
Systemic anticancer treatment (SACT) prolongs overall survival (OS) in patients with metastatic renal cell carcinoma (mRCC) but is associated with various adverse events (AEs). Many mRCC patients develop chronic kidney disease, that can progress to end-stage kidney disease (ESKD), requiring chronic hemodialysis (HD). Unfortunately, pivotal randomized trials usually exclude cancer patients with ESKD, resulting in a lack of high-quality data on the efficacy and safety of SACT in this population. The incidence of serious AEs, particularly bleeding and infection, and the primary outcome in terms of OS in mRCC patients with ESKD receiving SACT, remains unclear.
Method
We retrospectively identified all patients with mRCC and ESKD who received SACT with VEGFR inhibitors, immune check point inhibitors (ICI), or mTOR inhibitors, alone or in combinations, at the Institute of Oncology Ljubljana in Slovenia between December 2009 and January 2025. Data on the frequency and severity of bleeding and infections were collected from electronic health records. OS was defined as the duration of time from the initiation of SACT to death. Mean and median OS were calculated across all risk groups according to the International Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma Database Consortium (IMDC).
Results
We identified 38 patients with mRCC and ESKD treated with SACT. Their median age at SACT initiation of was 70.5 (64.3–75) years, with 30 patients (79%) being men. According to IMDC criteria, 12 patients had a good prognosis, while 26 (68.4%) had intermediate or poor prognosis. Eighteen patients (47%) experienced a least one cycle of ICI. Before SACT, 25 patients (65.8%) were already on HD and 16 patients (34.2%) later developed ESKD. Three patients (7.9%) had an eGFR of ≤15 ml/min/1.73 m2, and six (15.8%) had an eGFR of 15–29 ml/min/1.73 m2 at SACT start. Eight patients (21%) experienced bleeding episodes before SACT initiation, including three with gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB). Grade 4 epistaxis occurred in three patients, with one patient who developed hemorrhagic shock during first-line treatment with sunitinib. Two patients experienced grade 4 anal hemorrhage, one related to hemorrhoids during sunitinib therapy. Two patients required urgent nephrectomy during pazopanib or sunitinib treatment. One patient required urgent local treatment for massive upper GIB during corticosteroids therapy due to immune-related AEs. Overall, seven patients (18.4%) experienced grade 4 GIB during or after SACT. The cumulative incidence of grade 3/4 bleeding was 0.53 (20 events/38 patients), and all-grade bleeding was 1.24 (47 events/38 patients). Twenty eight patients (73.7%) experienced grade 4 infections during SACT, with seven developing sepsis, and one, experiencing septic shock while on HD and receiving first-line treatment with sunitinib. Across all prognostic groups, the median OS was 32 months (95% CI: 15.7–48.3) and the mean OS was 38 months (95% CI: 25.8–51). All censored patients were alive at the end of the study.
Conclusion
Serious bleeding and infections are common complications in mRCC and ESKD patients treated with sequential SACT. Clinicians should consider these potentially life-threatening complications when selecting the type and duration of SACT. Given the significant management challenges, treatment should occur in dedicated onco-nephrology services.
The IMDC risk model and the primary outcomes for mRCC and ESKD patients warrant further evaluation in prospective trials to enhance treatment strategies and improve outcomes.

title: #2764 Predictive factors for hospitalizations: comparison between incremental hemodialysis and conventional hemodialysis
authors: Abidi Safa; Nouha Ben Mahmoud; Mayssa Hadj Brahim; Meriem Ben Salem; Manel Ben Salah; Sirine Bchir; Hadhri Asma; Ahmed Letaief; Mouna Hamouda; Zohra Elati; Habib Skhiri
abstract:
Background and Aims
Hospitalizations of hemodialysis patients represent a major challenge in nephrology due to their frequency and their impact on patients' quality of life as well as healthcare costs. Various factors are responsible, including dialysis-related complications, comorbidities, and socio-economic constraints. Among the main causes of hospitalization are infections, cardiovascular disorders, electrolyte imbalances, and complications related to vascular access, such as thrombosis and infections.
Method
We collected data from 127 patients over a period spanning from January 2018 to January 2023 in two nephrology departments. The patients were divided into two groups: the first group consisted of 72 patients undergoing hemodialysis three times a week, and the second group consisted of 55 patients undergoing hemodialysis two or once a week.
Results
In our study, the hospitalization rate was significantly higher in the conventional hemodialysis group (31.9% compared to 10.9%). In univariate analysis, the predictive factors for hospitalization were conventional hemodialysis and the presence of hypertension (HTN) before, during, and after dialysis. Indeed, 79.31% of patients on conventional hemodialysis were hospitalized, compared to only 20.68% of patients who underwent incremental hemodialysis. Additionally, patients with HTN before dialysis (37.9% vs. 15.3%), during dialysis (37.9% vs. 15.3%), and after dialysis (27.6% vs. 10.2%) required more hospitalizations. We also identified inadequate and unsatisfactory HD as a predictive factor for hospitalization, with a rate of 51.7%. Furthermore, hyperkalemia and anuria were associated with more frequent hospitalizations, with 65.5% of hyperkalemic patients and 75.9% of anuric patients being hospitalized.
Conclusion
Early identification of these factors and the adoption of preventive strategies, such as enhanced patient education and optimized management of comorbidities, could help reduce hospitalization rates and improve clinical outcomes for hemodialysis patients.

title: #2882 Network analysis of hemodialysis patients' symptoms
authors: Hoda Mahmoud Mohammad Abdulaziz; Rasha Mahmoud; Ahmed Mohamed Naguib Attiya; Yusof Mohamed Omar; Ahmed Mohammed Helal; Rashad G Mohamed; Mohammed Ghanem Gabr Mohammed; Kariem Mohamed Salem; Basma Sultan
abstract:
Background and Aims
Individuals undergoing maintenance hemodialysis frequently report a high symptom burden that interferes with their quality of life. While the prevalence of symptoms has been previously well-studied in hemodialysis patients, exploring connections and relationships between symptoms using network analysis has been less well-investigated therefore we aimed to perform network analysis for symptoms experienced by a large cohort of hemodialysis patients.
Method
This was a cross-sectional study involving hemodialysis patients enrolled from 27 hemodialysis units distributed in different regions in Egypt. Symptoms were assessed using the validated Arabic version of the Chronic Kidney Disease Symptom Burden Index (CKD-SBI), which assesses the prevalence, distress, severity, and frequency of 32 symptoms. JASP version 0.18.0 (JASP Team) was used for network analysis. To gain additional insights into the structural importance of each node (i.e., symptom) in the network, three centrality indices (i.e., betweenness, closeness, strength) were estimated.
Results
A total of 1156 patients were included in the study. Network analysis investigated the relationship between 31 common symptoms among patients. It was found that the symptoms with the highest betweenness were nausea (rb = 2.70) and feeling nervous (rb = 2.33), indicating that they act as bridge symptoms with the greatest effects in symptom interactions. The symptoms with the highest closeness were feeling nervous (rc = 1.714) and nausea (rc = 1.497), denoting that they had the closest relationship with other symptoms. The symptoms with the highest strength were feeling nervous (rs = 2.386) and worrying (rs = 1.659), signifying that they were the most important symptoms in the network.
Conclusion
Feeling nervous and worrying were the core symptoms of the network. While bone or joint pain, feeling tired or lack of energy, and muscle cramps were the most prevalent symptoms, their low centrality indicates that they could be sentinel symptoms for other symptoms. Early discovery and management of negative emotions could potentially be a key to symptom management in hemodialysis patients, as it positively affects the management of other symptoms.

title: #2901 Analysis of primary survival and quality indicators of native arteriovenous fistulas performed during the period 2020–2023
authors: Sheyla Christal Álvarez Parra; Joselin MacÍas Murillo; Victor Tristan Calvo; Vanesa Camarero Temiño; Alejandra Martín Rosique; Anney Yelena Rosario Vargas; Marta Boya Fernandez; Badawi Hijazi Prieto; Raquel De Toro Casado; Irene Oñate Alonso; Basilia Gonzalez Diez; María Jesús Izquierdo Ortiz
abstract:
Background and Aims
The process from vascular access (VA) selection to creation and maintenance is still a challenge today. Based on studies and clinical guidelines, we can assess the quality of care of our patient's vascular access, thereby facilitating decision-making in daily clinical practice and ensuring better treatment and thereby increasing quality of life.
We reviewed our results over three years in accordance with the quality criteria of a clinical guideline on vascular access for hemodialysis [1].
Method
Retrospective study of native arteriovenous fistulas (nAVF) performed in our center during the period 2020–2023. The general characteristics of the patients and type of nAVF performed were collected, we calculated the primary survival of the vascular access for 40 months, analyzed by Kaplan-Meier and Log-rank methods. Subsequently, we proceeded to analyze the fulfillment of two quality indicators: Early failure of vascular access in the first 30 days from its creation (Outcome indicator; Standard: radiocephalic nAVF <35% and proximal nAVF <25% annually) and Immature arteriovenous fistula after 4 weeks from its creation (Process indicator, Approximate standard 28%–53% according to the literature).
Results
233 AVFs were performed (165 men and 68 women). Regarding the age at the time of the fistula, 3.4% of the patients were in the age range between 25 and 40 years, 12.9% between 41 and 56 years, 36.1% between 57 and 72 years and 47.6% between 73 and 88 years. Of the total AVFs, 52.4% were radiocephalic, 29.2% humerocephalic, 2.6% humerobasilic, 8.6% humeromedian, 1.7% ulnar-cephalic, 5.6% humeroaxillary. Since the event was reintervention and considering the time until the date of data collection 11/12/2024 at 11.8 months, the probability of primary survival is 75% with no statistically significant differences between the type of nAVF and age groups. The result indicator determined an early nAVF failure of 38.9%. The process indicator determined that 40.3% of all the studied AVFs did not meet maturation criteria. 72% of the nAVFs performed were reviewed during the first 3–4 weeks, the rest were reviewed at 8–12 weeks. 51% of the radiocephalic nAVFs required reintervention, followed by humerocephalic nAVF with 36.5%, humerobasilic 9.5% and the rest <2%.
Survival analysis Fig. 1.
Conclusion
We obtained an early failure rate higher than the recommended standard. As for the percentage of maturation, we were within the desired standard. Both indicators imply a worse survival of the vascular access. We believe that earlier follow-up during the first month after the procedure could imply an improvement for our results.

title: #2905 Recurrent liver cyst infections in an ADPKD patient on peritoneal dialysis
authors: Toufic Lteif; Joelle Yaman; Rita Slim; Hiba Azar
abstract:
Background and Aims
Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) is frequently associated with liver manifestations, and liver cyst infection is a serious complication. We present the case of a patient who experienced recurrent liver cyst infections over eight months while undergoing peritoneal dialysis.
Results
A 59-year-old male with a history of ADPKD and chronic automated peritoneal dialysis for 4 years presented four times to our institution in 2024 with hepatic cyst infections, with an average interval of two months between admissions. Common clinical features included high-grade fever, epigastric pain, nausea, vomiting, leukocytosis, elevated C-reactive protein, and positive blood cultures for gram-negative bacilli. The first episode was initially treated as septicemia with two weeks of intravenous antibiotics, as imaging findings were inconclusive. In the second episode, MRI confirmed the presence of an infected cyst, and antibiotic therapy was extended to 6 weeks. Notably, there was no evidence of peritonitis, as peritoneal dialysis effluent cultures were negative for infection each time, and there were no signs of diverticulitis on imaging. During the third episode, common bile duct dilation and intrahepatic stones were noted on MRI without clear evidence of cholangitis. PET-CT scan performed to search for a potential source of infection, revealed an ill-defined, radiotracer-avid hypodense mass in hepatic segment VI, along with fusiform dilation of the biliary ducts, particularly on the left side. Further evaluation with echo-endoscopy suggested cholangitis, revealing hyperechoic material in the main bile duct (likely pus/sludge under pressure), a dilated common bile duct (8 mm), and a 4 cm hepatic abscess. An ERCP with sphincterotomy and balloon sweeping was performed, retrieving thickened bile and some whitish debris. A plastic stent was placed, and antibiotic therapy continued for 6 weeks, with resolution of the infection confirmed by imaging. However, two months later, the patient experienced another cyst infection. The stent was removed, and ursodeoxycholic acid therapy was initiated. Following this intervention, no further infections were observed during follow-up. Of note, infection affected cysts at different locations at each time and the liver function tests were mildly elevated.
Conclusion
This case highlights the need to consider cholangitis as a potential cause of liver cyst infections in ADPKD patients undergoing peritoneal dialysis. In this patient, intrahepatic stones likely contributed to the recurrent infections, and the combination of endoscopic treatments and ursodeoxycholic acid effectively prevented further episodes. While hepatic abscesses in peritoneal dialysis patients are typically linked to peritonitis or diverticular disease, cholangitis should also be considered as a possible source of infection in ADPKD patients.

title: #3054 A single-centre, cross-sectional study of frailty prevalence and its related risk factors of Indonesian hemodialysis outpatients
authors: Riri Muzasti
abstract:
Background and Aims
Frailty is a major problem among maintenance hemodialysis patients, with reported rates up to 82%. The coexistence of frailty and hemodialysis is highly related to morbidity and mortality. The data related to frailty in hemodialysis patients are essential for the development of other healthcare services that should be available in Indonesia. However, the updated epidemiological data in Indonesia are lacking. This study aimed to find the current prevalence of frailty and its related factors among Indonesian hemodialysis outpatients.
Method
All outpatients aged 18 years and older with regular dialysis for more than three months (two times a week), without acute illness presenting to the Hemodialysis Unit of Universitas Sumatera Utara Hospital, located in Medan, North Sumatera, from September 25th to October 25th, 2024 were enrolled in a cross-sectional study. Frailty status was measured using a FRAIL scale and Edmonton Frail Scale questionnaire. Descriptive, bivariate, and multivariate analyses were conducted. P-value <0.05 was considered statistically significant.
Results
Among fifty-four participants were enrolled, 50.0% were male. The range age was 28–80 years and 31.4% were ≥60 years; 59.2% were overweight-obese. The main comorbidities associated with end-stage renal disease were hypertension in 37 patients (68.5%) and diabetes in 17 patients (31.5%). 44.5% were already in hemodialysis ≥36 months when the study started. According to the FRAIL scale, 6 (11.1%) were non-frail, 36 (66.7%) were pre-frail and 12 (22.92%) were frail, and according to the Edmonton Frail Scale, 42.6% were robust, 31.5% were pre-frail, and 25.9% were frail. Body mass index (BMI) was associated with frailty (OR 4.0, 95% CI 1.02–15.59). Based on the p-value of the results of bivariate analysis, BMI, age, dialysis vintage, and comorbidity (diabetes) were included in the multivariate analysis. The results of multivariate analysis showed that age and dialysis vintage were associated with frailty among Indonesian hemodialysis outpatients (OR 4.72, 95% CI 0.98–22.59 and OR 6.96, 95% CI 1.23–39.34, respectively.)
Conclusion
Approximately one in five hemodialysis outpatients in Indonesia is in a frail condition, highlighting a critical issue that demands urgent attention. Frailty is associated with older patients and shorter dialysis vintage. Our findings, despite being limited by a small sample size, a single center design, and a singular frailty assessment, indicate a high prevalence of frailty among hemodialysis outpatients in Indonesia. Therefore, it is imperative that the government, private sector, healthcare professionals, and the community collaboratively develop effective strategies and policies to address this issue.

title: #3104 Determinants of quality of life in chronic kidney disease patients on conservative management and on dialysis
authors: Aalaya Haridas; Ram Prasad E; Sandhya Suresh
abstract:
Background and Aims
CKDis one of the leading causes of mortality worldwide. WHO has defined Quality of life (QOL) as “an individual's perception of their position in life in the context of the culture and value systems in which they live and in relation to their goals, expectations, standards and concerns”. Health related quality of life (HRQL0, reflects the impact of health on an individual's ability to lead a fulfilling life. For patients with chronic medical conditions, HRQL also considers the effects of disease progression, treatment on disability and daily functioning and patient centered outcome questionnaires are used. The aim was to evaluate the quality of life in patients with kidney failure managed conservatively and with dialysis using the euroqol visual analogue scale (EQVAS).
Method
The study was a cross sectional study, conducted over 3-months, at dialysis centre, Nephrology at Sri Ramachandra Institute of Higher Education and Research, Chennai, India. Sample size was 200, in which 80 patients were on maintenance hemodialysis,120 patients on conservative management. Euroqol visual analogue scale (EQVAS), IPOS renal surveys,EQ-5D-5L scale were used to evaluate quality of life, sleep level, baseline symptoms and functional data.
Results
Of the participants, 0.5% were below 20 years, 15.5% were 21–40 years, 39% were 41–60 years, and 45% were above 60 years. Males made up 59.5%, and females 40.5%. Among them, 120 were conservatively managed ESRD patients, and 80 were on maintenance hemodialysis. The sleep scale average was 8.3 for conservative patients and 5.6 for hemodialysis patients. The EQ VA scale average was 82.9 and 53.5, respectively. Severe poor appetite was seen in 5% of conservative and 16.3% of hemodialysis patients (P = 0.029). Severe tiredness (9.2% vs. 23.8%, P = 0.001), sleep difficulty (6.7% vs. 32.5%, P < 0.001), muscle cramps (3.3% vs. 16.3%, P < 0.001), stress (1.7% vs. 18.8%, P < 0.001), mobility issues (3.3% vs. 12.5%, P = 0.009), and pain (0.8% vs. 15%, P < 0.001) were more common in hemodialysis patients. Kidney disease interfered with social activities (5.8% vs. 30%, P < 0.001) and daily life (21.7% vs. 87.5%, P < 0.001). Fluid (0.8% vs. 52.5%, P < 0.001) and dietary restrictions (3.3% vs. 23.8%, P < 0.001) were major concerns. Frustration (20% vs. 78.8%, P < 0.001), reduced work output (35% vs. 75%, P < 0.001), and activity limitations (31.7% vs. 75%, P < 0.001) were significantly higher in hemodialysis patients.
Conclusion
This study identified several significants associated with quality of life in patients with kidney failure both managed conservatively and with dialysis. Symptoms like pain, tiredness, difficulty in sleeping, muscle cramps, factors affecting mental health are stress, worries and anxiety, life style changes like fluid restriction, functional impairment associated with mobility, selfcare and usual activities, factors like frustration, lesser work accomplishment and limitations in activities have emotional impact on patients. Addressing these factors is essential to enhance the quality of life for patients with kidney failure.

title: #3643 Vascular access difficulties in patients of African descent—causes and consequences
authors: Ana Sofia Domingos; Tiago Assis Pereira; Patrícia Alves; João Figueiredo Martins; Luís Gaião Santos; Paula Milhazes Guimarães; Cristina Rego de Freitas; Mendes Jorge
abstract:
Background and Aims
In Portugal, many patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) are from Portuguese-speaking African countries and often experience worse vascular access (VA) outcomes for hemodialysis, potentially due to socioeconomic disparities and vascular characteristics. However, direct evidence addressing this issue is scarce. This study investigates the reasons behind these differences, focusing on vascular characteristics, comorbidities, sociodemographic factors, and clinical data. By comparing populations with and without African descent, we aim to identify factors contributing to disparities in hemodialysis access.
Method
This single-center observational study analyzed vascular ultrasound mapping and clinical data from advanced chronic kidney disease patients. Arterial and venous diameters and peak systolic velocities (PSV) were categorized as adequate or inadequate for VA creation, with continuous variables converted to binary form. Continuous variables are presented as means or medians and were compared using the Student's t-test, Welch test, or Mann-Whitney U test, depending on normality and variance. Categorical variables were compared using the Chi-square test. Multivariate logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, and comorbidities.
Results
The study included 304 patients (63 of African descent, 241 of non-African descent), with a mean follow-up of 401.1 days. No significant differences were observed in sex, diabetes, hypertension, heart failure, obesity, or cardiovascular disease. However, patients of African descent were younger (54 vs 75 years, P < 0.001), had lower tobacco use (14.3% vs 40.7%, P < 0.001), and lower rates of peripheral arterial disease (3.2% vs 11.2%, P = 0.011). Twenty two percent of patients were on HD, 58.4% were on pre-dialysis care, of which 19.9% started HD during follow-up.
Univariate analysis (Fig. 1) revealed significant differences in vascular characteristics particularly in PSV and diameters of ulnar arteries, as well as in venous diameters of the cephalic and basilic veins. To further assess the suitability of VA creation, arterial and venous characteristics were analyzed as binary variables based on established adequacy thresholds, with the results summarized in Fig. 2.
Multivariate analysis confirmed African descent as a strong independent predictor of worse vascular characteristics, namely in ulnar arteries diameter (P = 0.001), PSV in all arteries (P < 0.001) and venous forearm and arm cephalic and basilic veins (P = 0.016).
Regarding VA feasibility, patients of African descent were more likely to require a prosthetic arteriovenous graft (AVG) due to inadequacy for autologous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) (17.5% vs 7.1%, P = 0.009) and most patients initiated hemodialysis via central venous catheter (58.7% vs fistulae 32.8%, P = 0.040), either at the beginning or during follow-up. Among these patients, 12.5% constructed radiocephalic AVF, 67.5% umerocephalic AVF, 5% umerobasilic AVF, and 15% AVG, with immediate patency rates of 97.4% and 83.3% at 3 months.
Conclusion
Patients of African descent have poorer vascular characteristics for dialysis access, resulting in increased dependence on AVGs and CVCs for hemodialysis initiation, with both short- and long-term clinical consequences that can be devastating. These findings highlight the need for proactive vascular care tailored to this population to ensure equitable access to optimal hemodialysis treatment and to explore new biological and genetic mechanisms underlying this phenomenon.

title: #182 A pharmacist intervention with dose optimization of phosphate-binding medication (PIDO-P)in dialysis patients: effects on phosphate, pill burden, and adherence?
authors: Francisca van den Oever; Erwin Vasbinder; Yvonne Schrama; Teun Van Gelder; Patricia Van den Bemt
abstract:
Background and Aims
Phosphate-binding medication (PBM) is an essential component of hyperphosphatemia treatment in hemodialysis patients. However, non-adherence to PBM occurs in approximately 50% of dialysis patients and contributes to suboptimal treatment outcomes. Non-adherence to PBM is mainly caused by forgetfulness, a complex treatment scheme, and a high pill burden. It has been suggested that a reduction in PBM pill burden might improve adherence, but this hypothesis has not yet been tested. Our aim was to investigate if the PIDO-P intervention (Pharmacist Intervention with Dose Optimization of Phosphate-binding medication) would reduce mean phosphate levels in hemodialysis patients with hyperphosphatemia and a high PBM pill burden.
Method
This was a prospective, pre-post intervention study in the Franciscus Gasthuis and Vlietland, a hospital with a 250-patient hemodialysis facility in Rotterdam, the Netherlands. Hemodialysis patients with a mean phosphate level >1.50 mmol/L over the last 3 months and a PBM pill burden of ≥6 sevelamer tablet equivalents were included. The PIDO-P intervention consisted of 3 pharmacist consultations in 3 months. During the first consultation, self-reported adherence to PBM (using MARS-5), and barriers to adherence to PBM (using the Quick Barrier Scan) were assessed. During the second consultation (1–2 weeks later) the pharmacist discussed the identified barriers to adherence and reduced PBM dose according to a predefined treatment algorithm. After 3 months, the pharmacist performed an evaluation consultation, after which the nephrologist resumed hyperphosphatemia treatment (usual care). Primary outcome was mean phosphate level in the 3 months after versus 3 months before start of the intervention. Secondary outcomes were phosphate levels during total follow-up (12 months), percentage of patients within target range for phosphate at 3, 6, and 12 months, and PBM pill burden and self-reported adherence at 3 and 12 months. Statistical analysis was performed with SPSS version 29.0.2, using paired T-tests for phosphate levels and pill burden, and Wilcoxon signed-rank test for self-reported adherence.
Results
75 patients were included with a mean age of 65 years, 65.3% of them were male. Patients generally used 12.7 ± 5.0 (mean ± SD) different medications with a total daily pill burden of 22.3 ± 7.7. The main causes of dialysis were hypertension (30.7%) and diabetes (20.0%). The mean phosphate level was 1.99 ± 0.34 mmol/L before start of the intervention versus 2.03 ± 0.37 mmol/L in the 3 months after (P = 0.193, n = 72). The phosphate level remained stable the first 3 months after the intervention (2.04 mmol/L at baseline (BL) vs 2.01 mmol/L at 3 months, P = 0.991) and decreased to 1.86 mmol/L at 12 months (P = 0.025 vs BL, n = 54). title: #537 Prevalence of functional iron deficiency and its impact on mortality in hemodialysis patients in Hatay
authors: Can Huzmeli; Ayşe Şeker; Elif Durak
abstract:
Background and Aims
Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a major public health concern that has become an epidemic both globally and in our country. Iron deficiency and functional iron deficiency (FID) are common among CKD patients. The aim of our study is to investigate the prevalence of FID and its impact on mortality in hemodialysis (HD) patients.
Method
Our study was conducted between 2010 and 2024 in patients undergoing hemodialysis in Hatay province. Patients included were those aged 18 and above who had been on HD for at least three months and had accessible records of serum iron, total iron-binding capacity, and ferritin levels. Patients undergoing home HD, peritoneal dialysis, and those under the age of 18 were excluded. The prevalence of anemia, absolute iron deficiency (AID), and functional iron deficiency (FID) was calculated, and their relationships with mortality were evaluated.
Results
A total of 3.086 HD patients were included in the study. The prevalence of FID was found to be 14.7%, and AID was 4.1%. Five-year survival rates based on iron deficiency status were 44.1% for FID, 58% for AID, and 54.2% for normal patients. Mortality was higher in functional iron deficiency than in other groups (P < 0.05). The mortality rate in patients with absolute iron deficiency was lower compared to other groups, but no statistical difference was observed compared to normal patients. Patients with transferrin saturation <20% had a statistically significantly higher mortality risk than those with transferrin saturation between 20%–30% and 30%–50%. There was no statistical difference between ferritin levels and mortality. However, the lowest mortality rate was observed in individuals with ferritin levels <300 µg/L, and the highest mortality rate was observed in those with ferritin levels >800 µg/L. The highest mortality risk was observed in patients with Hb levels < 8g/dL. Patients with Hb levels >10 g/dL had lower mortality risk. The highest mortality risk was observed in patients with Hb levels <8 g/dL. Patients with Hb levels >10 g/dL had lower mortality risk (P < 0.001).
Conclusion
Anemia is common in HD patients. We identified an FID prevalence of 14.7%, with mortality risks higher in FID compared to normal and AID patients. Patients with transferrin saturation <20% had a statistically significantly higher mortality risk. These results suggest that clinicians should focus more on transferrin saturation rather than ferritin in HD patients.

title: #633 Pathogen distribution and clinical outcomes of aHUS patients on peritoneal dialysis
authors: Szu-Pei Lee; I-Ru Chen; I-Kuan Wang; Chiu-Ching Huang; Ping-Chin Lai; Huey-Liang Kuo; Chiz-Tzung Chang; Chin-Chi Kuo; Jiung-Hsiun Liu; Hung-Chieh Yeh; I-Wen Ting; Shih-Yi Lin
abstract:
Background and Aims
Atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (aHUS) is a rare, life-threatening thrombotic microangiopathy that can lead to end-stage renal disease (ESRD). While peritoneal dialysis (PD) is an option, infection may trigger aHUS instability. Some ESRD patients require ongoing anticomplement therapy for persistent extra-renal manifestations. This study examines PD outcomes in aHUS patients, comparing those with and without regular anticomplement therapy, and analyzes pathogen differences between aHUS and non-aHUS PD patients.
Method
We retrospectively analyzed aHUS patients on PD at a single Taiwan center (Jan 2017–Oct 2024). Outcomes and pathogen profiles were compared between those with and without regular anticomplement therapy, and pathogen distribution was examined between aHUS and non-aHUS PD patients.
Results
Twelve aHUS patients on PD were included, six developing peritonitis across 24 episodes. Three remained on regular anticomplement therapy due to multiple system involvement and prior flare-ups upon dose reduction, while three did not. In those on therapy, pathogens included Staphylococcus hominis, Staphylococcus epidermidis, Staphylococcus haemolyticus, Staphylococcus capitis, Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), and Proteus mirabilis (each in one episode). Polymicrobial infections involved Staphylococcus epidermidis + Staphylococcus haemolyticus, Streptococcus salivarius + Streptococcus mitis, Citrobacter freundii + Enterococcus faecalis, Serratia marcescens + Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Elizabethkingia anophelis, and Sphingomonas koreensis, with four culture-negative episodes. Five required PD catheter removal and hemodialysis (HD) conversion. In those without therapy, pathogens included Corynebacterium striatum, Streptococcus gallolyticus, Staphylococcus aureus, and Staphylococcus lugdunensis (each in one episode), while Staphylococcus epidermidis appeared in three episodes and Acinetobacter baumannii in one. Two were culture-negative, and one required HD conversion. No fungal infections were observed. Among 335 non-aHUS patients with 465 PD peritonitis episodes, 26 were polymicrobial (excluding secondary peritonitis). The most common pathogens were Staphylococcus aureus (59), Staphylococcus epidermidis (49), Escherichia coli (46), Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) (32), Staphylococcus haemolyticus (27), Pseudomonas aeruginosa (22), Klebsiella pneumoniae (16), Enterococcus faecalis (15), Staphylococcus capitis (11), and Streptococcus salivarius (10). Fungal peritonitis occurred in 16 episodes, with one tuberculosis-related case. Pathogen distribution did not differ significantly among non-aHUS, aHUS, and aHUS with/without regular anticomplement therapy (Fisher's Exact Test, P ≥ 0.05; RR analysis). One patient on regular therapy had a rare Elizabethkingia anophelis and Sphingomonas koreensis infection, possibly reflecting aHUS-related immune alterations. Though not statistically significant, these pathogens were rarely seen in non-aHUS cases, suggesting clinical relevance. All three patients on regular therapy discontinued treatment during peritonitis, yet none of the six aHUS PD peritonitis patients experienced instability or exacerbation.
Conclusion
Peritoneal dialysis is viable for aHUS patients with ESRD, including those on anticomplement therapy. Pathogen distribution showed no significant differences across groups. Despite treatment discontinuation during peritonitis, no aHUS patients experienced disease instability. Given the rarity of aHUS, monitoring hemolytic markers remains crucial in PD peritonitis.

title: #867 The association between national dialysis catheter use and kidney transplantation activity
authors: Amun Hofmann
abstract:
Background and Aims
This study investigates the relationship between catheter use among hemodialysis (HD) patients and kidney transplantation activity (KTX) on a national scale, exploring the hypothesis that higher KTX activity may be associated with increased catheter use in a given country. The rationale is based on the idea that shorter waiting times for kidney grafts in could make central venous catheters (CVCs) more favorable as a temporary bridge to transplantation compared to arteriovenous fistulas or grafts which require longer maturation times. A related observation has been reported from the Catalonian Renal Registry but remains to be validated in other countries.
Method
Nine national dialysis and transplant registries (Argentina, Australia, Austria, New Zealand, Portugal, Scotland, Sweden, USA, Turkey) were included in this analysis. Descriptive analysis of baseline information was conducted as well as crude association analyses using correlation analyses and regression to explore the relationship between CVC use and KTX per million inhabitants and for relevant confounders. Multiple regression analyses were performed to adjust for these confounders.
Results
Data from nine different national registries comprising general populations of more than 500mio. people combined was analyzed. CVC use and KTX activity had a weak to moderate positive correlation (r = 0.23, 95% CI 0.07, 0.39) in the crude analysis (Fig. 1). The proportion of CVCs among HD patients increased in all countries during the observational period (Fig. 2). Adjusting for temporal patterns, country-specific factors, and the proportion of female HD patients, there was still strong evidence for a moderate association of CVCs among prevalent HD patients with increasing KTX activity.
Conclusion
The use of CVCs among hemodialysis patients is on the rise globally. However, higher national KTX activity appears to be associated with a moderate increase in CVCs among prevalent HD patients even after adjusting for relevant confounders. This illustrates the intricate relationship between different modalities of kidney replacement therapy as the increased use of CVCs might be reflective of increased KTX rates.

title: #1339 Impact on peritoneal dialysis (PD) uptake through implementation of patient sharing session with chronic kidney disease (CKD) Stage 5 patients—a single centre retrospective review
authors: Kelly Lim; Yong Pey See
abstract:
Background and Aims
Incidence of end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) in Singapore is rising and peritoneal dialysis (PD) is the preferred modality, but uptake of PD remains low. In our centre, patients with advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD) undergo comprehensive one-to-one dialysis counselling on top of usual nephrologist outpatient care but many patients with no contraindication to home therapy continue to avoid PD. One of the common reasons quoted by patients is lack of confidence in performing home PD. Therefore, a PD patient-led sharing session was organised for PD patients to share perspectives with CKD 5 patients preparing to start dialysis.
This study aims to evaluate the impact of patient-led sharing session on CKD-5 patients choosing PD. Secondary aims of study is to evaluate avoidance of tunnelled dialysis catheter for dialysis initiation and patient self-reported knowledge on home dialysis pre- and post-session.
Method
This is a retrospective cohort study of CKD-5 patients who underwent dialysis counselling between 1/3/2022 to 31/3/2024 who have attended patient sharing session compared to those who did not. The primary outcome is patient expressed dialysis modality preference at their first nephrology visit post-sharing session. Proportion of patients started on PD, haemodialysis (HD) and need for tunnelled dialysis catheter insertion between groups was evaluated. Pre- and post-session survey on satisfaction and knowledge on home dialysis therapy was also analysed.
Categorical variables are presented as proportions and analysed using Chi-square test while continuous variables are presented as mean and median as appropriate and analysed with student t-test.
Results
A total of 186 patients were referred to the patient sharing session and sixty-eight patients (37%) attended the session. Amongst patients referred, 23 (12%) were already on HD. Excluding those who were already on dialysis, 70% who attended sharing session (n = 39/56) compared to 53% (n = 57/107) who did not attend chose PD as their preferred modality, P = 0.04. Proportion of patients already on dialysis, tended to stay on HD with only 39% (n = 9/23) converted to PD eventually.
At the end of observation, 70 more patients started on dialysis, with 22% (n = 41/186), 28% (n = 52/186), 4% (n = 7/186) actualising on PD, HD, and conservative care, respectively. More patients who attended sharing session, 77% (20/26) did not need a tunnelled dialysis catheter compared to 61% (27/44), but this did not reach statistical significance, P = 0.18. Amongst those on PD, more attended sharing session 50% (n = 19/38) compared to 40% (n = 22/55) but this was not significant, P = 0.34. More than 83% of patients responding to post session survey reported good review of the session in answering queries on home therapy.
Conclusion
Patient-led sharing session was well received and associated with increased patient acceptance towards choosing PD. However, patients already on hemodialysis at time of sharing are unlikely to change their modality. While avoidance of tunneled dialysis starts and eventual actualization to PD was better with sharing session, the numbers were too small to demonstrate statistical significance.

title: #1393 The impact of intradialytic physical activity on inflammatory markers in patients with diabetes mellitus
authors: Lola Daminova; Sitora Muminova
abstract:
Background and Aims
To evaluate the effect of intradialytic exercise on inflammatory markers in patients with diabetes mellitus.
Method
The study included 103 patients with stage 5 CKD undergoing program hemodialysis. Of these, 33 patients (32.04%) had diabetes as the main etiological cause. The average age of the patients was 54.79 ± 1.27 years. In all subjects, the activity of lipid peroxidation (LPO) processes was assessed by the concentration of malondialdehyde (MDA), markers of inflammation, endothelium-dependent vasodilation (EDVD), indicators of the antioxidant system (AOS).
Results
Before the hemodialysis procedure, the concentration of MDA in patients with DM was significantly higher than in patients with other etiologies of CKD (P < 0.05). However, no differences in MDA concentration were observed between the groups at 60–90 minutes and by the end of the HD session. Physical exercise positively influenced inflammatory markers, EDVD, and the balance of LP/AS in patients with DM and those with other etiologies of CKD. Intradialytic PE contributed to a reduction in inflammatory processes and an improvement in endothelial function. Intradialytic vasculopathy at advanced stages of CKD is primarily influenced by universal mechanisms associated with nephrosclerosis and uremia, which offset the differences caused by the underlying disease.
Conclusion
DM has a limited impact on the development of intradialytic vasculopathy in the context of CKD. This is due to the predominance of uremic and nephrosclerotic pathogenic mechanisms in the advanced stages of the disease. Intradialytic physical exercise demonstrates a pronounced protective effect, improving endothelial function, LP/AS balance, and inflammatory markers regardless of the CKD etiology.

title: #1448 Influence of gender and age on the type of vascular access in SPANISH hemodialysis patients
authors: María Dolores Arenas Jiménez; Julia Audije-Gil; Ramiro Cazar; Ana Botella Lorenzo; Delfina Yetman; Karina Furaz; David Hernán Gascueña; Paula Manso; Luis Nieto; Marc Handel; Fabiola Dapena; María Luz Sánchez Tocino
abstract:
Background and Aims
Sex- and gender-based differences in vascular access are gaining increasing attention in nephrology research. In dialysis, women are more likely to receive central venous catheters (CVC) rather than arteriovenous fistulas (AVF), with female sex identified as a potential risk factor. While this disparity has traditionally been attributed to biological factors, such as smaller vessel diameters in women, it remains uncertain whether it stems from sex-related differences in surgical outcomes or gender bias influencing clinical decision-making. This study aims to analyse sex-related disparities in vascular access among prevalent and incident haemodialysis patients across different geographical areas in Spain and to explore the underlying causes.
Method
A retrospective descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted in March 2022, including prevalent and incident haemodialysis patients from X outpatient centres across three geographical regions of Spain (Castilla y León, Galicia, and Madrid). Differences between men and women in terms of vascular access type (CVC, AVF, prosthesis) and location (radiocephalic AVF, elbow AVF, prosthesis) at haemodialysis initiation and during chronic treatment were analysed, along with potential underlying causes. Demographic and clinical data were obtained through a review of medical history. In patients who refused AVF creation, the reasons for refusal were assessed through targeted questioning. Analyses were performed with IBM SPSS Statistics for Windows, Version 29.0.2.0 (Armonk, NY: IBM Corp). The significance level was set at P < 0.05.
Results
A total of 637 haemodialysis patients were studied, with XX% (XX) being women. title: #1760 Not just an itch: a rare dermatological manifestation in chronic kidney disease
authors: Mafalda Santos Filipe; Ana Rita Almeida; Inês Lopes; Luis Falcao; Isabel Cristina Bettencourt de Simas de Mesquita; Alexandra Chaveiro; Sónia Marina Silva
abstract:
Background and Aims
Reactive perforating collagenosis (RPC) is a rare dermatological condition characterized by transepidermal elimination of extracellular matrix components, particularly damaged collagen, often triggered by trauma, degeneration, or inflammation.
The acquired form of RPC typically occurs in adulthood and is commonly associated with systemic conditions such as diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease (CKD), and certain malignancies, making its recognition crucial in patients with these underlying diseases.
Method
We report a clinical case of RPC diagnosed in a patient with CKD, highlighting the importance of accurate diagnosis for effective therapeutic management.
Results
A 48-year-old Caucasian woman, who works as a preschool teacher, with the diagnosis of CKD stage 5D due to autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD), has been on peritoneal dialysis since June of 2022. Her medical history includes long-standing hypertension treated with irbesartan, a surgically and endovascularly managed cerebral aneurysm in 2006, and a history of preeclampsia and HELLP syndrome during pregnancies (G5P5). She also has a family history of ADPKD (mother and two sisters). Current medications include esomeprazole, acetylsalicylic acid, sertraline, epoetin beta, folic acid, sevelamer, cinacalcet, cholecalciferol, calcitriol, and lactulose.
In December of 2023, she presented with multiple 1–2 mm hyperkeratotic pruritic micropapules symmetrically distributed on the extensor surfaces of her lower limbs. The onset of the lesions coincided with the initiation of atorvastatin therapy, which was discontinued without clinical improvement.
A referral to Dermatology led to a skin biopsy that confirmed the diagnosis of RPC. Treatment was started with acitretin 10 mg, allopurinol 100 mg, and emollients, resulting in initial improvement.
However, the emergence of new and bigger ulcerated lesions (Fig. 1) prompted a multidisciplinary discussion, leading to the decision to initiate phototherapy, which successfully reduced lesions and alleviated pruritus (Fig. 2).
Conclusion
This case underscores the importance of recognizing RPC as a rare but clinically significant skin disorder, particularly in patients with systemic illnesses like CKD. While uncommon, its association with systemic diseases highlights the need for a multidisciplinary approach.
After excluding potential drug-induced causes, a skin biopsy proved essential for an accurate diagnosis. Targeted treatment, including systemic and topical therapies, combined with phototherapy, allowed for significant symptom management. By alleviating the debilitating pruritus and improving the patient's quality of life, this case demonstrates the importance of early diagnosis and individualized management in the treatment of RPC.

title: #2663 Green tea polyphenol sandwich-assisted construction of endothelial biomimetic coatings with HA platform and NO release for hemodialysis access stents to prevent thrombosis and restenosis
authors: Chong Chen
abstract:
Background and Aims
Vascular stent is one of the main means of treating dialysis access stenosis. However, in-stent thrombosis (IST) and in-stent restenosis (ISR) always limit effectiveness of stents in clinical applications. Vascular endothelial cells play an important role in regulating the physiological structure and function of vessels, so endowing vascular stents with the bionic function of endothelial cells is an effective solution to address complications such as IST and ISR.
Method
In this paper, an endothelial bionic coating for stents constructed by layer-by-layer self-assembly method was developed. We used positively charged polyethyleneimine (PEI) and negatively charged hyaluronic acid (HA) as polyelectrolytes, assisted construction by a chelate sandwich of epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) with copper (Cu). The biocompatibility of the coatings was verified by systematic materialogical characterization, in vitro and ex in vivo hemocompatibility experiments, in vitro cell culture experiments, and in vivo experiments of subcutaneous implantation and stent implantation.
Results
The results showed that this strategy was able to improve the loading, stability and homogeneity of the coating through various interactions, such as electrostatic adsorption, hydrogen bonding, π-π stacking, and chemical cross-linking of phenalkamines. The coating was able to synergistically improve the antithrombotic ability, promote the rapidly endothelialization, inhibit intimal hyperplasia and regulate the inflammatory response of the stents with HA and nitric oxide.
Conclusion
This polyelectrolyte endothelial biomimetic coating constructed by metal polyphenol sandwich can effectively reduce complication such as IST and ISR of stents and improve the clinical outcomes of vascular stenting for dialysis access stenosis.

title: #3116 Energy protein wasting syndrome and phase angle: a predictive binomial of morbidity and mortality in hemodialysis
authors: Paloma Puerto Torregrosa; Alba Carmona Llanos; Angela Diaz Torralbo; Jary Lorenzo Perello Martinez; Álvaro Fernández García
abstract:
Background and Aims
The energy protein wasting syndrome (EPWS) encompasses a range of pathologies associated with increased morbidity and mortality, directly related to patients undergoing hemodialysis (HD). The determination of phase angle (PA) has been associated in the literature in a directly proportional manner to the inflammatory/nutritional status of patients. Frailty, malnutrition, and sarcopenia feed back into these patients due to the high protein catabolism induced in part by the technique itself, dietary restrictions, and the aging of our patients, making the detection and treatment of this pathology a necessity that could positively impact the evolution and survival of patients.
To describe the nutritional clinical status of patients in the Chronic Hemodialysis unit of a tertiary hospital. To determine the relationship of PA with nutritional status and morbidity/mortality.
Method
A unicentric cross-sectional study with a 12-month follow-up of patients in the chronic hemodialysis program at our hospital, with a multidisciplinary assessment (Nephrology and Nutrition). Nutritional status (NS) was determined by bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA), obtaining PA and extracellular water ratio (ECWr) as markers of inflammation and hydration, biochemical parameters, and global subjective assessment (GSA) to identify the prevalence of EPWS in our unit.
Results

The mean plasma albumin was 3.78 mg/dl. 39% of patients were diagnosed with moderate-severe malnutrition according to GSA. The mean ECWr was 0.401, which is associated with a state of overhydration. During the study, 18 patients (17.5%) died, with a mean PA of 3.9°. The mean plasma albumin was 3.6 mg/dl, and 38% of these patients presented clinical/analytical EPWS. Additionally, 10 patients (9.7%) underwent transplantation, with a mean PA of 5.49°. The mean plasma albumin was 4.06 mg/dl. Of the active patients in our unit (73), 27% met EPWS criteria based on the KDOQI guidelines of 2020.

PA lower than 4 and mortality: No significant relationship was found between a PA lower than 4 and mortality (P = 0.42), suggests that, within the context of the study, PA does not have a direct impact on mortality. Correlation between PA and mortality: The correlation coefficient of 0.21 indicates a weak positive relationship between PA and mortality, meaning that while there is a slight tendency for lower PA to be associated with higher mortality, the relationship is neither strong nor statistically significant. Degree of malnutrition and risk of mortality: The degree of malnutrition (P < 0.05) is associated with a higher risk of mortality (P = 0.006), and this finding is statistically significant. This suggests that more malnourished patients have a significantly higher risk of dying.
Conclusion
The prevalence of malnutrition in our hemodialysis unit is high and aligns with the range described in the literature. PA is proposed as a predictive variable for prognosis and mortality in these patients, similar to EPWS, showing a high percentage among deceased patients. We believe that advanced nutritional assessment should be part of the initial care for patients in hemodialysis. In conclusion, although low PA is associated with a higher degree of malnutrition, it does not have a direct significant impact on mortality. On the other hand, the degree of malnutrition is strongly related to a higher risk of mortality. However, studies with a larger number of patients are needed in order to continue demonstrating the relationship between these two variables.

title: #3223 Prevalence of uremic pruritus and its impact on quality of life in dialysis patients
authors: Marisse Mae Layson; Hariett Torres
abstract:
Background and Aims
In the general population, pruritus is typically a bothersome but temporary sensation. However, in patients with Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD), it can evolve into a debilitating condition that is recurrent and persistent, severely diminishing quality of life and even potentially affecting survival. A global study revealed that 42% of CKD patients experience moderate to severe uremic pruritus, which is closely associated with sleep disturbances, depression, and reduced well-being. This troubling symptom is especially common in the later stages of renal disease, although detailed case studies remain limited. Moreover, identifying effective treatments for uremic pruritus continues to be a top research priority. This study seeks to determine the prevalence of uremic pruritus in dialysis patients and its impact on quality of life, with the goal of optimizing treatment strategies based on the most efficient and relevant literature.
Method
This is a Prospective Cross-sectional Cohort Study. The study focused on CKD Stage V patients undergoing dialysis, aged 18 to 85 years old, with data collection including demographic details and creatinine trends over a 3-month period. Creatinine clearance was used to confirm CKD Stage V, with eligibility based on consistent eGFR readings below 15 ml/min/1.73 m² during the past three months. Patients whose eGFR fluctuated between CKD Stages III-V at the time of the study or those not on dialysis with potential acute kidney injury were excluded. Eligible participants, both with and without pruritus, were included, and phosphorus levels from the past six months were reviewed. The Kidney Disease Quality of Life-Short Form (KDQOL-SF) was administered to evaluate the impact of uremic pruritus on their quality of life. Data were organized in Excel, and responses were interpreted using the scoring manual for KDQOL-SF version 1.3, followed by statistical analysis.
Results
The study investigated the prevalence of uremic pruritus in 40 dialysis patients with CKD Stage V at Perpetual Succour Hospital. Key findings include Demographics: the average age of patients was 59.25 years, with a higher prevalence of pruritus in males (60%) compared to females (40%); Prevalence: 25 patients (62.5%) reported experiencing uremic pruritus, indicating a significant occurrence of this symptom; Quality of Life: Scores from the Kidney Disease Quality of Life-Short Form (KDQOL-SF™ v1.3) highlighted that dialysis staff encouragement had the highest score (98.75 ± 5.52), while the burden of kidney disease had the lowest (25.31 ± 10.10); Statistical Analysis: Pearson's Chi-square tests found no significant associations between age (P = 0.387) or gender (P = 1.000) and pruritus. However, a significant association with phosphorus levels (P = 0.003) was observed, with 18 patients having elevated phosphorus levels experiencing pruritus compared to only 3 with normal levels. Logistic Regression Analysis: the analysis indicated that elevated phosphorus levels significantly influenced the prevalence of uremic pruritus, with an odds ratio of 10.286 (P = 0.003), suggesting that patients with high phosphorus levels are more than ten times more likely to experience pruritus.
Conclusion
This study emphasizes the significant prevalence of uremic pruritus among patients with Chronic Kidney Disease Stage V undergoing dialysis.
Patients with elevated phosphorus levels are over ten times more likely to experience uremic pruritus compared to those with normal phosphorus levels even in dialysis patients, which adversely affects their quality of life.
Patients with ESRD on dialysis face significant challenges, particularly with the effects and burden of kidney disease, employment, and sleep quality, all of which substantially impact their quality of life. Cognitive function and social interaction are moderately affected. These insights highlight key areas, such as symptom management and sleep improvement, where targeted interventions could further enhance patient well-being.

title: #3401 Neoplasms in patients with renal substitute therapy and evaluation of the use of check point inhibitors in this population
authors: Verónica Ruth Mercado Valdivia; Gallegos Villalobos; Rocío Echarri Carrillo; Gabriel Ledesma Sánchez; Raquel Diaz Mancebo; Sílvia Caldés Ruisánchez; Gilda Carreño Cornejo; Yesika María Amezquita Orjuela; María Covadonga Hevia Ojanguren; Yolanda Hernández Hernández; Antonio Cirugeda García
abstract:
Background and Aims
Checkpoint inhibitors (CPIs) have improved the prognosis of patients with advanced malignancies. However, data on its use in patients on renal replacement therapy (RRT) are scarce because these types of patients have been excluded from trials. Therefore, estimating the risk of safety events and adverse events is really challenging.
To review the prevalence of neoplasms in patients with Renal Replacement Therapy (RRT) in Hemodialysis and Peritoneal Dialysis (PD) in our unit and evaluate the evolution under active treatment with PCI.
Method
Descriptive cross-sectional study in March 2023 in patients on RRT with a history of neoplasia or active neoplasia.
Results
70 patients were analyzed, 56 on hemodialysis and 13 on peritoneal dialysis. Of them, 18 (12 from HD and 6 from PD) were diagnosed with a neoplasia. 35 episodes of different neoplastic disease were evaluated, with a rate of 1.9 neoplasms per patient. Of them, 15 are men, 3 are women and 54% were diagnosed prior to entering TRS. 76% of neoplasms were of solid organ, with urological being the most prevalent at 48%. Three patients had tumor recurrence and 4 patients had metastasis. Regarding treatment, 43% received surgical treatment, 35% conventional chemotherapy and 22% PCI.
The neoplastic evolution per episode is stable in 43%, partial in 17%, complete remission in 34% and progression in 6%. Currently 15 patients have active neoplastic disease. In relation to the use of CPIs in the population with SDB, our short experience has been favorable and the characteristics of the patients, treatment and adverse effects are described in Table 1.
Conclusion
The incidence of neoplasia in our cohort is high, 20%. The rate of neoplasia/patient suggests early screening to optimize treatment. The use of CPIs in hemodialysis in our cohort is favorable.

title: #3672 Unsolved water hemodialysis accidents
authors: Rime Ossmane; Julie Peltier; Hafedh Fessi; Morgane Mailhe; Xavier Lescure; Ziad Massy; Pablo Antonio Urena Torres
abstract:
Background and Aims
Hemodialysis patients are exposed to numerous dialysis machine components including membranes, tubes, dialysate water, dialysate buffer, medications, etc. that can exceptionally induce anaphylactic, allergic or even more severe and life-threatening reactions. Particularly, the associations between numerous complications and hemodialysis water contaminants have been well described, ranging from sometimes benign (pruritus) to deadly (encephalopathy). Chloramine is widely known to cause hemolysis, anemia, and death in hemodialysis patients. Between February and April 2024, we observed 3 deaths from liver and hematologic failure in chronic hemodialysis patients returning from Mali.
Method
This is a descriptive clinical study of 16 patients residing in France who were dialyzed in the same hemodialysis centre in Mali between November 2023 and March 2024. Three patients were aged from 40 to 80 years. They died upon their return to France after being hospitalized in intensive care between February and April 2024, in a state of refractory shock associated to a severe asthenia, gastro-intestinal disorders, thrombocytopenia, haemorrhagic syndrome, and acute cytolysis.
Results
In all patients, microbiological investigations ruled out diagnoses of dengue, malaria, viral hepatitis, arboviruses, and viral haemorrhagic fevers. Toxicological analyses did not reveal any heavy metal poisoning, chloramines, organophosphates, medications or herbal treatments. Post-mortem liver biopsies from 2 patients showed intense hepatocellular necrosis and hepatocellular cholestasis without any pathogen (Fig. 1). A fourth patient, dialyzed in the same hemodialysis centre, died on their return journey, in a state of asthenia and undocumented gastro-intestinal disorders. Three other patients who were also dialyzed in the same centre, during the same period, experienced complications: one patient presented a hemopericardium and severe thrombocytopenia, another patient had hypermagnesemia (1.70 mmol/L) resolving without medication-related cause, and another patient had an unexplained arterial hypotension and thrombocytopenia. The other 9 patients remained clinically asymptomatic. No human-to-human transmission could be demonstrated.
Conclusion
We described 3 deaths due to severe liver and hematologic failure of patients returning after been hemodialyzed in Mali. No bacterial, virus, toxic or pathogenic agent could be demonstrated for the moment. However, these deaths might be related to microbial contaminants in the dialysate, as was described in Brazil in 1998, with a similar scenario and deaths linked to the presence of cyanotoxins in the water treatment circuit.

title: #3950 Lipoprotein a, cardiovascular events, and aortic stenosis in patients on hemodialysis
authors: Carolina Lancho Novillo; Sumaya Ed Daoudy Chagouani; Antonio Luis García Herrera; Ainhoa Jurado Vázquez; Kathia Hortensia Gallegos Aguilar; Pedro Luis Quirós Ganga
abstract:
Background and Aims
In the general population, Lp(a) is an independent risk factor for the occurrence of cardiovascular events and aortic stenosis (AS).
In the general population, 1 in 5 people worldwide have Lp(a) levels greater than 30 mg/dl.
The aim of our study is to analyze the levels of lipoprotein a in a population of patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) on hemodialysis and the association between Lp(a) levels and the presence of cardiovascular disease (CVD) and aortic stenosis (AS) in these patients.
Method
Observational, retrospective, cross-sectional, and descriptive study of a cohort of 76 prevalent patients on chronic hemodialysis in our unit.
We analyzed the presence of CVD defined as ischemic heart disease, peripheral artery disease, and stroke. We also analyzed the presence of significant AS, defined as at least moderate AS (aortic valve area <1.5 cm²).
Results
The characteristics of the patients (n = 76) are shown in Table 1. 40% (30/76) of our patients had Lp(a) levels higher than 30, which is double the estimated prevalence in the general population.
In our series, 6.5% of patients had significant AS (5/76) and 40.7% had CVD (31/76).
Both patients with CVD and those with significant AS had higher Lp(a) levels (30.4 ± 5 vs 47.9 ± 8, P = 0.07) and (35.7 ± 4 vs 65.7 ± 33, P = 0.1), although these differences did not reach statistical significance.
Patients with Lp(a) levels greater than 30 mg/dl showed a trend toward more CVD (53% vs 32%, P = 0.07), while those with levels lower than 15 mg/dl had a protective effect with a trend toward fewer CVD events (27.5% vs 49%, P = 0.054).
Extreme Lp(a) values (greater than 95 mg/dl) were significantly associated with the presence of significant AS (22% vs 4.8%, P = 0.05) and peripheral artery disease (40% vs 10%, P = 0.01).
Conclusion
Patients on hemodialysis have a high prevalence of elevated Lp(a) levels, which are associated with cardiovascular disease and aortic stenosis.

title: #399 Relationship between regularly used laboratory tests and carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity as a marker of arterial stiffness
authors: Luka Varda; Nino Vreča; Renata Smogavec; Nejc Piko; Mohammed Omar; Sebastjan Bevc; Robert Ekart
abstract:
Background and Aims
Carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity (cfPWV) is an important marker of vascular stiffness. Higher values are associated with poor outcomes, including higher morbidity and mortality in hemodialysis (HD) patients. Vascular health in this group of patients is multifactorial. The aim of this analysis was to investigate how cfPWV correlates with regularly used laboratory tests, which could also predict cardiovascular health.
Method
We conducted a single dialysis centre study with randomly selected adult HD patients. To be included in the study, patients had to have been on HD for at least 6 months, with no active clinically relevant infection or malignancy and no hospitalisation in the previous month. Because the cfPWV analysis was performed, patients with moderate or severe aortic stenosis, carotid stenosis, peripheral artery disease and chronic atrial fibrillation were excluded. We performed pre-dialysis measurements of cfPWV (Spygmocor® Atcor Medical, Sydney, Australia). A complete blood count was performed, and blood was drawn before the mid-week dialysis session. Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS® (version 29.0, Chicago, IL, USA). Statistical significance was set at P < 0.05.
Results
Nineteen chronic adult HD patients were included. Median age was 71 years (95% CI (58.7–71.3)), median dialysis vintage 51 months (95% CI (42.2–103.1)), 36.8% were male. Arterial hypertension was present in 18 (94.7%), diabetes mellitus in 5 (26.3%) and heart failure of any kind in 7 (36.8%) patients. We found a statistically significant positive correlation between cfPWV and C-reactive protein (CRP) (rs = 0.562; P = 0.019) and cfPWV and high-sensitive troponin I (hsTnI) (rs = 0.593; P = 0.012). We found a negative correlation between cfPWV and serum phosphate levels (rs = −0.722; P = 0.001) and between cfPWV and serum potassium levels (rs = −0.517; P = 0.034). All median/mean values and correlation coefficients with p values are presented in Table 1.
Conclusion
Even small, clinically insignificant increases in CRP and hsTnI could be associated with higher cfPWV values. Low potassium levels can cause endothelial dysfunction, increase vascular resistance and increase arterial stiffness. On the other hand, adequate potassium intake has previously been associated with better arterial compliance, which could lead to lower PWV and explain our results. While some studies have shown a positive correlation between serum phosphate levels and PWV due to its effect on vascular calcification, mean phosphate levels were not greatly elevated in our patient group, indicating adequate phosphate control and possibly better nutritional status, which could indicate better vascular health.
