title: #2015 Kidney transplantation and cardiovascular risk: the role of the underlying nephropathy
authors: Daniela Picciotto; Elisabetta Bussalino; Chiara Ivaldi; Lucia MacCio; Marta Schermi; Maria Teresa Gandolfo; Angelica Parodi; Francesca Viazzi; Pasquale Esposito
abstract:
Background and Aims
Cardiovascular (CV) complications represent the main cause of mortality among kidney transplanted patients (KTRs). Despite this well-known CV burden, post-transplant CV prevention in KTRs remains overlooked in the clinical practice. Therefore, with the aim of better stratifying the CV risk after transplantation, we analysed if the underlying nephropathy has an impact on the post-transplant CV risk.
Method
Our retrospective analysis includes 240 prevalent adult KTRs in follow-up at the outpatient Nephrology Clinic of San Martino Hospital, Genoa from 2016 to 2021. The cohort includes patients affected by 5 different underlying nephropathies: autoimmune diseases (AID) (n = 20), primary glomerulonephritis (GN) (n = 73), diabetic nephropathy (DN) (n = 32), autosomic polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) (n = 88) and congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract (CAKUT) (n = 27).
The outcomes are: 1. development of major CV events (MACE, defined as myocardial infarction, lower limbs revascularization, stroke and hospitalization for heart failure), 2. all-cause mortality and 3. a composite endpoint represented by MACE and all-cause mortality. Continuous variables are presented as means with standard deviations, while categorical variables are presented as the number of patients with a proportion. Differences between the subpopulations were analysed with ANOVA test or Fischer's test, as appropriate. Kaplan Meier analysis with log-rank test was carried out to compare the event-free survival curves. The relationship between baseline characteristics and time to the occurrence of the three analysed outcomes was assessed by univariate and multivariate Cox regression analysis. A p-value less than 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
Results
Baseline characteristics of the 5 subgroups are reported in Table 1: the cohorts differed significantly in terms of age, gender, previous history of MACE, dyslipidemia, number of transplants and maximum panel reactive antibody test (PRA) titer.
We observed a significant lower event free survival in AID and DN for the three analysed events, while CAKUT showed better survival curves (Fig. 1).
Among the evaluated nephropathies, only AID and DN were statistically significant predictors of time to outcomes’ occurrence, but only AID maintained its significance in the multivariate regression analysis (Table 2). For what concerns other analysed covariates, it is interesting to point out that significance was maintained in the multivariate analysis for the following variables: a previous history of MACE for MACE occurrence, (HR 4.85, IC 95% 2.22–10.60, P = 0.0001), pre-transplant diabetes for overall mortality (HR 6.69, IC 95% 0.92–22.67, P = 0.002) and pre-transplant MACE and diabetes and previous transplants for the composite endpoint (respectively HR 2.61 IC 95% 1.25–5.42 p 0.01; HR 4.36 IC 95% 1.37–13.81 P = 0.01; HR 2.63 IC 95% 1.32–5.26 P = 0.006).
Observing the role of previous immunosuppressive treatments among the 91 patients affected by AID and GN, a prior therapy with steroids was associated with a six-fold (HR 6.17, IC 95% 1.10–34.58, P = 0.04) higher risk in overall mortality and prior use of cyclophosphamide with a three-fold increased risk in developing the composite outcome (HR 3.06, IC 95% 1.07–8.74, P = 0.04).
Conclusion
Underlying nephropathies influence the CV risk even after transplantation. Surprisingly, AID have a similar or even higher risk than DN. This finding could lead to a more tailored CV follow up and thus to an improvement in post-transplantation CV outcomes in these patients.

title: #2079 Outcomes in elderly kidney transplant recipients: a national multicentre study
authors: Hamad Dheir; Erol Demir; Tuba Elif Ozler; Ulkem Cakir; Ayse Sinangil; Feyza Bayrakdar Caglayan; Aygul Celtik; Gizem Kumru; Tolga Yildirim; Bahar Gurlek Demirci; Pinar Ozdemir; Adem Uslu; Mevlut Tamer Dincer; Vural Taner Yilmaz; Yağmur Tahıllıoğlu; Ramazan Danis; Arzu Velioglu; Ebru Sevinç Ok; Mehmet Emin Demir; Ozgur Akin Oto; Şebnem Karakan; Gulay Asci; Abdulmecit Yildiz; Zeynep Akcalİ; Halil Yİldİz; İbrahim Berber; Alaattin Yildiz; Siren Sezer; Huseyin Kocak; Kenan Keven; Huseyin Toz; Aydin Turkmen
abstract:
Background and Aims
Kidney transplantation is the preferred treatment modality for end-stage renal disease in all age groups. However, there is still a lack of data on transplant outcomes in the elderly population. This study aims to evaluate the long-term outcomes of elderly kidney transplant recipients compared with the younger population.
Method
The study was a retrospective, multicentre cohort study and included patients aged 50 years and older who underwent kidney transplantation between 2015 and 2020. Patients with a follow-up period of less than six months were excluded. The elderly group was defined as patients aged 60 years and older, and patients aged 50–59 years were defined as the control group. The study's endpoints were death, death with a functioning graft, allograft loss, and allograft rejection, and the defined endpoints were compared between the groups.
Results
The study included 1305 patients. The median age of the patients was 56 years (50–76), and 39.4% of the participants were female. The median follow-up period was 61.5 (6–113) months in the elderly group and 65.0 (6–115) months in the control group, respectively (P = 0.007). With respect to living kidney transplantation, 79.4% (no. = 313) of the elderly group and 70.4% (no. = 641) of the control group had a living related transplantation (P = 0.001). In the elderly group (n = 396), the prevalence of diabetic nephropathy, deceased donor use, ischaemic heart disease, and induction therapy with basiliximab was significantly higher compared to the control group (P = 0.002, P = 0.001, P = 0.007, P = 0.01, respectively). In terms of the induction agents, ATLG was used in 337 (91.3%) and 772 (95.2%) patients in the elderly and control group; respectively(P = 0.01). The frequency of acute rejection after the first year was lower in the elderly group compared to the control group (P = 0.040). The mortality rate was 77 (21.9%) in the elderly group and 116 (14.4%) in the control group. In addition, graft loss occurred in 16 (4.6%) patients in the elderly group and 53 (6.7%) patients in the control group. Kaplan-Meier analyses showed that the frequency of hospitalization, all-cause mortality, and death with a functioning graft were significantly higher in the elderly group than in the control group (P = 0.029, P = 0.002, P = 0.04, respectively). According to Cox regression analysis, the risk of death in the elderly group was 1.65 times higher than in the control group (95% CI: 1.19–2.30, P = 0.002). In addition, the risk of death with a functioning graft increased 1.04-fold for each year increase after the age of 50 years (95% CI: 1.013–1.07, P = 0.003).
Conclusion

title: #3429 Biopsy-based transcriptomics allow earlier detection of rejection, gradual phenotyping and monitoring of anti-rejection treatment interventions in kidney transplant recipients: lessons from follow-up biopsies
authors: Lukas Weidmann; Florian Westphal; Dusan Harmacek; Elena Rho; Kai Castrezana Lopez; Britta George; Seraina Von Moos; Thomas Schachtner
abstract:
Background and Aims
Transcriptomics in biopsy-based diagnosis of kidney allograft rejection has the potential to detect rejection earlier than histopathology, offer continuous rejection phenotyping, and quantify disease activity and injury degrees to reflect anti-rejection treatment responses.
Method
From 2018 to 2024, we investigated 85 biopsy series (each consisting of a baseline and corresponding follow-up biopsy) assessed by histopathology (Banff classification 2022) and the Molecular Microscope Diagnostic System (MMDx).
Results
Baseline biopsies showed histological rejection in 47/85 (55%) cases, with concordant molecular rejection in 81%. Follow-up biopsies, obtained after a median of 8 months (IQR 4, 17), identified histological rejection in 13/38 (34%) cases without full histological rejection at baseline. These baseline cases had significantly higher rejection classifier (median 0.17 vs. 0.03, P = 0.01) and all antibody-mediated rejection (AMR) archetype scores (median 0.23 vs. 0.09, P = 0.007) than those without histological rejection at follow-up (n = 25). A gradual rejection phenotyping along the AMR and T cell-mediated rejection (TCMR) classifier activity identified molecular patterns of resolution and progression at follow-up. Cases with mixed molecular AMR/TCMR showed resolution of the AMR classifier activity only, if predominant TCMR archetype clusters were present at baseline. Treatment responses in anti-rejection interventions for molecular TCMR (pulsed steroids with/without T cell-depletion) were measurable through TCMR classifier scores, while interventions for molecular AMR showed significant reductions in AMR classifiers (P = 0.036) beyond histological changes.
Conclusion
Biopsy-based transcriptomics differentiate early rejection signs along histologically ambiguous baseline biopsies, aid in gradual AMR/TCMR phenotyping, and provide a tool for monitoring treatment effects after conventional anti-rejection therapies.

title: #3743 Tocilizumab for treatment of chronic active antibody-mediated rejection in kidney transplant recipients
authors: Nadzeya Rapetskaya; Kirill Komissarov; Margarita Dmitrieva; Aleh Kalachyk
abstract:
Background and Aims
Chronic active antibody-mediated rejection (cAAMR) is one of the leading causes of late allograft failure in kidney transplant recipients. However, there is no current consensus on cAAMR management. Less than a half of patients in Europe who develop cAAMR receive treatment beyond optimization of immune suppression. Tocilizumab, monoclonal antibody against IL-6, appears to be a possible treatment strategy. We report our single-center experience of using tocilizumab in patients with cAAMR.
Method
The prospective study was performed from July 2022 to October 2024. 13 kidney transplant recipients with biopsy-proven cAAMR who had been prescribed tocilizumab 8 mg/kg monthly were included. All patients were followed for at least 12 months after the last tocilizumab infusion clinically and by laboratory tests for graft outcomes.
Results
CAAMR developed at a median of 59 [23; 69] months posttransplant. 7 patients completed 12 infusions of tocilizumab and underwent control biopsy that showed significant improvement in microvascular inflammation (MVI) scores (P = .04). There was no significant change in serum creatinine, estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and proteinuria during the follow-up. There was a nonsignificant trend towards DSA titers decrease post-treatment with tocilizumab. 6 patients discontinued tocilizumab infusions, 3 of them due to moderate to severe treatment-related complications: cytomegalovirus infection, pneumocystis pneumonia, drug-induced hepatitis. 2 patients started dialysis during treatment, however they had eGFR less than 30 mL/min/1.73 m2 at the start of treatment.
Conclusion
Treatment with tocilizumab was associated with a reduction of rejection activity by improvement of MVI scores and stabilization of allograft function in kidney transplant recipients with cAAMR.

title: #406 Association between skeletal muscle mass and bone mineral density in kidney transplant recipients: a retrospective cohort study
authors: Morikuni Nishihira
abstract:
Background and Aims
Kidney transplant recipients have a higher prevalence of osteoporosis and osteopenia compared to the general population. Sarcopenia, characterized by loss of skeletal muscle mass and strength, is also common in this population and is hypothesized to impact bone health. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between skeletal muscle mass index (SMI) and bone mineral density (BMD) in kidney transplant recipients, addressing sex-specific differences and other related factors.
Method
This retrospective observational cohort study included 371 kidney transplant recipients at least six months post-transplantation, followed at a single center for kidney transplant follow-up in Japan. BMD was measured at the femoral neck using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA), while SMI was assessed using bioelectrical impedance analysis. Multivariate regression models were employed to analyze the independent association of SMI with BMD, adjusted for factors such as eGFRcysC and 25-hydroxy vitamin D (25(OH)D). Analyses were stratified by sex to account for biological differences.
Results
Of the 371 participants (65.4% male, median age 52 years), SMI was independently associated with BMD across both sexes. In multivariate analyses, eGFRcysC, 25(OH)D, and SMI were significant predictors of BMD. Additional sex-specific findings included hemoglobin as a significant factor in men, while age and serum albumin were influential in women. Neither dialysis history nor time since transplantation was significantly associated with BMD. Stratified comparisons by SMI and 25(OH)D levels highlighted their substantial impact on BMD.
Conclusion
Low SMI is independently associated with reduced BMD in kidney transplant recipients, underscoring the interplay between muscle and bone health. The findings suggest the importance of incorporating muscle mass evaluation into routine post-transplant care to better manage osteoporosis risk. Future prospective studies are warranted to explore whether interventions targeting skeletal muscle can improve BMD and reduce fracture risk in this population.

title: #618 Hydroxyproline as a urinary biomarker in renal transplantation
authors: María Carmen Ruiz Fuentes; María José Torres Sánchez; Elena Clavero García; Noelia Risquez Chica; María José Espigares Huete; Karla Ximena Espinoza Muñoz; Rosemary Wangensteen
abstract:
Background and Aims
Interstitial fibrosis/tubular atrophy in kidney transplantation is an unspecific lesion induced by immune and non-immune factors, which determines the progression of chronic kidney disease. Hydroxyproline is an imino acid in relation to collagen metabolism, a fundamental component of fibrosis. The aim of this study was to assess hydroxyproline in urine microvesicles as a marker of fibrosis in the renal transplant patient.
Method
Observational cross-sectional study in 46 renal transplant patients who had undergone renal biopsy with diagnostic intention, and 19 healthy controls. Clinical, histological and laboratory variables were collected at the time of marker determination and 2 years later (renal function). Hydroxyproline was measured in urine microvesicles.
Results
Renal transplant patients showed higher microvesicular concentration of hydroxyproline com-pared to the control group (median (interquartile IQR range): 28.024 (5.53) ng/ml vs 2.51 (1.16) ng/ml, P < 0.001. In the transplanted patients, patients in whom biopsy showed some score of total cortical parenchymal inflammation (ti) displayed significantly higher concentration of hydroxy-proline in urine microvesicles than those patients who did not score for cortical parenchymal inflammation (29.91 ± 2.797 ng/ml vs 22.72 ± 8.697 ng/ml, P = 0.034). No significant correlation was observed between urinary markers and serum creatinine, calcium and parathyroid hormone (PTH).
Conclusion
Concentration of hydroxyproline in urinary microvesicles is increased in renal transplant patients relative to healthy controls. Hydroxyproline in urinary microvesicles is a marker of chronic renal inflammation in transplanted patients and further studies are required to confirm this finding in other pathologies, as well as the association with fibrosis and evolution of renal function.

title: #812 Long-term changes in kidney function following living donor nephrectomy: a retrospective cohort study
authors: Monika Vitkauskaitė; Sigita Anisko; Elita Gruodytė; Loreta Vareikienė; Artūras Vinikovas; Marius Miglinas
abstract:
Background and Aims
Living kidney donation offers superior outcomes, including better graft and patient survival, compared to deceased donor transplantation. However, despite its benefits, it remains ethically, morally, and medically complex, relying on the expectation that donor risks are outweighed by the psychological benefits of altruism and improved recipient health. Kidney donation inevitably reduces functional kidney parenchyma, determining a reduction of kidney function. Therefore, the aim of this study was to evaluate changes in kidney function (eGFR) over time in living kidney donors following nephrectomy.
Method
This was a retrospective cohort study. Between 1999 and 2024, 163 living donor nephrectomies were performed at Vilnius University Hospital Santaros Klinikos, Lithuania. Exclusion criteria included incomplete data at the time of donation or loss to follow-up. We analyzed clinical and laboratory data from 105 donors. Using the CKD-EPI formula, we calculated the estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) before nephrectomy and at 6 months, 1 year, 5 years, and 10 years after donation. Categorical variables were summarized as frequencies and percentages, while continuous variables were presented as means with standard deviations (SD) for normally distributed data or medians with interquartile ranges (IQR) for non-normally distributed data. A linear mixed model was used to assess changes in eGFR over time following nephrectomy. Statistical significance was set at P < 0.05. Data analysis was conducted using IBM SPSS Statistics Version 30.0.
Results
The mean (SD) age of donors was 52.8 (9.0) years. Female donors accounted for 62.9% (n = 66) of all donors, and all donors were related to the recipients. Only one donor died from causes unrelated to the donation. The median eGFR (IQR) for donors before nephrectomy was 93.3 (79.0–102.4) ml/min/1.73 m². The analysis of kidney function (eGFR) over time following nephrectomy revealed a significant decline in eGFR (F = 36.23, P < 0.001). The most pronounced decline occurred within the first 6 months post-nephrectomy (B = 57.37, P = 0.006). The median eGFR (IQR) after 6 months was 65.9 ml/min/1.73 m² (82.7–55.9). Beyond this point, changes at 1 and 5 years were not statistically significant. Age had a significant main effect (F = 2.17, P = 0.002) on eGFR, while sex alone was not a significant predictor (F = 0.32, P = 0.574). However, the interaction between time and sex was significant (F = 2.639, P = 0.039), indicating that the pattern of eGFR change over time differs between males and females.
Conclusion
Our findings suggest that the most critical period for monitoring kidney function is within the first 6 months post-nephrectomy, and individualized follow-up strategies may be required based on sex-specific patterns of kidney function change.

title: #819 Erythropoietin modulates redox homeostasis and immunomodulatory functions of monocytes in kidney transplant recipients
authors: Nina Görlich; Mehek Ningoo; Laura Espinar Barranco; Diana Metzke; Cayetana Gisbert Vilanova; Pouneh Mirkheshti; Francisco Fueyo Gonzalez; Miguel Fribourg; Philipp Enghard; Paolo Cravedi
abstract:
Background and Aims
Erythropoietin (EPO) has been shown to exert immunomodulatory effects beyond its role in erythropoiesis. Immune cells, particularly monocytes, undergo metabolic reprogramming during activation, which affects their function. This study aims to investigate the immunomodulatory effects of EPO in human kidney transplantation, with a focus on elucidating the effects of EPO on the metabolic state of immune cell subsets using redox homeostasis as a proxy.
Method
Healthy donor (HD) peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) and kidney transplant recipients (KTR) PBMC (without EPO treatment in vivo) were treated with EPO in vitro to assess direct EPO effects. Additionally, a cohort of stable KTR (n = 34) with anemia (Hb < 10.0 g/dL) was enrolled and studied before and after 4 weeks of EPO therapy. As a proxy for redox set point, glutathione (GSH) levels were monitored with FJF375, a novel small molecule selective GSH fluorescent sensor developed in the group. Immune phenotyping, cytokine quantification, and bulk RNA sequencing were performed to explore molecular mechanisms of EPO's effects.
Results
EPO treatment in vitro induced metabolic alterations in monocytes, as detected by our GSH sensor. While no significant changes were observed in T cells or B cells, monocytes significantly decreased GSH baseline levels after EPO treatment in vitro (P = 0.005). KTR treated with EPO in vivo exhibited immune modulation associated with monocyte phenotypes. A significant decrease in GSH levels in monocytes (P = 0.017) was observed, correlating with a marked reduction of TNF-α release (P = 0.0037). RNA sequencing deconvolution analysis further revealed a tendency toward increased IL-4 levels, an anti-inflammatory cytokine associated with M2 macrophages.
Conclusion
EPO treatment induces cell-specific changes in GSH levels in monocytes, but not in T cells or B cells. EPO may influence immune cell function in KTR by promoting a shift in monocyte phenotyping from a pro-inflammatory M1 profile to an immunomodulatory M2 profile through alterations in redox homeostasis. Future studies are planned to investigate the functional consequences of these metabolic alterations in immune cells and their potential implications for transplantation outcomes.

title: #3261 Impact on accessibility to renal transplantation in hipersensitized recipients with antigen avoidance based allocation in argentina
authors: Liliana Bisigniano; Daniela Hansen Krogh; Viviana Tagliafichi; Carlos Soratti; Ariel Antik; Pablo Miguel Raffaele
abstract:
Background and Aims
Patients with hypersensitivity (HP) are less likely to undergo transplantation. In August 2023, the Argentine Authority of Organ Procurement and Transplantation (INCUCAI) modified the regulations for distribution on the waiting list for renal transplantation, resulting in a change to the prioritisation of hypersensitised patients (HP). Patients presenting anti-HLA antibodies by solid-phase assay in excess of 85% are assigned renal donors as a priority in the distribution of deceased donors. Previously, the prioritisation criteria included the awarding of a supplementary score to the general waiting list score, which was comprised of time on dialysis and HLA match. However, this did not take into account the presence of antigens to be avoided in the donor. The aim of the present study is to evaluate the accessibility to transplantation of this group of patients as well as the results of patient and graft survival and the incidence of acute rejection.
Method
A cohort comparison study was conducted to examine the impact of the new regulations, implemented between the pre-period (10 November 2022 to 14 August 2023) and the post-period (15 August 2023 to 16 June 2024). The patients who received a deceased donor renal transplant were the subject of analysis. The pre-period cohort comprised 111 patients, while the post-period cohort comprised 236 patients. The prevalence and percentage of transplants (calculated on the total incidents on the waiting list of that period) of HP are described. The following transplant outcome variables were compared between both periods: graft loss and post-transplant death.
Results
A total of 5,420 patients are currently awaiting renal transplantation, of whom 546 have been identified as being hypersensitive. There were no statistically significant differences in dialysis time or cold ischemia time between the two groups. Similarly, there was no difference in post-transplant mortality between the two groups. However, there was an increase in the transplantation of hypersensitised patients following the modification of the regulations, The new policy resulted in a significant improvement in access to transplantation for hypersensitized patients on the waiting list, with 23% of these individuals gaining access, compared to the 6% access rate under previous criteria. Furthermore, the implementation of the new policy led to a notable reduction in the rate of rejection (P < 0.0001) and graft loss (P < 0.0001)—as illustrated in Table 1.
Conclusion
The implementation of an antigen-avoidance-based renal allocation policy for hypersensitised patients was associated with a significant increase in access to transplantation, a reduction in the incidence of acute rejection and graft loss.

title: #3275 Urinary metabolomics evaluation in sensitized kidney transplant recipients
authors: Maria Styliani Trivyza; Panagiota Georgiopoulou; Stella Chasapi; Theodoros Ntrinias; Marios Papasotiriou; Angeliki Vittoraki; Georgios Spyroulias; Dimitrios Goumenos; Evangelos Papachristou
abstract:
Background and Aims
Chronic kidney disease is a global public health problem and treatment options for patients with end-stage kidney disease are either dialysis or kidney transplantation. Kidney transplant recipients (KTRs) require long term monitoring of allograft function which is traditionally based on serial measurements of serum creatinine and proteinuria. However, when changes in these variables become evident, histological alterations might be irreversible. It is therefore of outmost importance to develop non-invasive, sensitive biomarkers to timely monitor allograft function. As kidneys are organs with a very high metabolic rate, a metabolomics approach could provide insights for early detection of systematic changes in KTRs and has the potential for monitoring allograft function.
Method
In this cross-sectional study we analyzed the urine metabolomics fingerprint of KTRs with Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) spectroscopy. We studied eleven KTRs with preformed or de novo donor specific antibodies (DSA+) and nine KTRs without donor specific antibodies (DSA−). Urine samples were collected and centrifuged, the supernatant was collected from each sample and stored at −80 °C until NMR analysis. Analysis of the samples was performed using a Bruker Avance III HD 700 MHz NMR spectrometer equipped with a cryogenically cooled TCI probe. For each urine sample one-dimensional 1H NMR NOESY presat experiment and a two-dimensional (2D) J-resolved experiment was performed. In multivariate statistical analysis the method of Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was used and the Partial Least Squares-Discriminant Analysis (PLS-DA) was chosen as the main supervised method for reducing the number of variables.
Results
Baseline kidney function (eGFR) of DSA(+) and DSA(−) KTRs was similar (57 ± 27.3 vs. 63 ± 22 ml/min/1.73 m2, P = 0.54). Following multivariate statistical analysis with PCA and PLS-DA, variable importance in projection (VIP) scores ranging from 3.5 to 2.2 suggested that 1-Methylnicotinamide, glucose, histamine, 2-Hydroxyisovalerate, citrate, threonate, myo-inositol are the most important variables in descending order. Univariate analysis was further performed on the successfully identified metabolites, targeting only the non-overlapping metabolites’ peaks for integration and non-parametric Kruskal–Wallis test, followed by a false discovery rate (FDR) correction was conducted. In total, 21 metabolites were detected and all of them were expressed with higher intensity in the DSA(–) group. None of these metabolites, however, was found to be statistically significant, with a p-value ranging from 0.082 in formate to 0.934 in acetate.
Conclusion
Urine metabolites including 1-Methylnicotinamide, glucose, histamine, 2-Hydroxyisovalerate, citrate, threonate and myo-inositol tend to differ between KTRs with and without DSAs, even though no statistical significance was ascertained in this study.

title: #3349 Experiences of performing ABO-incompatible kidney transplantation in Argentina
authors: Pablo Miguel Raffaele; Adriana Margarita Lituma; Liliana Bisigniano; Nadia Viviana Fretes; Ignacio Gru; Marcela Fortunato
abstract:
Background and Aims
Living donor kidney transplantation is the best renal replacement therapy for patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD). Thirty percent of potential living donors are rejected due to human leukocyte antigen (HLA) antibodies of ABO incompatibility. In Latin America, few centers, including ours, have initiated this type of transplantation. This study reviews our experience with a case series of ABOi transplantation.
Method
Retrospective, observational and descriptive cross-sectional study conducted between 2015 and 2023 in patients with ABO incompatible kidney transplantation. Immunological risk was classified according to isoagglutinin titer as low <1/8, moderate 1/16–1/64 and high 1/128–1/256. Isoagglutinin titration was performed according to haemotherapy service standards (semi-quantitative titration technique). The desensitization protocol included rituximab, plasma exchange (PEX) and intravenous immunoglobulin. All patients were monitored post-renal transplantation with isoagglutinins daily during hospitalization and weekly on an outpatient basis until day +15. Data are presented as absolute and relative frequencies for categorical variables and as medians (IQR) or means ± SD for continuous variables.
Results
Baseline donor and recipient characteristics are summarized in Table 1. The mean baseline anti-ABO IgM/IgG antibody titres were 1:32 and 1:64, respectively (range, 1:4–1:128). Our patients received an average of six pre-transplant PEX sessions and one post-transplant session (Table 2). Overall patient and graft survival at 1 year was 90%. The mean GFR was 74 ± 18 ml/min/1.73 m2. Two out of ten patients had acute post-transplant rejection (+14 days and +7 months post-transplant). Infection was the most common complication in ABOi kidney transplant patients. One patient died and lost the graft due to human herpesvirus 6 (Table 3).
Conclusion
ABOi kidney transplantation is a viable option in our setting for those who do not have a compatible donor. Strengthening these non-conventional modalities of kidney transplantation will increase the number of living donors, organ self-sufficiency, reduce the waiting list and decrease mortality in chronic kidney patients. However, high costs and infections remain major concerns. It is of common interest to promote the development of crossed kidney transplants to limit incompatible transplants.

title: #3618 Three years of kidney transplantation in the Yaounde General Hospital, Cameroon
authors: Aristide Eric Nono Tomta
abstract:
Background and Aims
Hemodialysis has long been the unique long-term kidney replacement therapy available in Cameroon. Only few financially viable patients could benefit from kidney transplantation abroad. In 2021 Yaounde General Hospital began a living related donor kidney transplantation program in collaboration with the Hopitaux Universitaire de Genève. We hereby present, the strengths and weaknesses of the program.
Method
This is an observational cross sectional study of kidney transplantations done in the Yaounde General Hospital from 2021 to 2024. At the beginning of the program compatibility tests were done at the Geneva University Hospitals and a transplant surgeon from the same hospital performed the transplantation with a local surgical team of vascular surgeons and urologists. Selection of donors and recipient, their evaluation prior to transplantation and their follow-up was done by the local team and the Geneva team by videoconference. Most of the tests were done in the hospital and few viral serology tests were done abroad. Renal pathology was not available. The whole process was free of charge for the patient. In the last year, the hospital owns a Luminex and therefore performs compatibility tests locally and in the same last year, the local surgical team solely performs the whole transplantation procedure.
Results
A total of fourteen patients have been transplanted (1st year: 04, 2nd year: 03, and 3rd year: 07), with 07 (50%) recipients and 09 (64.3%) donors being males. It was the first transplant for all recipients. The mean age of recipients was 30.57 ± 6.06 years and mean age of donors was 34.85 ± 9.77 years. Dialysis vintage ranged from 3 months to 14 years with a median of 7 [3–11] years. Concerning the relationship between donors and recipients, we had 7 brothers, 3 sisters, 1 cousin, 1 mother, 1 uncle and 1 aunt. In all, 5 pairs were HLA identical (one homozygous twins), 6 pairs HLA semi-identical and 3 HLA different. There was no donor specific antibody. The homozygous twin received no immunosuppressive therapy. Twelve recipients received basiliximab and one thymoglobulin as induction. In addition to mycophenolic acid, eleven received cyclosporine, and two received tacrolimus as maintenance therapy. Corticosteroids were stopped at 6 months for all the recipients. No cases of acute rejection were recorded. All but one patient recovered normal kidney function after 2 weeks of transplantation. Two immediate complications were observed and successfully corrected. Two early complications occurred in two patients (one lymphocele with ureteral compression treated by laparoscopy and one delayed wound healing). Three female recipients experienced a single episode of urinary tract infection while two had recurrent urinary tract infection. The kidney function of all the recipients has been stable since their surgery. One of the female recipients (homozygote twin) gave birth to a healthy baby after 17 months of the transplant.
Conclusion
Three years after the beginning of the first transplantation program in Cameroon, the outcome of patients is satisfactory. Local expertise has grown with total independence. However, the absence of renal pathology remains the main issue.

title: #1101 Kidney transplantation outcomes of racial minority groups in a Central European setting: a retrospective cohort study
authors: Zuzana Pichova; Ivan Zahradka; Istvan Modos; Filip Tichanek; Vera Kocova; Ondrej Viklicky
abstract:
Background and Aims
It has been previously reported that Caucasian population has superior kidney transplantation outcomes compared to other racial groups, especially in the US. Data from the Czech Republic are lacking.
Method
In this single centre retrospective cohort study, we analysed 2315 kidney transplant recipients between years 2014–2024 and identified 24 ethnic minority patients (Asians n = 20, African Europeans n = 4). A control group consisting of Caucasian population was established by propensity score matching in a 3:1 ratio considering recipient and donor age, recipient sex, body mass index (BMI), maximum panel-reactive antibody (PRA max), number of HLA mismatches, living donor, time on dialysis and order of transplantation. The primary endpoint was a composite of poor graft function (defined as a persistent decline in eGFR <40 ml/min/1.73 m2), graft failure, rejection and all-cause mortality at 1- and 5- years post-transplant. Secondary outcomes were individual components of primary endpoint, eGFR at 1- year post-transplant and incidence of delayed graft function. Furthermore, we compared the differences in time on dialysis prior to transplantation, time on the waiting list prior to transplantation and time from starting dialysis to being wait-listed between the racial minority group and the Caucasian population.
Results
There was no difference in the incidence of primary composite endpoint between the racial minority group and the Caucasian control group at 1-year (16.7 % vs. 19.4 %, respectively; P = 0.84) and 5-years post-transplant (20.8 % vs. 26.4%, respectively; P = 0.751). There was also no difference in the incidence of secondary outcomes. However, we found that the racial minority group spent longer time on dialysis before being wait-listed compared to the Caucasian population [median 1.2 years (IQR 0.9–1.9) vs. 0.8 years (IQR 0.26–1.64), respectively; P = 0.030]. Furthermore, there was also an evident trend towards longer time on dialysis prior to transplantation in the racial minority group compared to the Caucasian group [median 2.4 years IQR (1.4–4.3) vs. 1.75 years (IQR 0.74–3.3), respectively; P = 0.051] and on the waiting list prior to transplantation [median 1.2 years IQR (0.34–2.7) in racial minority group vs. median 0.56 years IQR (0.16–1.56) in Caucasian population; P = 0.094].
Conclusion
In this study, kidney transplant outcomes were similar between the racial minority group and a well-matched Caucasian control group. As the Czech Republic has universal healthcare coverage, these results suggest that the previously reported discrepancies of transplantation outcomes in racial minority groups likely stem from socioeconomic factors, different healthcare coverage across countries, potential discrimination and language barrier influencing access to healthcare rather than biologic and genetic factors. However, racial minority groups are still disadvantaged by longer time on dialysis before reaching transplantation. Further study of underlying factors is necessary.

title: #3814 The unexplored impact of SGLT2 inhibitors in diabetic kidney donors: a multicenter retrospective study
authors: Arshdeep Singh Singh; Florentino Villanego; Verónica López; María José Torres-Sánchez; Román Hernández Gallego; Luis Alberto Vigara; José Manuel Amaro; Blanca Serrano Muñoz; Teresa María GarcíaÁlvarez; Pablo Castro; María Auxiliadora Mazuecos Blanca
abstract:
Background and Aims
The demand for kidney transplantation (KT) remains high, with limited availability of suitable organs. In Spain, an increasing trend in utilizing kidneys from diabetic (DM) donors has been observed. Despite this, the rate of kidney discard from DM donors is rising due to concerns over poorer graft function and recipient outcomes. Recent advancements in DM management, such as sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors, have demonstrated efficacy in improving glycemic control and altering the progression of DM, yet their impact on KT outcomes from DM donors remains unexplored. This multicenter retrospective study aims to evaluate the role of SGLT2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) in DM kidney donors, focusing on graft survival, recipient survival, and proteinuria.
Method
We performed a multicenter retrospective cohort study from the KT recipients who received a kidney from a DM donor with at least 5 years of diagnosed DM and who had undergone SGLT2i therapy for 6 months or more. Study period was from 01/01/2016 to 31/12/2023. Data were collected from the Andalusian centers that perform KT and Badajoz. Three groups were defined and a case-control study was conducted in a 1:1:1 ratio. Group 1 (cases): DM donor with SGLT2i therapy, group 2 (control): DM donor without SGLT2i therapy and group 3 (control): non-DM donors. Donors were selected according to transplant date, donor type, age and duration of DM evolution.
We collected clinical and demographical data from donors and recipients. Biopsy scores as well as glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and proteinuria, were compared between the three defined groups. Finally, recipient survival was also analyzed.
Results
Thirty-six recipients were included in each group. Non-DM kidney donors exhibited significantly better histological quality, with a median biopsy score of 2, compared to DM donors treated with SGLT2i 4 and those untreated 4 (P < 0.001). Arteriolar hyalinosis was significantly higher in DM donors receiving SGLT2i than in those without (1 vs. 0; P = 0.013). Other histological parameters showed no significant differences among the groups.
eGFR at all follow-up points was slightly better in non-DM donors but did not reach statistical significance. However, proteinuria was significantly lower in DM donors treated with SGLT2i at 1 year (P = 0.008) after KT, suggesting a potential protective effect. One year post-KT, eGFR was similar between DM donors treated with SGLT2i (44.6 ± 12.96 mL/min) and those untreated (42.3 ± 17.8 mL/min) compared to non-DM donors (50.9 ± 21.4 mL/min) (P = 0.253).
Long-term outcomes revealed that 5-year graft survival remained high across all groups (100% in non-DM donors, 85.7% in DM donors with SGLT2i, and 89% in those without). However, 5-year recipient survival was markedly lower in DM donors without SGLT2i compared to those treated and non-DM donors (58.5% vs 84.2% vs 83.4%, P = 0.499).
Conclusion
SGLT2i in DM kidney donors were significantly associated with lower proteinuria and may improve recipient survival compared to untreated DM donors. Although initial findings are promising, further studies with larger cohorts and longer follow-up are necessary to better elucidate the impact of SGLT2i on long-term graft and recipient survival outcomes.

title: #2892 Perioperative dapagliflozin does not associate increased risk of urinary tract infections in incident kidney transplant patients
authors: Paula Ardura; Teresa Ronda Serrat; Aya Moultamis; Beatriz Fernández Carbajo; María Fernández Martín; María Martínez Manrique; Arturo Lorenzo Chapatte; Ana Lucía Valencia Peláez; Alicia Mendiluce; Armando Coca Rojo
abstract:
Background and Aims
Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) have shown promising potential to reduce ischemia-reperfusion injury through multiple potential mechanisms, such as downregulation of inflammation, improved autophagy or regulation of mitochondrial dynamics. Ischemia-reperfusion injury is one of the main drivers of early graft dysfunction after kidney transplantation (KT). As such, SGLT2i could provide renal protection against this type of renal damage. However, their use in the peritransplant period is limited due to the potential risk of increasing the incidence of urinary tract infections (UTI) in immunosuppressed patients. In the present study we aim to compare rates between patients who received SGLT2i in the early peritransplant period vs historical controls.
Method
Prospective, uncontrolled pilot study of consecutive, incident KT patients that were treated with dapagliflozin 10 mg daily, starting immediately before surgery and continuing until completing the first post-transplant week or graft failure. All patients provided written informed consent. Subjects with liver dysfunction, known allergy to SGLT2i, programmed for live-donor or multiorgan kidney transplantation or unable to provide informed consent were excluded. All patients received a preoperative dose of 2g cefazolin as UTI prophylaxis. The primary outcome was the development of UTI during index hospitalization, defined as either a positive urine culture and/or fever plus other clinical findings suggestive of UTI. For comparison purposes, a retrospective sample of consecutive patients that received a KT prior to the start of this study was selected as the control group.
Results
Demographic and clinical characteristics of the study sample are summarized in Table 1. Treated patients and controls showed similar rates of UTI (18.8 vs 18.6%, respectively) and prescription of antibiotic therapy for UTI (21.7 vs 20%, respectively). Results of urine cultures and type of administered antibiotic therapy are shown in Fig. 1A and 1B.
Conclusion
We observed no differences in the incidence of UTI or prescription of antibiotics for UTI between treated patients and controls. In the study sample, perioperative treatment with dapagliflozin associated no increased risk of UTI or prescription of antibiotic therapy due to UTI, compared to historical controls.

For comparison purposes, a retrospective sample of consecutive patients that received a KT prior to the start of this study was selected as the control group.

Demographic and clinical characteristics of the study sample are summarized in Table 1. Results of urine cultures and type of administered antibiotic therapy are shown in Fig. 1A and 1B.
Conclusion
We observed no differences in the incidence of UTI or prescription of antibiotics for UTI between treated patients and controls. title: #218 Vitamin D supplementation can reduce the levels of soluble T-cell Ig-mucin-3 and HMGB1 in kidney transplant recipients
authors: Bin-Qi Yang; Yangjuan Bai; Yamei Li; Zeng-Jie Wang; Yuan-Zhen He; Yun-Ying Shi
abstract:
Background and Aims
Kidney transplantation is the most effective treatment for end stage renal disease (ESRD). However, the long-term survival rates of graft kidneys have not significantly improved. It has been found that the expression and interaction of T cell immunoglobulin mucin 3 (Tim-3) and high mobility group protein B1 (HMGB1) play a crucial role in cellular immune regulation and inflammatory response in recent years. Further investigation is needed to explore the changes in Tim-3/HMGB1 expression in kidney transplant recipients (KTRs) and their correlation with graft function.
Method
A prospective cohort of 337 KTRs treated with or without Vitamin D were enrolled. Serum levels of vitamin D metabolism and the levels of soluble Tim-3 (sTim-3), HMGB1, renal graft function, and routine blood biomarkers were tested and dynamically tracked within 12 months post-transplant. Multivariate regression models were used to explore the factors influencing sTim-3 and HMGB1 levels after kidney transplantation.
Results
The supplementation of vitamin D effectively increased the serum concentration of vitamin D in KTRs in the treated group. During the course of supplementation, the treated group exhibited a gradual increase in eGFR levels, and the levels of sTim-3 and HMGB1 in the treatment group showed a significantly decreasing trend with vitamin D supplementation compared to untreated group. Multifactorial regression analysis revealed a significant association between post-transplant vitamin D supplementation and a decrease in post-transplant sTim-3 and HMGB1 levels.
Conclusion
KTRs receiving regular post-transplant vitamin D supplementation experienced a significant decrease in sTim-3 and HMGB1 levels, along with a notable increase in eGFR and vitamin D levels. Multifactorial regression analysis indicates that vitamin D supplementation administered after transplantation is an independent predictor of sTim-3 and HMGB1 Levels at 12 months post-transplant.

title: #1423 Impact of vitamin D supplementation on kidney transplant recipients: a systematic review and meta-analysis
authors: Bin-Qi Yang; Yangjuan Bai; Yamei Li; Zeng-Jie Wang; Yuan-Zhen He; Yun-Ying Shi
abstract:
Background and Aims
Vitamin D deficiency or insufficiency is prevalent among kidney transplant recipients. Reliable conclusions regarding post-transplant vitamin D supplementation in this population are lacking from any single trial. We conducted a meta-analysis to aggregate the available evidence and analyze the impact of vitamin D supplementation on the outcomes of kidney transplant recipients.
Method
We conducted a systematic literature search in the PubMed, Web of Science, and Cochrane databases. The included articles compared the clinical efficacy of vitamin D supplementation in kidney transplant recipients by evaluating various parameters.
Results
A total of 9 studies were included. The studies reviewed spanned the period from 2005 to 2023, with the number of recipients ranging from 79 to 536. The mean age of KTRs varied from 39 to 54 years, and the percentage of male participants ranged from 49% to 58%. The total follow-up duration across the studies varied from 12 to 27.7 months. Dose of vitamin D ranged from 800 to 7000 IU daily. There was a significant improvement in 25(OH)D levels (WMD 11.63 ng/ml, 95% CI 5.71–17.55). Post-transplant vitamin D supplementation was linked to lower levels of parathyroid hormone without increasing the risk of hypercalcemia (P = 0.049). Additionally, vitamin D supplementation was associated with higher post-transplant femoral neck bone mineral density scores (P = 0.036). No correlation was found between vitamin D supplementation and serum creatinine levels. Sensitivity analyses showed good stability of the pooled results.
Conclusion
Post-transplant vitamin D supplementation in kidney transplant recipients significantly improves hyperparathyroidism, increases femoral neck bone mineral density, and alleviates post-transplant bone disease.

title: #2112 Dialysis initiation after renal graft failure: do outcomes differ from low-clearance-clinic patients?
authors: Mar Huelva-López; Cayetana Moyano Peregrín; Carlos Fernando Novillo Sarmiento; María Luisa Agüera Morales; Victoria Eugenia García Montemayor; Maria Sagrario Soriano Cabrera; Raquel Ojeda López
abstract:
Background and Aims
There is ongoing debate about whether kidney transplant recipients with a failing graft should be managed in general transplant clinics (TC) or low-clearance clinics (LCC) to optimise their preparation for the initiation of renal replacement therapy. At our centre, only patients with native kidney dysfunction are followed up in LCC.
The aim of our study was to compare whether there were differences between both patient profiles before starting dialysis and their outcomes after one year on the technique. We analysed patients from two separate periods, 15 years apart.
Method
We included all patients who started dialysis at our centre from general TC and LCC during two periods: 2000–2006 and 2015–2021. Clinical and demographic data, as well as one-year outcomes after dialysis initiation, were collected for each patient. The results were compared.
Results
During the two study periods, a total of 1.108 patients initiated dialysis. Patients from the TC (n = 194) were younger (51.95 ± 14.2 vs 67.6 ± 13.7 years, P < 0.001), had less diabetes (16% vs 28%, P < 0.001), and started dialysis with a higher estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) based on the CKD-EPI formula (8.4 ± 3.2 vs 7.1 ± 2.5 ml/min/1.73 m², P < 0.001) compared to patients from the LCC (n = 914). One year after starting dialysis, we had data from 937 of them: 92.5% of patients from TC remained on dialysis, 2.1% had died, and 5.3% underwent retransplantation. Survival analysis showed better outcomes for patients from the TC compared to the LCC (P < 0.001), which was confirmed in multivariate analysis (P = 0.003) (Fig. A). Survival analysis by periods showed that TC patients had a significant advantage in both periods. However, multivariate analysis only confirmed this in the recent period (P = 0.03) (Fig. B).
Given the previous results, we compared only previously transplanted patients by periods (96 from the earlier vs 91 from the recent period). Fewer women started dialysis in the recent period (56.3% vs 73.6%, P = 0.009), with higher proportion of diabetes (23.1% vs 9.7%, P = 0.009), older age at dialysis initiation (56.2 ± 13.6 vs 48.2 ± 13.8 years, P < 0.001) and better eGFR (9.1 ± 3.1 vs 7.8 ± 3.2 ml/min/1.73 m², P < 0.001). One year after starting dialysis, 91.2% of patients from the recent period remained on dialysis, 1.1% had died, and 7.7% underwent retransplantation. Survival analysis showed no significant differences between the two periods (P = 0.319).
Conclusion
At our centre, patients who initiated dialysis from the TC were younger, with a lower proportion of diabetes and better eGFR. We observed better overall survival in these patients after one year on dialysis, especially in our recent period.

title: #2273 A surrogate marker for graft-to-recipient allocation could be identifying patients at risk of postoperative complications using donor data as predictors
authors: Carolina Salgado; Felipe Vera Cid; Francisca Gonzalez-Cohens; Fernando Gonzalez
abstract:
Background and Aims
A key challenge in kidney transplantation is optimizing graft allocation to maximize graft survival, recipient survival, and dialysis-free survival time. Variables such as delayed graft failure (DGF) and serum creatinine are widely recognized as reliable prognostic factors, and most allocation algorithms use these values as surrogate markers, relying on donor, recipient, and transplant data. This study aimed to investigate whether other transplant-related outcomes, such as early post-transplant complications, could be predicted with similar accuracy to DGF and serum creatinine.
Method
We analyzed 831 kidney transplants performed between 1989 and 2020 across three transplant centers using machine learning (ML) models. The dataset included 14 donor variables, 7 transplant variables, and 60 recipient variables. Four problem types were defined based on independent variable combinations: donor-only (D), donor + transplant (DT), donor + recipient (DR), and donor + transplant + recipient (DTR).
Of the patients, 355 (42.7%) experienced at least one complication during the first three months post-transplant, while 476 (57.3%) did not. Complications included biopsy proven acute tubular necrosis, vascular and urological complications, lymphocele, urinary tract infection, renal arterial stenosis, or atheromatous disease. Six ML models were used: Support Vector Machine (SVM), Decision Trees (DET), Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boost (GB), Extreme Gradient Boost (XGB), and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP). Performance was evaluated using accuracy and AUC-ROC metrics.
Results
The best AUC-ROC scores were:
• D: 80% (Decision Trees).
• DT: 78% (Gradient Boost).
• DR: 83% (Random Forest).
• DTR: 80% (Random Forest and Gradient Boost).
Conclusion
Although the highest predictive performance was achieved using donor and recipient data, donor-only data effectively predicted post-transplant complications. This finding underscores its potential use in assessing donor quality and improving graft allocation decisions.

title: #2578 Evaluation of the relationship between post-transplant graft elastographic findings and cardiac strain in renal transplant patients
authors: İsmail Emre Özbelen; Cansın Tulunay Kaya; İrem Müge Akbulut Koyuncu; Yavuz Metin; Gizem Kumru; Şule Şengül; Kenan Keven; Sim Kutlay
abstract:
Background and Aims
The aim of this study was to detect cardiac fibrosis that may develop with renal fibrosis in transplant patients by shear wave elastography and echocardiography, which are non-invasive, easy to apply, inexpensive and easily reproducible methods. Strain represents the contractility of a myocardial segment relative to its original size and is expressed as a percentage. In individuals with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), many echocardiographic and laboratory markers appear normal in the early stages. However, with speckle tracking echocardiography (STE), left and right ventricular global longitudinal strain(LV/RV GLS), right ventricular free wall strain(RV FWS), and left atrial strain(SR) have been shown to indicate diastolic dysfunction. Early detection of renal fibrosis can facilitate treatment at an earlier stage. While the gold standard for detecting renal fibrosis is renal biopsy, its invasive nature, the potential for complications, and high cost have led to a greater focus on noninvasive techniques. Among these techniques, ultrasound is the most widely used due to its practicality, low cost, and effectiveness in early evaluation and long-term follow-up of kidney grafts in the post-transplant period. Shear wave elastography (SWE), available in the latest ultrasound devices, applies acoustic radiation force to tissues at high power (2.67 MHz frequency) and short duration (0.03–0.4 ms) via ultrasound probes instead of external compression. In the SWE method, tissue stiffness is measured using the Young's modulus of elasticity and expressed in kilopascals (kPa).
Method
The study is a single-center, cross-sectional and prospective study. Using STE, strain parameters such as LV/RV GLS, RV FWS, and SR values were evaluated before transplantation, at the 6th month after transplantation, and at the 12th month after transplantation. Additionally, left atrial volumes can also be measured with STE. In elastographic evaluations, kPa values were assessed at the 1st week, the 6th month, and the 12th month post-transplantation. The collected data were compared over time, aiming to indirectly reach conclusions.
Results
According to pre-transplant echocardiographic parameters, none of the patients were found to have diastolic dysfunction. Similarly, when evaluated based on post-transplant echocardiographic parameters, no patients were identified with diastolic dysfunction at the 6th or 12th month. LV GLS, RV GLS and RV FWS values decreased at 6 months and 12 months after transplantation compared to pre-transplantation, but statistical significance was not found (p: 0.091, p: 0.368, p: 0.368, respectively). In addition, kPa values increased during the process, but again no statistical significance was found (p: 0.074). Descriptive analyses of elastographic and strain parameters are given in Appendix-1 and Appendix-2. When the follow-up of strain parameters was analyzed, only RV GLS values showed a statistically significant recovery at 12 months post-transplantation compared to pre-transplantation (p: 0.028).
Conclusion
Despite the narrow sampling and limited follow-up period, the statistically significant recovery in right ventricular GLS values and the clinically significant but not statistically significant increase in kPa values are remarkable.

title: #621 Dynamic assessment of cardiovascular risk factors in kidney transplant recipients
authors: Maria Smaliakova; Aleh Kalachyk
abstract:
Background and Aims
The incidence of cardiovascular diseases in patients with Stage 5 Chronic Kidney Disease is more than twenty times higher than in the general population.
The aim of the study was dynamic assessment of cardiovascular risk factors in patients with chronic kidney disease in the preoperative period and after kidney transplantation.
Method
The study included 43 patients of the kidney transplant waiting list. At the time of kidney transplantation the average age was 45.3 ± 11.9 years; 53.5% (n = 23) were women, 46.5% (n = 20)—men. Patients were examined in the preoperative period, six months and five years after transplantation.
Results
The incidence of arterial hypertension was unchanged during the observation period, while episodes of hypotension in the postoperative period were diagnosed less frequently than in the preoperative period—4.7% (n = 2) versus 44.2% (n = 19), P < 0.001. Five years after transplantation, the average body mass index of recipients became higher and the incidence of obesity increased: 26.0 ± 4.8 kg/m2 versus 24.6 ± 4.2 kg/m2 and 25.6% (n = 11) 7.0% (n = 3), P < 0.01, respectively.
The blood level of total cholesterol decreased only in the late postoperative period in comparison with the previous stages: 5.20 ± 1.09 mmol/l versus 5.91 ± 1.24 mmol/l and 5.70 ± 1.34 mmol/l, P < 0.05. Blood triglyceride levels decreased progressively: from 2.31 (1.58–3.37) mmol/l to 1.54 (1.16–1.94) mmol/l after six months and to 1.30 (0.90–1.80) mmol/l after five years, P < 0.05.
The blood glucose level of recipients was comparable in the preoperative period and six months after transplantation—6.1 (5.5–6.3) mmol/L and 5.8 (4.5–6.3) mmol/L accordingly and decreased five years after transplantation—5.2 (5.0–5.8) mmol/l, P < 0.001, as the frequency of hyperglycemia did: from 44.2% (n = 19) and 32.6% (n = 14) to 11.6% (n = 5), P < 0.05.
The average blood concentration of hemoglobin increased in the long-term postoperative period: from 108 ± 17 g/l to 125 ± 18 g/l and 127 ± 18 g/l, P < 0.001, and the frequency of anemia decreased from 79.1% (n = 34) patients in the preoperative period to 48.8% (n = 21) after six months and 34.9% (n = 15) five years after transplantation, P < 0.01. Transplantation also helped reduce the incidence of iatrogenic hypererythropoietinemia: from 27.9% (n = 12) to 4.7% (n = 2), P < 0.05.
Dialysis patients had a high level of brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) in the blood—3300 (1800–3300) pg/ml. In the postoperative period it was significantly lower than in the preoperative period—175 (60–350) pg/ml after six months and 225 (60–500) pg/ml five years after transplantation, P < 0.01. An increased level of NT-proBNP was detected in all recipients in the preoperative period and decreased to normal values in 37.2% (n = 16) in the postoperative period, P < 0.001.
Echocardiography showed no changes in ejection fraction and left ventricular myocardial mass index, the incidence of diastolic dysfunction: 64.4 ± 8.1%, 118.79 ± 43.93 g/m2 and 18.6% (n = 8) in the preoperative period versus 66.0 ± 7.5%, 117.32 ± 37.38 g/m2 and 11.6% (n = 5) in the long-term postoperative period, P > 0.05. The absence of negative changes in the structural and functional state of the heart for five years of observation in patients with chronic kidney disease can be considered as a positive stabilizing effect of transplantation.
Conclusion
Based on the study it was found that in the long-term postoperative period, compared with the preoperative period, kidney transplant recipients have a decrease in the incidence of hypotension, anemia, hypererythropoietinemia, an increase in body mass index and blood hemoglobin concentration, a decrease in the blood levels of total cholesterol, triglycerides, glucose and NT-proBNP, as well as stable the structural and functional characteristics of the heart.

title: #2928 Risk factors of mucocutaneous manifestations in kidney transplant recipients
authors: Wejden Ltaief; Meriem Ben Salem; Yosra Soua; Nouha Ben Mahmoud; Manel Ben Salah; Sirine Bchir; Ahmed Letaief; Mouna Hamouda; Habib Skhiri
abstract:
Background and Aims
Kidney transplant recipients may be more susceptible to mucocutaneous manifestations due to prolonged immunosuppressive therapy, which can increase their risk of infections and dermatological conditions. This study aimed to evaluate the prevalence and the risk factors of mucocutaneous manifestations in this population.
Method
Kidney transplant recipients may be more susceptible to mucocutaneous manifestations due to prolonged immunosuppressive therapy, which can increase their risk of infections and dermatological conditions. This study aimed to evaluate the prevalence and the risk factors of mucocutaneous manifestations in this population.
Results
In a cohort of 139 kidney transplant recipients, 65 patients (46.7%) developed mucocutaneous manifestations. The average age was 42.12 years with a male predominance (71.2%). The mean age at transplantation was 30.28 years. Living-related donors accounted for 69.8% of cases. Induction immunosuppressive therapy included Thymoglobulin in 82% and basiliximab in 9.4% of cases. Maintenance therapy regimens were: low-dose corticosteroids, tacrolimus, and mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) in 51.8%; low-dose corticosteroids, ciclosporin, and MMF in 12.2%; and other combinations, including azathioprine and sirolimus, in the remaining patients.
Among those with mucocutaneous manifestations, 30.2% had a single lesion, 9.4% had two lesions, and 7.2% had multiple lesions. Infectious origins accounted for 44 cases, involving fungi, viruses, or bacteria. Inflammatory dermatoses, such as eczema, and pre-neoplastic lesions, including seborrheic and actinic keratosis, were also noted. Neoplastic lesions were observed in seven cases : basal cell carcinoma in situ, invasive squamous cell carcinoma, Kaposi's sarcoma, and anogenital carcinoma. Additionally, 21 cases were identified as iatrogenic lesions resulting from immunosuppressants.
The analytical study identified several risk factors for mucocutaneous manifestations: younger average age, female gender, monthly exposure to high-intensity ultraviolet rays, family history of chronic renal failure, and personal history of sunburn.
Conclusion
These findings underscore the importance of regular dermatological monitoring and tailored interventions for kidney transplant recipients, especially those with identified risk factors, to manage and mitigate mucocutaneous complications effectively.

title: #3297 High donor-derived cell-free DNA levels do not reflect kidney allograft status in aHUS patient
authors: Magdalena Kuriata-Kordek; Kornelia Gajek; Adrian Domagalski; Dawid Przystupski; Karolina Marek-Bukowiec; Weronika Smulska; Patryk Jerzak; Marek Ussowicz; Miroslaw Banasik
abstract:
Background and Aims
Kidney transplant (KT) rejection remains a major challenge in transplant medicine, as it significantly contributes to graft dysfunction and, if left untreated, can ultimately lead to allograft loss. Early detection and timely intervention are crucial for improving long-term graft survival. However, due to the risks and invasiveness of biopsy, there is growing interest in developing non-invasive and reliable methods for detecting KT rejection. Plasma donor-derived cell-free DNA (dd-cfDNA) has emerged as a promising biomarker for non-invasive diagnosis of renal allograft rejection. Any injury to the transplanted kidney that leads to necrosis or apoptosis results in the release of substantial amounts of dd-cfDNA into the bloodstream. In clinical practice, when other causes of renal injury are excluded, elevated dd-cfDNA levels often indicate ongoing subclinical rejection. Atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (aHUS) is a rare disease, affecting approximately 2 in a million individuals, and is characterized by thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA). If not properly managed, aHUS can progress to end-stage renal disease (ESRD), necessitating renal replacement therapy, including kidney transplantation. Despite advancements in transplant monitoring, data on the kinetics of %dd-cfDNA in kidney transplant recipients with aHUS remain limited, particularly regarding its effectiveness in assessing graft health in this unique patient population. The aim of this study was to evaluate the kinetics and clinical utility of dd-cfDNA as a biomarker for monitoring graft health in kidney transplant recipients with aHUS.
Method
Thirteen kidney transplant recipients provided informed consent and were enrolled at the University Hospital in Wrocław. The cohort included 11 non-aHUS patients with stable renal function and two with aHUS. Transplantations were performed between April 2022 and February 2023, and recipients were monitored for two years to assess graft health. Blood samples were collected at four time points: one week (D7), two weeks (D14), one month (M1), and two months (M2) post-transplant. dd-cfDNA was quantified using the AlloSeq cfDNA Kit (CareDX Inc., Brisbane, CA, USA) and analyzed on a MiSeq instrument (Illumina Inc., San Diego, CA, USA). The results were expressed as %dd-cfDNA, with levels above 0.5% considered indicative of a high risk of rejection. Sequencing data was analyzed using AlloSeq cfDNA Software (CareDX). To comprehensively assess graft health, clinical data—including serum creatinine levels, kidney biopsy findings, and the presence of donor-specific anti-HLA antibodies (DSA)—were collected over two years post-transplant.
Results
The median percentage of dd-cfDNA at specific time points for each group is depicted in the graph below. In non-aHUS kidney transplant recipients, the median %dd-cfDNA ranged from 0.72% to 0.12% at approximately one month post-transplant. In aHUS patients, the median %dd-cfDNA level fluctuated around 1% during the first month. None of the patients had detectable DSA during the observation period. Additionally, no significant correlation was observed between %dd-cfDNA levels and serum creatinine across the study cohort.
Conclusion
Although current guidelines associate dd-cfDNA levels above 1% with a high risk of transplant rejection, our findings indicate that in aHUS kidney recipients, elevated dd-cfDNA levels do not predict long-term allograft rejection. No cases of rejection occurred in aHUS patients during the two-year follow-up. This suggests that while increased %dd-cfDNA may indicate graft injury, it does not universally indicate rejection. Larger studies are needed to further clarify its role in this unique patient population and assess its predictive value for clinical decision-making.

title: #3456 Less is more? Evaluating lower thymoglobulin induction in kidney transplantation
authors: Ana Rita Pereirinha Ramos; João Figueiredo Martins; Andreia Curto; Fernando Caeiro; Ines Aires; Manuel Anibal A Ferreira; Cristina Rego de Freitas; Mendes Jorge
abstract:
Background and Aims
Thymoglobulin is widely used for induction therapy in kidney transplantation, but higher doses are associated with increased infectious complications. In August 2023, an institutional protocol modification reduced the Thymoglobulin induction dose from 10.5 mg/kg to 6 mg/kg, adjusted the tacrolimus regimen from a pre-transplant dose of 0.1 mg/kg and post-transplant dose of 0.05 mg/kg to a consistent dose of 0.2 mg/kg both pre- and post-transplant, and expanded Thymoglobulin coverage to include Black patients and those with a detected donor-specific antibody. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of this change on renal function, incidence of acute rejection, and infectious complications.
Method
This retrospective cohort study included kidney transplant recipients who underwent transplantation between September 2022 and June 2024 at a reference transplant center. Only first kidney transplants from brain-dead donors who received induction therapy with Thymoglobulin were included. Patients were stratified according to the immunosuppressive regimen (10.5 mg/kg vs. 6 mg/kg) following the institutional protocol modification. All patients underwent protocol biopsies within 14 days post-transplant and followed for at least 6 months. Clinical and laboratory data, including kidney function, rejection, infections, and post-transplant diabetes, were assessed. Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS (version 29).
Results
We analyzed 43 kidney transplant recipients meeting the inclusion and exclusion criteria from a total of 165. The mean age at transplantation was 51.02 ± 12.15 years, with 55.8% Caucasian, 34.9% female, and 24% receiving kidneys from expanded criteria donors (mean age 56.5 ± 28.0 years). Most (39.5%) had five HLA mismatches, and 55.8% had preformed donor-specific antibodies (mean fluorescence intensity of 1824 ± 1264). Cold ischemia time averaged 659.6 ± 296.1 minutes. The sample was stratified into a 10.5 mg/kg (n = 21, 48.8%) and a 6 mg/kg (n = 22, 51.2%) Thymoglobulin group, with comparable demographic, clinical and immunological characteristics.
Patients receiving 6 mg/kg of Thymoglobulin had a significantly lower infection rate than those receiving 10.5 mg/kg (27.3% vs. 57.1%, P = 0.047), with urinary tract infections requiring hospitalization being the most common.
Acute rejection was significantly more frequent in the 6 mg/kg Thymoglobulin group compared to the 10.5 mg/kg group (54.5% vs. 19.0%, P = 0.016). Of the 16 observed cases of rejection (37.2% of the population), 30.2% corresponded to T cell-mediated rejection, while 7% corresponded to antibody-mediated rejection. The predominant treatment approach (14%) involved a combination of methylprednisolone pulses and Thymoglobulin.
At 6 months post-transplant, the estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) was significantly higher in the 6 mg/kg Thymoglobulin group compared to the 10.5 mg/kg group (57.67 ± 20.58 vs. 46.90 ± 17.37 ml/min/1.73 m², P = 0.025). Consistently, renal dysfunction (eGFR < 45 ml/min/1.73 m²) was significantly more frequent in the 10.5 mg/kg group (66.7% vs. 23.8%, P = 0.005).
Conclusion
Reducing Thymoglobulin induction from 10.5 mg/kg to 6 mg/kg was associated with a lower infection rate and improved renal function at 6 months, despite a higher incidence of acute rejection. However, protocol biopsies enabled early detection and treatment, mitigating its impact on graft function. These findings suggest that a lower Thymoglobulin dose may be a viable strategy to reduce infectious complications while maintaining graft function.

title: #3626 Long-term cardiovascular and skeletal effects of bisphosphonate treatment in the first year after kidney transplantation; a 13-year prospective follow-up of a randomized controlled study of ibandronate vs placebo
authors: Ruth Strommen; Markus Hovd; Kristin Godang; Trine Finnes; Eva Kirkhus; Anders Åsberg; Jens Bollerslev; Hege Kampen Pihlstrøm
abstract:
Background and Aims
Kidney transplant recipients are at high risk of fracture with significant individual and societal cost. Bisphosphonates are effective antiresorptive agents reducing bone turnover, with known increased risk of atrial fibrillation despite reduced cardiovascular mortality; however, such effects are not established in kidney transplant recipients. Prospective studies investigating the effect of bisphosphonates in kidney transplant recipients are few, of limited size and generally of shorter duration, hence possible long-term benefits and risks are unclear. Our aim was to investigate the long-term effect of intravenous ibandronate in the first year after kidney transplantation on pre-specified cardiovascular events, cerebrovascular disease, changes in bone mineral density (BMD), fracture incidence and all-cause mortality.
Method
We conducted a pre-specified 13-year, prospective follow-up of a randomized, placebo-controlled trial. Study treatment consisted of ibandronate/placebo in addition to calcium (1 g/day) and active vitamin D3 (calcitriol 0.25 mcg/day) in kidney transplant recipients during the first post-transplantation year. Routine biochemistry and biomarkers of bone turnover, dual energy X-ray and X-ray of the thoraco-lumbar-spine were performed at baseline (time of transplantation), 10 weeks, 12 months and 13 years post-transplantation.
Results
A total of 129 patients with a mean (SD) age of 51.4 (13.8) years were included in the original study, of which 69 patients completed a 13-year follow-up visit, 40 patients had died, and 20 patients were lost to follow-up. There was no significant difference between treatment groups in incidence of cardiovascular events. In the ibandronate group, no change in hip BMD was observed from baseline to the 13-year visit. In contrast, the placebo group demonstrated a mean (95% confidence interval) change of −0.10 g/cm2 [−0.15, −0.06] for dual total hip BMD and a mean change of −0.10 g/cm2 [−0.14, −0.06] for femoral neck BMD. For lumbar spine BMD, a mean improvement of 0.05 g/cm2 [0.0019, 0.097] was observed in the treatment group only. Group difference in BMD change was statistically significant for dual total hip (P < 0.0001), femoral neck (P < 0.0001) and lumbar spine (P = 0.0390). A new morphometric fracture occurred in 11% (n = 4) of patients in the ibandronate group and 16% (n = 5) patients in the placebo group.
Conclusion
There was no difference in the incidence of cardiovascular events between the ibandronate and placebo group. BMD was reasonably well preserved 13 years after transplantation irrespective of treatment, with even a small protective effect of the 1-year ibandronate study intervention.

title: #3741 Kidney transplantation in patient with ureteral and renal agenesis in sirenomelia: five years of experience
authors: Carolina Ciavaglia; Elisa Buti; Alberto Magnasco; Antonella Trivelli; Luigi Cirillo; Carmela Errichiello; Francesca Becherucci; Iris Fontana; Paola Romagnani
abstract:
Background and Aims
Sirenomelia is a rare congenital malformation driven by fused lower extremities and associated with other anomalies of genital, urinary and gastrointestinal systems, single umbilical artery and sever oligohydramnios. It is a lethal condition in the perinatal period and only 1% of cases can survive the 1st week after birth. The survival and prognosis are closely connected to an appropriate kidney function.
Method
We describe 5 years of experience after renal transplantation (RT) in a rare case of sirenomelia.
Results
A 22-years-old gravida delivered at 40 weeks’ gestation a 2450-g female infant. No malformations were documented prenatally. At the birth, the newborn presented sireniform malformation. Radiological imaging showed a single dysplastic and ectopic kidney located in pelvic region with bladder and urethral agenesis. Alteration of the excretory tracts was characterized by absence of ureteral with a cutaneous orifice that allowed the urinary outflow. A single median ovary was recognizable; but uterus, vagina and external genitals were absent. On second day of life a terminal ileostomy was performed for anorectal and descending colon atresia. Furthermore, a surgical team succeeded in total separation of the lower limbs. The girl had progressive chronic renal failure with initial serum creatinine of 1.7 mg/dL. Subsequently, during a pyelonephritis, she developed an acute kidney injury (serum creatinine 9.2 mg/dL). We started continuous renal replacement therapy. No improvement in clinical condition was observed; pelvic nephrectomy surgery had to be performed. The gradual resolution of illness allowed us to start intermittent hemodialysis.
At 16 years old, the patient received cadaveric RT and contextual ureterocutaneostomy was performed. The induction regimen consisted in basiliximab; whereas the maintenance immunosuppressive treatment consisted of tacrolimus, mycophenolate mofetil and corticosteroid. No surgical or immunological complications were reported. Her post-transplant course was characterized by some infectious events, particularly pyelonephritis. Therefore, we decided to insert a ureteral stent to allow the urinary outflow.
Five years after RT, patient presents good general condition with normal blood pressure. The ureteral stent is replaced every three weeks. The most recent laboratory test reveals normal blood count, creatinine 1.14 mg/dl (eGFR 69 mL/min/1.73 m2), no electrolytic alteration, no significant proteinuria, no inflammatory markers and negative screening for viruses.
Conclusion
We report a rare case of sirenomelia with overall survival of approximately 21 years old and 5 years after RT. Our experience demonstrates a greater survival rate in patients with maintained renal function. The kidney transplantation may represent a management strategy in patient with similar urinary tracts anomalies.
